body:
Fixes #860
Fixes #861

Both Issues are in `00-foundations/02-governance-projects-and-retention.ipynb`, and they
are in one pull request because they cannot be verified apart: the notebook execution
that proves #860's fix also regenerates cell 15, whose output is what #861 is about.
Committing #860 alone would have left section 6's prose contradicting the output
printed four cells below it, in the same file. If you would rather see them split, say
so and I will raise the prose change separately and rebase this one onto it.

## What changed and why

**#860.** The first code cell under `## 1. Projects` archived every project whose name
started with `samples-foundations` before creating its own, selected by a name prefix
rather than by an identifier the run created. The account is shared, `GET
/v1/organization/projects` is account-wide, and the demo name was the fixed constant
`samples-foundations`, so two runs of the notebook were not independent: the second
run's sweep archived the first run's live project. The comment above the loop argued
the opposite, "matching on the name is the whole test", which is the reasoning that
made it unsafe. The sweep is removed, the project is `samples-foundations-<uuid4
hex[:8]>` per run, section 3's rename derives from the same stem, and section 7 already
archived by the identifier the create call returned, so it needed no change. Two
sentences in section 1 carry the reason and say how to clean up after an interrupted
run.

**#861.** Section 6 stated that `AWS/Bedrock` carries no `Project` dimension and that a
per-project graph is not available for `bedrock-runtime` traffic. The namespace now
publishes a `ProjectId` dimension, so the premise was false, and the cell below the
paragraph printed `per-project graphs: True` against prose denying the dimension. The
section's advice is unchanged, because the one value of that dimension is `default`:
the prose now says what was measured and why the printed `True` means the dimension
exists rather than that it separates workloads.

## Evidence

All measurements from the sandbox on the Bedrock test role, venv built from
`requirements.txt` only (boto3 and botocore 1.43.59), 13 November 2026.

`ListMetrics` walk of `AWS/Bedrock`, `us-east-1`, run independently of the notebook:

```
AWS/Bedrock 14 metric names
     732 streams by ModelId, ResolvedServiceTier, ServiceTier
     727 streams by ModelId
      68 streams by ModelId, ProjectId
      13 streams by account only
       9 streams by ProjectId
   level 'ModelId, ProjectId' metric names: ['CacheReadInputTokenCount', 'EstimatedTPMQuotaUsage',
       'InputTokenCount', 'InvocationClientErrors', 'InvocationLatency', 'InvocationThrottles',
       'Invocations', 'OutputTokenCount', 'TimeToFirstToken']
   level 'ProjectId' metric names: (the same nine)
   distinct ProjectId values: {'default': 77}
   per-project graphs test: True
```

The same walk in `us-west-2`, which is why the note is scoped to a Region rather than
written as a property of the namespace:

```
us-west-2 AWS/Bedrock 14 names
     119 streams by ModelId
      13 streams by account only
       4 streams by ModelId, ResolvedServiceTier, ServiceTier
       3 streams by ContextWindow, ModelId
   ProjectId values: {}
```

Oregon has runtime traffic in the window and published no `ProjectId` stream.
`ListMetrics` returns only metrics with data in the past two weeks, so this does not
show the Region cannot publish the level; it shows this account did not see it there,
which is as much as the notebook claims.

The service contradicts the documentation, and the service wins here. The [runtime
metrics page](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/monitoring-runtime-metrics.html),
read 13 November 2026, lists under the dimensions it supports:

> ModelId – all metrics
> ModelId + ImageSize + BucketedStepSize – OutputImageCount
> ModelId + ContextWindow – Invocations, InvocationLatency, InputTokenCount,
> OutputTokenCount, EstimatedTPMQuotaUsage

No `ProjectId`, and no `ServiceTier`/`ResolvedServiceTier` either, though this notebook
has counted the service-tier level since it was written. The paragraph quotes the page
and says both levels are undocumented.

For #860, the condition that makes the old sweep unsafe held when I checked it: `GET
/v1/organization/projects` in `us-east-1` returned 20 projects, 18 of them tagged by
other work, and none of them named `samples-foundations*`. That last part matters for
this PR's own verification: it means executing the notebook on `main`'s code during
this cycle would not have archived anything, so nothing belonging to another project
was touched while I was testing. I did not reproduce the destructive case by creating a
stand-in project; Issue #860 already carries that measurement, and reproducing it would
have meant archiving a project in a shared account to prove a point the code makes
plainly.

## Verification

Executed the notebook top to bottom in the sandbox, from its own directory, with a venv
built from `requirements.txt` only:

```
cd ~/repo/00-foundations && jupyter nbconvert --to notebook --execute --inplace \
    02-governance-projects-and-retention.ipynb
```

No error output in any cell. Committed outputs are the ones that run produced, fetched
back with `sandbox_fetch`. What the run showed:

```
cell  4  created : samples-foundations-de134e4f proj_7tmr4d6w... | status: active
cell  6  Responses        (OpenAI-Project)     : Canberra
         Chat Completions (OpenAI-Project)     : Canberra.
         Messages         (anthropic-workspace): Canberra
cell  8  rename          -> 200 samples-foundations-de134e4f-v2
cell 10  from the stored response  : Ada
         from the unstored response: 400 previous_response_not_found ...
         deleted the stored response
cell 15  AWS/Bedrock  ... 68 streams by ModelId, ProjectId / 9 streams by ProjectId
                       per-project graphs: True
cell 17  archive -> 200 archived | still in the listing: False
         GET by ID -> 200 archived | archived_at set: True
```

The five dimension levels the new paragraph names are the five the cell prints, in the
same account and Region. The known-answer cells are right: Canberra three ways, and
`Ada` recalled from the stored response while the unstored one is refused. Three runs
of the notebook across this cycle each created a project under a different random
suffix and each archived its own identifier in section 7; nothing else in the account
was archived, and no project was deleted or archived by a listing. Four sandbox
sessions were started this cycle and all were stopped.

## Security gate

`scan_all` on the clone, run after the last edit: `gate_passed: true`. bandit 0,
semgrep 0, checkov 0, ash 0 across its five scanners (bandit, checkov, detect-secrets,
npm-audit, semgrep); `did_not_run` empty, 43 files scanned. Committed output carries no
credential and no real account identifier: the one account identifier in it is the
`123456789012` placeholder that `safe_print` substitutes into the
`bedrock:GetAccountDataRetention` denial in section 5, and project and response
identifiers go through `redact_ids`. Steps 4 to 7 took two laps: self-review sent me
back for the two findings below, then the gate and the review ran again.

## Self-review findings I fixed

- The new section 1 note first said to archive a leftover project "by the ID that run

author: brayniac
body:
The batched rate path's union stage held far more points than it needs while combining a process group's members. Over a source that spans a producer restart, this was most of a dashboard browse's peak memory. Part of #400; follows #413.

## Before, problem, change

**Before.** Over a process group, `grid_rates` sends each member series' grid points to a `UnionStage`, which queues them per unit (one label set) until every member of the unit can answer at that time (`settle`), then picks one member's point by the S3 coverage rule. Since #413 this includes a source with several producer epochs, one member per epoch.

**Problem.** On a 12 h recording of 655 cgroups with one agent restart, a display of `sum(irate(cgroup_syscall[5m]))` with a 512 MiB pool still peaked at about 3.0 GB after #413; dhat put 2.6 GB of the 2.85 GB live at the peak in these queues (`UnionStage::emit`, one queue per member series). Three causes:

1. `settle` ran only after each chunk (up to eight segments), so each series queued up to a chunk of points.
2. `scan::interleave` read every scan it had not read yet before the others (an unread scan counted as starting at 0). The later epoch's first chunk was read right after the earlier epoch's first chunk, and its points waited until the earlier epoch had been read through to the restart.
3. A member not read yet has its rate's cursor at the grid's start and an empty row track, so it blocked every time from the start, even a member whose epoch starts hours later.

**Change.**
1. `grid_rates` also calls `settle` after each segment.
2. New `ChunkReader::unread_start` (provided, `None` by default): a time no row of the reader's unread segments is before, known without reading them. `CounterScan::unread_start` forwards it. `SegmentedScan` gives it from its catalog (`rest_from`), and `None` once no segment remains. The query-side wrappers `RecordedChunks` and `RecordingChunks` forward it. `interleave` orders a scan not read yet by it, and uses it in `rest_start`; a scan that gives none is still read first.
3. `UnionStage::firsts`, from `UnionMember::rows.0`: a member whose span starts after `t` no longer blocks `t`; it has no point and no row there.

## What a caller sees differently

- Answers are unchanged.
- `metriken_storage::scan::ChunkReader` gains a provided method; an implementor that does not override it behaves as before. An implementor that returns a time later than one of its unread rows makes the batch path drop comparison rows and flush grouped display points too early; the doc states the contract.
- `interleave` returns chunks in a different order when its scans give `unread_start`: a scan that starts late is no longer read first, so its series' `ended` report comes later.

## Decisions

- Chosen: three small changes over making the union stage aware of epochs. Each is a general rule (settle when you can; read in time order; a member cannot answer before its span) and each is needed: undoing any one alone takes the new test from 29 to 169, 188 or 2018 points per series.
- Not done: the union stage still holds each point for the coverage rule's look-ahead (nine rows of the member's own) and a segment; and between members read side by side (copies of one recording), a chunk of lag remains, as `BOUND` in `union_memory.rs` documents.

## Where to look

1. `metriken-storage/src/scan.rs`: `ChunkReader::unread_start` and its use in `Interleaved`.
2. `metriken-storage/src/segmented.rs`: `SegmentedScan::unread_start`.
3. `metriken-query/src/batch_rate.rs`: `UnionStage::firsts` in `settle`, and the per-segment `settle` in `grid_rates`.
4. `metriken-storage/tests/union_memory.rs`: `a_restarted_source_holds_its_points_a_segment_at_a_time`.

## Testing

- `cargo nextest run -p metriken-storage -p metriken-query --all-features`: 1008 passed. Doctests pass, clippy and fmt are clean.
- New test `a_restarted_source_holds_its_points_a_segment_at_a_time`: one source restarting halfway, 17 series, 20-row segments; rows on the second and half a second past it; the whole recording and a range starting after the restart. It bounds the union stage's held points at 40 per series (measured 29) and compares every batched and display answer with the per-series path. Undoing each part alone fails it: per-chunk settle 169 per series, unread scans first 188, no later-epoch exemption 2018. The half-second case was added after the review found that an exhausted scan reported `Some(u64::MAX)`; with that bug it fails at 1495 per series.
- Memory, 12 h recording, full 426-query browse, jemalloc as the allocator, macOS, both builds on main with #406, #407 and #413, four interleaved rounds:

  | File, pool | #413 alone | this PR |
  |---|---|---|
  | `.dendro`, 512 MiB | 3804–3869 MiB | 1640–1695 MiB |
  | `.dendro`, 2 GiB | 5373–5412 MiB | 3204–3233 MiB |
  | v3 `.rez`, 512 MiB | 1837–1839 MiB | 1810–1848 MiB |
  | v3 `.rez`, 2 GiB | 4060–4069 MiB | 4049–4065 MiB |

  Three runs a side: the first round ran while other builds loaded the machine and read up to 2807 MiB lower in five of its eight cells, and is left out. The `.rez` file records no restart, so it reads as one member and has no union stage; it is the control. Every answer is the same on both builds (per-query hashes, floats rounded to 9 significant digits). Browse times are not quoted: the machine was loaded throughout.
- The all-cgroups query alone, `.dendro`, 512 MiB, on builds without #406/#407: 2995–3015 MiB in 2.3–2.6 s before, 860 MiB in 1.9 s after (two runs a side).
- Not measured: the cost of settling after every segment on a large group with no restart (for example many copies of one recording). `settle` loops over the partition's units each time.
- Not tested: Linux, glibc malloc.

## Production-only risks

A reader outside this workspace that wraps a `ChunkReader` and forwards `later_rows` but not `unread_start` gets the old read-first order for that scan; correct, but without this PR's memory saving.

Review: one fresh-agent review, then two re-checks.
- The first returned "fix first": an exhausted `SegmentedScan` reported `Some(u64::MAX)`, so a member with an empty scan (a range starting after the restart, between two segments) was read last and held every point of the range, 1495 per series, worse than before the PR (fixed, with the half-second test case); the test's doc assigned its numbers to the wrong causes (it measured the attribution now in the doc); the per-segment settle comment overstated what it bounds; the `unread_start` contract did not state the lower bound callers rely on; two `interleave` docs parsed wrongly; the test checked no answers (now compared with the per-series path). All fixed. It found parts 1 and 3 sound and checked every other `interleave` caller and `ChunkReader` wrapper in the workspace.
- The first re-check returned "fix first" on text only: one test-doc clause claimed every query had an empty scan (only `irate` does), a long doc line, and a wording fix. Applied as given.
- The second re-check covered the CHANGELOG: it asked that the left-out round and the unchanged `.rez` control be stated (both now in the entry). Applied as given; it also checked the one sentence added to #413's entry.

_Requested by **Ben** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_014iF1BVbZJaVhkKSCvBC7Yf)_

## What changed

The Homebrew cask update moves out of `release.yml` into its own workflow, `homebrew.yml`. Release still calls it after every stable release, and it can now be run by hand (Actions > Homebrew cask > Run workflow) to point the cask at an existing release, defaulting to the latest.

It reads each dmg's sha256 from the release's asset digests instead of downloading ~550 MB (it falls back to downloading if a digest is missing), refuses drafts and prereleases, and writes a note in the run summary when `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` is missing.

Betas get no separate cask: signed builds update themselves, so Homebrew users install the stable cask and pick Settings > Updates > Update channel > Beta. README and the update-checks PRD say so.

## Why

Releases v0.2.0 and v0.2.1 were signed and notarized, but the `homebrew` job skipped both in 0 seconds because the `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` secret isn't set, so `Benbentwo/homebrew-tap` still has only its README. Once the secret exists, this lets the cask catch up without cutting a new release.

## How I tested it

- `actionlint` on both workflows passes.
- Ran the job's script locally against the real v0.2.1 release with stubbed `git`: it produced the cask with sha256s matching GitHub's digests and my own `sha256sum` of both dmgs. Against `v0.3.0-beta.23` it fails with the prerelease error.
- `ruby -c` on the generated cask.

## Checklist

- [x] No Conductor code, icons, images or text copied
- [x] Agents use official Claude access only (Agent SDK or API key)
- [x] Third-party code is MIT-compatible and noted in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md

## What and why
The lint rule `reserved-python-model-member` now NFKC-normalises a property name before comparing it with the reserved model members (`to_dict`, `from_dict`, `additional_properties`, `additional_keys`). CPython NFKC-normalises every identifier it parses, so the fullwidth `to_dict` and the long-s `additional_properties` lookalikes, which the real generator writes into the model unchanged, shadow the member at runtime but passed lint. They are now refused, and the finding still names the original property in its pointer and message. This is item 1 only of [ISSUE branchLeft/workspace#1618](https://github.com/branchLeft/workspace/issues/1618).

Unchanged source: `Tests  2 failed | 13 passed (15)`, each failure `AssertionError: expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0`. After the change: `Tests  15 passed (15)`. body:
設計書の 2.1・2.2・2.5 の受信の部分。画面と SSE は次の PR。

## 中身
- **モデル** (`src/lib/model.ts`): Eew・Quake・Tsunami・Advisory。**緊急地震速報の予想震度はモデルに入れない** (SSE でブラウザに渡すのもこの形なので、出ようがない)。設計書もそう直した
- **気象庁 XML** (`sources/jma.ts`・`jma-xml.ts`): eqvol.xml を 60 秒ごとに `If-None-Match`・`If-Modified-Since` で取り、取る種別だけ電文を取る。起動時と 10 分以上途切れた後に eqvol_l.xml。XML は `Bun.XML.parse` (依存は足さない)
- **P2P地震情報** (`sources/p2p.ts`): ws の 551・552・556。つながるたびに `/v2/history` で埋める。`id` で重複を除く
- **Wolfx** (`sources/wolfx.ts`): jma_eew。heartbeat に `ping`。`OriginalText` は受けたら捨てる (raw_messages には鍵だけ)
- **張り直し** (`sources/retry.ts`): full jitter のバックオフ。Wolfx は 90 秒無通信で張り直す
- **SQLite** (`db.ts`・`store.ts`・`merge.ts`): 原文 (gzip、30 日)・events (SSE の通し番号)・いまの姿。版の判定は報数・取消 (一連の情報)・訓練・P2P の仮の姿を XML で置き換え
- 受信は `hooks.server.ts` の `init` で起こし、adapter-bun の `sveltekit:shutdown` で止める (止めないと SIGTERM で終わらなかった)
- CI の Docker のスモークテストは `SONAE_RECEIVE=off` で情報源につながない

## 実際の受信で確かめたこと (コンテナで 2 回、計 3 分ほど)
- 気象庁: 長期フィードから VXSE51 9・VXSE52 6・VXSE53 47・VXSE61 1・VXSE62 1・VTSE41 1・VYSE52 1 を取り、読み取りの失敗は 0。2 回目は全部既に取ったものとして取り直さなかった
- P2P: history から 551 を 30 件。気象庁の XML と時刻で結ばれ、`jma+p2p` の地震になった (例: 2026-11-13 03:48 茨城県沖 M3.6 最大震度 1)
- **P2P は heartbeat を送ってこない**ので、90 秒の無通信で切ると張り直しを繰り返した。P2P だけ無通信では切らないようにし、設計書を直した
- Wolfx: 75 秒つないだままで切れなかった。SIGTERM で 3 つとも止まり、プロセスが終わった

## 試験の出典
- 気象庁のサンプル電文 (`jmaxml_20260917_Samples.zip`) から 17 通を、そのまま `tests/fixtures/jma/` に。出典と利用条件は同じ所の README
- P2P は API 仕様書 v2.3.0 の例 (`tests/fixtures/p2p/README.md`)
- Wolfx は項目の一覧から作ったもの (本物の原文は入れない)

## 未決のまま
- 震度速報と地震情報を番号が合わないときに結ぶ閾値は、仮に「時刻の差 90 秒以内で地域が重なる」(設計書の未決の点 5 に書いた)

author: mixedrealityio
body:
## Summary

Adds `voice_rag/`, a voice conversational agent whose answers come only from the RAG backend. The client today is a PC microphone; the WebSocket protocol is the one the HoloLens app will use.

- **Orchestrator** (`orchestrateur.py`): WebSocket `/ws` with server-side speech detection, streaming audio in and out, optional barge-in, and `POST /texte` for testing without audio.
- **Function-call interception** (`qwen.py`): streams Qwen-Omni, collects the `rechercher_rag` call (native `tool_calls`, with a fallback to a `<tool_call>` text tag when the server rejects `tools`), and forces a search when the model answers from memory.
- **RAG client** (`rag_client.py`): uses `/chunks` when it exists, otherwise `/ask` with the backend's written answer discarded and only `data` and `sources` kept. Results are cleaned before they reach the model (HTML, markdown, embeddings, duplicates, prompt-injection lines, length budget).
- **Answer control** (`controle.py`): each sentence is checked before it is spoken — figures must appear in the sources, `[Sx]` markers must exist, and the wording must be anchored in the retrieved text.
- **Local memory** (`memoire.py`): per-user file with the last 10 RAG responses, used first when the user picks a menu option.
- **Image and video**: an image or the latest camera frames can be attached to a question.
- **System prompt** (`prompts.py`) restricting answers to the RAG results.
- **PC client** (`client_micro.py`), **mock backends** (`mock_backends.py`) and a README.

## Test plan

- `python -m pytest voice_rag/tests -q` — 13 tests pass against the mock backends (cleaning, control, menu memory, `/ask` → `/chunks` switch, forced search, text tool-call fallback, end-to-end WebSocket audio turn).
- Live smoke test: both uvicorn servers started locally and one audio turn driven through a real WebSocket.

Not tested: the real Qwen-Omni API, a real RAG backend, the microphone client and the webcam (no audio device or API key in the build environment).

author: gregmeyer
body:
## What went wrong

A notebook was asked for jobs "well matched to my LinkedIn profile". The profile page couldn't be read, and nothing of it reached the notebook. Then:

1. The finder's plan was written with blanks: `"[profile target role]" "[profile location]"`. Nothing looked at the queries.
2. The searches (codex) filled the blanks themselves. The run records show `notion.search "LinkedIn profile"`, `"resume"`, `"career"`, `"job search"` and `notion.fetch`: codex's connected **apps** were on, so the search went into the operator's own Notion, built a profile from it, and reported jobs as matches to "the profile".
3. sua switched the operator's codex MCP servers off only on attempts with sua tools, and never switched codex apps off.

## What changed

**The finder (`notebook-finder`)**
- Plan prompt: use only what is written in the notebook; when the search depends on something the notebook refers to but doesn't contain, plan nothing and return `{"needs":"…","searches":[]}`.
- New `vet` node (code) between plan and the searches: a plan that says it needs something, or any query with a blank (`[…]`, `<…>`, `{…}`, `TBD`, empty), runs **no** search. The loop and merge read `vet`.
- `merge` then files nothing and prints `needs` in its block.

**The step**
- `applyKeeperResult` / `directBlock` carry `needs`: nothing filed, no search counted, no keeper model asked to read it.
- The step stops after that one try, stuck, with: "Nothing was searched: it needs your LinkedIn profile or résumé, and the notebook doesn't have it. Nothing was guessed. Add it under Edit (in what the notebook is for, or as a limit), then Try again."

**The searchers and the checker**
- `notebook-find-one`: who the notebook is for comes only from the notebook's words; never from anything else it knows or can find.
- `notebook-checker`: new judge verdict `not given` for a check that compares against something the notebook wasn't given. It is never ticked, isn't sent to web research, and the summary counts it ("1 couldn't be judged (the notebook wasn't given what it compares against)").

**Codex isolation (core, amends ADR-0044)**
- Every codex run, with or without tools, now gets `mcp_servers.<name>.enabled=false` for the operator's servers and `features.<f>=false` for `apps`, `plugins`, `remote_plugin`, `browser_use`, `browser_use_external`, `computer_use`, `memories`.

## Checked

- Clean rebuild; 278 tests pass in the touched files (finder vet + merge, checker pending/verify, step outcome, codex args).
- codex-cli 0.157.1, real calls: by default the Notion tools are discoverable; with `features.apps=false` they are not.
- Preview on a copy of live data with the real model, the failing request run again: plan returned `needs`, `vet` passed it on, the loop ran 0 searches, the step ended stuck with the message above, nothing filed.
- An ordinary job search on the preview: plan and `vet` passed five real queries and a search ran with `web-fetch` and no connector calls. I stopped the preview before that run finished, so its `merge` was only covered by the unit tests.

Not changed: codex's own shell (read-only sandbox) and the claude CLI. The notebook asking you for the missing thing and handing it to its steps is the next PR.

author: 7etsuo
body:
## Problem

`npm audit --omit=dev` reported advisories in 20 production packages: 2 critical, 15 high, 3 moderate.

## What changed

- Exact pins: `shell-quote` 1.10.0 to 1.11.0 and `tar` 7.5.19 to 7.5.23.
- Lockfile only, inside the ranges already declared: `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.29.0 to 1.32.2, `axios` 1.18.1 to 1.20.0, `js-yaml` 4.3.0 to 4.3.2, `sharp` 0.35.3 to 0.35.5, `@mendable/firecrawl-js` and `firecrawl` to 4.52.0, and the transitive packages `@hono/node-server`, `hono`, `qs`, `body-parser`, `proxy-addr`, `ip-address`, `fast-uri`, `follow-redirects`, `node-forge` and cheerio's `undici`.
- The lock is npm's own output (`npm install`, `npm audit fix` and `npm update` with `--package-lock-only`): no overrides and no hand edits. Every changed entry resolves to the npm registry with the integrity the registry publishes.

After the change `npm audit --omit=dev` reports 2, both high: `zod` 3.25.76 and `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime`, which depends on it. No zod 3.x release clears the advisory and every sandbox-runtime release requires zod 3, so clearing them needs the zod 4 major.

## Decisions worth knowing

- **`shell-quote` stays on 1.11.0**, the first fixed release. Under 1.12.0 `parse()` returns `>|`, `&>`, `&>>` and `<>` as single operators, and the runtime's redirection code then stops capturing the file those forms write. A new test, `runtime/tests/utils/bash/commands.test.ts`, fails on 1.10.0 and on 1.12.0.
- **`@hono/node-server` crosses a major version** (1.19.14 to 2.1.6). No 1.x release is free of its advisory, the MCP SDK's range allows 2.x, and the runtime never loads the package.
- **Fresh releases are avoided where an older fixed one exists.** `npm audit fix` takes the newest release in range, which had put five packages on releases a few days old. The lock is regenerated with `--before` so that `hono`, `follow-redirects`, `ip-address` and cheerio's `undici` use fixed releases at least two weeks old. Four stay recent because their first fixed release is: `node-forge` 1.4.3, `firecrawl` and `@mendable/firecrawl-js` 4.52.0 (all 2026-11-04), and `@hono/node-server` 2.1.6 (2026-11-02). That last one was on 2.1.5 until two advisories against 2.0.0 to 2.1.5 were published while this change was in review. `tar` 7.5.23 is from 2026-11-11, and its JavaScript is byte-identical to 7.5.21.

## Behavior changes that come with the MCP SDK

- An HTTP or SSE MCP server whose URL answers with a redirect to another host, port or scheme no longer connects; the error names the target. The MCP docs now say an `endpoint` must be the final URL.
- The SDK's stdio transport closes the connection on a single message over 10 MiB. That reaches agent-scoped stdio servers, the `agenc mcp` checks and `agenc doctor`. The main session's transport keeps its own 16 MiB limit.
- Stored MCP OAuth sign-ins keep working. The SDK warns on stderr (in the interactive screen, in the error log) that stored tokens have no `issuer`, until the runtime's OAuth provider stores that field. That is a follow-up.

## Red after this change until the benchmark baseline is recorded again

The FND benchmark baseline stores digests of `package-lock.json` and `runtime/package.json`, and both change here. Until the baseline is recorded again on the benchmark machine, these fail with "benchmark evidence bindings are stale":

- `runtime/tests/fnd/benchmark-baselines.contract.test.ts` (one test in the default suite)
- `npm run check:fnd-benchmark-baseline` and the fresh-clone variant

The baseline holds measurements from a specific machine and Node version, so it is not re-recorded in this change. The stored digests were not edited by hand.

## Validation

Local, on the branch rebased onto `main` at `58cbc212a` (Node 26.5.0, `umask 022`), after a clean `npm ci` of this lockfile:

- `npm ci` and `npm ls --all`: clean. `npm install --package-lock-only` leaves the lockfile unchanged.
- `npm audit --omit=dev`: 2 high (`zod`, `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime`), nothing else.
- `npm run check:sbom`: passed (681 canonical packages). The gatekeeper's dependency-source check accepts the lockfile.
- Full hermetic suite, `node scripts/run-hermetic-vitest.mjs run`: 3,487 files and 45,566 tests, 23 failed, all three files expected. `tests/packaging/install-sh.test.ts` (21) and `tests/benchmarks/fuzzy-search-benchmark.contract.test.ts` (1) need the pinned Node 26.12.1 and fail the same way on `main` on this host, which has 26.5.0. The third is the FND baseline test named above (1).
- `node scripts/check-launcher-preflight.mjs --check`, and `tsc --noEmit` for the runtime, test-support and TUI projects: clean.
- `npm run build`, `check:package-entrypoints`, `check:tui-runtime-startup`: pass. `check:startup-modules` reports the same two LSP modules as on `main`.
- `runtime/tests/utils/bash/commands.test.ts` passes on `shell-quote` 1.11.0 and fails 3 tests on 1.10.0 and 5 on 1.12.0.
- `git diff --check`: clean.

Fixes #3444

- `WSP-55/test_operator.py`: six predeclared WSP53 **SELFTEST only** noncommuting fixtures, A/B heldout, swap-order contrasts, negative action-cost, tamper and cold controls, whole-process timing and memory. Negative outcome is preserved as negative, not reclassified as workflow failure.
- Dedicated two-platform focused workflow; does **not** run WSP53 DEV/PRIMARY or duplicate WSP54 full regression.

## Scientific limitations
The finite modular-affine prior is deliberately source-family aligned; the 48/12 observation boundary is still supplied by the frozen protocol even though prediction has no `use_phase` input. No general-language or AGI claims. No fully trained neural/exhaustive independent symbolic comparator yet. No SCIENTIFIC_PASS, production integration, scientific first-use, merge or promotion authorized by this PR.

## Gate
Check Linux and Windows focused workflow on exact candidate SHA; evaluate the frozen aggregate >=48/792 exact, zero wrong-confident, >=1 correct swap-order contrast. Any failure remains an exploratory negative. Full inherited regression and G29 exact-source atlas must subsequently qualify the unchanged candidate before engineering closure.

author: dbattaglia0823-design
body:
## Problem
The Morrow Coast importer deliberately leaves `doc.props` empty unless a baked prop has an explicit authoring ID. The actual playable archive contains many thousands of baked buildings, trees, parking objects and foliage in `raw.props`, which are only shown in a read-only runtime preview. The editor's **Entities → Scenery** list and counts derived from `doc.props.length` therefore misleadingly show **0 assets** even on a populated map. The editor also initially zoomed to the entire ~6,400×4,800 metre world, making 7-metre trees and 12-metre roofs almost invisible.

## Fix
- Show the actual total of backed, renderable game scenery in the map status, asset status and **Map assets** panel. Do not count source-owned procedural props as editable overlay objects.
- Offer a bounded **Game scenery & edits** browser of real baked scenery nearest the player spawn, with coordinates and distinct tags for editable game props versus protected gameplay landmarks. Click to zoom/focus; selecting ordinary scenery converts it into the existing undoable, explicit source override. Landmark buildings stay read-only.
- Preserve the real 19k-scale scenery in spatial preview buckets, not the limited authoring overlay. Avoid duplicate drawn rows for already adopted/editable props and keep exact counts when existing authored IDs appear in both raw and overlay.
- Build the preview before refreshing the UI, avoiding temporary zero counts; open the map near the actual player start at legible 0.65 zoom. **Fit** still displays the entire coastline.
- If the playable world truly has zero baked assets, show a rebuild-required error rather than claiming the map loaded normally.
- Add Node tests for zero authored vs thousands of real game assets, no source mutations, read-only landmarks, browser caps and direct game archive integrity. Extend the real Godot startup smoke test to assert >1,000 baked objects **and** visible scenery renderer nodes around the player spawn.

No world source data, positions, road geometry, vehicle size, or procedural generator seed are changed. Existing map edits and saves remain compatible.

author: tauceti-ai-for-science
body:
This PR proves that the genus of a binary lattice of square discriminant is a coset of the squares. Two binary lattices whose primitive norm forms have discriminant `s²` (`s ≠ 0`) lie in one genus exactly when their contents agree and their oriented split proper classes differ by a square in the group `SplitProperClass s ≃* (ZMod s)ˣ` (`IntegralLattice.sameGenus_iff_binaryContent_eq_and_isSquare_inv_mul_binarySplitProperClass`). The statement holds for every choice of orientations.

It advances milestone **B3 (Compatibility, and the ring class field)** of `IntegralLattices/README.md`, Layer B. This is the split-branch clause "the genus of `L`, in the sense of 3F, is a coset of the subgroup of squares `((ℤ/mℤ)ˣ)²`". Its inputs are 3F (`SameGenus`) and B2's split classes (`SplitProperClass`, `splitProperClassEquivUnits`), both already on main. After this PR, B3 still needs the nonsquare-branch genus statement (the genus as a coset of the squares in `Pic`/`NarrowPic`), the split genus counts that follow from this theorem, and the torus clause, which depends on B6.

How the proof goes: a lattice whose split class is that of `sxy + ay²` has a carrier basis with norm form `c(sxy + ay²)` (`exists_binaryNormForm_eq_smul_splitTriangularForm`). Its Gram matrix is then `!![0, cs/2; cs/2, ca]`.
- (⇐) If `a' ≡ az² (mod s)`, an explicit change of basis gives the isometries. It is `u⁻¹e₀, te₀ + ue₁` over `ℤ_p` for `p ∣ s`, and unipotent at the other primes and over `ℚ`. This is the general lemma `LinearMap.BilinForm.equivalent_of_toMatrix_eq_isotropic`. The rational isometry gives equal signatures through the existing `sameGenus_iff_localIntegralForm_equivalent`.
- (⇒) A local isometry sends the second basis vector to some `xe₀ + ye₁` of the same norm. Hence `a' = sxy + ay²` in `ℤ_p`, so `a' ≡ ay² (mod p^k)` for every `p^k ∣ s`. The Chinese remainder theorem glues these congruences (`ZMod.exists_intCast_eq_mul_sq_iff`, in the new file `TauCeti/Data/ZMod/SquareMultiple.lean`).

Two small lemmas go into `BinaryQuadraticForm/Split/Composition.lean`. `exists_eq_splitProperClassMk` gives every split class a triangular representative. `isSquare_inv_mul_splitProperClassMk_iff` says two triangular classes differ by a square exactly when `d ≡ cz² (mod s)`.

The new file sits next to the existing split-class file, so this PR moves that file into a `Split/` directory, as the placement rule requires. Only the path changes; no module imported it, and no declarations are renamed.

| old module | new module |
| --- | --- |
| `TauCeti.NumberTheory.IntegralLattice.Binary.SplitClass` | `TauCeti.NumberTheory.IntegralLattice.Binary.Split.Class` |

Nothing is vendored from Mathlib. References: Cox, *Primes of the Form x² + ny²*, §3 (genus theory); Cassels, *Rational Quadratic Forms*, Chapter 8 (integral local equivalence).

Roadmap: IntegralLattices

body:
Closes #7025

`check:deletes` binds the sign-off of a deleted item to the whole patch of some changed files. Each such file holds the item's last segment. A common segment as `ledger` names 39 of the 45 files of pull request 7017. An edit of a `since` cell in `ledger/features.sql` then moves the sign-off of the driver's `ledger()`, though the cell names nothing of it. The sign-off now binds, in each such file, the words of the changed lines that hold the segment. The architect rules this on #7025, and it narrows the ruling of #6852.

## Observation

The probe of the issue (comment 6839724829) reads the two runs of the queue against pull request 7017. Each reads the sign-off of 22:52 at `8b938e606`. The head is `e6019ea4e`:

```text
1:  8b938e606 = 1:  e3b89a74b perf(workflow): move the ledger tasks to gandr-ledger
-:  --------- > 2:  e6019ea4e docs(workflow): name #7017 in the since of the four moved rows
```

|Reading|Before|After|
|---|---|---|
|the files that move between `8b938e606` and `e6019ea4e`, for the 6 segments of the pull request's rows|`ledger/features.sql`, by its patch id|none, in 0.72 s|
|the files that the segment `ledger` binds|39 of 45|39 of 45, each by its words that hold `ledger`|

The cases of `.config/deletes/moved-cases.bash` build a scratch repository with a signed change to a shared file:

|Case|Result|
|---|---|
|a restack over a row that a landing below adds|no move, as before|
|an edit of another cell of a line that names the item|no move (#7025)|
|a change to a word that names the item|moves that file alone|
|a new file that names the item|moves|
|a new file that names the item nowhere|no move (#7025)|
|a reader row that names the item lands below|joins the readers, as before|

## Sources read

- `.config/deletes/moved.bash` — taken: `moved` takes the items' segments and compares, in each file, the words of the changed lines that hold each one.
- `.config/deletes/check.bash` — taken: the segment of each item, and the call of `moved` with them. `changed` maps each item to its files.
- `.config/deletes/account.jq` — taken: `signs` and `moves` read `changed` for each item. The stale line names the words of the file.
- `.config/deletes/deletes.jq` — taken: the doc of `changed`.
- `.config/deletes/moved-cases.bash` — taken: the cases of #7025, and the cases of #6852 on a row that names the item.
- `.config/deletes/cases.json` — taken: `changed` keyed by item.
- `#6852` — departed: the ruling binds the whole patch of each named file. The sign-off now binds the words in it that name the item. The architect answers so on #7025, since a common segment binds most files.
- `#7012` — read: the read of a sign-off's commit. It needs no change.

## Readings

|---|---|---|
|Identity|`univalent`|not applicable: a workflow script|
|Locality|`oracle`|not applicable: no certificate|
|Locality|`descent`|not applicable: one reading of each sign-off|

## Concerns

|---|---|
|`collapse`|no|
|`fork`|no|
|`measure`|no|
|`nominal`|no|
|`oracle`|no|

## Engineering

|Row|Answer|
|---|---|
|change|unchanged: a sign-off whose words that name the item hold, 1 of the 2 heads of pull request 7017; edit: a sign-off whose words move, refused with the file named, as the cases show|
|complexity|2 diffs with no context for each sign-off, in place of 2 diffs for each of the 45 files of pull request 7017 before. Each changed line is read once against each of the 6 segments|
|latency|0.72 s for one sign-off of pull request 7017: 45 files and 6 segments|

none. The change adds no request of GitHub's API.

none. The patch id of a file leaves `moved`, and no item, test or row leaves the tree.

`SDP_ALLOW_SANDBOX_PROJECTS=false` (the mirror of `SDP_ALLOW_PRODUCTION_PROJECTS`) makes a deployment mainnet-only. Unset keeps today's behavior, so this changes nothing on any deployment until infra sets it.

- Sandbox projects are hidden and refused at the edge and in money admission. New orgs get no sandbox project, and no sandbox cron work is registered.
- **An org without mainnet access may only read its organization, projects and members and request mainnet access.** Every other action answers 403 `reason: "organization_not_admitted"`, checked in `requireAction`. Invitations are refused too, so unapproved orgs can't send prod Clerk invitations.
- On a deployment that admits no production project (beta), mainnet requests are refused. The mainnet-access read adds `sandboxOnly` and `mainnetOnly` for the dashboard, and **every signed-in member may read it** (`organizations.read`; requests stay admin-only), since the dashboard decides from it where a member lands. Its parse defaults both to false for older API revisions.
- Both settings `false` fails at boot.
- **"Mainnet enabled" reads as a welcome and is sent even with alert emails off** (so is "Mainnet disabled"); the request page promises it.
- Runbook: `docs/ops/beta-cutover.md`.
- Docs: the new 403 is in the authentication guide's error table.

author: depfu[bot]
body:
🚨 Your current dependencies have known security vulnerabilities 🚨 This dependency update fixes known security vulnerabilities. Please see the details below and assess their impact carefully. We recommend to merge and deploy this as soon as possible!
Here is everything you need to know about this update. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ↗️ addressable (_indirect_, 2.5.1 → 2.9.2) · [Repo](https://github.com/sporkmonger/addressable) · [Changelog](https://github.com/sporkmonger/addressable/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Addressable display_uri can show misleading hosts with invalid Punycode A-labels

Impact

Addressable::IDNA.to_unicode, in the pure-Ruby IDNA implementation, decodes Punycode labels (labels beginning with xn--) that are not valid A-labels. Those labels are returned in decoded form, when they should be returned unchanged. That includes:

  • labels that decode to only ASCII characters, e.g. xn--google- decodes to google;
  • labels that decode to text that doesn't convert back to the same label (RFC 3490 §4.2), e.g. text that isn't in normalized form.

Addressable::URI#display_uri uses to_unicode, so for https://xn--google-.example.org/ it displays the host google.example.org, while #host, #normalized_host and any connection made from the URI use xn--google-.example.org. An attacker who controls a domain can therefore have a URI displayed as a host they don't control. Applications that compare the result of to_unicode against a list of trusted names can likewise treat two different hosts as the same.

The native IDNA implementation, used when libidn and the idn-ruby gem are installed, is not affected. to_ascii and normalized_host are not affected.

Affected Versions

This vulnerability affects Addressable >= 2.0.0, the first version with the pure-Ruby IDNA implementation, when that implementation is in use. It is fixed in 2.9.1, where such labels are returned unchanged, as with libidn.

Workarounds

  • Install libidn and the idn-ruby gem, so that Addressable uses the native IDNA implementation.
  • Don't make security decisions on display_uri or to_unicode output. Compare hosts using normalized_host.

Credits

Reported by @tonghuaroot.

For more information

If there are any questions or comments about this advisory:

  • Open an issue

🚨 Addressable: Denial of service in URI path normalization

Impact

Addressable::URI.normalize_path takes time quadratic in the number of nested dot segments in a path (e.g., "/" + "a/" * n + "../" * n, which for n = 3 is /a/a/a/../../../), because it removes one dot segment per pass over the whole path. URI#normalize, URI#normalized_path, URI#==, URI#=== and URI#join all call it. Normalizing, comparing or joining a URI taken from user input can result in uncontrolled resource consumption, leading to denial of service. On 2.9.0, normalizing a 34 KB path takes about 3.5 seconds on MRI Ruby 4.0, and the cost grows with the square of the path length.

This affects every Ruby implementation, including MRI Ruby 3.2 and later. URI.parse by itself is unaffected, as is code that never normalizes, compares, or joins URIs from untrusted sources.

Affected Versions

This vulnerability affects all versions of Addressable prior to 2.9.1. It is fixed in 2.9.1.

Workarounds

  • Limit the length of URIs taken from user input before calling normalize, == or join on them. Web servers often limit request lines to about 8 KB, which keeps the cost to about 150 milliseconds per call on typical hardware, but URIs from other sources (request bodies, headers such as Location, stored data) may not be limited.
  • Reject paths with many dot segments before normalizing them.

Credits

Reported by Matthew Mongeau (@halogenandtoast), Ruby Central Gem Security, who also suggested the single-pass approach used in the fix.

For more information

If there are any questions or comments about this advisory:

  • Open an issue

🚨 Addressable display_uri can show misleading hosts containing bidi and invisible characters

Impact

Addressable::IDNA.to_unicode decodes Punycode labels (labels beginning with xn--) that contain characters which change how text is displayed without being visible themselves. These include bidirectional controls such as U+202E RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE and U+2066–U+2069, zero-width characters, and other invisible format characters. Addressable::URI#display_uri uses to_unicode, so it can display a host whose characters appear reordered or which looks identical to a different host. For example, the host of http://xn--abcmoc-dm0c.com/ is displayed as abc, U+202E, moc.com, and the override makes everything after abc render right to left.

Parsing, host, normalized_host and any connection made from the URI are not affected. Only the displayed form is. Applications that show display_uri to users (link previews, chat and email clients, admin interfaces) can be used to make a malicious domain look like a trusted one.

  • In the pure-Ruby IDNA implementation, all such characters are decoded, including those that IDNA's nameprep profile prohibits.

body: ## Docked overvoltage With the nest at 15.0 V the servos would see 14.7 V (calc only), and the 12 V STS3215 page tops out at 14 V. Three options, one pick: - Dropping the nest to 13.6 V leaves a 0.4 V gap under 14 V and none of the 1.4 V drop budget. Contact resistance and adapter tolerance are still open, so that shared rail does not hold both the charger and the servos. - The BQ24133 power path connects the system node to the adapter while docked, so servos on that node see the nest again. Wiring them only to the pack stays under 12.6 V, but fourteen idle servos are 0.294 A and termination is 0.10 A, so the charger never sees the end of charge. - The pick is the Pololu 2815, fed only from the pack through DK7. The nest is not on that input, so turning the switch on while seated cannot put 15 V on the servos. The sit with the rail cut, sim pass only, hottest high corner at 32 C: cells 35.98 C, trunk air 37.00 C, wall 33.73 C. All under the cited cell and PLA lines. ## One interlock, shared with the sit pull request The Pi drives the switch. Dock detect forces the rail off during charge. The Pi end-charge line releases that clamp and pulls ISET below 40 mV, which disables the charger. The Pi can then request the rail on, from the pack, before the duck stands. | Dock | End charge | Rail request | Rail | |---|---|---|---| | yes | no | yes | off | | yes | yes | yes | on, pack, still seated | | no | no | yes | on, pack | Parts: LM393BIDR for the dock flag, FDME910PZT for the clamp gate, and three 2N7002 devices. author: raulmoranguerra
body:
## Why

In HIL runs on the GTX 1080 box (pipeline on the Orange Pi), the pipeline watchdog tripped EBS mid-run. The sequence was `/watchdog/emergency`, then `/force_ebs`, then the AS state went to Emergency (`/dv/status` 5, `/assi/state` 1).

The benchmark kept polling until `timeout_s` and recorded a timeout:
- autocross: 55 s in, then waited until about 250 s;
- trackdrive: waits out 2400 s of sim time, about 37 min lost.

The trips themselves are a HIL network artifact being fixed separately. A tripped run should still cost seconds, not the whole timeout.

## What changes

- **Mission Control:** `/api/event/state` adds `as_state` and `dv_status`.
  - The ROS bridge already followed `/dv/status`; it now also subscribes to `/assi/state` with the uplink QoS.
  - Both values read `null` when older than 1.5 s, and are absent without the ROS bridge.
- **`run_mission_benchmark.py`:** ends the run with outcome `emergency` on `dv_status == DV_EMERGENCY`, or on `as_state == AS_EMERGENCY` once the run has been seen in `AS_DRIVING`. The AS state latches, so a leftover Emergency from the previous run does not end the next one. A referee finish is checked first.
- **What gets recorded:**
  - `emergency_at_s` in `manifest.json`;
  - `race/emergency` and `race/emergency_at_s` in `results.json`;
  - the time in the `events.csv` dnf row;
  - laps, telemetry and doo events as for any other run.

## Testing

- `tools/sim_benchmark/tests/test_run_mission_benchmark.py`: 24 passed. The new tests cover an emergency ending a 2400 s run within seconds, a latched AS Emergency not ending a run, and a finish winning over the EBS that follows it.
- `tools/mission_control/backend/tests/test_ros_bridge_handshake.py`: 9 passed, including a new `as_snapshot` freshness test.
- `tools/tests`: 99 passed.
- Not run against a live stack: the box is busy until the current checks end.

author: junyu06
body:
## What changes

- A caption now ends where the speaker pauses. The app listens to the audio it passes to the recognizer; when speech is followed by a short quiet it asks the speech analyzer to finalize, and that final result is the caption, translated once.
- Each sentence starts on a line of its own, on both rows. A translation longer than its row is shown from its beginning and then turns to the rest.
- A finished sentence is kept whole up to one and a half times the length limit.
- The earlier rules (sentence endings in the recognizer's guesses, a guess that stops changing, length limits) remain as the fallback for audio that never goes quiet.

## Why

With quick conversation the previous version showed captions seconds late and cut them by length. The recognizer finalizes such speech only every several seconds, and its guesses carry few marks, so nothing in the text said where a turn ended.

## Evidence

- 277 unit tests pass (`cd JimakuCore && swift test`).
- On a Mac, the app's recognizer class, pause detector, transcript, and language-pack translation over a 145-second recording of quick Japanese conversation: the first translation at 3.2 seconds instead of 10.7.
- On a physical iPad through a screen broadcast, logged by the app: the first build acted on none of 67 pauses, because the analyzer's volatile range stops about a tenth of a second short of the audio handed over there. With that fixed, all 19 pauses of a 46-second session were acted on at once and the Chinese was ready 0.2 to 0.3 seconds after each pause.
- Not run on an iPhone.

Details are in `docs/decisions/`, `docs/pitfalls/`, and `docs/cases/translation-004-a-caption-appears-when-the-speaker-stops.md`.

author: iamsamuelrodda
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a lab whose accounting system prices items with GST inside got invoices with 10% added on top. A $200 item that is $200 including GST in Xero went to Xero as $200 plus $20 GST, because Flow always sent tax-exclusive lines and took each line's GST from the work system's taxable flag.

## User Impact

- New setting **Prices include GST** (Settings, Invoicing, Drafts; `amountsIncludeTax`, default off). With it on, new invoices hold each GST line's tax as one eleventh of its amount, the total is the sum of the lines, the PDF shows "Includes GST 10%", and Xero gets `LineAmountTypes: Inclusive`. An invoice keeps the setting it was made with.
- With it on, the work system's subtotal (its prices before the GST it adds) is compared with Flow's total; its GST is not compared.
- New Price list setting **Invoice line GST** (`lineTax`): **Job** (default, the work system's flag) or **Price list** (the price item's tax, which the price check keeps the same as the accounting item's). With Price list, a work system flag that differs stays on the line (`workTaxCode`) and the job waits for a person ("a source line's GST differs from its price item").
- Both are off by default, so nothing changes until a lab turns them on.

## Why This Change Was Made

`money.js` gets an inclusive mode for line and invoice totals. `invoices.amounts_include_tax` and `billing_obligations.amounts_include_tax` record the mode (migration `0034`, add only), so issued versions and jobs keep their meaning when the setting changes. `buildDraft` reads the document's mode. Line mapping gets `lineTax` beside `linePrice`.

## Evidence

- New tests: inclusive line and invoice totals (`money.test.js`); `lineTax: 'list'` picks the item's tax and records a different work flag (`line-mapping.test.js`); an inclusive document sends `Inclusive` (`xero-drafts.test.js`); a database test where the setting changes a job's totals ($200 total, $18.18 GST), the source subtotal check, the GST clash reason, and a drafted and issued invoice that keeps the mode (`ledger.test.js`).
- Full suite locally (Postgres 16): 1100 tests; after two expectation updates (new column, new mapping default) all pass except `a published Replit app never uses the local folder`, which fails only because the container runs as root (a chmod 555 folder is still writable). The same test fails on `main` here.
- Data in tests is synthetic.

author: cristianonescu
body:
A star too broad for one satin column now becomes **one branch column per point**. The five-point star at 25 mm goes from sewn coverage 0.54 with an 11 mm gap to **0.992, meeting every one of #526's boxes**. Part of #526.

## The cause
`object.deriveSkeleton {branches: true}` (`skeleton::branches`) split the star the same way at every size:
- one main column from the top point to the bottom-right point, **as wide as the whole star at its middle**;
- a stub at one tip.

At 10 mm that column is 9.9 mm wide and happens to sew the star. At 25 mm it's **24.7 mm**, and the engine already warned "satin over 10 mm sews loose". The other points never became arms, because the main column's width swallowed them.

## What changes (new functions; one call in `branches()`)
- **`star_kites`:**
  - A single closed outline, simplified, whose vertices alternate sharp convex tips and concave notches (at least 3 of each), is star-like.
  - It tiles into **kites**: a tip, its two notches and the centre (the notches' mean). Every cut from a notch to the centre must lie inside the outline.
- **`kite_column`:** each kite's column runs from the tip to the centre. At every point, 0.5 mm apart and at the notches' feet, it is as wide as the kite's chord square to it, so the rungs tile the kite.
  - Towards the centre each chord is `joinOverlap` longer on each side, so neighbouring columns overlap by it.
  - The tip stays a point.
- **`star_columns`:** used only when the plain split's widest column is over **10 mm** (`STAR_SPLIT_WIDTH`, the width at which the engine warns that satin sews loose).
  - The star at 10 mm (9.9 mm wide) keeps its split exactly.
  - So do Y, K, X, R, A, y and the ring, whose columns stay under 10 mm.
- **Not the same idea as #976** (N, M, W): #976 carries an edge straight on across the shape, while a star is cut from each notch to the centre.
- I didn't touch `split`, `arms_from`, `capped`, `unkinked`, `Trim`, `reach_into_joins`, `reach_free_ends` or `derive`, nor #976's functions. The kite columns don't go through `reach_*`: they reach the tip and the centre by construction.

Grades each day against the timetable copy its trips match, which fixes wrong rail grades on 2026-09-10 and 2026-10-14, and stops lines 9 and 22 from failing the silent-lines check.

author: zenowangzy
body:
Refs #1038

Fixes a stop-loss requeue refusal for closed units. `closed_unit_stop_loss_open` read the issue state through GraphQL (`gh issue view --json state`). Under the secondary rate limit that read returned empty, so an OPEN issue on a scheduler-stop-loss hold was refused with the `--recut` advice (seen on issues 4456 and 5727).

## Change
- `closed_unit_stop_loss_open` reads REST (`gh api repos/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .state`). Returns 0 for open on a stop-loss hold, 1 for not eligible or closed, 2 when the read fails.
- `closed_unit_refusal` takes an optional rc. rc 2 gives "GitHub issue state could not be read; retry the ruling", never the recut advice.
- `rule_entry` requeue on a closed unit requeues only on rc 0; rc 2 refuses and leaves the unit and its hold unchanged.
- The reroute refusal goes through the same helper, so it inherits the rc 2 message.

## prior-art
no external prior art: this is a local fix to the engine's own state read (GraphQL to REST), using the `gh api` pattern already in `hold_rule`.

## Tests
- `engine/hold-rule.test.sh` (whole file, rc 0): the closed-unit cases now stub the REST read with lowercase `open`/`closed` and answer only that call. New cases: an unreadable read refuses requeue and reroute with no `--recut` or `--requeue` advice, and leaves the unit closed with its stop-loss hold.
- `engine/size-ratchet.test.sh`, `engine/mac-autopilot/scheduler.d/exit-trap-lint.test.sh`, `engine/test-env-exit.test.sh`: rc 0 each via `tools/test-receipt.sh`.

Not changed: other `gh issue view ... --json state` reads, including `supervisor-arbiter.sh:406`, which the requeue path calls after the stop-loss check passes.

author: washcycle
body:
## Summary
OpenSpec proposal (no code) for working behind corporate proxies: `openspec/changes/corporate-proxy-support/`.

**Problem:** gRPC (grpc-js) only honours *lowercase* proxy env vars and ignores VS Code's `http.proxy`, while Lookout's `https` calls go through VS Code's proxy patching. On the same machine, job-set browsing can work while submit, cancel and stream fail with "Is armada-server running?". `caCertPath` (already on main) covers TLS-inspection *trust* but not routing, proxy auth or diagnosis.

**Plan:**
- One resolved proxy per endpoint for gRPC **and** Lookout. Precedence: context `proxy` → `armada.proxy` (`inherit`/`off`/URL) → VS Code `http.proxy` → env (lower- and upper-case).
- curl/Go-style `NO_PROXY` (suffix, CIDR, port, `*`); loopback always bypassed.
- Basic proxy auth via URL with credentials masked everywhere; NTLM/Kerberos users are pointed at cntlm/px.
- Stage-specific failures (`proxy-connect`, `proxy-auth`, `proxy-refused`, `tls-untrusted`, `http2-blocked`) in Test Connection, the config panel and the status bar.
- **New separate `proxy-tests.yml` workflow** (nightly + dispatch, not required). It runs the integration suite through squid (CONNECT, with/without auth), mitmproxy (TLS interception plus `caCertPath`) and uppercase-env-only, with **direct egress blocked**, and asserts CONNECT entries in the proxy log.

**Main risk:** grpc-js has no public option for an explicit proxy URL. Task group 1 is a spike comparing internal channel options (version-pinned, with a contract test) against a scoped env override.

`openspec validate corporate-proxy-support --strict` passes.

author: jrandolf
body:
## Why

- The viewport is the second of the five parts of Scroll Area. It is the element that scrolls. It makes each measurement that the root state and the later parts read.
- Three CSPProvider cases and one case of the root render the viewport. They waited for it.

## What

- `ScrollArea.Viewport`, with its context, its data attributes and its CSS variables. `@vase-ui/vue/scroll-area` exports it.
- The viewport measures at mount, on each scroll, on a resize, and after the animations of its subtree end. It sets the overflow state of the root and the four `--scroll-area-overflow-*` variables.
- The server HTML has the viewport out of the tab order. After the first measurement, a viewport that scrolls has `tabindex="0"`.
- `KeepAlive`: a deactivated viewport stops its observer, its scroll end timer and its animation wait timer. An activated viewport starts the observer and the animation wait again. It measures again, because the browser resets the scroll position of an element that left the document.
- `ScrollAreaScrollbarCssVars.ts`, because the viewport writes the thumb size variables. The entry point does not export it yet.
- Parity: the rows of the viewport are gone. The other cases of the root and viewport tests now wait for the scrollbar.

## Tests

- The conformance suite and 12 upstream cases of the viewport, 1 of the root and 3 of CSPProvider. They run in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, and on Vue 3.5.0.
- Own cases: a resize, the stop of the observer at the unmount, `KeepAlive`, the end of a user scroll after 100 ms, the server render, and a hydration that waits for the measurement and compares with a client-only render.
- The resize case waits one frame at its end. A case that ends inside the delivery of a `ResizeObserver` makes the next case that creates an observer get a loop error from the browser.
- Not tested here: 8 upstream viewport cases and the thumb branches of the measurement need the scrollbar and the thumb.

author: ldsenow
body:
Opened by the tscs scheduled task.

## Brief
- **Problem:** every global constructor interface in the pinned `lib.es5.d.ts` (`ObjectConstructor`, `StringConstructor`, `ErrorConstructor`, `ArrayConstructor`, …) declares call signatures `(params): R` and construct signatures `new (params): R`. tscs rejected them in two ways:
  - at scan time with `TSCS1001: Unsupported syntax 'new'`, the first blocker of 29 of the 147 statements;
  - with `Expected a supported named object property`.

  Anti-sprawl: this is needed to load and check the standard library (A2).
- **Done criteria:**
  1. Valid non-generic call and construct signature declarations check clean, the same as the pinned Go CLI.
  2. Their parameter and return types are checked in source order with the other members. An unresolved name gives TS2304 at the reference position.
  3. These forms fail closed with TSCS1001. They are never typed silently and never get a diagnostic the reference does not report:
     - any use of such a type
     - generic signatures (`<T>(…)`, `new <T>(…)`)
     - heritage in both directions
     - reopened interfaces
     - declaration-identity comparison
     - recursive references (the reference accepts them; tscs's cycle check would say TS2456)
     - `typeof` of a signature's own parameter
     - duplicate method parameter names (TS2300 is not modelled)
  4. `new` is still rejected everywhere outside an object type member.
  5. `check-library-statements` does not drop, `check-standard-library` is unchanged, original acceptance is unchanged, and the full gate is green.

## Change
- **`Scanner`:** `new` followed by `(` or `<` reaches the parser when it comes after `{`, `;`, `,` or a line break. This works like the existing tuple-label exception. The parser accepts it only at the start of an object type member.
- **`Parser`:** adds `CallSignatureSyntax` members on `ObjectTypeSyntax` (pinned `parseTypeMemberSemicolon`). Duplicate parameter names in `ReadObjectMethodType` fail closed.
- **`ObjectTypeSyntax.HasSignatures`** (index, call or construct) replaces `HasIndexSignatures` in every fail-closed path from #263: Binder, `DeclarationTypeIdentity`, `TypeResolver.Resolve`, heritage and reopening.
- **`TypeResolver.ValidateSignatureMembers`** (was `ValidateIndexSignatures`) checks call and construct signatures in member order.
- **`Resolve(FunctionTypeSyntax)`** fails closed on a `typeof` of any parameter of the function type or of an enclosing one (`QueriesParameter`). On main these resolved to an outer value or gave TS2304, which affected methods and function types too.

## Verification evidence
- **Toolchain:** the local toolchain worked (`scripts/setup-dev-environment.sh`; SDK 10.0.402, Node 24.22.1, Go 1.27.3).
- **Baseline:** main e331acc is the squash of #263's head 1e728c4, whose body records `./scripts/verify.sh` EXIT 0 with 20,277 xUnit. That result was reused, not re-run.
- **`./scripts/verify.sh` on head cbbc63c:** EXIT 0, **20,312 passed / 0 failed**. This includes 35 new `CallSignatureDeclarationTests`; the 36 `IndexSignatureDeclarationTests` still pass.
- **`node tools/check-library-statements.ts`** (pinned upstream 8d9b6da): 29 → 29 of 147, and no statement regresses. 26 statements now get past the signature syntax to their next blocker:

  | First blocker | Statements |
  |---|---|
  | generic call/construct signatures | 12 |
  | `this` | 11 |
  | bounded Array/String contracts | 10 |
  | `TS2304 Error` (correct when checked alone) | 7 |
  | signatures in inheriting interfaces | 6 |
- **`node tools/check-standard-library.ts`:** unchanged — 116/116 clean, required 20/20, 2,250 global symbols (791 merged), 0 diagnostics, 0 unresolved names.
- **`node tools/original-acceptance.ts … --expect-headline docs/STATUS.md`** on cbbc63c: 3 PASS / 0 FAIL / 15,520 SKIP.
- **`scripts/verify-original-emptyfile-go.sh`:** reference PASS, with the pinned Go runner built locally.
- **Differential against the pinned Go CLI** (built from the pinned checkout): the independent verifier ran 258 inputs. Every result is clean on both sides, has the same first code and position, or is TSCS1001.
- **`node tools/check-docs.ts`:** ok; STATUS is 25,588 B.

Original acceptance: 3 PASS / 0 FAIL / 15,520 SKIP → 3 PASS / 0 FAIL / 15,520 SKIP.

## Review
This is not a small PR (about 110 product lines). Codex reviewed 7b93eaa, and an independent agent reviewed and verified every head; their comments are below.

| Head | Result | What happened |
|---|---|---|
| 0c27d06 | PASS, 3 low findings | Recursive `interface C { new (s: string): C }` gave TS2456; fixed in 7b93eaa |
| 7b93eaa | PASS | Codex P2: `(x: number): typeof x` gave TS2304; fixed in 300c340, thread resolved |
| 300c340 | FAIL | A parameter shadowing an outer value still resolved `typeof x` to the outer value; fixed in cbbc63c |
| cbbc63c | **VERDICT: PASS** | — |

## Decision log
- Uses fail closed, as #262 and #263 did. Modelling signatures in the type model is a later step.
- These pre-existing gaps were found during the run and are out of scope here:
  - Recursive interfaces (`interface S { p: S }`) report TS2456 instead of being accepted.
  - The `minimal.d.ts` bootstrap globals (`Function`, `String`, `Number`, `RegExp`) cannot be resolved as type names. This is now the first blocker of `FunctionConstructor` and `StringConstructor`.
  - Function types like `(a, a) => void` accept duplicate parameters.
  - Function declarations resolve `typeof param` in their return annotation to an outer value.
  - Duplicate property TS2300 is reported at the second occurrence, not the first.
  - `typeof` of a type-only name gives TS2304 instead of TS2693.

author: lneto
body:
A device already on the bus that a `hid.register` table matches has no driver while the script runs: the registration releases it from `hid-generic` and probes it on the script body's task, before the runtime is ready, where the probe is refused, so a mouse connected before `lunatik run` stops working until the script stops.

The probe now runs inside `hid.register`, as it would for a device plugged in after the body returns, and a `stop` in the body delivers `remove` and the probe of another driver of the runtime that takes the device:

```lua
local hid = require("hid")

local loading = true -- cleared once the body returns
hid.register({
	name = "silent_mouse",
	id_table = {{bus = 0x05, vendor = 0x2717, product = 0x5014}},
	probe = function(_, hdev)
		print(hdev.name, loading and "was already connected" or "was just connected")
	end,
})
loading = false
```

The core gains the pair a binding opens around such a registration, `lunatik_enterreplay` and `lunatik_leavereplay`, and `lunatik_run` runs a callback the registration delivers on that task; `notifier.netdevice` replays through it in place of its own copy. A `hid.register`, a driver's `stop` or a `notifier.netdevice` called from such a callback raises "not allowed inside a replay": the callback holds the device lock a nested `hid.register` or `stop` would take, and a nested registration would end the replay it runs in. A device plugged in on another task while the body runs is refused as today, and the driver probes synchronously whatever asynchronous probing the kernel command line or the module asks for. `gesture` ran on the host's three QEMU 0627:0001 devices, which were bound to it while it ran and back on `hid-generic` after its stop, where master leaves them without a driver; `linkflap`, `netfailover`, `dropreason`, `echod` and `systrack` ran; `keylocker` and `spyglass` only loaded, since the host has no local keyboard to type on; `xiaomi` was not run, since the host has no Xiaomi Silent Mouse, and `ifquarantine` neither, since loading it quarantines the host's uplink. Alternative to #2324.

Closes #1351

author: octavia-bot[bot]
body:
## Overview
**:point_right: TL;DR:** Facebook Marketing insights streams moved their saved bookmark backwards while re-reading recent days, so every interrupted sync made the next one re-read a wider date range. The bookmark now only moves forward. Not a breaking change: the state format is unchanged and every lookback date is still requested. Specifically, `AdsInsights._advance_cursor` no longer lowers `date_start` below the value loaded from state, and the `state` getter stops persisting `slices` at or before the cursor.
Resolves https://github.com/airbytehq/airbyte-internal-issues/issues/19857: - https://github.com/airbytehq/airbyte-internal-issues/issues/19857 Close on merge: no — customer-filed; support confirms the fix with the customer before closing. ## Changes - `_advance_cursor` skips the cursor update for completed slices at or before the committed cursor, so `date_start` stays put during the lookback re-read and advances only once contiguous completion passes it. - New `_pending_slices` helper: the emitted state lists only completed slices ahead of the cursor. Older ones are still tracked in memory for the lookback walk. - Mock-server test for an interrupted attempt followed by a retry; `test_state` cases updated for the pruned `slices`. - Version `6.1.13` and changelog row. ## Review Spotlight Reviewers with limited time, please review first: - [`base_insight_streams.py` `_advance_cursor`](https://github.com/airbytehq/airbyte/blob/devin/19857-fb-cursor-monotonic/airbyte-integrations/connectors/source-facebook-marketing/source_facebook_marketing/streams/base_insight_streams.py#L424-L440): the monotonic guard - [`base_insight_streams.py` `_pending_slices`](https://github.com/airbytehq/airbyte/blob/devin/19857-fb-cursor-monotonic/airbyte-integrations/connectors/source-facebook-marketing/source_facebook_marketing/streams/base_insight_streams.py#L271-L278): which slices are persisted ## Risks - After a sync that is interrupted inside the lookback window, the saved `date_start` now stays at the previous value instead of dropping. The next attempt starts from `date_start - insights_lookback_window`, the same window an uninterrupted sync reads, so I don't see a way for this to skip data. - Connections whose cursor already regressed are not repaired retroactively. Their cursor catches up on the next sync that completes; that sync still reads the already-widened window once. - `slices` at or before the cursor disappear from state. As far as I can tell from `_generate_async_jobs`, nothing reads them across syncs (the skip condition only applies to dates before the first generated interval). - Not validated against the live API or the customer's connection; no Facebook credentials were available in this run. ## Declarative-First Evaluation Not applicable: `source-facebook-marketing` is a Python CDK connector (`language:python`, `cdk:python`), with no manifest. ## Test Coverage Behaviour changed: emitted state. - New: `unit_tests/integration/test_ads_insights_action_product_id.py::TestIncremental::test_given_sync_interrupted_in_lookback_window_when_read_then_cursor_never_goes_below_input_state`. A real `read` through `HttpMocker` with saved cursor `2023-01-09` and a 2-day lookback; the second day's report download fails. It asserts the emitted state stays `{"date_start": "2023-01-09", "slices": []}`, and that a retry from that state requests exactly `2023-01-07`..`2023-01-09` again (an earlier job start has no mock and would fail the read). - Without the production change it fails on the state assertion: `[{'date_start': '2023-01-08', 'slices': ['2023-01-03']}] == [{'date_start': '2023-01-09', 'slices': []}]`. With it, it passes. - `poetry run pytest unit_tests/`: 515 passed. ## Root cause
Show/Hide Content - At sync start `_get_start_date()` sets the first slice to `cursor - insights_lookback_window`, which is intended. - As those lookback slices complete, `_advance_cursor()` assigned `_cursor_values[account_id] = ts_start` for each one, so the emitted `date_start` dropped to the start of the lookback window and climbed back up slice by slice. - The CDK checkpoints after every slice. If the attempt stops partway, the platform keeps the lowered cursor, and the next attempt subtracts the lookback window from it again. - Triage observed this on the customer's connection: input state `date_start: 2026-09-20` on attempt 0 and `date_start: 2026-08-28` on attempt 1 of the same job.

body:
Painted colours are now shared out over an object's parts sliced one by one, as the reference does, instead of over the object sliced as one mesh.

## Why
On the lettered multi-colour project (mcbrim_test plate 1) walls and solid were 3-5% short of the reference and sparse infill 23% over. With the paint stripped from the project, walls, solid and sparse are all within 1% of the reference, so the wall and infill generators were not the cause. Each object there is three parts standing 1-6 µm apart; slicing them as one mesh filled the cracks between them, and the paint on the inner part's faces was lost.

## What changed
- `edge-engine/src/paint.rs` `outlines`: each part sliced separately, grown 1 µm, unioned, islands and holes under 0.01 mm² dropped, shrunk back; the reference's simplify (0.5 µm) and `remove_duplicates` (0.01 mm, 30°) steps ported (`segmentation_by_painting`, MultiMaterialSegmentation.cpp).
- `edge_3mf::Painted` carries `parts` instead of a merged `solid`. Two tests.

## Plate 1 against the reference
| Feature | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Outer wall | -4.5% | -3.4% |
| Inner wall | -2.4% | -1.9% |
| Internal solid | -3.2% | +0.6% |
| Sparse infill | +22.5% | +6.9% |
| Gap infill | -13.3% | -6.0% |

Plates 2 and 3 unchanged (already within 1%).

## What is left, on purpose or for later
- About 0.9 m of outer wall: the reference lays walls and gap fill around each µm crack inside solid material (`Layer::make_perimeters` merges same-colour regions with only a safety offset). Not copied, as `paint::apply` already says; it also accounts for most of the remaining sparse and gap-fill difference.
- About 0.6 m (1.4%): the shape of the colour boundaries; the reference's side-colouring (`colorize_contours`, `MMU_Graph`, about 1,500 lines) is not ported.

## Checks
- Workspace tests 1285 passed, 0 failed; desktop tests 169 passed; clippy `-D warnings` clean in both; fmt and both generator checks clean.

author: heyderekj
body:
Makes `@heresmychurch/lookup` easier to set up in apps, ahead of publishing it to npm.

## What changed

**Types**
- `ChurchRecord.fields` is now a typed `ChurchFields`, so `record.fields.city` is `string | null` with no casts. It matches what `worker/src/record.ts` returns.
- Types resolve under every TypeScript `moduleResolution`, including `node10`, which used to fail with TS2307. The type test now installs the package into a throwaway app and checks bundler, node16, nodenext and node10.
- React 19: the `onchurch-*` event props, HTML props and `fieldMap`/`strings`/`lookup` are typed. Vue templates get typed `@church-*` events.

**Entries**
- `@heresmychurch/lookup/react` exports `useChurchLookup`, with React as an optional peer dependency. The registry hook is now generated from it.
- Every entry also has a `.cjs` build with `.d.cts` types, so Jest loads the package without transforms.

**Client and element**
- New `timeout` option (15 s by default). A timed-out request fails with a `LookupError` whose `code` is `"timeout"`; a caller's own abort still rejects with `AbortError`.
- On local dev hosts, the console warns once when `client` isn't set, or when a chosen church found no fields to fill.

**Publishing**
- Pinned script URLs at `/sdk/<version>/`, served as immutable for a year. `copy-assets` writes each version once and never replaces it.
- npm metadata (repository, homepage, keywords, `publishConfig.access`), LICENSE and CHANGELOG in the tarball, and a CI workflow.

## For reviewers
- **Breaking, types only:** unknown camelCase props on `<church-lookup>`, such as `maxResults`, are now type errors in React 19. Use `max-results`.
- **Core size budget** goes from 5 KB to 5.5 KB gzipped (it's 5.16 KB now), for the timeout and setup hints.
- **`site/sdk/0.3.0/` and `site/sdk/0.4.0/` are committed on purpose.** A deploy serves only what's in `site/`, so old pinned versions have to stay in git.
- **Not tested through the Worker:** `wrangler dev` fails at startup. That's not caused by this branch: workerd rejects the `ATTRIBUTION` const exported from `worker/src/index.ts`. Please check `/sdk/0.4.0/element.js` and its cache headers after deploying.
- **New CI workflow:** it hasn't run on GitHub yet; this PR is its first run.

## Testing
- `pnpm test`: registry check, 207 Worker tests and 188 SDK tests, all passing.
- `pnpm typecheck` passes, and the shadcn demo type-checks.
- In a browser on localhost, the pinned 0.4.0 build searched, picked a church and filled fields. Spanish text loaded from `/sdk/0.4.0/strings-es.js`, and the two setup warnings each printed once.
