_Requested by **Dan** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_015rfrUJrym6gUeCoCAtLfJk?thread=cmsg_015rfrUJrym6gUeCoCAtLfJkC3UEkQVSf1PMqEdrfp7AhW)_

**TL;DR:** Every task commit is a push to `main`, so every unfiltered push-to-`main` workflow runs on it. This ADR weighs three fixes and recommends one. Dan picks.

## Problem

Task state commits to `main`. The path filter that stops CI running on them has been missed three times (canonical's bookkeeping callers, tanplan's brand-ratchet, tanplan's e2e). Since 12 Nov, 53 of tanplan's 73 e2e runs were task commits.

## Options in the ADR

| Option | Breaking | Stops CI on task commits |
|---|---|---|
| A. Keep `main`, enforce filters (doctor warning, then failure) | No | Only where a filter was added |
| B. Keep `main`, mark every state commit `[skip ci]` | No (MINOR) | All Actions push workflows, every repo, no per-workflow edit |
| C. Move tasks to a `flow-state` branch | Yes (MAJOR, 8 repos + inflight) | Everything, deploy hooks included |

**Recommendation: B now, C only if B leaks.** Confidence medium. The ADR says what would change it.

## What this PR changes

# Q953: Lilypad-G shell at cap 953 ("Huhlahup")

## Summary
Pareto row at 953 qubits and 1,935,454 average executed Toffoli (score 953 x 1,935,454 = 1,844,487,662). Parent: odinfree add470cc-2795-4888-a94d-d2388bbdba75 (Q950 x 1,936,620, commit 77d377b4bf14004ddf64e3945d30ac9cb5a9e81f). Two literals changed against that commit: the Lilypad-G shell cap 950 -> 953 and the tail nonce 95000000000031 -> 95300000000005. No circuit idea in this row is new. It moves one existing width dial three qubits to the right, saves 1,166 Toffoli with it, and finds a clean nonce at the new width. This row is one of a sweep of the same two-literal recipe across the empty widths between Q900 and Q1021; the first row of the sweep was the sibling 215a0d77-ce77-4f57-8804-28722bede376 (Q940 x 1,941,349). This row is submitted from a second account operated by the same team as the account odinfree, whose rows on this sweep it continues.

This targets the width/Toffoli Pareto frontier. It does not claim the best overall product; the lowest product on the board is Q1227 x 722,696 = 886,747,992 (odinfree) and the product of this row is higher. At the time of the final board read (2026-11-13 04:57 UTC) the nearest frontier rows were Q952 x 1,935,764 on the left and Q954 x 1,935,044 on the right, and no valid row with Q <= 953 had a Toffoli count at or below 1,935,454. The board already held a Q953 row (Nadai2010, 1,935,456 Toffoli); this row is 2 Toffoli lower.

## Credit
This row exists because other people showed that the cap dial works and published trees to turn it on. Credit, carried from the parent note and extended:

- Parent row: odinfree add470cc-2795-4888-a94d-d2388bbdba75 (Q950 x 1,936,620). Its own parent was odinfree 9532e5a0-f9da-43ea-bc78-ad21857ba154 (Q898 x 1,988,305; the phase pass and the 899 -> 898 cap).
- jieyilong 8adb9845-c2da-4cbd-ac6d-840ccdc3c59b (Q899): cap deferral, lazy X2, the 11-tick cap, inverse boundary repairs, shell compares and windows. jieyilong's Lilypad-GCD ancestry underlies all of it.
- gnuchev d9e6ed49-3831-4ad2-803b-ae8a5c5106ef (885 cap, width/split transform, carry pool).
- jackylee0424 b2e963af-e85b-4f89-bbf5-3ad0692c7512 (870 Lilypad-G).
- odinfree 9b5b2d6 (lazy-product fix pair and post-passes).
- gopikannappan: the recipe of changing only the Lilypad-G shell cap and the tail nonce (rows cdf96e0d-dc05-42e0-a1f4-4caa31a391f1 at Q897 and the Q1014-Q1057 run from 0bf5063f-97f4-4a39-a428-cc29d6b6ec4f to 843b7c95-63b8-4e92-be10-c48be07de367). gopikannappan also published cap sweeps on earlier Lilypad-G and Lilypad-GCD trees at the neighbouring widths, which showed that the dial is monotone and that clean nonces exist across it: Q930 d390cf43-f0f0-4ac4-972c-4bdaf1075661 and c859e8a8-57c3-4ad7-8b98-86df46bebe65, Q960 886726c3-259f-436b-9f9e-ab5ece569dc0 and 1a66f89a-3617-4389-9be8-6af23a8181db, Q975 75225df2-a44a-40f9-b049-9e7f522ed9b3, 481d09a2-0f94-4aac-8e30-bbf8da70a337 and 630cfbce-8f1d-4fdd-86ea-29eb25009bc0, Q990 1a1e5066-8287-4383-b3df-e7514d9681b1 and cd2a0ff4-273c-4814-8c46-cb0e1a4fbea0, Q1005 13ff720b-620d-4745-9cc8-c2782d1be260 and 84873d64-1160-47f1-a6d7-67e63b9dcab3. Those are other trees, not the one used here.
- RealAdii: showed the cap sweep on this very tree (the Q950 tree) at other widths: Q930 d47afa31-cb2b-4d90-9b86-c83409e791e2 (1,947,816), Q960 a74ce9fe-c576-4dd8-9174-ebcd7d1204d5 (1,932,874), Q975 4fd158d1-f911-45c6-91aa-fd6288dcf964 (1,928,030), Q990 671b4231-bd1e-44bf-b0cc-9992d34f44b6 (1,924,122) and Q1005 3df9c632-91b7-4de8-bfbf-15775f6800e3 (1,921,540). Their rows fix the shape of the curve on this tree. We did not copy any of their code or nonces; we used their rows as evidence that the dial behaves the same on this tree at other widths.
- odinfree 215a0d77-ce77-4f57-8804-28722bede376 (Q940 x 1,941,349): our own first row of the same two-literal recipe on this tree, made by hand before the sweep that produced this row.

## What changed
Exactly two source literals, against commit 77d377b4bf14004ddf64e3945d30ac9cb5a9e81f:

1. `PEAK0`, the `HALF_COFACTOR_G` arm, in `src/point_add/frogtail_batch/pointadd_lilypad.rs`: `950` -> `953`. As the source comment says, this is a feasibility cap for the shell; the independently allocated inverse workspace remains authoritative and may exceed it. At 953 the stream still peaks at exactly 953 qubits (measured, below).
2. `LILYPAD_TAIL_NONCE` in `src/point_add/mod.rs`: `95000000000031` -> `95300000000005`.

The tail nonce convention is `cap * 10^11 + k`: the shell cap times 100,000,000,000 plus a small index k that selects a nonce inside that cap's own range. For cap 953 the base is 95,300,000,000,000 and the chosen index is k = 5. The nonce is encoded as X/X identity pairs on qubit 0 or 1 at the end of the stream, so it changes only the Fiat-Shamir challenge hash and never the circuit semantics, the qubit peak or the Toffoli count. k = 5 is the first clean index at this width: k = 0 through 4 each leave at least one failing shot among the 9,024. The scan covered 12 nonces in total and found no other clean index, so 1 of 12 was clean.

Nothing else differs from the parent tree. The two files carry one changed line each; the diff is 2 insertions and 2 deletions in total.

## Measured results
Measured locally with a replica of the official evaluator (fasteval, which reproduces the official Fiat-Shamir shot generation, totals, failure counts and score), on the official 9,024 shots. We did not run the stock `eval_circuit` binary on this final stream; the platform's own evaluation is the authority.

| average executed Toffoli | 1,935,453.775 (rounds to 1,935,454) |
| total executed Toffoli over 9,024 shots | 17,465,534,866 |
| average executed Clifford | 20,121,268.934 |
| classical mismatches / phase-garbage batches / ancilla-garbage batches | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| failing shots (any channel) | 0 of 9,024 |
| emitted ops | 25,108,250 |

Against the parent Q950 row (1,936,620 Toffoli, 25,153,467 ops, score 1,839,789,000) this is 3 more qubits for 1,166 fewer average Toffoli (-0.06 percent) and a higher product by 4,698,662. Against the other rows on the same tree, Toffoli rises as the cap falls: 1,921,540 at Q1005, 1,924,122 at Q990, 1,928,030 at Q975, 1,932,874 at Q960, 1,935,454 here at Q953, 1,936,620 at Q950, 1,941,349 at Q940, and 1,947,816 at Q930.

## Validation
- All 9,024 shots pass on the replica with 0 classical, 0 phase and 0 ancilla failures.
- The scan was run on an emit made with nonce index 0, and the final stream was then emitted separately from the source with the winning nonce. The scan emit with its 108 tail ops rewritten for the winning nonce is identical to the final emit in the decompressed domain (raw sha256 90c435d08ffe8c3d3590c155f0215cfcae99efaeee482d84286050612526dbb3; 0 prefix records differ, 0 tail mismatches); the two compressed ops.bin files are not byte-identical, so only the decompressed streams were compared.

body:
Part of #672.

plans/049 stage 2b-2a: the streaming runner gets the seam, the driver keeps the decisions. No production wiring in this PR.

## Why a seam and not a direct import

`@drec/zero-upload` is rank 0.35, `@drec/upload-runtime` is rank 0.5, and the layering test forbids upward dependencies. So `PartSubmitter` is declared in `@drec/core` (rank 0) and the assembly layer injects an implementation. `LivePumpSession` keeps its WAL, its spool bookkeeping and its recovery loop; it borrows only the decision rules.

## What changed

- `packages/core/src/upload-submitter.ts`: `PartSubmitter` with `ensureArchive` / `appendParts` / `verify`. Credentials are absent on purpose - the implementation is bound to one account, so a part cannot switch accounts mid-broadcast.
- `LivePumpSession` accepts `submitter` (and `submitterTargetId`). When present, `submitPart` goes through it; when absent, the legacy in-process path is untouched.
- The confirmation block moved into `recordConfirmed`, used by both paths, so the WAL keeps exactly one shape no matter which path wrote it.
- A `needs-manual` outcome returns `needsManual: true` with the part left unconfirmed, the spool kept and the intent still on disk. That is the whole point: a retry after an unreadable outcome is how a part gets appended twice.

## Proof

- 4 new cases in `packages/zero-upload/src/live-pump-submitter.test.ts`: P1 goes through `ensureArchive` and records the returned archive id; P2 appends to that id; `needs-manual` keeps the spool and leaves the part unconfirmed; a refused submit is called exactly once (the runner does not retry).
- The existing `live-pump.test.ts` suite: 224 passed, unchanged behaviour on the legacy path.
- Mutation: breaking the `needs-manual` mapping (`err.failure === "needs-manual"` -> a never-matching string) turns the third case red; reverted.
- `pnpm typecheck` 0 errors, `arch:check` in sync, `pnpm bundle` `0.0.379-50c314`.

## Scope / decision point

No production wiring: nothing passes a `submitter` today, so live behaviour is identical. The remaining slice (2b-2b) is the assembly side - build the submitter from the driver plus the UPOS target in cli and pass it in - and it is `needs-decision` because it flips "no archive id in the response" from retry-with-a-second-archive to `needs-manual`.

body:
## What

An index package root can declare `publishers`, the signers trusted for that package. The client verifies the platform-selected manifest against that list on install, pull and on-demand installs, with no local configuration. This is the first slice of the release-signing work: the client side only.

- **Index:** `publishers` uses the `[[trust.policy]]` signer vocabulary. A keyless entry matches on identity, issuer and a `claims` map over Fulcio certificate extensions, by name or raw OID. A key entry verifies with no Sigstore network access. An entry of an unknown kind matches nobody.
- **Mode:** `signatures` under `[registries."<host>"]` is `if_declared` (default), `required` or `off`.
- **Operator policy:** where `[[trust.policy]]` covers the same package, both rounds must pass.
- **Opt-out:** `--no-verify` and `OCX_NO_VERIFY` skip the check with the existing one-line warning.
- **Attestations:** `publishers` is the signer set, and `ocx package sbom` returns the newest verified SBOM.
- **No new requests:** committed resolves, `--offline`, `--frozen` and `ocx.lock` installs add no index request.

Design: `.claude/artifacts/adr_publisher_trust_distribution.md`, `.claude/artifacts/system_design_publisher_trust.md`. Plan: `.claude/artifacts/plan_publisher_trust_client.md`.

## Breaking changes

- A package whose index entry declares `publishers` installs only when a listed publisher signed it: exit 77 (`publisher_mismatch`) for another signer, exit 79 (`no_signatures_found`) for an unsigned release.
- Content of such a package that is already in the store is verified once before it is served again.
- `ocx package sbom` with several SBOM candidates of one type returns the newest instead of exiting 65 (`multiple_attestations`). Recorded in `crates/ocx_schema/contract/ledger.toml`.
- `ocx package sbom` and `ocx package verify --attestation` resolve the package before they check identity flags, so an unresolvable package reports the resolve failure first.

## Evidence

- Acceptance scenarios S-001 to S-017 in `test/tests/test_publisher_trust.py` and `test/tests/test_publisher_trust_previous.py`.
- Public end-to-end run against real GitHub-issued certificates: https://github.com/ocx-sh/e2e-index/actions/runs/43365086954 (17 passed). The client was built from a snapshot of this tree before two Markdown-only edits. Fixtures: https://github.com/ocx-sh/e2e-package and https://github.com/ocx-sh/e2e-index.

## Follow-ups

- #694: sign, attest and verify fail on an image-index subject on ghcr.io.
- #695: land the `ocx-mirror` test that pins `publishers` through the root rewrite.

AI assistance drafted this change.

author: tianming-1996
body:
## Root Cause Analysis

The schedule reminder popup widget had 6 UI rendering parameters that did not match the design specification: title font size used FontSizeTwelve instead of FontSizeFourteen, textColor alpha was 0.7 instead of 0.6, source text color reused timeColor (alpha 0.6) instead of having a separate alpha 0.4, divider line had no explicit pen width (should be 1.0px), DRADIUS corner radius was 10 instead of 12, and content left padding was 27px instead of 20px with width padding 35 instead of 40. All mismatches have file:line evidence cross-referenced with the design annotation image.

## Fix Approach

Adjust all 6 rendering parameters to match the design specification values: change FontSizeTwelve to FontSizeFourteen for title, lower textColor alphaF from 0.7 to 0.6 (both light and dark themes), introduce a separate sourceColor variable with alphaF 0.4, set explicit divider pen widthF 1.0, change DRADIUS from 10 to 12, and fix content left padding to 20px with width padding to 40px.

## Change Safety Assessment

### Code Safety

- **Risk Level**: Low
- All changes are local constant value adjustments and local variable introductions within CenterWidget class internals and one constant in constants.h — no function signature changes, no public API modifications, 0 external callers affected
- Historical insight: DRADIUS was introduced by commit a99e07d2 to add rounded corners; this change adjusts the radius value (10→12) without removing the rounding functionality, so the original fix intent is preserved

### Business Impact Scope

- **Schedule Reminder Widget display**: the popup shown when hovering over schedule entries in calendar month/week/day views — affects title font size, text color opacity, source text opacity, divider line width, corner radius, and content padding
- All changes are within CenterWidget class internals and constants.h, 0 external callers, no signature changes
- User scenarios: visual appearance of the schedule hover popup in both light and dark themes

### Verification Suggestion

1. Verify the schedule reminder popup in light theme — check font size, color opacity, divider line, corner radius, and padding against the design spec
2. Repeat in dark theme
3. Test with organizer/attendee info to confirm divider line displays correctly

---

## 根因分析

日程悬浮提示框的 6 项 UI 绘制参数与设计标注不符：标题字号使用 FontSizeTwelve（应为 FontSizeFourteen）、textColor 透明度 0.7（应为 0.6）、来源文字复用 timeColor 透明度 0.6（应为独立 0.4）、分割线未显式设置画笔宽度（应为 1.0px）、DRADIUS 圆角 10（应为 12）、内容左内边距 27px（应为 20）且宽度 padding 35（应为 40）。所有偏差均有 file:line 级代码证据与设计标注图对照。

## 修复方案

将 6 项绘制参数调整为设计标注值：标题字号 12→14、textColor alphaF 0.7→0.6（亮色+暗色）、来源颜色独立设 alphaF 0.4、分割线显式 setWidthF(1.0)、DRADIUS 10→12、内容左内边距改为 20px 且宽度 padding 改为 40px。

## 改动安全评估

### 代码安全评估

- **风险等级**: 低风险
- 所有改动均为 CenterWidget 类内部局部常量值调整和局部变量引入，以及 constants.h 中 DRADIUS 常量值调整——无函数签名变更、无公开接口修改、0 外部调用方受影响
- 历史洞察：DRADIUS 由 commit a99e07d2 引入以添加圆角显示，本次改动仅调整圆角半径值（10→12），圆角功能仍然存在，不撤销原有修复意图

### 业务影响范围

- **日程悬浮提示框显示**：日历月/周/日视图中鼠标悬停日程时显示的提示弹窗——影响标题字号、正文颜色透明度、来源文字透明度、分割线宽度、圆角大小、内容间距
- 所有改动均在 CenterWidget 类内部和 constants.h 常量，0 外部调用方，无签名变更
- 用户场景：用户在日历视图中悬停日程条目时看到的提示弹窗外观变化

### 验证建议

1. 亮色主题下打开日程悬浮提示框，检查标题字号、正文颜色透明度、来源文字透明度、分割线宽度、圆角大小、内容左间距是否符合设计标注
2. 暗色主题下重复上述检查
3. 含参与人信息的日程提示框，确认分割线显示正常

## Summary by Sourcery

Update the schedule reminder popup styling to match the approved design specification.

Bug Fixes:
- Align the schedule reminder popup’s visual parameters with the design specification across light and dark themes.

Enhancements:
- Refine popup typography, text opacity, source text styling, divider rendering, corner radius, and content spacing for consistent schedule hover details.

author: bcordis
body:
Under "Remove IDs from URLs" the site router looks a message or series up by alias alone, so two rows sharing an alias share one address and only one of them can be reached. This stops new duplicates, repairs the ones already stored, and adds `UNIQUE KEY idx_alias` to `#__bsms_studies` and `#__bsms_series`, as `#__bsms_teachers` already has.

## Stopping new duplicates

- **A typed alias another row holds is refused** by `check()` on both tables, only when the alias is new or changed. The refusal says when the holder is in the trash.
  - In the administrator, for a user whose admin list already shows the holder (the lists' location and view-level filter), it names that row and links to its edit form.
  - Everyone else, and any save from the site or the API, is told only that the alias is taken. Naming the holder unconditionally would let a guessed alias reveal the title of a message the user cannot see; the commit's security review flagged this.
- **An alias built from the title takes the next free `-2`, `-3`, ...** with a warning, as core does for articles.
- **Save as Copy** with the title unchanged steps it to the next `(2)`, `(3)`, ... whose alias is free, so a second copy of the same original becomes `(3)` with `-3`, not another `(2)`. The alias is built from that title. An alias the user typed is kept, and `check()` refuses it if it is taken.
  - Core's `generateNewTitle()` steps the alias's own trailing number instead, so a copy of `psalm-23` would become `psalm-24`. Titles here end in chapter, verse and year numbers often enough to rule that out.
- **The series model's Save as Copy and batch copy were broken.** They called `generateNewTitle()`, which loads rows by `catid`; the series table has no `catid`, so `Table::load()` threw. Both now work, and batch copy numbers titles the same way. Neither is offered in the series screens today (the edit toolbar has no Save as Copy button, and the batch dialog has no copy), so this only matters for a direct request or once a button is added.
- **Direct inserts** (setup wizard, CSV import, PreachIt and SermonSpeaker converters) bypass the Table, so they now pick a free alias themselves.

## Repairing what exists

- `Cwmalias::ensureUniqueAliases()` handles each shared alias:
  - The published or archived row with the lowest id keeps it. That is the row the router already serves, so no working address changes.
  - Every other row gets the next free numbered form.
  - An empty alias is built from the title.
  - Then the unique index is added. Once the index exists, the method does nothing.
- **When it runs:**
  - Postflight on every install and update. This is PHP rather than update SQL because the schema fixer would replay a bare `ADD` on its own and fail on the duplicates. Install matters because a reinstall over tables an uninstall kept skips their `CREATE TABLE`.
  - After a backup restore, in both the single-request and step-by-step flows.
  - From Admin Center **Fix** and from the 9.x upgrade helper.
- Each rename is written to the install log, and one notice per table lists them. A row that had no alias only gains one, so it is logged but not listed.
- `install.mysql.utf8.sql` carries the index, and `verify-migrations.php` now asserts it.

## Verification

- **PHPUnit:** the full suite passes, 3890 tests.
- **New tests:**
  - `CwmaliasUniqueTest`: the repair, on a temporary table.
  - `AliasUniquenessCheckTest`: the refusal and when it names the holder.
  - `GeneratedAliasTest`: numbering and the warning.
  - `CwmaliasCopyTest`: Save as Copy titles and aliases on both tables, against real rows, including a second copy and a title ending in a number.
- **Mutation checks:** turning off each behavior (the refusal, the warning, the copy numbering, keeping a typed alias, the visibility gate) fails its tests.

author: aviralgoelamd
body:
## What this adds

On gfx950, dense attention now accepts any `sliding_window` length. Before this change, the window had to be a multiple of the KV tile width (`block_n`), and any other length was rejected. Common model windows are not tile multiples. For example, a "128 keys back plus the diagonal" window is 129 keys.

## What changed

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `library/kernels/gfx950/attention_dense.py` | One helper, `_window_tile_counts`, gives both window tile counts. Both builders (grid and persistent) use it. |
| `library/kernels/common/attention_dense_spec.py` | New per-arch hook `_supports_any_window_size`. It is on for gfx950 and off for gfx942. |
| `platform/cpp` (spec port, `abi.h`, `abi.py`) | Mirrors the hook as a traits field, appended last. `ROCKE_ABI_VERSION` goes 17 → 18. |
| Tests and goldens | Exact visible-key tests on silicon, dispatcher tests for both arches, new IR harness cases and goldens. |

## Why it works

The kernel used one tile count, `W // block_n`, for two different jobs.
- **First KV tile to load:** this count must round **up**, `ceil((W-1)/block_n)`. Otherwise the oldest visible key is skipped.
- **Tiles needing no mask:** this count must round **down**, `W // block_n`. Otherwise a tile that is only partly inside the window skips the mask.

The two counts are equal when `W % block_n` is 0 or 1. So every window that was already legal emits byte-identical IR.

The per-element mask was already exact for any `W`. Only the tile ranges changed.

## Scope

- gfx950 dense only: grid, persistent, wide-DMA, paged and packed varlen.
- gfx942 still rejects non-multiple windows with a clear reason. Its tile loops assume whole window tiles. This is a known gap, not a hardware limit.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Existing IR (golden, all LLVM flavors) | unchanged; additions only |
| Python vs C++ lowering, 960 window configs | identical |
| Build, host ctest, byte identity | pass |
| Platform pytest (local) | no failure that develop does not also have |
| Library pytest | runs in GitHub CI ("Test hipkernelprovider"); a one-off local run also showed no failure that develop does not have |
| gfx950 numeric file on silicon | all pass, including exact visible-key sets for W ∈ {1, 63, 65, 127, 129, 130, 255, 257} over 4 tile shapes |
| Mutant controls | two deliberately broken copies (start tile rounded down; mask-free bound rounded up) fail exactly the cases predicted on CPU before the GPU runs |

## Notes

Accuracy against an fp32 reference was checked on silicon at model shapes. The numbers are on the internal tracking page.

JIRA ID : AICK-3159

author: lawrencecchen
body:
## Summary

Tests that set a read timeout on a Unix socket after the far end can have closed no longer fail on macOS by the order of two processes.

macOS refuses `SO_RCVTIMEO` with `EINVAL` (os error 22) on a socket that can send no more and receive no more; Linux accepts the call. A test that does `set_read_timeout(..).unwrap()` after its peer can have closed is then green on Linux and red on macOS when the peer wins the race. Five merged PRs each mended one site of this cause (#30740, #30780, #39459, #39583, #42270). The tip of `feat-cmux-next` had 13 more such test lines on Unix sockets and 2 in the SDK's mock server. This PR gives them one rule.

- `cmux_tui_platform::read_timeout_or_ended(&stream, timeout) -> io::Result<ReadWait>` (new, `cmux-tui/crates/cmux-tui-platform/src/read_wait.rs`) sets the timeout. A refusal is `ReadWait::Ended` only when a poll that does not block says that the socket can receive no more (`Stream::peer_closed`, the hang-up poll that the daemon uses). A read then returns at once with what is left and then the end, so the test needs no timeout. A refusal on a socket that is open is an error that says so; the site's `unwrap` fails the test.
- 13 test lines call it in the place of `set_read_timeout(..).unwrap()`.
- `cmux-tui/bindings/rust/tests/mock_server.rs` gets a local function of the same rule for its 2 lines: the SDK crate doesn't depend on cmux-tui-platform.
- `cmux-tui-core/src/server/tests/outbound_and_scheduler.rs:545` sets its timeout before its `shutdown(Write)`; no helper is needed there.
- `cmux-tui-core/src/server/remote_entry_tests.rs:143-144`: the test of a refused process sends its 2 lines through the file's `send_racing_close`. The entry closes that connection at once, so a write after the close is a broken pipe; the read stays the assertion that no reply comes.

A person sees nothing in the app: this PR changes test code and one module that only a test build contains.

## Where the helper lives, and why no app build

`cmux-tui/crates/cmux-tui-core/tests/git_lane.rs` is a test file (an integration test of the crate); no product code calls the helper.

The module is behind a feature that only `[dev-dependencies]` turn on:

- `cmux-tui/crates/cmux-tui-platform/src/lib.rs:16` and `:24`: `#[cfg(all(unix, any(test, feature = "test-support")))]` on the module and on its re-export.
- `git grep -n 'cmux-tui-platform.*test-support' -- '*Cargo.toml'` gives 3 lines, each under `[dev-dependencies]`: `cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/Cargo.toml:195`, `cmux-tui/crates/cmux-tui-core/Cargo.toml:90`, `cmux-tui/crates/cmux-tui/Cargo.toml:215`.

The helper was first written in `cmux-unix-socket`, which is an input of the app FFI pin (`scripts/cmux-next/check-app-ffi-pin.sh --list-inputs`). The built library would not have changed, but the pin hash would, and the merge would have started an FFI release build on a macOS runner and a re-pin PR for the same bytes. The helper moved to `cmux-tui-platform`, which is not an input:

- `git diff --stat 8a2f035fd3b9..HEAD -- cmux-tui/crates/cmux-unix-socket` is empty.
- Of the 19 changed paths, 18 are under no directory that `--list-inputs` prints. One, `cmux-tui/bindings/rust/tests/mock_server.rs`, is under `cmux-tui/bindings/rust/tests`, which `--list-excluded` prints.

`cmux-tui/Cargo.lock` has one new line (`cmux-tui-platform` in the dependency list of the package `cmux-tui`). It was written by hand; step `14c8f141e858c19e3e79a816` ran cargo with `--locked` and is its proof.

## Testing

All steps ran on the fleet (`cmux-ci run --class light --script scripts/ci/cmux-tui-rust-check.sh --ref SHA --os OS --arg MODE --arg FILTER`). Nothing was compiled on a developer machine. Each macOS step was sent with `--label macos-27`. The Linux `all` step (fmt, clippy with `--all-targets`, tests) and the macOS test steps are the compile proof of this head; there is no pool build.

The red tests went in as their own commit before the helper's rule (d6aa9516b2b2, when the file was in `cmux-unix-socket`). The focused command is `test read_wait_`.

| Command (OS MODE FILTER) | Result |
|---|---|
| Linux `test read_wait_` at d6aa9516b2b2, the red commit (6 tests, before the helper's rule) | RED as designed, step `90cecb94df617f80e318c56f`: 6 run, 2 failed, 4 passed. Failed: `read_wait_a_refusal_on_a_socket_that_ended_is_the_end` and `read_wait_a_refusal_on_an_open_socket_is_an_error_that_says_so`. These 2 give the helper a made `EINVAL`, so they are red on each OS before the rule. The 4 others pass on Linux, which doesn't refuse the call |
| Linux `test read_wait_` at the head f6baa81b21ab | GREEN, step `14c8f141e858c19e3e79a816`: 6 run, 6 passed, each `cmux-tui-platform read_wait::tests::`: `read_wait_a_peer_that_closed_first_gives_the_end`, `read_wait_a_peer_that_closed_first_leaves_its_lines_and_then_the_end`, `read_wait_a_socket_where_each_side_ended_its_writes_gives_the_end`, `read_wait_a_refusal_on_a_socket_that_ended_is_the_end`, `read_wait_a_refusal_on_an_open_socket_is_an_error_that_says_so`, `read_wait_an_open_socket_gets_its_timeout`. cargo ran with `--locked` (`scripts/ci/cmux-tui-rust-check.sh:682`) |
| Linux `all remote_entry` at the head (fmt, clippy, the tests with `remote_entry` in the name) | GREEN, step `ac48d6b3a5c24b751b6e8ebd`: fmt pass; `cargo clippy --workspace --exclude cmux-holder-v3 --all-targets --locked --keep-going -- -D warnings` pass; 38 run, 38 passed, with `cmux-tui-core server::remote_entry::tests::a_process_that_is_not_the_link_gets_nothing_and_registers_no_client` (the test with the 2 racing writes) |
| Linux `test git_lane_` at the head (`tests/git_lane.rs`: the body of `read_line_in` changed) | GREEN, step `377046e964982b65cfa6279f`: 26 run, 26 passed, each `cmux-tui-core::git_lane git_lane_...`, with the 3 tests of the test client: `git_lane_the_test_client_sees_a_close_that_came_before_its_look`, `git_lane_the_test_client_reads_the_replies_that_a_closed_connection_left`, `git_lane_the_test_client_finds_the_reply_that_a_closed_connection_left` |
| Linux `test write_side_eof_drains` at the head (`outbound_and_scheduler.rs:545`: the order of 2 lines changed) | GREEN, step `3c371de01cbdc0e3e5ad93dc`: 1 run, 1 passed: `cmux-tui-core server::tests::outbound_and_scheduler::write_side_eof_drains_accepted_surface_requests` |
| Linux `test read_wait_` at the merged tree 6b142c957d00 (this head + `feat-cmux-next` 219227b61a3c; a branch that never merges) | GREEN, step `9d296f626655f7e97ceb054a`: 6 run, 6 passed, the same 6 names. `feat-cmux-next` changed `cmux-tui/Cargo.lock` 3 times after the base of this branch; this step is the `--locked` proof of the merged lock (the lock of the tip + the one line of this PR). An earlier step, `c4656e8bfd8a5ddab6a85e2a` at c04247a3a439 (this head + f571281739fd), was green too |
| Linux `test @affected=8a2f035fd3b9` at the head (the workspace, 118 crates) | NO VERDICT, step `0c3f5abb1c3567529e7d420e`: its runner was lost during the step, the step went back to the queue and got no worker; cancelled. The 2 rows above ran in its place |
| macOS 27 `test read_wait_` at d6aa9516b2b2 (what macOS does for each of the 6 cases) | NOT RUN at this text: no macos-27 worker takes a step |
| macOS 27 `test read_wait_` at the head | NOT RUN at this text: no macos-27 worker takes a step |

### Observed / Not run

Observed (ran and read the job log):
- The steps of the table.
- `python3 scripts/cmux-next/prepush-gate.py` at the head: `arch-ratchet: no architecture count rises`, `no new violations`.
- The checks of this head, one read each after their end: `clippy (changed cmux-tui packages)` passed (the product form of the changed packages compiles with `-D warnings`), and the step `Check the app FFI pin` of `cmux-next checks (god files, concurrency, crash safety, l10n)` passed. So no app build and no launch were run: a product build reads no dev-dependency and has the feature off.
- The SDK's 2 changed tests ran in the checks `rust package` and `Rust SDK

author: dizys
body:
Part of #570, milestone M5 · Replace 1Panel. First slice of Track K: measure what other stores convert to, keep CI from letting it fall, prove a sample runs on real Docker, and take the biggest gate, images on a tag that moves.

## Today's rates, and after this PR

Measured through the control plane's own fetch and converter, at the commits `internal/catalog/convert/rates.json` pins:

| Store | Apps | Before (main) | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1Panel's app store (`55061b99`) | 269 | 93 (34%) | 99 (36%) |
| Dokploy's templates (`4f0ddfb5`) | 612 | 169 (27%) | 299 (48%) |
| Coolify's templates (`93c7e53e`) | 384 | 78 (20%) | 199 (51%) |

Before, by reason: 1Panel scripts 61, another app's database 25, shipped files 25, amd64 alone 20, Compose keys Dockwell can't run 19, no version that stays put 15. Dokploy no version 182, shipped files 93, a secret inside a longer value 57 (and most of its 39 "fails the catalog's checks" are the same), Compose keys 49. Coolify no version 168, catalog checks 32 (again mostly a secret inside a longer value), marked to leave out 34, shipped files 30.

The converter stops at an app's first reason, so ADR 0085 also records what each gate holds back, measured by letting each through in turn: moving tags, then a secret inside a longer value, then shipped files, then scripts, then amd64 alone, would reach 1Panel 151, Dokploy 446 and Coolify 233. Those are the next slices.

## What changes

**Measured, in the repository, with CI holding it**
- `dockwell-catalog rates` converts each store at its pinned commit through `convert.Fetch` (the server's two-round fetch, factored out of `catalogapi.convertOne` so both share it) and `convert.OnServer`, and prints apps, converted, rate, and the rest by reason. `--list` names each app left out; `--show 1panel/<id>` prints one converted entry, or its reason. Under ten seconds for all three.
- `internal/catalog/convert/rates.json` records each store's commit and every app that converts. `make store-rates` fails when an app that converted no longer does, naming it, and when the record isn't current; `RECORD=1` writes it, `PIN=1` moves each store to its branch first. `convert.MeasuredOf` embeds it, for Track C's store gallery.
- A new CI job, **Other stores on Docker**, runs `make store-rates`, then `make store-e2e`: `scripts/store-e2e.sh` adds each store at its pinned commit and installs `1panel/linux-command`, `dokploy/excalidraw`, `dokploy/mazanoke` and `coolify/privatebin` from their converted entries; each plan pins its images, every container runs (healthy where it has a check) on loopback alone, the app answers on its port, and it's removed through a plan. It runs for any Go change, as Catalog on Docker does (rule and examples in `scripts/ci-jobs.sh`). Its first run found that Dokploy's CyberChef publishes port 80 where its image now listens on 8080 (broken in Dokploy too), so the sample takes `dokploy/mazanoke` instead; ADR 0085 notes a plan could warn of such a port later.
- The job's agent reads registries as a server does, under `DOCKWELL_TEST_REGISTRY=public`, while `DOCKWELL_TEST` keeps STUN and metadata off. Without it a test still reads no registry.

**A tag that moves (ADR 0085)**
- On the server, an image named by `latest`, `stable`, `main` and the like converts, as a version's tag does: the plan pins the build it points at, through the agent, and shows the digest (ADR 0078). An image named with no tag is written as `latest`. A 1Panel app whose only version folder is `latest` converts. The offline converter, which pins as it converts for a published catalog, still leaves these out.
- A catalog install that runs such a tag is checked for new builds with ADR 0079's HEAD, offered each as an update (kind `digest`) through its catalog, so the panel's Update and automatic updates of that kind upgrade the install and name no image. Upgrading reads each moving tag again: with no newer release it plans only a new build ("Update moving to the newest build of nginx:latest"), backed up first like any upgrade.
- The agent keeps the digest its update check read beside a plan's digest reads, so an update planned right after Check now pins the build the check saw.

## Safety

Nothing from a store is ever run. A moving tag is pinned at the plan exactly as a version's tag already is, so what runs is the digest a person approved; nothing about the image is trusted that wasn't before. `docs/security/catalog-sources.md` says so, and ADR 0085 records why each is safe and what was turned down.

## What a novice and a power user get

A novice sees about 250 more Dokploy and Coolify apps install with defaults, and "Pull the new build" when `latest` moves. A power user gets `go run ./cmd/dockwell-catalog rates --list` and `--show <store>/<app>` to see exactly why an app is out, and the plan's digest for every build.

## Checks run

- `make lint`: 0 issues (after the rebase onto #564 too).
- `go test -race` on `internal/catalog/...`, `cmd/dockwell-catalog`, `internal/control/catalogapi`, `internal/control/serviceupdates`, `internal/registry`, `internal/agent`, `internal/cli`, and the whole `internal/control` (through heavy.sh).
- New tests: the rates command and its record; moving tags on the server and offline; `catalog.Moving`; the keeper's new builds for an install; a control test that installs a `latest` app from a converted store, moves the registry's build, sees the check offer it through the catalog, and upgrades to it; test-mode registry reads.
- `scripts/store-e2e.sh` rehearsed on the fake engine with Docker's CLI and real digest reads from Docker Hub and GHCR: every step but the HTTP answer, which the fake can't give. CI's job is its first run on real Docker.
- The whole panel suite.

No proto, store migration or panel change. The new job needs adding to the branch rule's required checks if it should block merges.

body:
### Problem
Every Global Defaults save cleared the whole site cache, even with no changes. `on_update` passed `None` to `frappe.db.set_default` (for `account_url`, which is no longer a field, and for an empty Link, because `self.get(key, "")` passes `""` as filters), and it then called `frappe.clear_cache()` as well.

### Fix
Drop the stale `account_url` key, pass `cstr(...)` of each value, and remove the explicit `frappe.clear_cache()`. `set_default` already clears the cache when a default changes, and the property setters clear their doctype's cache. A disabled default Currency is now re-enabled through its controller, which clears the cache itself.

### Steps to reproduce
1. In the console: `frappe.get_doc("Global Defaults").save()`.
2. `frappe.cache.set_value("probe", 1)`.
3. `frappe.get_doc("Global Defaults").save()` again, without changes.
4. `frappe.cache.get_value("probe")` returns `None` instead of `1`.

Closes #65640

## Summary
- Voices every narration and reader line of episode 33's screenplay with the lifted narrator engine: Kokoro af_aoede 0.88 (0.84 in the Echo) narrates, am_michael 0.86 reads every testimony line, each as its own cast voice.
- `studio/news/voice_episode.py` (net-new): groups lines by cast voice, re-checks quote-verbatim (text sha256 == quote_sha256) before any line reaches the model, applies an optional one-token pronunciation respelling (`studio/pronunciation.json`) that never changes a line's hash, and writes the manifest `studio/news/voicing_manifest.py` validates (schema `omnibus-voicing/1`, checked out byte-identical from E9i/PR #19 since that's the schema render.py reads) at `episodes/33/audio/voice.json`. Wraps the whole voicing loop in `studio/engine/vision.py`'s shared `HeavyLock` (imported, not copied) and refuses before anything reaches the model if another job holds it; also has a CLI `main()`.
- `studio/engine/kokoro_worker.py` now calls `Kokoro.create_timed` (was `create`) so each take's phoneme timeline is reported when the pinned model exposes one; `studio/engine/narrator.py`'s `words_from_timings`/`words_timed` group it into one span per written word, cached beside the take (`.timeline.json`).

author: damodar-datta
body:
## What does this PR do?

Once the reference speckle is measured, the subset slider runs from the **SSSIG size** (the least the accuracy target allows) to **50 px above it**, capped at 121. It **starts at the size that spans three measured speckles**, kept inside that range. Before a measurement it is unchanged: 15–121, at 41.

**Starting size**
- Three speckles fit in less than the SSSIG size, or the speckle wasn't measured → the floor.
- They need more than SSSIG + 50, or no subset can span three → the top.
- At the very top (SSSIG 121, weak texture) the range is 119–121, so the slider keeps two distinct ends.

**The range holds for every size.** A typed, pasted or Re-run subset outside it moves to the nearer end. A size the user set moves too when a new reference or ROI moves the range. A Re-run at subset 21 on a reference whose SSSIG size is now 41 runs at 41.

**For reviewers**
- `SubsetRecommender.Tuning` now searches the full 15–121. It used to read the slider's current ends, which would now tie a new measurement to the previous one's range.
- `fitRange()` sets `valueFrom`/`valueTo` and moves the value inside in the same call, because Material's slider throws on draw if the value is outside its ends. One test draws the slider after a range change to check this.
- The shaded band and the span chip work as before. The span chip shows less often, since the slider now starts at the three-speckle size.
- The subset ⓘ text, `OPERATING_MANUAL.md`, and QC steps 5.1.11 and 5.2.9 in `WORKFLOWS.md` describe the new range.

body:
## What this changes

One way of working for the whole team (and each person's Codex): **whoever you are and whatever you work on, every time start a new branch from the latest `main`, and merge back into `main` through a pull request. `main` is always the current version.** Roles change; the process does not. The branch prefix depends on the kind of work, not on the person: `fix/` bug fixes, `ui/` UI, `feat/` features, `docs/` docs.

- `AGENTS.md`: rules Codex reads automatically. Pull the latest `main` before starting, create a new branch by task type, never change `main` directly, no code in the root, run compile and tests, then open a PR. `CLAUDE.md` makes Claude Code read the same rules.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/team/`: team members, process, folder map, and GitHub Desktop steps.
- `.github/`: CODEOWNERS (every PR asks @Yokiwa for review), PR template, and bug, UI / design and task issue templates.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: on every PR, checks for code files in the repository root, then runs the type check, tests and build.
- `design/`: `mockups/` for designs, `incoming/` for UI drafts not yet in the code.
- The 13 UI files uploaded to the root moved to `design/incoming/2026-11-12-VNzia/`. The extension builds only from `src/`, so those files never took effect. The README there has a table saying which file in `src/` each one belongs to.

body:
## 요약
곡 선택 화면의 렉(PC 모드 9ee7036과 같은 증상)을 안드로이드에서 고쳤습니다. 원인은 PC와 달랐습니다.

- **미리듣기**: 곡을 넘길 때 메인 스레드가 100~150 ms 멈췄습니다. 원인은 디코드가 아니라 NVorbis가 곡 길이를 구하려고 OGG 전체 페이지를 읽는 일이었습니다(스트리밍 클립도 생성 중 첫 시크에서 같은 스캔을 합니다). 길이는 파일 끝 Ogg 페이지의 granule로 바로 읽고, 페이지 스캔은 곡 목록에 들어올 때 백그라운드 스레드에서 미리 합니다 → 곡 전환당 7~8 ms. 넘겨 본 곡마다 전체 PCM이 메모리에 남던 문제도 없어졌습니다.
- **본곡**: 준비 화면에 들어올 때 백그라운드로 미리 풉니다(길이 스캔 없음). 전체 디코드 클립은 한 곡 것만 들고 있습니다.
- **커버**: `Sprite.Create`를 `SpriteMeshType.FullRect`로 → 장당 21~52 ms → 1~4 ms.
- **계측**: `perf.ts`가 100 ms 넘는 프레임을 `mod.log`에 `frame-hitch`로 남깁니다.

## 확인
- 개인판(같은 코드 + 보존 모드)으로 SM-G991N 실기 확인: 미리듣기 재생(출력 RMS 0.24~0.35), 배틀 본곡 재사용 `ready:true`, 싱크 −0.004/−0.004/−0.001초.
- 이 공개 빌드 자체는 기기에서 실행하지 않았습니다. `um publish check` 61 files 0/0, 빌드 결과 해금 문자열 0건.

body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"robot-head"} -->
_Requested by **Matt Stone** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Htihx2UVHLeHt1gSDCxe3J?thread=cmsg_01Htihx2UVHLeHt1gSDCxe3JVg2nUa2yhn5KT48ecLfefN)_

Closes #217. Closes #218. Picks up the §39 formatter gaps left after the Codex claims #111–#120 merged (#115, #142). It doesn't touch the formatter work Codex still holds (#170 tuple macros, #214 macOS Lean timeout).

## §39.2 layout (#217)

Before this change, a line over the 100-column ribbon put every space on a new line:

```
fn
filter_ids_unoptimized(
    inout
    shard
    .{metrics.requests}:
...
```

Now the §39.3 showcase signature formats as:

```
fn filter_ids_unoptimized(
    inout shard.{metrics.requests}: WorkerShard,
    in shard.{config.limit}: WorkerShard,
    in raw_ids: Slice[u64]
) -> u32 eff [Alloc, Io, Clock, Random, Network, Filesystem, Spawn, Cancel] {
    let total = compute_something_long(
        first_argument_value,
        second_argument_value,
        third_argument_value,
        fourth_argument_value
    );
```

- Spaces inside a line never break. Line breaks go, outermost first, at `(...)`/`[...]`/`.{...}` lists (one item per line, each item in its own group), `->` (in its own group), member-chain dots and infix operators (both indented one level). `::` paths never split.
- The formatter still never adds or removes a token, so a trailing comma in the source keeps the list vertical. This also gets rid of the old `Slice[u64],)` flat output.
- Token/comment conservation, the reparse check and the idempotence check are unchanged.

## Workspace formatting (#218)

The README runs `vesper fmt --check` with no path, which used to fail with `fmt requires a file`. Now:

- `vesper fmt [PATH...]` formats the current directory when no path is given. Directories are walked for `.ves` files in sorted order. Symlinks aren't followed, and hidden, `target/` and `bazel-*` directories are skipped. The walk stops at 200,000 entries.
- Each file goes through the existing staged single-file commit. If one file fails, it is reported in `files` and the other files are still processed. The command exits nonzero on any error, or with `--check` when any file needs formatting.
- A single file argument keeps the old JSON report schema.
- `tests/stylus_cli.rs` and `scripts/check-stylus.py` used to require a directory argument to fail. They now pass `--check` and still assert that nothing was written.
- The old `options_and_missing_files_fail` case called a bare `fmt` from the test's working directory. With this change that would rewrite the repository's `.ves` files, so the bare-`fmt` check now runs the real binary inside a disposable directory.

## Note for the owner

Running `vesper fmt --check` at the repository root currently reports many existing `examples/**` and fixture files as noncanonical, and some fixtures are deliberately invalid. Nothing in CI runs that command, and this PR doesn't reformat those files.

## Validation

- `cargo test --manifest-path crates/vesper-fmt/Cargo.toml` (all suites; 5 new layout tests)
- `cargo test --test fmt_cli --test stylus_cli --test lsp_actions --test lsp_cli --test source_models --test format_proof_cli` and the `fmt_commands` unit tests (2 new directory tests). Lean isn't installed locally, so format_proof_cli skipped its kernel cases; CI runs them.
- `scripts/check-stylus.py` and `scripts/check-source-tooling.py` against the built binary
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings` on the touched targets

## What changed

An extra that rides beneath its dish without a ticket of its own (for example "+ Peppers") was named three different ways depending on where a cook looked. The printed kitchen ticket used the extra's **staff** name; the kitchen station screen and the pass used its **customer-facing** text, so in English mode a cook could read the Spanish menu wording on screen (backlog A1220: «Pimientos de Padrón» on screen where the paper said "+ Peppers").

All three surfaces now show the extra's **kitchen** name, falling back to its staff name when it has none — the same rule dishes, options answers and split-off extras already followed, and what `docs/developers/products.md`'s "three names" table says the kitchen ticket and kitchen display read. Customer surfaces (receipts) and the till's own "Make now" list are unchanged.

- `buildTicketItems` (`apps/server/src/kitchen-print.ts`) prints the `+` line through `kitchenPresentationName`. **This changes the paper too:** a following extra's `+` line now prints its kitchen name where it used to print its staff name.
- `readCancelledExtra` (same file) names a cancelled extra by its kitchen name on the CHANGED / HOLD CHANGED slip and the station screen's notice, so the slip no longer lists kept extras by kitchen name and the removed one by staff name.
- `readQueueSubItems` (`apps/server/src/working-order.ts`) sends each following extra as `name` (its kitchen name) in place of the customer `descriptions` map. author: jestyr27
body:
## Summary

Two intermittent failures in the o11y receiver capability survey's probe test on macOS, both now reproduced and fixed.

1. **`_kill_group` raised `PermissionError`.** On macOS, `os.killpg` returns EPERM for a process group whose leader is exiting. With a child that writes past the output limit and exits, 6 parallel loops of 800 runs produced 35 EPERMs out of 4800, all at the first kill after the limit trips. In 13 of them the child had already exited; in 22 it had not finished exiting when checked. `_kill_group` now treats EPERM like `ProcessLookupError`. That is safe: `_run` then waits 0.2 s and, if the child is still alive, kills and waits again. Under the same load the fixed version gave 0 errors in 4800 runs, with no hang and no leftover children.
2. **The test raced its own 0.05 s deadline.** The test set `PROBE_TIMEOUT` to 0.05 s for all three cases, so under load the oversized case came back `probe_timeout`: about 3% of runs at 0.05 s, 0 of 4800 at the 4 s default. Only the timeout case shortens the deadline now.

Limit, stated: EPERM on the second kill is now swallowed too, so a child that is alive but cannot be signalled would make the final unbounded `process.wait()` hang where it used to raise. The survey runs only `/usr/bin/id`, `systemctl`, `uname` and `loginctl` as the receiver's own user, so EPERM there can only mean a child that is exiting.

## Tests

- New `test_kill_group_tolerates_a_group_that_is_already_gone_or_exiting`, for both errors. Mutation-checked: removing `PermissionError` from the `except` fails it.
- `test_o11y_receiver_capabilities.py` passed 5 runs in a row and 180 runs under parallel load.

## Checks

- `/simplify` and `/security-review`: two files, one widened `except` plus tests. Nothing to simplify, and no security impact (no secret handling, no new process or input).

Merge held for v0.21.0, as with #1137: v0.16.0 is at its file budget.

author: codinganarchy
body:
Fixes #1820.

**Bug:** `a_panic_in_a_callers_turn_never_hangs_shutdown` (from #1808) raced the shard's driver for a message, with up to 10,000 caller tries, and lost twice on macOS CI:
- #1819: after 0.02 s, with the driver having handled nothing. It was still starting up, and held the token.
- #1817: the driver handled 8,881 of the 10,000 messages first.

**Fix:** the setup no longer races.
- Both shards run on one driver thread (`shard_threads = 1`).
- Shard 1's handler holds that driver inside its own turn, with two barriers, while the test submits to shard 0 and runs a caller's turn there.
- Shard 0's token is then free, and no other thread can take it. So the caller's turn takes the message and panics on the first try.
- The test then releases the driver, and requires `shutdown` to return within 30 s and report "shard 0 panicked in a caller's turn", as before.

#1820 also asked whether anything else keeps a caller out. Nothing does:
- **An idle driver holds no token:** its spin poll takes and releases it at each look, and it parks holding none.
- **`driver_wants` doesn't explain it:** that flag, which makes callers back off, is set only by a driver turn that left work, and such a turn would have handled messages.

So both failures were the race itself: a driver that hadn't run yet, then one that simply won.

**Tests, locally:**
- 40/40 alone, and 40/40 with eight copies running at once.
- With #1808's fix undone (the driver keeps the failed cell), the test still fails on its 30 s shutdown bound.
- clippy is clean.

Test-only, so no changelog fragment and no sweeps.

Every remaining packed or table resource the catalogue names now has an editable text form beside the pack, read back into the game through the existing accessors; `game/` changes only in the regenerated catalogue.

## What changed

- **Maps and tilemaps** (`frontend/maps.c`, `<pack>.maps`): every packed resource that isn't graphics is written as a grid of cells its codec names: a location's map (`lz:field-map`: header lines, each layer's map, then each tile's attributes, packed into runs again as the cartridge did), tile sets' looks (`lz:looks`), tilemap entries as `TTT:P:hvp` (`lz:tilemap:32`), byte and hex-digit grids, colors, mode 7's byte-a-pixel tiles (`lz:chunky`); scripts and place lists in hex. The row at `$F5:0000` is map 165, not the chests' table. What the packed kinds share moved to `frontend/packed.c`.
- **Text** (`frontend/text.c`, `<pack>.text`): the 4695 dialog/menu strings as they read (glyphs as letters, dictionary words in `<…>`, control codes by name in braces, anything else in hex), the battle's names in quotes, and the dictionary a word a line.
- **Records** (`frontend/records.c`, `<pack>.records`): the sprites' records, the locations' exits and chests (runs re-made as they are read), tile sets' blocks and the battles' rules.
- **Battlefield pool** (`$D0:0000`, `tiles:plane-pool`): cut into 3203 two- and three-plane tiles by the descriptors at `$CF:A000`, which cut it end to end; the 320 bytes after as `rest`.
- **Attract sequence**: its resources typed by what the scene code does with each (tiles, tilemaps, colors, mode 7 tiles and maps, the scaler's byte-a-pixel pictures).
- **Palettes in mixed rows** (#274): menus' and portraits', windows' designs', battle cursor/number/flash/member/background-set colors, world map view's and last sprite palette's, each a `palette:N` row.
- **Untyped rows**: `$F6:6CF0` is the palette animations' frames (read through `palette_frame_color`), zero from `$F6:7B80`; the attract sequence's raw colors at `$FE:4B7A`, `$FE:8D15`, `$FE:F91E`; the chests' table, the tile sets' blocks and the rules. Untyped bytes 16418 → 5998; mixed bytes 213596 → 211528 (mixed rows 33 → 38, since splitting a palette out of the middle of one leaves two).
- A decoded text's opening comment names the catalogue it was written from; a text of another catalogue is passed over with a warning and the pack's own resources play (a stale `.maps` beside a pack otherwise stopped the routes).
- `tools/sheets.py` draws a location's map assembled from its tile set, blocks and palette (`--location N`), a tilemap with a graphics resource's tiles (`--tilemap NAME --tiles NAME`), and the pool in eight greys.

## How it was measured

- ROM-free tests with made-up data: `maps_test`, `text_test`, `records_test` (new), `tiles_test` (pool), `palettes_test` (catalogue stamp); each writes and reads back every resource of its kind, serves edits, and refuses wrong text at its line. With the ROM staged, every map, text resource, table, pool and palette of the cartridge reads back as its bytes.
- Edits reach the game: clearing eight rows of BG1 in map 60 changes Crono's house at frame 6000 of `movies/new-game.ctm`; changing Crono's mother's first line shows at frame 6500.
- Lean gate `suite OK` on the merged head; clang (mingw target) builds warning-free.

## Follow-ups

- Scripts (`lz:event`, `script:*`) and place lists are hex only: their own text needs the interpreters' operand tables (#130).
- Attract resources still in hex: the 8bpp planar tiles (`attract_resource_ptrs.54`), two pictures of packed four-bit pixels (`.15`, `.46`); `.0`, `.50` and the program are read by no port.
- 38 mixed rows remain, with readers (#127); `$F5:EE02`, `$F5:F7E6`, `$E1:DDB2` and four other untyped runs have no reader found yet.
- Accessors still look resources up by address (#128).

Closes #274
Closes #275
Part of #130
Part of #273
Part of #127

author: gbirman
body:
## Why

Drive's root lists every folder the user can reach, at any depth (intended, and unchanged here), and each nested row showed its parent folder's path by sending its own `POST /projects/preview`. After a large folder upload the root fills with that tree's subfolders, so one page load sent up to one request per row (up to 100). My Files does the same for document rows: on a small 13-folder tree, the Drive root sent 4 of these requests and My Files 8.

## What

- Drive provides the folders its sidebar already loads through a new `KnownFoldersProvider` (`features/entity/context/known-folders.ts`). `ProjectBreadCrumb` builds the path from them when it knows the folder and every folder above it (`utils/folder-path.ts`), so Drive's rows send no path requests.
- A folder the host doesn't hold, or one whose ancestors it doesn't hold, falls back to the server through the shared preview loader (`previewDataLoader`), which batches the folders asked for together (up to 50 per request) instead of one request per row. The same holds on other surfaces that show folder breadcrumbs.
- The project preview type declares the `path` the REST preview already returns.

On a local stack with that tree, the Drive root and My Files show the same paths with 0 preview requests. Phone rows show no folder breadcrumbs, before or after.

## Follow-ups

- The 12 s client abort on REST Soup lists (the fallback when GraphQL Soup flags haven't loaded) is left as it is.

author: melovegupta
body:
## What
Milestone B8. 2 migrations (`20261113100001`–`02`), Worker changes, consent and analytics frontend, a real privacy page, `docs/backend/ANALYTICS.md`, pgTAP 230–240, Worker tests and a consent Playwright spec.

- **Consent:** banner (Accept all and Reject all equally prominent) and settings dialog (Essential, Preferences, Analytics, Marketing); first-party cookie plus append-only `consents` through `record_consent` (notice-version check, rate limit, anonymous id linked at sign-in). A new notice version asks again. Direct writes to `consents` are closed.
- **Browser analytics:** `posthog-js` loads only after Analytics consent (pageviews, limited autocapture, 20% sampled recordings with inputs masked and `ph-no-capture` on sensitive areas, identify by user id only, immediate opt-out and storage purge on withdrawal). Interest events: `event_viewed`, `filter_applied`, `search_performed`, `squad_viewed`.
- **Server funnel:** triggers queue events in `analytics_outbox` only for people who currently allow Analytics; the Worker's `flush-analytics` job sends them to PostHog EU after re-checking consent; `partner_link_clicked` from `/go`. Private feedback never produces an event.
- **Marketing pixels:** loader does nothing without ids and Marketing consent; CSP names Meta/Google only when ids are set.
- **Preferences:** theme and last filters saved to the browser only with Preferences consent, otherwise in memory.

## Deviations from the plan
- No audit trigger on `consents` (the table is the append-only record).
- Recording sampling is done in the app (hash of the session id) because posthog-js has no client sample-rate option. Set minimum duration to 5 s in the PostHog project.

## Tested locally
1,370 pgTAP tests, RLS check, `db:race`, advisors (no issues), lint, typecheck, 71 Worker tests, build, generated types. Playwright: new consent spec (no PostHog/Meta/Google requests before consent, after Reject all, or after withdrawing; choice linked at sign-in; no queued events for a rejecting user) passes; the other specs passed in the full run, and `auth` plus `consent` were re-run after the final fix. **Staging not verified.**

## Check by hand on staging
1. Set `POSTHOG_API_KEY` (Wrangler, staging), `VITE_POSTHOG_KEY` and `VITE_APP_ENV=staging` (Pages), and the Vault secrets for the cron job.
2. User A: Accept all, sign up, finish onboarding, join, get approved, reconfirm, check in, give tags: the funnel shows A through `feedback_given`.
3. User B: Reject all and do the same: PostHog shows nothing and the browser makes no request to `posthog.com`.
4. Withdraw A's Analytics in Cookie settings: requests stop at once.

## Open questions
- Deleting a person's PostHog data on account deletion is not automated (needs a PostHog personal API key and a Worker route).
- The privacy page needs a contact address.
- Bump the notice to `v2` at launch? It stays `v1` for now.
- `search_performed` means "a filtered event search finished" (there is no free-text search).
- A forged `u` on `/go` can only add a click for someone who already consented.

`MOCK=0` now runs against Gmail and Calendar. Tools, prompts, the gate and the store are unchanged; `tools.use_google()` swaps the adapters.

### Not verified against real Google
No test here has called a Google endpoint. I cannot complete a browser consent from the build session. Everything is tested against fakes, including a real loopback round trip on localhost. **Please run the steps below before merging** and treat the first real run as the test.

The one Standards finding (duplicated test setup), the Spec finding (crash recovery lacked the pause required by guarded resume), and four Biome import-organization failures were fixed in one isolated repair pass. New crash/reload and outstanding-comment receipt regressions cover the recovery correction; strict accounting guards remain unchanged.

### Resumo da Implementação
Implementação dos módulos `app/ficha/familias.py`, `app/ficha/relevancia.py` e `app/ficha/montagem.py`, além da rota `GET /api/documentos/{codigo}/ficha` em `app/routers/ficha.py` (Requisitos RF72 a RF76, Contrato C22 e Revisão 13/11).

1. **Famílias (`app/ficha/familias.py`):**
   - Função `derivar_familia(doc, candidatos)`: CTR e NT com valor e prazo -> `contrato`; NG e RG -> `norma`; PX, GU, FL, FM, TB, PP -> `procedimento`; NT e CT sem valor -> `nota_tecnica`.
   - Tabela `FAMILIA_BLOCOS`: mapeamento dos blocos da mesa de decisão para `contrato`, `norma`, `procedimento` e `nota_tecnica`.
   - Omissão automática de blocos vazios (sem item verificado e sem alerta comprovado).
   - Fallback gracioso: família com menos de 3 blocos preenchidos cai para lista simples sem erro.

2. **Relevância por Regra (`app/ficha/relevancia.py`):**
   - Fórmula determinística documentada em docstrings com pesos configuráveis (`PesosRelevancia`):
     - `0.35` urgência de prazo
     - `0.25` peso do valor
     - `0.20` risco (financeiro / penalidade / vedação)
     - `0.15` divergência ou versão substituída / referência ausente
     - `0.05` mudança recente / nova regra
   - `relevancia.motivo` cita o fato que mais pesou ("maior valor do contrato", "vence em 13 dias", "risco financeiro", "referência ausente", etc.).
   - Desempate 100% determinístico baseado na ordem padrão de template da família.

3. **Montagem da Ficha (`app/ficha/montagem.py`):**
   - Orquestra a montagem completa de `FichaDocumento`.
   - Extrai `bluf` extrativo (objeto, vigência e valor global) sem IA, com fontes verificadas.

## 무엇을
회계 화면 '지출 원장'에 **파일로 가져오기**를 붙였습니다. 쓰던 지출 엑셀(.xlsx)이나 CSV를 고치지 않고 올리면 원장에 들어가고, 정산·이상치 검증이 그 숫자로 돕니다.

- 파일은 브라우저 안에서만 읽습니다(서버·외부 AI로 보내지 않음).
- 흐름: 파일 선택 → 열 자동 맞추기(틀리면 사람이 고름) → 계정→관리비 항목 맞추기 → 미리보기 → 확인 후 반영
- 같은 건물·같은 양식은 열·계정 대응을 기억해 다음부터 묻지 않습니다.
- 같은 파일을 두 번 올려도 중복으로 들어가지 않습니다.
- 가져온 묶음마다 되돌리기가 있고, 승인된 정산이 있는 월은 가져오기·되돌리기를 막습니다.
- 합계·소계 줄은 건너뛰고, 못 읽은 줄은 0원으로 넣지 않고 줄 번호와 이유를 보여 줍니다.

설계: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-13-file-import-design.md` · 계획: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-13-file-import.md`

## 검증
- 테스트 57개 통과(새로 27개), 타입 검사·빌드 통과

- 로컬 화면 확인: 샘플 CSV·XLSX 올리기 → 미리보기 → 반영 → 재업로드 시 중복 0 → 정산 실행 시 가져온 금액 반영 → 되돌리기. 손상 파일·.xls·빈 파일·필수 열 없는 파일 안내 확인. 콘솔 오류 없음.
- 브랜치 전체 리뷰 1회. 지적된 4건(저장 공간 초과 시 상태 어긋남, 글자 금액이 0 처리, 못 읽은 날짜가 화면 월로 들어감, 적요 '합계…' 줄 오판)은 실패 테스트를 먼저 쓰고 고쳤습니다.

## 한계
- **실제 건물 지출 파일로는 확인하지 못했습니다.** 열 이름 후보는 가정이라 실제 파일 1~2개로 맞춰야 합니다.
- 수납 내역 가져오기(2단계)는 이번 범위가 아닙니다.

`npm audit`의 기존 경고 2건(jspdf·dompurify)은 이번 변경과 무관합니다.

author: patrick-ogrady
body:
`Output::revealed` lists a player once enough of the selected dealers reveal its dealing. It counts those reveals and nothing else, so it is not a complete list of exposed shares. A Byzantine player can reveal its own share outside the protocol, and an adversary that knew an honest player's share before a reshare may use it with the round's reveals to rebuild new shares that are not listed. This PR says so in the method's docs, points to the module's Share Reveals section, and adds the reshare case to that section.

A reshare dealer's polynomial has its previous share as the constant term. With `n = 3f + 1` players the degree is `2f`, so that share, the `f` dealings held by Byzantine players, and `f` reveals determine the whole polynomial. With `3f + 2` or `3f + 3` players the degree is higher, and those points no longer suffice.

```text
n = 4 and f = 1, so rows have degree 2 and listing takes reveals from 2 of the 3 dealers

            previous           dealing to player
              share        A       B       C       D
            +-------+  +-------+-------+-------+-------+
dealer A    |   L   |  |   *   |   R   |   X   |   *   |  <- L, R and X fix this row
            +-------+  +-------+-------+-------+-------+
dealer B    |   .   |  |   .   |   .   |   X   |   R   |
            +-------+  +-------+-------+-------+-------+
dealer C    |   X   |  |   X   |   X   |   X   |   X   |  <- Byzantine
            +-------+  +-------+-------+-------+-------+
                                                   |
                                                   v
                        D's new share combines *, R and X, which are all known
                        only R is a reveal and listing needs 2, so D is not listed

L leaked earlier   R revealed in a log   X known to Byzantine C   * derived   . private
```

The shared secret is unaffected. An honest dealer exposes at most `2f` evaluations of its polynomial, and recovering its previous share takes at least `2f + 1`.

body:
## どの画面の何をどう直したか

- **すとんブロック（ルームのあそぶ画面・じゃまのある回）**: 自分で相手を選んでいないときのじゃまの送る相手を、「並びのつぎの人」から「この回で最後にじゃまを送ってきた人」に変えた。まだだれからも来ていない・その人が「ここまで」になったときは、これまでどおり並びのつぎ。
  - 送ってきた人は受けとったじゃまの `from` から決め、`boards/{自分}/back` に来るじゃまの数と同じ1回の update で書く（置くたびの盤にも入れる）。ほかの人の画面の「ねらってる」の印・ねらわれた人数（＋火力）も同じに数える。読み込み直しても戻る
  - 人を押して選ぶ・「ねらってきた人みんなに送る」はそのまま。もう一度押すと、このはじめの送り方にもどる
  - 待合室の説明・あそびかた・説明スライドの「つぎの人へ」の言い方を合わせた
- **いろつなぎ（対戦）**: 送る相手を同じ決まりにした（送る相手を押して選ぶしくみは足していない）。`back` を盤に書き、読み込み直しても戻る。待合室の説明・あそびかた・説明スライドも合わせた
- `?v=` を上げた（すとん 20261113a・いろつなぎ 20261113e）。`apps/updates.json` に2行（`from: feedback`）

## 確認したこと

- `bash scripts/lint.sh` エラー0・警告0
- しくみのテスト: すとん 41・いろつなぎ 17 合格
- E2E（隔離したエミュレーター）
  - すとん 新しい e2e11（23項目）: はじめは並びのつぎ・届くと送ってきた人に「送る」・back を書く・ほかの人の画面の「ねらってる」も同じ・読み込み直しても戻る・押して選ぶ／もう一度でもどる・送ってきた人に届き並びのつぎには届かない・その人がここまでなら並びのつぎ
  - すとん e2e1〜e2e10 すべて合格。e2e8 の F7・F9 は「＋4段」→「＋5段」に直した（1回目で送られた はる の相手が送ってきた あおい になり、メンターと2人にねらわれるので、もとからある「2人にねらわれて＋1」が付く。main のままなら＋4段で通ることを確かめた）

author: hrygo
body:
## 背景

#656/#641 之后，同一类风险还剩两片。本 PR 收口其中优先级最高的两组：

- `tests/unit/controller/test_warmup_deadline.py`：`partial_progress`（0.4 s）、`attempts_share`（0.35 s）两条把「真实 loopback POST 必须挤进短预算」当判据；同一文件 7 条在 macOS 上因绑定 `127.0.0.2` 直接红（`[Errno 49]`）。
- `tests/unit/backend/test_tts_durable_intent.py::test_recovery_budget_bounds_original_query_and_result_reads`：0.03 s 预算配 `elapsed < 0.5`，余量最小。

只改 `tests/`，未动产品代码。

## 逐条：原判据 → 为什么依赖调度 → 新判据

| 用例 | 原判据 | 依赖调度之处 | 新判据 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `warmup::test_partial_progress_cannot_extend_the_total_warmup_deadline`（3 参数） | 0.4 s 内必须发出唯一 POST + `not completed` | POST 建立（connect+发送+对端读取）必须挤进 0.4 s；负载下一抖动就 `len(requests)==0` | 对端事件：唯一 POST 收到、对端**观察到客户端主动断开**（`aborted`，EOF 检测）、对端响应从未完成（`completed` 保持未置位）；预算 1.0 s，对端停顿 6 s。判据全部来自对端与请求序列 |
| `warmup::test_attempts_share_one_deadline_and_exhaustion_sends_nothing_more` | 0.35 s 预算 + `elapsed < 0.35*2` | `elapsed` 是机器速度，不是被测语义；预算到期靠真实时间推进 | 注入模块时钟：锚点 1.0 s、第二条 observation 复用同一锚点（断言 `_warmup_deadlines` 不变）、对端观察到 hangup；把时钟推过锚点后 3 次 observation 不再发 POST（`len(requests)==2`） |
| `warmup::test_a_stalled_response_is_non_ready_and_never_retried_at_another_address` | 0.3 s 内必须发出 POST | 同上 | 1.0 s 预算 + 第二个地址上真实存活的 `::1` 对端证明「没有重发」（`not second_requests`），不再是靠绑定失败制造「不可达」 |
| `warmup::test_an_intent_resumed_in_the_same_process_spends_the_remaining_budget` | 假时钟 0.3/0.4，**只剩 0.1 s 真实预算**完成第二次 POST | 0.1 s 必须完成真实 HTTP；实测负载下 POST 建立 p99 200 ms、max 216 ms，比预算还大 | 假时钟锚点 5.0 s、剩 1.0 s；判据是「第二次 `_run_warmup` 拿到的 deadline 仍是原锚点 5.0 s 而不是新窗口」（`deadlines == [5.0, 5.0]`）与 `_only_progress().deadline` |
| `warmup::test_a_new_intent_after_a_restart_anchors_its_own_budget` | 0.4 s 真实预算内一次 POST | 同上 | 假时钟锚点 5.0 s（判据是锚点值），POST 余量随之放大 |
| `warmup::test_an_exhausted_warmup_reports_a_reason_and_keeps_the_peak_hold` / `test_a_restart_keeps_the_persisted_deadline_reason` | 0.3 s 内必须发出 POST | 同上（负载下实测翻面 1 次） | 预算 1.0 s；判据仍是错误码/持有峰值/请求序列，未改语义 |
| `tts::test_recovery_budget_bounds_original_query_and_result_reads`（3 阶段） | 0.03 s 预算 + `elapsed < 0.5` | `elapsed` 含桥接派发与线程调度；对 query/receipt 阶段 0.2 s 慢操作本身 < 0.5，旧断言几乎抓不到「没被切断」 | 对端操作事件：`query`/`receipt` 的**完成事件**从未置位（定时器按 deadline 顺序先触发取消，与机器快慢无关）；`object` 的**阻塞读从未返回**（只由测试 finally 释放）。三阶段都不再测量返回耗时 |

### macOS 地址族

双容器地址场景（「失败后不得在下一个容器地址重发」+「发唯一 POST 前先选可达地址」+「stall 不换地址」）原本用 `127.0.0.2`。macOS 只把 `127.0.0.1` 挂到 lo0，绑定是 `[Errno 49]`；更糟的是**连接** `127.0.0.2` 不是立即拒绝而是黑洞（实测 0.3 s 超时），所以 `test_choose_a_reachable_address…` 也红。

改为双栈 loopback：`127.0.0.1` + `::1`（`AF_INET6` 子类服务器）。两个字面地址在 macOS 与 Linux 上都是恒存在的 loopback，且都能真实 bind/connect；「不可达的第一个地址」改成 `::1` 上无人监听 → `ECONNREFUSED`（两平台均 ~0.1 ms 立即返回），不再依赖 127.0.0.0/8 是否整段本地。

**v6 不可用时**：模块级 `requires_ipv6_loopback` 能力探测（`socket.has_ipv6` + 对 `::1` 试 bind），这三条会以明确 reason 跳过，避免把「主机禁用 IPv6」伪装成时序红。两个目标环境（macOS 开发机、Linux CI）都不触发：macOS `32 passed`、Linux 容器 `32 passed`，均 **0 skipped**。

## 压力验证（同命令、同负载、各 3 轮）

`HOGS=80` 忙循环 + 32 个并发 pytest（约 6 倍 oversubscription，M5 Max/18 核，无 QoS 降级）。目标集含对照文件 `tests/unit/controller/test_docker_runtime.py`（32 条，无墙钟断言）：

```
before(035e3c16) round 1: 32/32 runs failed (timing 2, address-family 30)
before(035e3c16) round 2: 32/32 runs failed (timing 1, address-family 31)
before(035e3c16) round 3: 32/32 runs failed (timing 4, address-family 28)
before(035e3c16) TOTAL: 96/96 runs failed (timing 7, address-family 89)

after(final)     round 1: 0/32 runs failed
after(final)     round 2: 0/32 runs failed
after(final)     round 3: 0/32 runs failed
after(final)     TOTAL: 0/96 runs failed
```

对照文件在所有 192 次运行中 **0 失败**（失败 id 全部落在预热文件，从未出现 `test_docker_runtime.py`）——负载不是钝器。

纯负载暴露的真实翻面（改前）：`test_an_intent_resumed_in_the_same_process_spends_the_remaining_budget` 6 次、`test_an_exhausted_warmup_reports_a_reason_and_keeps_the_peak_hold` 1 次。两者都不在本卡原始清单里，但同文件、同类、余量更小（0.1 s / 0.3 s），已按同一模式一并收口。

## 注入（如实标注：注入而非纯负载）

### 1) 连接延迟注入（同机制：慢容器网络）

在 runtime 的地址探测前注入固定延迟，看「唯一 POST 还能不能发出」：

| 注入 connect 延迟 | 0 / 0.1 / 0.2 / 0.3 / 0.35 / 0.4 / 0.5 / 0.7 / 0.9 / 0.95 / 1.0 / 1.1 s |
| --- | --- |
| before（macOS，`partial_progress`） | 绿 ≤0.35，0.40 s 起 3/3 红 |
| after（macOS，`partial_progress`） | 绿 ≤0.95，1.00 s 起 3/3 红 |
| before（Linux 容器，`partial_progress`+`a_stalled_response`） | 绿 ≤0.20，0.30 s 起 3/3 红 |
| after（Linux 容器，同上） | 绿 ≤0.95，1.00 s 起 3/3 红 |

### 2) 真实 POST 建立耗时（为什么 1.0 s 是够的）

同一产品路径、budget 30 s、对端即时应答，测 connect+POST+完整响应：

```
idle     n=20  median 3.2 ms  max 19.2 ms
loaded   n=160 median 6.5 ms  p99 200.6 ms  max 215.8 ms
```

1.0 s 预算 = 最坏观测的 **4.6×**；0.3–0.4 s 的旧预算是 1.4–1.9×，这正是那批用例会翻面的量级。同时 1.0 s 仍只有对端停顿（6 s）的 1/6，两侧余量都在 4.6×/6× 量级（几何均值最优解 ≈1.15 s，取 1.0 s 兼顾运行时长）。

## 反例（先红后绿，全部实跑，临时用例已删除，未入库）

```
1) 旧墙钟判据 elapsed < 0.35*2 + 注入 0.5 s 调度延迟
   assert 0.8631282080023084 < (0.35 * 2)        ← 红（行为本身正确）
   同注入、新判据（对端事件+锚点）                ← 绿
2) 旧判据 elapsed < 0.5 + 注入 0.55 s 派发延迟
   assert 0.5600143330084393 < 0.5               ← 红（预算已被遵守）
   同注入、新判据（3 阶段完成事件）               ← 绿
3) 去掉「到期即停」（预算放大到读不被切断）
   assert False = wait(1)   # 对端从未看到 hangup ← 红；且 completed 置位
4) 去掉「只发一次/不续期」（把花掉的锚点续期）
   assert 4 == 1  # 4 次 POST                      ← 红
```

## 测试与门禁

```
macOS  pytest tests/unit/controller/test_warmup_deadline.py
       before: 7 failed, 25 passed        （全部 [Errno 49] 绑定 127.0.0.2）
       after : 32 passed, 0 skipped       （不是靠 skip；7 条真实通过）
macOS  pytest tests/unit -q
       before: 7 failed, 6786 passed, 3 skipped
       after : 0 failed, 6793 passed, 3 skipped
Linux  pytest tests/unit -q（python:3.14 容器，8 天前 ci 镜像同款）
       before: 6795 passed, 1 skipped
       after : 6795 passed, 1 skipped
Linux  pytest tests/unit/controller/test_warmup_deadline.py → 32 passed, 0 skipped
```

`ruff check .`、`ruff format --check .`、`mypy`（1425 files）、`mypy --platform linux`（1425 files）、`lint-imports`（9 kept, 0 broken）全部通过。

## 仍依赖真实墙钟的用例与理由

- `partial_progress`、`a_stalled_response`、两条 `…deadline_reason`、`an_intent_resumed…`：被测语义本身就是「一个受总预算约束的动作必须在预算内发出它唯一的 POST」，墙体时钟无法完全消除；已把判据移出墙钟，只保留「预算 > POST 建立」这一侧，并用上表给出 4.6× 余量与 6× 切断余量。
- `test_recovery_budget_bounds_original_query_and_result_reads`：`0.03 s` 预算本身是墙钟（asyncio timer），但取消与慢操作的先后由 timer 到期顺序决定，不随负载改变；断言只看「慢操作是否完成」，不再看返回耗时。
- 本卡未处理的其他文件（前一片清单里的低风险项）保持原样。

## CI 实跑结论（run 43368965956）

- **Python: tests, coverage and package build — pass（7m7s）**：Linux 全量 `pytest -q` 通过
  （`5554 passed … 146 subtests`，含本次改动的 `test_warmup_deadline.py` 与
  `test_tts_durable_intent.py`，日志里可见 `test_partial_progress…`、`test_attempts_share…`
  在慢用例清单中正常通过）。这是 Linux 侧 `::1` 方案的 CI 证据。
- `Web: lint…`、`Compose`、`Deploy`、`Docs`、`Scope routing` 均 pass。
- **Python: lint, types and contract compatibility — fail，唯一原因是 `ruff format --check .`
  命中两份 docs 的既有漂移**（不是本 PR 的文件）：
  `docs/reviews/2026-11-13-ci-acceptance-gate.md:399`、
  `docs/reviews/2026-11-13-reference-acceptance-rework.md:399`。
  该红在 `origin/main` 自身即存在：同一 commit `0e511118` 的 CI run 43367391496
  在同一个 job、同样两条路径上失败；本 PR 相对 base 只改两个 `tests/` 文件。
  未在本 PR 顺手改 docs（本卡边界：只改 `tests/`）；开放中的 #663 正触及这两份文件。
- `Gate: Python execution and static checks` 随之失败（其输入 `CONTRACTS_RESULT=failure`），
  测试本体 `Python execution=success`。

## 未验证项

- 上述 lint 红随 main 的两份 docs 修复而消失；本 PR 未改它们，无法在本分支转绿。
- 未在 Windows 上验证（仓库 CI 不含 Windows，`::1`/`AF_INET6` 方案按 POSIX 双栈设计）。
- 本机是 macOS（18 核 M5 Max）；「6 倍 oversubscription」压测的绝对数值不构成 CI 容量结论，
  只用于改前/改后同条件对照。

author: jasperf
body:
## Purpose

`wp-frontend-builder` tells the agent to run `node <toolbox>/skills/html-page-review/measure.mjs …`, and `html-page-review` writes `/ABS/SKILL/DIR/…`. Nothing said where that folder is. In the bakery demo round 6d, the agent searched for the script with `find /Users/<you>/code /Users/<you> -maxdepth 4 -name measure.mjs`. That was slow, and it asked for approval because the home folder is outside the granted folders.

## Change

- `agents/wp-frontend-builder.toml` plus the regenerated `-subagent` copy: `<toolbox>` and `/ABS/SKILL/DIR` mean the folder Vibe loads skills from.
  - Read it from `skill_paths` in `~/.vibe/config.toml` (`grep -n -A3 skill_paths ~/.vibe/config.toml`) and write it out as an absolute path.
  - Never search the home folder with `find`.
- `skills/html-page-review/SKILL.md` (1.5.0 → 1.5.1): the same, at the top of step 1.
- `docs/install.md`: a `vibe-path:exact:` grant for `~/.vibe/config.toml` in the shell and `read_file` allowlists. The agent already reads this file for `supports_images`, and now also for `skill_paths`; the grant covers that file only.
- `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Checked

- Both agent TOML files parse.
- `grep -n -A3 skill_paths ~/.vibe/config.toml` returns the `~/code/wp-vibe-toolbox/skills` entry on the maintainer's machine.

After merging:
- run `rsync -a ~/code/wp-vibe-toolbox/agents/ ~/.vibe/agents/`;
- add `"vibe-path:exact:/Users/<you>/.vibe/config.toml"` to `[tools.bash]` and `[tools.read_file]`.

- [x] In merge queue / [Merged](https://app.ravion.com/org/cky23guyu0004xjjemof84k5j/merge-queues?queue=mq_3KphfwHjQ9gjpSwkHxdx9Zkql8V) - [ ] Prioritize ## Summary EKS add-ons 1.4.0 makes Mimir's distributors compress what they send to ingesters (`ingester_client.grpc_client_config.grpc_compression: snappy`). This is now a default for every cluster that runs Mimir. A distributor decompresses each remote write, then sends the raw protobuf to all three ingesters, and Mimir doesn't compress that stream unless told to. On a cluster spread across zones, most of the stream crosses zones and is billed as inter-zone data transfer. It's also several times larger than the writes the distributors received. Snappy brings it back to about the compressed size. - **Rollout:** every Mimir component is the same binary and decodes snappy, so ingesters that haven't restarted yet still accept compressed pushes. - **HA:** replication factor, ingester count and zone spread are unchanged. - **Cost:** a little extra CPU on distributors and ingesters. ## Testing - `tofu -chdir=compute/eks/addons test`: 292 passed. A new assert in `mimir_runs_classic_on_s3_with_three_copies` failed before the change and passes after it. - `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s compute/eks/addons/tests -p 'test_mimir_chart_placement.py'`: OK. - `tofu fmt -check -recursive compute/eks/addons`: OK. - `cli.js guardrails`, `cli.js compile` and `cli.js readme --check`: OK (README table updated to v1.4.0).

Confidence Score: 5/5

This PR appears safe to merge; no actionable issues were found.

Summary

Sets `ingester_client.grpc_client_config.grpc_compression` to `snappy` for Mimir’s distributor-to-ingester traffic. - Mimir distributors compress writes to ingesters with Snappy. ## Summary
- The OCIRepositories for oauth2-proxy, reloader and victoria-logs now `verify` each chart's keyless cosign signature. Each one accepts only a certificate that GitHub Actions issued to that project's own repo:
  - oauth2-proxy/manifests
  - stakater/Reloader
  - VictoriaMetrics/helm-charts

## Summary

This is the current-mainline replacement for the older draft PR #137. That branch is 444 commits behind current `main`, has a dirty merge state, and predates the current CDN origin handlers and newer Backend runtime. This branch starts from current `main` and ports only the required Data Centre media integration while preserving current Federation, Fresh API, CDN assertion and social code.

## Included

- Dedicated Data Centre client and policy-only upload intent factory.
- Bounded upload gateway that claims the intent, spools exact-size bytes, computes SHA-256 server-side, creates exactly one Data Centre upload grant, and uploads with redirects disabled and a bounded timeout.
- Persisted server-computed checksum and completion that waits for Data Centre primary verification plus protected replica state before marking the Backend asset ready.
- Data Centre-backed private downloads, media listing, deletion, quarantine and janitor cleanup.
- CDN origin integration for both public and private assets. Public origin requests require the CDN service credential and a canonical ready/public Backend asset row; private requests additionally require a valid viewer-bound assertion.
- Method-correct GET and HEAD origin signing, preserving range and conditional headers.
- Appwrite owner ID grammar parity (letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens).
- Route-specific 40-minute upload socket deadline, while ordinary API requests retain their shorter timeouts.
- `FRESH_MEDIA_ENABLED=false` by default. Data Centre URL/token are passed through the Backend Compose service, but B2/R2 credentials remain exclusively in Data Centre.

## Safety gates

Do not enable fresh media until live B2/R2 staging PUT, independent SHA-256 read-back, replica recovery, CDN public/private cache isolation, and Flutter upload/playback integration tests pass. CI uses no real provider credentials and is not evidence of live storage writes.

## Validation

CI will run on this branch against the current mainline. The older PR #137 is retained for reference and must not be merged; this PR supersedes its Data Centre integration changes.
