body:
## Problema
Del día 30 al 34 se retuvieron 10 veces las creencias de Uxío 2 (lado B), marcadas como `politica_real`. El texto era «…compartir es la mejor previsión que **podemos** tener…». En `sim/moderacion.py`, «podemos» está en la lista de partidos y se compara como palabra suelta. Lo mismo pasaría con «sumar», «franco», «ciudadanos», «pp», «vox» o «sánchez». Además, cada caso se registraba dos veces al día porque la ficha se publica más de una vez.

## Cambios
- `sim/moderacion.py`
  - Esas 7 palabras pasan a la lista `AMBIGUAS_POLITICA`. Solo cuentan como política real en estos casos:
    - se escriben todo en mayúsculas (PP, VOX);
    - llevan mayúscula en mitad de una frase (como nombre propio);
    - van junto a vocabulario político (partido, votar, elecciones, gobierno, presidente, izquierda, derecha, dictadura…).
  - Los nombres que no se confunden con nada (psoe, feijoo, marx, capitalismo…) siguen bloqueándose siempre.
  - Nuevo parámetro `revisar(texto, estricto=True)` para las preguntas del público, que siguen bloqueando como antes.
  - `registrar` guarda cada texto de un mismo habitante y campo una sola vez.
- `entrevistas.py` y `sim/narrador.py`: las preguntas del público usan `estricto=True`.

## Pruebas
- 14 frases de prueba se moderan como se esperaba, incluida la de Uxío 2, que ya no se bloquea. «Yo votaría a Podemos», «El PP y el PSOE…» y «Pedro Sánchez y el gobierno» se siguen bloqueando. Una frase con «Sumar» en mayúscula después de «;» pasa, porque se toma como inicio de frase.
- Registro: el mismo texto repetido en tres días queda en una sola fila.
- `python ejecutar.py --dias 3` funciona y todo compila.

`bash /srv/miovsnuestro/actualizar.sh` (como root). No toca `datos/` ni `.env`.

author: fpippi
body:
Implements roadmap **v1.0 — Reports**. NetPulse can now produce a printable report to send to your ISP and export all raw data as CSV. Tagged versions also ship self-contained binaries for Windows and Linux.

## What's new

- **Report page** (`/report`, linked from the header). You pick a period (the last 30 days by default) and, optionally, the download and upload speeds in your contract. The page then builds a connection quality report with these sections:
  - **Summary**: Internet outages, total Internet downtime, and average download and upload speed as a share of the contract.
  - **Latency, loss and availability** for each target.
  - **Outages**, each with its likely cause.
  - **Speed tests**, including how many measured less than half the contracted speed.
  - **How this was measured**: interval, timeout, outage threshold and method.
- **Print / Save as PDF**: a print stylesheet hides the dashboard and prints only the report, black on white, so the browser's "Save as PDF" gives a clean document.
- **Outage causes**, judged by what else was down at the same time:
  - *Local network*: the router didn't answer either.
  - *Internet (ISP)*: the router answered but every public host was down.
  - *Single host*: only that host was down.
  - *Unknown*: the gateway isn't monitored.

  Only Internet outages count toward the Internet downtime. Overlapping outages of different hosts count once.
- **CSV export** of ping samples, outages (with cause) and speed tests, linked from the report page. The files use RFC 4180, a `.` decimal separator and ISO 8601 UTC timestamps.
- **API**: `GET /api/report` (the report as JSON), plus `GET /api/export/samples.csv`, `/api/export/outages.csv` and `/api/export/speedtests.csv`. Each takes `days` or `from`/`to` dates.
- **Release binaries**: pushing a `v*` tag runs the new `Release` workflow. It tests the code, publishes single-file, self-contained builds for `win-x64`, `linux-x64` and `linux-arm64`, and attaches them to a GitHub release together with `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

## Design

- The logic lives in `NetPulse.Core` and has no dependencies:
  - `Reports/IspReportBuilder` assembles the report from data that is already aggregated.
  - `Reports/ReportPeriod` resolves `days` or inclusive local dates, and never ends in the future.
  - `Reports/Csv` and `CsvExport` write the files.
  - `Outages/OutageClassifier` finds the outage causes.
  - `Stats/LatencyAccumulator` gives the same result as `LatencyStats.From`, one sample at a time.
- Reports over long periods use little memory. The new `ISampleStore.StreamAsync` reads samples from SQLite as an `IAsyncEnumerable`. `ReportService` feeds them into one accumulator per target, and the samples CSV is written straight to the response.
- The release workflow uses only `actions/*` and the `gh` CLI. Pull requests that change the workflow build the archives without releasing, so this PR's checks also exercise it.

## Tests

37 new NUnit tests (256 in total). They cover:
- CSV escaping and formatting, including under `it-IT` culture;
- the three CSV exports;
- `LatencyAccumulator` against `LatencyStats.From`;
- every outage-cause rule;
- report building: target order, merged Internet downtime, and the comparison with contracted speeds;
- period parsing: defaults, clamping, local days, rejected ranges.

## Notes

- I ran the report and the CSV downloads end to end against a local instance, including printing the report to PDF with Chromium.
- I published `linux-x64` and `linux-arm64` locally. The `linux-x64` binary runs and serves the dashboard.
- The `win-x64` build is only checked by this PR's Release workflow run.
- To release v1.0 after merging to `main`: `git tag v1.0.0 && git push origin v1.0.0`.
- The binary reads `appsettings.json` and creates `data/` in the current directory, so it should be started from its own folder. The README says so.

author: ogoldberg
body:
EXP.4 (docs/ROADMAP.md): Web MIDI in the studio.

## What

- New `midi.js` (pure, Node-tested): support check, port lists, part channels (melody on the chosen channel, harmony on the next one skipping 10, drums on 10), reading note on/off and sustain-pedal messages, a key recorder that turns a take into melody notes timed from the end of the count-in, the song as timed MIDI messages with the MIDI file's programs and drum keys (daw.js), silencing a device, and a lookahead sender.
- Studio: a **MIDI keyboard** track, shown only where `navigator.requestMIDIAccess` exists (hidden in Safari and the Mac app's WKWebView). Devices are requested only when **Connect MIDI** is pressed, so the browser's permission prompt never appears unasked.
  - Keys sound as they are played on the melody instrument (velocity, sustain pedal), or go through to the chosen MIDI output on the melody channel.
  - **Record from keyboard**: one bar of count-in with a click at the project tempo, then the song plays; Stop adds the take to the melody as one undoable edit ("Record from MIDI keyboard"). The take's zero is mapped from the audio clock to the MIDI clock and moved by the output latency.
  - **Play to** a MIDI output: Play sends melody, harmony and drums there (band and voice-as-instrument audio still play here), scheduled 200 ms ahead from a 25 ms timer so Stop leaves nothing queued in the browser; Stop sends All Sound Off / All Notes Off / pedal up on every channel used.
- `playback()` takes `{lead, click}` and returns the audio time of the song's zero; `stop()` ends a take, the timer and the live keys.
- `/midi.js` route, precached in `sw.js` (CACHE `tandem-v35`), CI runs `tests/midi.test.mjs`.
- Docs: ROADMAP (EXP.4 done, real-device QA open), TESTING (EXP.4 tests and a manual matrix entry), ARCHITECTURE, CLAUDE.md.

## Tests

- `node --test tests/midi.test.mjs`: 15 tests.
- `e2e/test_midi.py` (Chromium, mocked `MIDIAccess` with one input and one output that keeps what it is sent): hidden without Web MIDI; no device request before Connect; a take after the count-in lands in the melody at the played times as one undoable edit, a key let go during the count-in is not kept; an empty take changes nothing; Play sends programs and the three parts on their channels timed ahead in order and Stop silences them and sends nothing more; keys go through to the output, or sound here without one.
- Full suites locally: `python -m pytest -q`, `node --test tests/*.test.mjs`, `python -m pytest e2e -q`.

## Not verified

Recording from a real keyboard and playing to a real synth are manual QA for the operator (docs/TESTING.md, manual matrix).

## Skip note

Earlier roadmap items skipped at claim: they are HUMAN-only, already done (stale entries), need the operator's paid AI key (AI.2, AI.5), or are parked by ADR-012 (STORE.2, 2b, 2c).

author: fatihmuradovich
body:
## What changed

Most of Phase 2 of the [roadmap](ROADMAP.md): people can move their reading list in, take it out, and delete their account.

- **Import** (Settings → Import): Pocket CSV and HTML exports, Instapaper CSV, and browser bookmark files (Chrome, Firefox, Safari). The file is parsed in the browser, a preview shows counts ("9 articles · 7 unread · 2 archived · 1 tag"), then items are saved in batches of 200 with a progress bar. Tags, read/archive status and original saved dates carry over; links already in the library are skipped.
- **Fetch the article text**: imported articles arrive as links; the reader now offers a button to fetch and extract the text.
- **Export** (Settings → Export): the whole library with tags, highlights and notes as **Markdown**, **JSON**, or a **Pocket-compatible CSV**.
- **Settings page**: import, export, sign out, delete account. The header's "Sign out" is replaced by "Settings".
- **Delete account**: type "delete my account" to confirm; removes the account and all its data.
- **Privacy page** (`/privacy`): what the app and the extension store, where, and how to export or delete. Linked from the landing page and Settings. The Chrome Web Store requires one.

## Notes for review

- **Migration** `20261113120000_delete_account.sql`: a `security definer` function `delete_my_account()` that deletes `auth.users` where `id = auth.uid()`; existing `on delete cascade` foreign keys remove the user's data. `execute` is revoked from `public`/`anon` and granted only to `authenticated`. **Already run on production**; an anonymous call returns `permission denied`.
- **Parsing in the browser** keeps large files off the server; the Server Action re-validates every field (URL rules, lengths, status, dates, tag names) and limits batches to 200 so requests stay under the 1 MB Server Action limit.
- **Duplicate detection** (found while testing): re-importing an export added one article twice. Its stored link had a `gclid` saved before tracking-parameter stripping existed, so the cleaned link no longer matched. Now: more tracking parameters are stripped (`gad_*`, `gbraid`, `wbraid`, `msclkid`, `_ga`, `_gl`, …), and both import and save compare against existing links normalized with today's rules (save looks up candidates by origin + path).
- **Export CSV** neutralizes cells starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@` (CSV injection). Export pages through results 1,000 rows at a time (PostgREST limit).
- **Open question before the Web Store**: the privacy page's contact link points to this repo's GitHub issues, which only work if the repo is public.

## Testing

- **Parser**: 23 unit tests across Pocket CSV/HTML, Instapaper and bookmarks: quoted commas, `""` escapes, newlines in fields, BOM/CRLF, private `instapaper-private://` links, `javascript:` bookmarks, duplicates, implausible dates.
- **Export**: 10 tests, including a round trip (export CSV → import it back with the same parser) and CSV injection.
- **URL cleanup**: Google Ads, Microsoft and analytics parameters stripped; meaningful ones (`id`, `page`, `ref`, `source`) kept. Duplicate check: an old link stored with `gclid` is recognized when saved again; a different path on the same site is not.
- **Database** on a local Postgres 16 with all three migrations: re-importing the same rows inserts nothing (`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`); saved dates kept; duplicate tag links ignored; `anon` can't call `delete_my_account`; user A deleting their account removes all of A's rows and leaves user B's untouched.
- **Manual with a real account**: exported Markdown and CSV, re-imported the CSV → "0 articles added, 9 were already in your library".
- `npm run lint`, `tsc --noEmit` and `next build` pass.

author: retain-ap
body:
Uploading file B while file A was importing could lose B's completed review when A's response arrived. A slow initial appointment request could also replace a newer appointment list and hide a just-saved booking. Both orderings were reproduced with deferred responses before the fix.

The importer now allows one operation to own its controls and completion state. File selection/drop, Cancel, mapping and row edits wait for the in-flight operation, failed operations release the lock, and changing workspace resets the private review. Late results cannot update a replacement importer or restart its history reads. Confirmed writes still finish on the server and notify their original workspace through a scoped `leads:changed` event; the dashboard ignores notifications for another workspace while retaining existing unscoped-event behavior. No automatic retry or claim of import cancellation was added.

Editing import options also invalidates the previous review immediately. A failed recount shows unavailable counts and an explicit Retry review button; Import stays disabled until the current options have a successful review. The commit handler checks the accepted review generation too. Old retry responses cannot restore an outdated mapping or cross into another workspace. Retry review only repeats the read-only recount, never an import write.

Appointment reads now publish only the latest request for the active dashboard lifetime. Workspace changes clear the previous workspace's appointments, current lookup failures preserve the last confirmed list, and a late Quick Add completion cannot refresh or alert a replacement workspace. Existing contact follow-up, consent, lead-save conflict and provider permission behavior is unchanged.

Validation on official Node 24.19.0:
- 40 frontend suites / 285 tests passed, including 19 new actual-component deferred-response regressions covering import lock/failure, replacement-workspace preview success/failure, confirmed-write handoff, appointment request ordering/failure, workspace changes and unmount invalidation. Recount coverage includes mapping/duplicate-option failure, explicit retry with current inputs, stale retry success/failure and replacement-workspace success/failure.
- Full frontend ESLint passed with zero warnings; production build and all 14 prerendered routes passed.
- Actual `npm audit --omit=dev --json` returned zero production vulnerabilities. No dependency or lockfile changes.
- `git diff --check` passed. Tests used fictional data and mocked provider requests; no live contacts, messages or appointments were changed.

Scope: `ImportContacts.jsx`, `CrmDashboard.jsx` and two new regression files only. No merge, production deployment, provider send, credential or spending change. Local receipts are in `outputs/retain-import-races-20261113` in the shared Codex workspace.

author: enderwolf50
body:
Refs #676：計畫的第 3 個 PR，`agent/actions.py` 檔內整理：兩個以上頁面段共用的 24 個名稱收成一區，`Shop.on_map` 改成模組層的 `on_map`；之後的：第 4–11 個 PR（各頁面檔搬出去，第 4 個是 `lux_actions.py`）。

## 為什麼

之後每個頁面段搬成自己的檔，只 `from actions import …`。兩個以上頁面段共用的名稱得留在 `actions.py`，不然頁面檔要互相 import，開局段和商店段還會循環（#676「風險」2）。

- `on_map` 是真正擋住拆分的那個：它是 `Shop` 的 staticmethod，地圖段的 `forfeit` 經 `Shop.on_map` 讀到 `Shop`，商店段就搬不走（下面「證據」的「之前」）。改成模組層的函式後，`forfeit` 不再讀 `Shop`。
- 另外 24 個名稱：#689 的 `split_actions.py` 只搬 `MODULES` 表的名稱，`STAY` 表的名稱原地不動，所以它們留在原處也切得開。收成一區是為了讓留下的共用名稱有一個標題，說明它們為什麼不搬進頁面檔，而不是散在各段被搬走後的空隙裡。

## 摘要

只動 `agent/actions.py`。21 個敘述（24 個名稱）原封不動搬到 `finish` 之後、開局段 `PlanRun` 之前，也就是核心段的結尾：八個頁面檔搬走後，這區就是 `actions.py` 的最後一段。區內先放多處共用的常數，再放函式；只有一個函式讀的常數放在那個函式正上方，跟原本一樣。每組都照原本在檔裡的順序。

```diff
 def finish(context, reason): ...
+# Read by the helpers above or by two or more page sections (#676): ...
+BACK_KEY                                                      # 地圖段（back() 在讀）
+GET_TITLE, GET_CONFIRM  GET_NAME  GIFTS  GIFT_NAMES  GIFT_IDS # 商店段
+DIALOG_TEXT  DIALOG_CANCEL, DIALOG_CONFIRM                    # 結算段
+def node_results                                              # 組裝段
+def run_packs  def columns                                    # 開局段
+FEATURE_MATCH  FEATURE_PAD, FEATURE_ALIGN  def seen          # 地圖段（on_page、tap_then 在讀）
+def saturation                                                # Formation 段
+def data                                                      # 事件段
+def owned_now  def leave_shop  def want_of                    # 商店段
+WHITE_GOSSYPIUM  def avoided_gifts                            # 商店段
+def on_map                                                    # 原本是 Shop.on_map
 @AgentServer.custom_action("PlanRun")
 class PlanRun(CustomAction): ...
```

`on_map` 的 4 個呼叫點：`forfeit` 一處、`Shop.run` 兩處、`Shop.way_out` 一處，`Shop.on_map(` 改成 `on_map(`。`rg on_map` 確認 tests 和 tools 沒有人用 `Shop.on_map`，所以測試不用改（計畫第 3 列的「測試改動 0」）。

## 取捨

- **區塊放的位置**：放在核心段結尾（`finish` 之後），不放在讀畫面工具那段（`number` 之後）。核心段在 `finish` 結束，後面全是頁面段，所以放這裡不會插進任何一段中間；拆完以後它是 `actions.py` 的尾巴。
- **載入順序**：搬到前面的名稱裡，import 時就會執行的只有 `GIFTS = gift_cells.load()` 和讀它的 `GIFT_NAMES`、`GIFT_IDS`，三行一起搬、順序不變。留在商店段、import 時讀 `GIFTS` 的 `GIFT_TIERS` 在區塊之後。往後搬的 `node_results`（組裝段 → 區塊）只在函式裡被呼叫。用 AST 檢查過：沒有任何 top-level 敘述在 import 時讀到比它晚定義的名稱。
- **`BACK_KEY` 也收進來**：它只有核心的 `back()` 在讀，沒有頁面段直接用，但它定義在地圖段中間，計畫第 5 項把它列進這區，地圖段搬走後它才不會單獨留在原處。標題因此寫「上面的 helper 或兩個以上頁面段讀的」（`seen` 也一樣，`on_page`、`tap_then` 在讀）。
- **`on_map` 的 docstring 照舊**（`the shop was left`），雖然 `forfeit` 也呼叫它：改字會多出 `move_check` 的剩餘行，這個 PR 只搬不改。

## 證據

`uv run python tools/move_check.py origin/main HEAD` 的全文。剩下的就是計畫寫的幾類：新區塊的兩行標題註解、4 個呼叫點、拿掉的 `@staticmethod`。`def on_map` 和它的 docstring、`return` 去掉縮排後跟原本相同，算成搬移。

```text
== 6 added lines not moved
agent/actions.py:1648: # Read by the helpers above or by two or more page sections (#676): each section moves to a module of its own that
agent/actions.py:1649: # imports only actions, so what they share stays here, or the page modules would import each other.
agent/actions.py:3697: until(context, lambda im: not on_map(context, im), timeout=2)
agent/actions.py:4949: if on_map(context, image):
agent/actions.py:4959: tap_then(context, *LEAVE_CONFIRM, lambda im: on_map(context, im), timeout=2)
agent/actions.py:4987: if on_map(context, image):
== 5 removed lines not moved
agent/actions.py:3636: until(context, lambda im: not Shop.on_map(context, im), timeout=2)
agent/actions.py:4936: if Shop.on_map(context, image):
agent/actions.py:4946: tap_then(context, *LEAVE_CONFIRM, lambda im: Shop.on_map(context, im), timeout=2)
agent/actions.py:4951: @staticmethod
agent/actions.py:4979: if Shop.on_map(context, image):
```

兩次都在暫存副本上做（repo 沒動）：放進 #689 的 `tools/split_actions.py` 和 `tools/move_check.py`，依序切 8 個頁面檔（lux、shop、map、battle、event、run_start、settle、daily）。

**之前：**（`origin/main` 的副本）`lux_actions` exit 0，接著 `shop_actions` exit 1，什麼都沒寫：

```text
the table does not fit agent/actions.py; nothing written:
actions.py:3323: forfeit stays in actions.py and reads Shop, which goes to shop_actions
```

**之後：**（這個 PR 的 HEAD 的副本）8 個都 exit 0，`actions.py` 剩 1,162 行（計畫估約 1,160）。副本上 `tests/test_agent_modules.py` → `2 passed`，`ruff check --select F agent tests tools` → `All checks passed!`。

## 合併風險

**門：** 雙向。只是檔內搬移，revert 一個 commit 就回到原狀。

**影響範圍：** 小。bot 的行為不變；會衝突的是同時改到這 24 個名稱或 `Shop` 離開商店那段的 PR。

## 驗證

- Tests: `uv run pytest tests/test_agent_modules.py tests/test_actions.py` → `302 passed, 0 failed`；完整檢查交給 CI 的 `ci-ok`
- Live: not run: 不改 bot 的行為，照 #676「每個 PR 怎麼證明行為沒變」的「實機」，合併後的下一次例行實機沒出新錯誤就算過（#676）
- Acceptance: `每個搬移 PR 的 move_check --module 只剩上面列的幾類行`（第 3 個 PR 是 `move_check 只剩 on_map 的那幾行：4 個呼叫點、它的 def 和拿掉的 @staticmethod，加上新區塊的標題註解`）→ 達成：見上面的全文，`def` 算成搬移所以不在剩餘行裡
- Fixtures: 無
- Review：push 前跑了 `code-review`（Standards + Spec，固定點 `origin/main`，spec 是 #676）。Spec 0 項；Standards 2 項判斷題（標題對 `BACK_KEY`、`seen` 說得不對；`WHITE_GOSSYPIUM` 離唯一讀它的 `avoided_gifts` 太遠），已在 `da1aecbb` 修正

author: clockwork-bot
body:
The first PR of design 0002's `rhi-transient` slice (R23): the per-frame transient allocator, as pure logic over chunks from a `ChunkSource`. The Vulkan backend implements the source, and `GpuResources` gains `begin_transient_frame` and `end_transient_frame`, in a later PR of the stack.

## What's here

- **`TransientFrame::allocate`** bumps the current 4 MiB chunk's offset with a compare-and-swap, so threads recording a frame allocate without a lock. A thread that finds the chunk full takes the frame's lock, gets a new chunk from the source and makes it current.
- **Chunk slots** are each set once, in segments of 16 allocated as the frame needs them, so a thread that read the current index uses its chunk without the lock, with no unsafe code.
- **Allocations larger than a chunk** get a chunk of their own.
- **Dropping a frame** gives its chunks back to the source to retire, as ending it will.
- **`TransientAllocation`** borrows its frame, so it can't be written once the frame has ended. `bytes_mut` is the one `unsafe` block.
- **`ChunkSource` is an `unsafe trait`**, stating what `bytes_mut` relies on: each chunk is mapped for its whole size and untouched by anything else until it's retired. Each chunk taken is checked for its size and its alignment.

## Design revision

Alignment is limited to `MAX_TRANSIENT_ALIGNMENT` (256 bytes, the largest `minStorageBufferOffsetAlignment` Vulkan allows), so an allocation as large as a chunk always fits in an empty one. A frame uses at most 256 chunks (1 GiB), beyond those of large allocations. Both are recorded in design 0002's "Transient memory" section and its revision history.

## Tests

T0 tests cover:

- bumping and alignment
- a full chunk moving to a new one
- large allocations
- retiring
- source errors
- misaligned chunks
- the limits

Two concurrent tests:

- Eight threads filling chunk after chunk, with a slow fake source, take exactly as many chunks as they fill.
- A property test allocates small and large sizes from eight threads at once, across several chunks, and checks that every allocation is aligned, inside a chunk, and overlaps no other.

Mutation checks:

- A racy bump fails the property test.
- Removing the recheck in `take_next_chunk`, wholly or in part, fails the concurrent tests.

`cargo xtask check` passes. This PR doesn't touch the GPU.

author: txsixman-dev
body:
## What
`apps/web/scripts/public-reads.test.mjs` runs `app/api/games/[id]/comments` and `app/api/games/[id]/score-report` as they are. They run as the **anon** role, on PGlite with every migration, through the same PostgREST-like client as the fan route tests.

9 tests cover:
- **The switch:** with FAN_SIGNIN off, both reads give a bare 404 and the database is never asked.
- **Never a call:**
  - A key that can't be a game (bad characters, too long, a quote) answers empty without a database call.
  - So does a site with no Supabase settings.
- **Rows that are never shown:**
  - Comments carry only `id, author, body, createdAt, edited`.
  - Never a hidden post, a banned fan's post or a user id. A muted fan's comment still shows.
  - Score status gives only a count until two **established** fans agree. New or banned accounts never confirm, and two competing scores confirm nothing.
  - On a played game, a score shows only when an established report matches the Results watch score.
  - Never who reported.
- **Limits and paging:**
  - 30 comments a page, oldest first, with the total.
  - Offsets are whole numbers and never negative; junk counts as 0.
  - The offset is capped at 10,000 before the call. The test asserts the values sent: `p_offset: 10000, p_limit: 30`.
- **No internals:** a database error (a transport error, or the real anon role losing the function) gives 502 `{error: "failed"}`, logged by SQL state only.

The fake client, the module stubs and the request helpers move from `fan-routes.test.mjs` to `scripts/route-harness.mjs`, shared by both files. It now also stubs `@supabase/supabase-js`'s `createClient`, which `publicClient()` uses. No site code changes. CI already runs `apps/web/scripts/*.test.mjs` with PGlite installed (PR 13). Locally: 131/131 pass, plus typecheck and Knip.

## Noted, not changed
Past the last page, the comments route answers `total: 0`, because the SQL's window count has no row to ride on. The page only asks for the next page while `posts.length < total`. So if a comment is hidden between two loads, the heading's count can drop to nothing until the next reload. It's cosmetic; a fix would need a second query.

## Security review
Tests only. No site code, workflow or permission changes. Fake values only.

author: hsk-dk
body:
## Hvorfor
Stravas API er nu kun for abonnenter. Uden abonnement svarer Strava `Application Inactive`, og der hentes ingen løb (sidste sync 14. april). Appen kan derfor hente løb fra Smashrun i stedet ([API-dokumentation](https://api.smashrun.com/v1/documentation)).

## Hvad
- **Kilde-lag:** migration 9 (`activities.source`, `source_id`, tabellen `smashrun_accounts`). Smashrun-løb gemmes med negativt id, så de ikke kan støde ind i Stravas.
- **Dubletter:** et løb, der allerede findes fra en anden kilde inden for 2 minutter, tilføjes ikke igen.
- **Forbindelse pr. person** under Mere → Mig:
  - Personligt token fra Smashruns API Explorer (user-level access): valideres, gemmes uden at blive vist igen, viser udløbsdato og advarer de sidste 14 dage.
  - App-nøgle (OAuth, kode-flow) med automatisk fornyelse af token, hvis `SMASHRUN_CLIENT_ID/SECRET` er sat.
- **Synkronisering:** første gang hele historikken, derefter inkrementelt (`fromDateUTC` med to dages overlap). Knappen Synkronisér kører alle forbundne kilder; en fejlende kilde stopper ikke de andre.
- **Fejl med årsag:** `UpstreamError` → 502 med kildens besked (fx `Application Inactive`) i stedet for en tom 500. En eksisterende test, der krævede 500 uden årsag, er ændret til at kræve 502 med årsagen.
- Banner "Forbind dine løb", advarsel om udløbende token, brugernavn skjult i headeren på små skærme.
- Docs i `docs/MULTI_USER.md`, nye variabler i `env.example`.

## Ikke med endnu
- Kilometer-splits og rute fra Smashrun (venter på eksempeldata fra rigtige svar).
- Automatisk synkronisering; i dag sker den ved knaptryk.

## Test
- Backend 228 tests, frontend 73 vitest, `vite build`. Smashrun er testet mod en falsk klient; intet er kørt mod den rigtige Smashrun.
- Feltnavne i Smashruns svar er læst fra dokumentationen, ikke set i et rigtigt svar. Løb, der ikke kan læses, tælles som `skipped` i Admin.

author: nabokihms
body:
#### Overview

A refresh for a user who was deleted or disabled upstream now answers 400 `invalid_grant` for the ldap, atlassiancrowd and local password connectors, instead of 500.

#### What this PR does / why we need it

- Adds `connector.ErrUserRevoked`. The refresh grant treats it like an upstream `invalid_grant`: 400 to the client, logged at info.
- ldap returns it when the user is no longer found, or the username now resolves to a different DN.
- atlassiancrowd returns it when `/user` answers 404 with `USER_NOT_FOUND`, or the user is inactive. A 404 without that reason, such as one from a wrong base URL, stays a server error.
- The local password DB returns it for a deleted user, or one replaced by another user with the same email.

Clients can then tell an ended session from a Dex failure and send the user to log in again.

Closes #5143

#### Special notes for your reviewer

A disabled Active Directory account that still exists passes the ldap refresh, since `Refresh` only searches for the user. Excluding disabled accounts in `userSearch.filter` covers that case.

**Second fix: the 25, not the bull.** With one dart left on 65 the coach's setup tip said Bull. Cause (measured at every tier): the model has two aims on the bull, the centre and a point on the 25 ring. A wide spread lands in the 25 ring about as often from the centre, so the centre aim won on a hair (0.554 vs 0.548 at semipro) while its tip said "Bull", though the 25 leaves 40 (D20) and the 50 leaves 15. The aim was never the problem; the name was. `aimLabel` (`shared/coach/model.ts`) now names the bed the model values more (the 25 or the bull) for either bull aim, with no threshold, and the tip's "leaves" follows that bed. Used by the setup tip (`setupAim` returns `label`), and by the coach's "better aim" note. I tried the other way first (one merged bull aim): it makes world-class 65 with one dart say T11, because the ring-point aim is what makes the 25 reachable for sharp players, so I kept both aims. Test: 65 with one dart is the 25 at all six tiers; 82 is the bull (leaves D16).

**Break.** `COACH_VERSION` 32 to 34 (the coach's note text changes) so stored coach legs regrade with the new text. No layout change, so no screenshots. Test pins the four routes. Ran `pstack:thermo-nuclear-code-quality-review` over the diff: nothing to fix.

author: pukujan
body:
Starts the move of the Studio UI to Vite + React + TypeScript (#404, PLANS.md §5). **Scaffold only: no screen moves.**

Read docs/engines/hermes-and-connections.md, docs/engines/meshy.md, docs/engines/sound.md and docs/engines/video.md: `server/server.mjs` is on each page's Glue line. This PR adds only a static `/next/` route (and `server/next.mjs`), before every engine route; no Hermes, Meshy, sound or film behaviour changes, so none of the pages' claims change. Their `server/server.mjs:<line>` citations past line 2613 are now 16 lines lower.

## What it does
- **`ui/`**: Vite 8.3.5, React 19.1.10, TypeScript 7.0.2 (strict), XState 5.33.3 + `@xstate/react` 6.1.0, React Aria Components 1.22.1, Tailwind 4.3.3, Storybook 10.6.5 (telemetry off). Its own `package.json` + lockfile, development only, **every version exact** and at least two weeks old.
- **Coexistence** ([decision 0013](docs/decisions/0013-react-ui-coexists.md)): the build `ui/dist/` is committed (fixed names, no hashes or source maps). The plugin's server serves it at **`/next/`** as one document: script and styles inline, the token put in at serve time and never in `ui/dist/`. It's the same pattern as `server/page.mjs`, so it also works in the Desktop pane's opaque-origin frame. **Nothing is built, downloaded or installed on the person's machine.** `/` and `web/` are unchanged (zero diff in `web/`).
- **Routing from the statechart:** `ui/` runs `web/nav.js`'s own machine (imported as `@studio/nav`, typed by `ui/src/nav/studio-nav.d.ts`). Its vendored XState import resolves to the same npm version. URL ↔ state matches spec 34: `/next/?project=…&version=…&room=deck` is the same place as `/?…`, and push/replace follows `web/studio.js` (a test keeps the two rules equal). Until a screen moves, `/next/` shows the screen's OBJECTS.md name and **Open in the Studio** at the same address.
- **Theme:** `tools/dev/tokens.mjs` (Style Dictionary) also writes `ui/src/theme.css`, a Tailwind v4 `@theme inline` whose utilities read the token variables (`bg-void` → `var(--void)`), so the light theme and the Hermes host's fonts still apply. Tailwind's own colours and fonts are cleared. `font.mono` becomes `font-monospace`, because `--font-mono` would loop with the host's variable. `tokens:check` covers both outputs.
- **Primitives** on React Aria (Button, Menu, Dialog, TextField) with stories, plus frame stories that start the real machine at an address.
- **Checks:** `tools/dev` gains `typecheck:ui`, `deps:ui` (dependency-cruiser using swc, since TS 7 has no compiler API) and `ui:check` (the committed `ui/dist` must be a fresh build). CI runs them, plus a `storybook` build job. `check.sh` asks `/next/` for one document with its token. `tests/next.test.mjs` covers the inlining, token escaping, the XState pins agreeing, exact pins, `@studio/nav`'s declared names against `web/nav.js`, and the address rules.
- **Docs:** decision 0013, `ui/README.md` (the porting recipe: component per OBJECTS.md name, story, state from the machine, audit gates before and after), README "What it does on your machine" line, AGENTS.md checks, PLANS.md §5.

- **Audit gates on `/next/`** (rebased onto #419): `AUDIT_APP=next` runs the same suite on the same screens at the same addresses under `/next/`, against its own `.ui-audit-known-violations.next.json`. CI's `ui-audit` job runs both. Today that list holds 32 entries, all from the stand-in: breadcrumb and loading on 8 screens at 2 widths. A moved screen gets a `nextReady` selector, and its entries may only shrink (AUDIT.md, ui/README.md). The brand sheet has no address, so it joins once its way in moves. The first `/next/` run also caught a mismatched accessible name on the logo button, which is fixed.

## Verified
- `/next/` in a real browser: deck address renders, the link keeps the address, Esc → Projects pushes history, Back restores, ☰ Light/Dark switches the shared `swarm-theme`, Esc on an open menu closes only the menu. Dialog story renders from the Storybook build.
- Both audits pass locally: `/` 20 passed, `/next/` 16 passed with 2 skipped.
- Locally green: typecheck, deps, tokens:check, typecheck:ui, deps:ui, ui:check, build-storybook, `tests/next.test.mjs`, and every `check.sh` section (python, server, hosted).
- Rebased onto #420 (LF checkout): the whole of `check.sh` passes locally on Windows (638 tests) and `vendor.mjs --check` matches.
- `ui:check` failed on CI because a Windows build left stray `\r` in `ui/dist/index.html`. A small Vite plugin now writes the page with `\n` everywhere, and the committed build is the LF one.
- `motion-check` "replay differs" (a cursor fade in the replay) can't come from this PR: `web/` is untouched and the only server change answers `/next` alone, so `/` serves the same bytes. It is rerun on this push.
- The lockfile resolves only from registry.npmjs.org and records the linux-x64 binaries; `ui/dist` holds no local paths.

## Notes for the next ports
- INVENTORY.md is not updated: `/next/` shows no screen yet. Its ☰ Light/Dark is the existing setting, and the inventory follows with the first port.
- Esc from a build room goes to Projects, because `web/nav.js` has no `back` there. The first room port should settle "up one level".

author: adeahejshshsh
body:
本仓原本没有 `internal/proxypool`，所以 `3d0f293e`（出口画像）无对象可改。按要求**补模块**。

## 补了什么
按上游同 ref（`3d0f293e`）整包取回 12 个文件，模块路径改本仓：

| 文件 | 行数 | 作用 |
|---|---|---|
| `pool.go` | 654 | 代理/路由持久化、按账号与域绑定、健康探测 |
| `subscription.go` | 516 | 订阅解析（含流式数组形态） |
| `transport.go` | 471 | 按代理协议造 `http.Transport`（http/https/socks5/overlay） |
| `intel.go` | 175 | **出口画像**：国家 / 住宅或机房 / ISP，6h 缓存 |
| 测试 ×4 | 800+ | 含 `intel_test.go` 与订阅流式数组回归 |

## 一处替代（不是简化）
`golang.org/x/net/proxy` 在这个环境**拉不到**（`proxy.golang.org`、goproxy.cn/io、阿里云镜像的 DNS 全部 `connection refused`），而 `transport.go` 只用到它三个符号。于是写了 `internal/proxypool/socks5.go`：CONNECT + RFC 1929，行为对齐 x/net ——
- 目标按域名下发由代理解析（`socks5` 与 `socks5h` 的差别在调用方，不在拨号器）；
- 认证失败、REP≠0 一律报错，**不静默降级成直连**（「配了代理却走直连」是最难查的事故）；
- `DialContext` 同一 ctx 约束建连与握手。

副作用是本仓的 proxypool 变成**零外部依赖**。

## 尚未接入（本批不含，说明清楚）
模块就位但还没有调用方。上游的接入是另一次重构，本仓还没到那个形态：

1. `internal/upstream/proxy.go`：上游把 **13 个出站点收敛**到 `do(req, a, chat)` 再交 `ProxyPool.Do(...)` 按账号选出口。本仓出站是 `do(req)`（无账号参数）—— 要接入必须先做这个收敛，否则会「一部分请求走代理、一部分直连」，指纹不一致比不接更危险；
2. `internal/panel/proxies.go`：9 条 `/panel/api/proxies*` 端点 + 账号/域绑定，依赖 `p.cfg.ProxyPool`（本仓 `Config` 无此项）；
3. `cmd/server/config.go` 的 proxies 配置段、`main.go` 的 `Manager` 装配、面板代理页 UI。

author: sacredtrees
body:
Stacked on #106, the WBGapTest harness. Merge #106 first; this PR's base then becomes main. It touches WBGapTest.c, WBGapTest.script and the build scripts, like #112 and #114, so the later merges take a small merge.

This is Workbench build plan row 7, from Team 5's baseline note: the M rows should drive each item, not only check that the item's name exists. MENUS still checks the names. The new mode, MENUDRIVE, picks the items with the mouse in RAM:WBGap's drawer window, the way a hand does:

1. It finds the item in the window's Intuition menu strip. `wbgap_menu_path` turns the menu's, item's and sub-item's boxes into a path for the pointer: title, down into the items, the item, then along the item's row into a sub-menu.
2. DragTest drags along that path with the right button held. `DragTest DRAG` now takes more than two points and pauses at each one, so a sub-menu can open.
3. It checks what the item did:

| Row | Item | Checked by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M12 | Select Contents | the window's pixels change |
| M30 | Clear Selection | the window's pixels return to their state before Select Contents |
| M15 | Show > All Files | the pixels change (RAM:WBGap/noicon has no icon); then Only Icons |
| M16 | View By > Name | the pixels change; then By Icon |
| M6 | About | a window opens; its button closes it |
| M2 | Execute Command | a requester opens; Cancel |
| M8 | New Drawer | a drawer is made: a requester's offered name accepted with Return, or the drawer made at once; it is then removed |
| M9 | Open Parent | RAM:'s window opens, or (GFOpenBench) the same window moves to RAM:, or RAM:'s open window becomes active |
| M10 | Close (last) | the window goes; it is opened again for the steps after |

An item that isn't there or is disabled is SKIP, because MENUS already reports a missing item. About and Execute Command are taken from any Workbench window's menus, since GFOpenBench keeps them on the desktop's own window. The harness only reads pixels, windows and files and sends input events, so the draw-through-OpenLayout rule isn't touched. Worst wins in the report: a FAIL from MENUDRIVE overrides a name PASS from MENUS.

## Tests

- **Host:** `tests/host/test_wbgap_menu.c` (new, in `run.sh`, 19 checks) covers:
  - an item under its title;
  - a sub-item reached along the item's row;
  - a title wider than its items;
  - a sub-menu starting below the item's row;
  - empty boxes.
  
  `tests/host/run.sh` all passed.
- **Build:** `build-amiga.sh` on the os32-gcc16-open6 stove, clean under `-Werror`.
- **Lab:** picking from a real menu needs a running Workbench, which no unit test reaches.

| Lab | M12 | M30 | M15 | M16 | M6 | M2 | M8 | M9 | M10 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3.2.3 (Workbench 47.42) | PASS | PASS | PASS | PASS | PASS | PASS | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| Copy of Instance-32 with #107's GFOpenBench 0.1.56 | PASS | PASS | PASS | PASS | FAIL | FAIL | FAIL | PASS | PASS |

**New finding on GFOpenBench 0.1.56:** About..., Execute Command... and Window > New drawer... open nothing when picked.
- Screenshots taken while the menu was held show the pointer on the right item, highlighted, and no window after it was let go.
- Amiga-E on the desktop opens no Execute Command requester either, so the cause isn't the harness's mouse path.
- All three go through a requester (`of_req_string` or EasyRequest), so that is the place to look.
- MENUS only checked that the names exist, and passed these three.

author: agustinvalencia
body:
Closes #526. Part of #520 (the runtime self-heal and the client-facing message; the remaining CLI-side points of #520 stay open).

## The problem

A damaged `index.db` that SQLite still opens, with page-level damage inside a table, does not return `DatabaseCorrupt` or `NotADatabase` on ordinary reads, so nothing noticed it:

- reads kept working;
- each write that touched a damaged page landed on disk but reported `index stale after successful commit (1 error(s))`, which named no cause;
- the sweep's reconcile returned `Ok(report)` with per-note errors, logged at INFO as a bare count, so the `Ok(Err(_))` arm this issue planned to act on never fired;
- a restart reopened the same file, since the open-time self-heal (#206) only catches a file SQLite refuses outright.

Recovery needed someone with a shell on the host. See the comment on #526 for the recurrence that motivated this.

## What changes

**Assess.** Both MCP servers run `PRAGMA quick_check` when they open (`open_vault_checked`), and `cdno-mcp-server` runs it after every reconciliation sweep (about 50 ms on a vault of a few hundred notes). The CLI is unchanged: it opens once per command, and the check's doc comment still holds for it. A tool call that meets a corruption error wakes the loop at once for the thorough `integrity_check`.

**Repair.** A rebuild builds a fresh index beside the live one, under a name unique to its process and attempt, with a full reconcile and then a quick catch-up pass, while the live index keeps serving. Then, under the vault's cross-process write lock, it does two things. It carries the archival snapshots across: the one table the notes cannot regenerate. And it copies the fresh index into the live file with SQLite's online backup API.

The file is never renamed or reopened. So every connection to it, in this process and in any other (a second server, `cdno watch`, a CLI command), reads the repair on its next query. No commit lands half before and half after. A copy of the damaged file is kept as `index.db.previous`.

The fresh index must pass `quick_check` first, and the copy is one write transaction, so any failure leaves the live index as it was. A database with no schema also fails the check, so an empty index can never pass as an empty vault (the point raised on #520). Rebuilds within one server are serialised and spaced at least a minute apart.

**Report.**
- `IndexStale` now names its first cause: `… (1 error(s)): SQLite error: database disk image is malformed`.
- The sweep logs the first five failing notes, with reasons, at WARN.
- A corruption error sent to a client adds that the notes on disk are intact, that the repair has started (on both servers, sweeps or not), and whether that call's write was saved. It says "saved" only for an `IndexStale` commit.
- New tools:
  - `index_status` (read-only, so it is on `--read-only` servers too): a fresh check, the latest sweep and rebuild, and any damage found at start.
  - `rebuild_index`: forces a rebuild; refused with `rebuild_refused` while one is running or within a minute of the last.

The line from #526 holds: only derived state is repaired automatically. No note is read differently or written.

## Verification

- New core tests build a real file with page-level damage (it opens and migrates, and only `quick_check` sees the damage). They cover detection, the rebuild repairing it behind the same handle, the live index left alone when `populate` fails or keeps the fresh handle, and `set_aside`.
- New `cdno-mcp` tests cover the checked open, a sweep repairing a damaged index behind the vault's handle (search answers from the new file), the rebuild interval, snapshot carry-over, and both tools.
- I replayed a genuinely damaged index file (rowids out of order, pages referenced twice, `idx_*` entries missing, a malformed FTS5 inverted index) against a copy of its vault with the release binary. The server reported the damage at start, rebuilt it, `index_status` came back healthy, and the following sweeps indexed every note with no errors.
- `cargo fmt`, `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, and `cargo test --workspace` (3676 passed).

## After review

A review round changed the design from a rename swap to the in-place backup copy above. The rename swap left other processes on the moved-aside file, and two processes rebuilding at once collided on one temp name. The round also:
- carried snapshots for notes archived during a rebuild;
- made a sweep with failing notes run the thorough `integrity_check`;
- added the corruption listener to the stdio server and to `--reconcile-interval-secs 0`;
- fixed the "saved" wording;
- made `healthy` judge the index only, with notes that do not parse in `notes_not_indexed`;
- stopped a check that cannot run at open from blocking start-up.

Replayed again: one server repaired the damaged file at start, a second server then opened the same vault, and a forced `rebuild_index` on the first left the second reading a sound index with every note.

## Notes for review

- `CORRUPTION_SEEN` is a process-wide `Notify`, because `into_mcp_error` is a free function with no server at hand. One process serves one vault.
- `rebuild` takes the vault write lock only for the final carry-and-copy step. Taking it for the populate passes would deadlock, since reconcile takes it per note and the lock is per open file.
- `integrity_check` holds the index mutex for a full scan. It runs only on demand (a sweep with failing notes, or a corruption signal), not on every sweep.
- `cdno reindex` still deletes the file and so still drops the snapshots. Moving it onto `reconcile::rebuild` would be a small follow-up.

author: ifiokjr
body:
## Why

Milestone M1 of the tax plan (`docs/tax-jurisdictions.md`). An entity can now be created in any country, and every entity needs its own currency to be the base. Today `CurrencyCode` knows 27 values, which silently rules out most of the world: a Kenyan, Chilean or Thai entity has no way to hold its own money as the base.

## How

- `CurrencyCode` is generated from `openbudget_core/data/iso4217.json`, the ISO 4217 List One published by SIX, the maintenance agency, on 2026-09-17. The file records the publisher, document, URL and retrieval date for the currency list, and the same for the CLDR 49.0.0 symbols.
- 166 codes: every active ISO 4217 currency that has a published minor unit (165), plus BTC. Exponents are the published ones, including 4 for the two funds (CLF, UYW) the standard gives four decimal places.
- The 26 ISO codes and BTC that existed keep their names, symbols and exponents byte for byte, and stay first in their original order. `try` is a Dart keyword, so TRY's member is `try_`.
- The 13 codes ISO 4217 publishes without a minor unit (precious metals, units of account, the testing code and the no-currency code) are recorded in the data file as excluded instead of being given a fabricated exponent. No amount can be written in them, and `XXX` stays unsupported.
- `dart run tool/generate_currencies.dart` writes the enum and `--check` fails when the committed Dart drifts from the data. CI's `lint` job runs it beside the generated icon check.
- The FX service stopped sending a currency filter to currencyapi.com: the provider answers 422 when one filtered code is not in its list, and it prices 155 of the 166 codes. The request now asks for everything the provider prices and the parser keeps the supported ones. The 11 unpriced codes work as a base currency, and cross-currency writes use the existing manual-rate path.
- `openbudget_core/test/constants/currencies_test.dart` parses the data file and checks the enum against it member by member, pins the original 27, pins the excluded set, and records currencyapi.com's priced list. It names the 11 unpriced codes (BOV, CHE, CHW, COU, MXV, SSP, USN, UYI, UYW, VED, XAD) and asserts each one parses, which is the only gate `EntityService.create` applies to a base currency, so none of them can block entity creation.

author: tmatens
body:
## Summary

The CL-0014 fix deletes a `logging:` block whose only key is `driver: none`, and its caveat says the default driver is restored. That is not true for a service that uses `extends:`: the base's `logging:` block takes effect once the local one is gone.

```yaml
services:
  log-template:
    image: nginx:1.27
    logging:
      driver: syslog
      options:
        syslog-address: "tcp://203.0.113.7:514"
  web:
    extends: log-template
    logging:
      driver: none
```

On `main`, `fix --apply --only CL-0014` removes the two lines under `web` and the file then deploys `web` with the syslog driver.

- The fixer returns a reasoned refusal for a service that uses `extends:`, so the finding is listed under "fix by hand" with the reason. CL-0003's fixer already refuses an `extends:` chain.
- The base of an `extends:` is still fixed: nothing above it supplies another block.
- A service with no `extends:` is fixed as before.

A narrower test, refusing only when the base really defines `logging:`, would apply the fix in more files but needs a walk of the chain. Refusing every `extends:` is the safe first step.

## Tests

- `tests/test_CL0014.py`: the fixer refuses the service above with a reason, and still fixes the base.
- `tests/test_fix_apply_refusals.py`: the reason is printed and the file is unchanged, for the short and the mapping form of `extends:`.

This changes what `fix` declines, not what CL-0014 reports. `docs/rules/CL-0014.md` says when `fix` leaves the block alone.

**Does this fix a security defect?** No. Whoever can write the base service can write the same `logging:` on the service directly.

Fixes #1252

## Summary

Phase 9C adds **local grounded multimodal answers with application-resolved text and visual citations**, building on merged Phase 9B.2 combined retrieval.

- Build a bounded context from retrieved text chunks and stored **unverified** model-generated visual interpretations, treating all retrieved content as untrusted data.
- Generate structured, single-turn answers with the existing local Ollama text model and preserve abstention when evidence is insufficient.
- Resolve model-supplied temporary citation labels to application-owned document/chunk or visual-element/interpretation identities, including source page and PDF bounding-box coordinates.
- Recheck cited source records in a fresh read-only PostgreSQL snapshot after generation; fail closed on deletion or mutation.
- Correct the PostgreSQL `NUMERIC(12,4)` vs retrieved `float` equality issue using `Decimal(str(value))`, so unchanged fractional coordinates are accepted while coordinate mutations are rejected.
- Tighten Ollama completion validation and add an opt-in, **development-only** `POST /collections/{collection_id}/multimodal-answer` endpoint. Existing text-only answer API remains unchanged.

## Testing

**Codex-reported local verification** (not GitHub CI):
- Full suite with disposable PostgreSQL: **431 passed, 0 failed, 8 skipped**.
- Focused tests: **18 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped**; targeted source checks **3 passed**.
- One local EmbeddingGemma/Qwen3 smoke test passed on synthetic evidence, **not** an accuracy benchmark.
- Python compilation, `git diff --check`, and changed-file secret-pattern check passed.
- No real application database migration or modification; disposable database removed/stopped.

**Review:** One consolidated source-archive review, then focused verification of the fractional-coordinate fix and PostgreSQL regression. The pushed branch was compared with `main`, and the fix and test are present.

## Security, limitations and scope

- Visual citations must retain `model_generated_interpretation` and `unverified`; source identity validation **does not prove** that an answer claim is factually supported.

body:

## Qué incluye

Nuevo bloque **Módulos** en el menú lateral (en el móvil, accesos rápidos en Inicio).

- **Casa**: gasto de vivienda del periodo, coste mensual medio y anual, gastos fijos al mes, comparativa mes a mes con el año anterior, desglose por subcategoría y quién registró cada gasto. **Gastos recurrentes** (mensual, trimestral, anual) con botón "Registrar cuota", pausa, edición y fecha de fin.
- **Viajes**: nombre, destino, fechas, presupuesto, estado y participantes. En el detalle: coste total, coste por día y por participante, presupuesto frente a gasto real, gasto por categoría (vuelos, hotel…) y por persona, y lista de gastos. Comparativa entre viajes. Desde el formulario de cualquier gasto se puede asignar a un viaje.
- **Comidas y restaurantes**: total de alimentación, supermercado frente a comer fuera, media mensual, evolución de 12 meses y reparto por tipo.
- **Presupuestos**: mensuales, anuales, personalizados y de viaje; por categoría o generales; personales o compartidos. Muestra lo consumido, el % y lo que queda, con aviso al 85 % y al superarlo.
- **Objetivos de ahorro**: fondo de emergencia, viajes, vivienda, inversiones u otros. Progreso manual o vinculado al saldo real de una cuenta, con lo que hace falta ahorrar al mes para llegar a la fecha.
- Detalles: los porcentajes usan coma decimal y las cuentas personales de tu pareja salen como "Cuenta de <nombre>".

## Base de datos (migración 0006, ya aplicada en Supabase)

- `register_recurring`: crea la cuota como movimiento normal y avanza la fecha. Un índice único impide registrar dos veces la misma cuota.
- `trip_expenses` sincroniza `transactions.trip_id`. En un viaje compartido todos los gastos son compartidos.
- `budget_progress` y `trip_summaries`: funciones SECURITY INVOKER, así que respetan la RLS.

## Pruebas

- `npm run test:rls`: 23 escenarios (8 nuevos de la fase 2) con tres usuarios. Pasan todos.
- E2E en navegador contra Supabase con dos usuarios (escritorio y móvil): recurrente y cuota (850 €), viaje compartido con un gasto de cada uno (405,50 €, el mismo total para los dos y "Personal" bloqueado), presupuestos (súper 205,84 €; ropa personal de 45,99 € que la pareja no ve; viaje superado en 5,50 €), comidas (súper 120,34 € y comer fuera 85,50 €) y objetivo (1.500 € de 6.000 €, 25 %). Sin errores en consola.

body: ## Summary This PR adds support for abstract models and Java sealed discriminator hierarchies to the Java JAX-RS Spec server generator. ### Changes - Add the `x-abstract` vendor extension for explicitly declaring abstract models. - Support Java 21 sealed model hierarchies with discriminator-based inheritance. - Improve Jackson `@JsonTypeName` handling for inherited discriminator mappings. - Add generator tests and OpenAPI specifications covering abstract and sealed model hierarchies. - Add a generated JAX-RS Spec sample demonstrating the new functionality. - Update generator documentation. ### Validation - `./mvnw clean package` — BUILD SUCCESS (all 8 modules; Maven Central used via a separate settings file). - Full core library test suite — 5,791 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 18 skipped. - Targeted JAX-RS Spec tests — 215 tests passed. - `./bin/generate-samples.sh bin/configs/jaxrs-spec-sealed.yaml` — successful, no generated changes. - `./bin/utils/export_docs_generators.sh` — completed, no generated changes. ### PR checklist - [x] Read the contribution guidelines. - [x] Run Maven build and tests. - [x] Regenerate the relevant JAX-RS Spec sample. - [x] Export generator documentation. - [x] Commit all changes. ### Follow-up JSON-B discriminator deserialization support is implemented separately and will be submitted as a follow-up PR. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds the `x-abstract` vendor extension and sealed discriminator hierarchy support to the jaxrs-spec generator. Models marked `x-abstract` are generated as abstract classes with protected constructors and without builders or JSON creators, and they can be combined with `useSealed` to produce sealed hierarchies with final leaves. **Details** - Explicit discriminator mappings to an abstract model fail generation; implicit ones are replaced by mappings to its concrete subclasses. - With `useSealed`, an abstract model needs a generated subclass, otherwise generation fails. - For allOf grandchildren, `@JsonTypeName` is now resolved from the nearest ancestor discriminator that maps the model. - `x-abstract` is supported by jaxrs-spec only; `jaxrs-cxf-cdi` ignores it because it uses its own templates. - JSON-B discriminator deserialization is not included in this PR. Written for commit 6dc225e20d77514db44adeb462af86ab302967c7. Summary will update on new commits.

author: fooftilly
body:
## Summary

Since PG-C2 every PRKS web process authenticates requests (`PRKS_AUTH=session` by default), and #1223 added the browser sign-in page. Several security texts still described the old model. This PR is docs only.

- **`SECURITY.md`**:
  - Drops "single-user application with **no built-in authentication**". It also drops the rule that being able to use an exposed instance without logging in is not a vulnerability.
  - Now describes:
    - the two `PRKS_AUTH` modes;
    - the Library role checks;
    - that `loopback-owner` runs only on a loopback-bound `--testing` instance;
    - the supported exposure, which is an HTTPS reverse proxy with `PRKS_PUBLIC_ORIGIN` and `PRKS_TRUSTED_PROXIES`.
  - In scope, and to be reported privately: bypasses of sign-in, sessions, attempt limits, role checks and cross-origin checks. The scope list gains a matching line.
  - Not vulnerabilities by themselves:
    - `loopback-owner` acting as owner, as documented;
    - password guessing within the attempt limits;
    - attacks that need plain-HTTP exposure or a proxy configured other than as documented.
- **`docs/wiki/Troubleshooting.md`**: "PRKS does not provide application-level authentication" becomes "sign-in protects the Library, but PRKS serves plain HTTP; use an HTTPS reverse proxy".
- **`docs/wiki/Security-and-Operations.md`**:
  - The page said a missing `Origin` is allowed for local scripts. That is no longer true (`origin_allowed` in `backend/api/session.py`): without `Origin`, the request needs `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`, and a client that sends neither is refused. The page now says this.
  - The `PRKS_TRUSTED_HOSTS` note now points to `PRKS_PUBLIC_ORIGIN` for HTTPS proxies.
- **`docs/postgresql-architecture.md` §1**: marked as the pre-0.8 baseline, because its "No authentication" bullet reads as current state.

## Related issues

Part of #641 (PG-C2), the docs sweep.

## Scope / non-goals

- No code change. The policy wording is a proposal for review: it changes what the project treats as a vulnerability.

## Validation

- `tests/test_ci_docs_only.py`, `tests/test_engineering_invariants.py`: pass.
- I checked each claim against the code and `docs/login-security.md`:
  - `origin_allowed` refuses `Origin: null` (an unparseable origin).
  - `PRKS_PUBLIC_ORIGIN`'s host is accepted without listing it in `PRKS_TRUSTED_HOSTS`.
  - `loopback-owner` requires `--testing` and a loopback bind, and answers only loopback peers.

## Migration / compatibility impact

None.

## Checklist

- [x] No tests removed, skipped or weakened.

author: acmerfight
body:
## Problem
`openManaged` (a sidebar click) and `newConversation` (leaving a loading conversation for a draft) announced `onRestart`, and the workspace's `onRestart` restarts the home load **and** the directory load. The directory of conversations does not depend on the selection, yet every sidebar click re-requested the whole list, put the sidebar into `refreshing` (spinner, `aria-busy`, refresh button disabled) and re-armed the directory's status basis.

## Change
- A selection change announces its own `onSelectionChanged`, which the workspace maps to `startHomeLoad` only.
- `onRestart` keeps its meaning of starting over (setup completed, Computer changed or replaced, a load timed out, an explicit retry) and still reloads both loads.
- Entry that is not ready (`!homeCanStartConversation`) still starts over, as before.

The deeper split (moving the Computer pairing/configuration watch out of `load` into the Computer status workflow) is not done here: it is a larger change to the recovery paths and nothing observable depends on it today.

## Verification
- Related web integration tests (lifecycle, status, titles, sidebar actions and outcome recovery, Computer offline and connection recovery, active conversation, message handoff): 9 files, 62 tests passed. Typecheck and lint passed through the commit hook.
- No new test: the effect is an extra request and a spinner for one round trip, and a deterministic assertion would need to hold the directory request, which the web harness does not expose for this path.

## Compatibility and recovery
The user explicitly authorized dropping compatibility for Morty (pre-launch, no users). In-page behavior only; no protocol, storage or deployment change. Rollback restores the previous restart behavior.

author: bawes
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"BAWES"} -->
_Requested by **Khalid** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KqMcAJsofjAhKVAToS3skr?thread=cmsg_01KqMcAJsofjAhKVAToS3skrCSbwU6yjdrLnGs9yxmJoh7)_

Part of game issue BAWES-Universe/workadventure-universe#2001 (Brick 10: Apps), step 7, the Orbit half, built to the approved mock "Lending Apps to a team" (https://claude.ai/artifact/517CDr8XBQDKpxHZneCyF1). **Stacked on #935, which is stacked on #928**: this PR's base is #935's branch (`claude/project-thread-x3q2uf-apps-4`) so the diff shows only this step. Bases need moving to develop as the ones below merge. The game screens come in the game PR on top of #2014.

## Lend one of your apps to a universe (works like an AI key)
- `POST /api/me/apps/:id/lends { universeId, things?, usesPerDay? }`, `PATCH` and `DELETE /api/me/apps/:id/lends/:universeId` ("Lend", "Change", "Take back"). Needs Manage bots in that universe (403 otherwise). `things` narrows bots to some of the four headings (look up, make, change, delete or send), null for all; `usesPerDay` is a whole number or null for no limit. No cap on how many universes.
- **Only an app added with a link and a key, a token or nothing can be lent.** One signed in as the person (a sign-in page, a listed app, a ready-made app) answers 409 and is never lent. A database trigger holds the same line against direct writes. `GET /api/me/apps/:id` now answers `lendable`, `lentTo` (each universe with its limits, today's uses, and each bot with its uses this month) and `canLendTo`.
- **Lending moves no bot.** A person who manages a bot there lets that bot use it: `GET/POST /api/bots/:id/apps/available` ("More apps it can use here", "Let Guide use it"). An app you lent shows only to you there, and only you can let a bot use it.
- **Take back stops bots at once**: the bots' grants and every approval for them end in the same step as the lend. Lending again later gives them nothing back.
- **Use check** (`/use`): for a lent app or a universe's own app the bot server must send `callId` (and, for a lent app, `heading`); without them the answer is `incomplete` and nothing is counted, never a use let through unchecked. A lent grant is allowed only while the lend exists, the lender still has Manage bots in that universe (else `gone`: someone who left, or lost the role, no longer has their app serving it or billed to them), the row is on, the heading is one the lender allowed (else `not_lent`), and the day's uses are not used up (else `limit_reached`). Any visitor of the bot may ask, as the mock says. Each use is written once under the bot's own call id (two bots may share an id), under a lock, so a retry counts once and two calls at once can never take the last use. Days start at 00:00 UTC. The answer says who pays (`paidBy`): the lender for a lend, the universe for a universe's own app. When the day's uses run out the lender gets one notice a day (kind `app-lend-limit`). Nothing is refused to the person asking: the bot carries on without it.
- A person's own app used by their own Brick works exactly as before.

## A universe's own apps
- `AppConnection` now belongs to a person **or** a universe (`owner_id` is nullable, `universe_id` new, a check makes it exactly one), so a universe's app has no owner and **stays when anyone leaves or deletes their account**.
- `GET/POST /api/me/universes/:universeId/apps`, `GET /api/me/universes` ("Your universes"), `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/me/team-apps/:id`, `POST /api/me/team-apps/:id/managers`, `DELETE .../managers/:personId`. Same checks as a person's own app when adding. Whoever connects one becomes a manager. Managers add managers (people with Manage bots there; 422 otherwise). Anyone else gets 404.
- **Managers are computed, not copied**: the universe's owner always, plus named managers who still have Manage bots there. Someone who leaves stops managing it at once, with nothing handed over. The view marks each manager with `owner` (owns the universe, not removable) and `you`, and `connectedBy` with `you`, for the game screens.
- Its page data says who connected it and whether they still manage it, who manages it now, the bots that use it, and this month's uses (counted for the universe). A manager starts or reconnects the sign-in with the existing `/api/me/apps/:id/sign-in`, and signing in again names who did it.
- A grant to a bot of the universe needs a manager of the app who also manages the bot. Disconnect by a manager stops every bot and ends every approval at once. A database trigger allows a grant only to: a person's own Brick for their own app, a bot of the owning universe for its own app, or a bot of a universe an app is lent to.

## Not here
- The game screens (the Apps page sections, the app pages, the bot page group), on top of #2014. This only provides the data and routes for them.
- Team apps are a connection like any other for sign-in notices: the card goes to whoever connected it while they can manage that bot, else the bot's maker.

## Checks
- `tsc` (only the old test-file errors) and 32 real-database tests (`ROLES_DB_TEST=yes`, skipped in CI): lending needs Manage bots; sign-in apps are never lent; lending moves no bot; only the lender lets a bot use it; other universes and no-lend refused (also by direct write); heading held; a use with no call id or heading is refused; a lender who loses Manage bots stops serving; day's limit, retry counted once, same id from two bots counted twice, one notice, two at once never over the limit; take back stops bots and ends approvals; a person's own Brick unchanged; a universe's app has no owner, outlives a manager who leaves and a deleted account, owner always manages, named managers add and remove, a stranger sees nothing, disconnect stops all.
- Known, not from this PR: `ownership-transfer-db.test.ts` (fails without this change too), `brick-visit-db` 2b in one environment, and the integration suites that need a running server.

author: juchengquan
body:
The swap: `/opt` serves the redesign, `/opt/next` sends a bookmark there, and the old dashboard is deleted. The owner's parity check happens at merge time: the boxes are below and **unticked**.

```
before                                     after
/opt       -> index.html -> src/main.tsx   /opt       -> index.html -> src/next/main.tsx
              (the old App)                              (the redesign)
/opt/next  -> next/index.html -> Next      /opt/next  -> next/index.html: meta refresh +
                                                         location.replace("/opt/" + search + hash)
```

## What changed

**1. Entries (`7f93d88`).** `frontend/index.html` now loads `src/next/main.tsx`, with the redesign's head (`viewport-fit=cover`, `color-scheme`). `next/index.html` is a redirect page, and both build entries are kept.

**The redirect, and why it isn't Caddy.** The redirect is a meta refresh plus `location.replace("%BASE_URL%" + location.search + location.hash)`. Vite fills `%BASE_URL%` with `UI_BASE`, so the bundle has it as `/opt/`. A Caddy `redir` would mean writing `/opt` into `deploy/Caddyfile` a second time: tailscale strips the prefix and does not rewrite `Location` (the Caddyfile already says this). It would also need the UI agent restarted, while the page change ships with the bundle. Caddy's existing `try_files {path}/index.html` still serves `/next` as a file with no trailing-slash redirect. The Caddyfile changed only in a comment. The new `src/__tests__/Entries.test.ts` checks both entries.

**2. Deletion (`11d352b`), as `OldPage.test.ts` listed it.** All 16 modules at the top of `src/` except `vite-env.d.ts`:
`AddForms.tsx`, `AddPanel.tsx`, `App.tsx`, `Holdings.tsx`, `MutedTables.tsx`, `OpenedField.tsx`, `PaceLine.tsx`, `RowActions.tsx`, `RowDetail.tsx`, `ServicePanel.tsx`, `SnapshotView.tsx`, `TopLine.tsx`, `WatchlistTable.tsx`, `main.tsx`, `useSnapshot.ts`, `useTableFit.ts`.
The 43 tests in `OLD_PAGE_TESTS` went too: 15 browser and 28 jsdom. `Modules.test.ts` lost its claims about `App.tsx`, `useTableFit.ts` and `useSnapshot.ts`.

**`OldPage.test.ts` is deleted**, as #301 said once its lists were empty. A guard against "a file at the top of `src/`" would get in the way of the planned `src/next/` → `src/` move.

**3. Trim (`0eb8307`).**
- `shared/columns.ts` and `shared/cells.ts` are deleted outright. The page used only the `Column` type for its picker, and `isPinned` for the old single-leg table's cookie.
- `ColumnPicker` now takes `{key, label}[]`. `readHidden()`/`writeHidden()` lost their table argument but still use the **`ui_cols_combo`** cookie, so the owner's column choice survives.
- The signal, band and grouping preferences are removed (#338). The tests for code that no longer exists went with it: `Fitting`, `Grouping`, `LastTrade`, `Signal`.
- Dead code nothing reaches is removed: `createWatch`, `recordHolding` and their helpers in `api.ts`; `fmt`, `alarmText` and `FIELD_COLUMN` in `format.ts`.
- In `app.css`, every class rule and colour token nothing renders is removed (`.topline`, `td.hl`, `.imminent`, `tr.group`, `.badge`, `.snapshot*`, `.table-scroll`, and the alarm ramp). The element rules for `table`/`th`/`td` **stay**, because the journal's table and a split's table still use them.
- Source comments that called the old page "`/opt`" or "today's page" now refer to it in the past tense.

**4. Rename (`b893ffa`).**

| Where | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| The desk's `+` button | "add a spread" | "add" |
| Its panel | "adding a spread" / "Add a spread" | "Add a spread or contract" |
| The phone's sheet title | "Add a spread" | "Add a spread or contract" |
| The phone sheet's description | | "A spread or one contract, and the Monitors it starts with, saved together." |
| The palette action | "Add a spread" | "Add a spread or contract" |

The forms inside keep their own names, "add a spread" and "add one contract". The suites' queries were renamed to match.

**5. Docs (`809a14b`).**
- **ADR 0023:** status is now Built, 2026-11-13. A new section, "What the swap dropped", records the five drops from #338 with the owner's reasons, and the known gap #351. "How it ships" and "Double polling" are now in the past tense.
- **ADR 0008:** status amended. A closing section says what still holds now that its tables are gone.
- **ADR index:** both rows updated.
- **CLAUDE.md:** the frontend paragraph describes one page, the redirect page, the `src/next/` name, and the cookies.
- **`CONTEXT.md`** names no old components, so it is unchanged.

**6. Bundle (`0e89506`).** Rebuilt with `make build-ui`.

## Test files, before → after

| Suite | origin/main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| jsdom `__tests__` | 78 | 48 (−28 old-page, −OldPage, −4 trimmed, +Entries, +Snapshot, +Format) |
| browser, desktop | 31 | 16 |
| browser, iphone | 15 | 15 |

The browser config's instances and `optimizeDeps.entries` use globs (`src/__browser__/**/*.test.tsx`), so they list no deleted file and needed no change. Every remaining file still runs in its own instance.

`check-served-root` reads the served root from the plist and checks that it holds an `index.html`. It never knew about `next/`, so it is unchanged and still passes.

## Coverage restored after review (`d0c8100`)

`OLD_PAGE_TESTS` correctly took every test that reached an old module, but some of those also held live shared code:

- **`__tests__/Snapshot.test.ts`** imports only `shared/snapshot`, with nine cases:
  - `snapshotName`;
  - `captureBox`'s ceiling of 2, the area limit (`AREA_LIMIT`) and the side limit (`SIDE_LIMIT`), and that it never scales up;
  - `deliver`: the share sheet, the download when there is no share sheet, the download when the sheet claims it can share and then refuses, and the cancel.

  The no-share-sheet case now also asserts that `share` was never called, because a share that throws and is caught also ends in a download.

  | Mutation | Result |
  |---|---|
  | Flat 2× resolution | 2 failed |
  | Side limit removed | 1 failed |
  | Refusal fallback removed | 1 failed |
  | Download fallback removed | 2 failed |
  | No-share-sheet path forced to share | 1 failed |

- **`Modules.test.ts` "keeps the camera off the tree it points at"**, restated for the new page: `next/snapshot/useSaveImage.ts` must not import `Still` or `Next`, and must import `shared/snapshot`. Adding `import type { StillProps } from "./Still"` makes it fail (1 failed).

- **`__tests__/Format.test.ts`** has twelve cases, from the deleted `Columns`, `LastTrade`, `Opened` and `Clock` suites:
  - `shortContract`: the SPXW case, plus pass-through for an SPX code, a fractional strike and a non-contract;
  - `shortStamp`: positive and negative zones, no zone, unrecognised input, and an ISO `T` stamp of the wrong shape;
  - `marketDay`: the Singapore-morning rollover;
  - `clockTime`: 24-hour, padded, no locale text.

  | Mutation | Result |
  |---|---|
  | `marketDay` in Singapore | 1 failed |
  | `clockTime` unpadded | 2 failed |
  | Looser `shortContract` regex | 1 failed |
  | `shortStamp` accepting only positive zones | 1 failed |
  | `shortStamp` accepting an ISO `T` | 1 failed |

Also from the review (`c9f5d00`):
- CLAUDE.md's bounded-call invariant now states what is polled. ADR 0023's double-polling consequence is made accurate.
- The bot's standing-note docstring now names `next/pace.ts` instead of `PaceLine`, in both backends.
- `still.css` and `shared/snapshot.ts` no longer name deleted CSS or the deleted `Rasterize` test.
- The redirect has an end date (below).

## Verification

**After the review fixes, at `519f01b`.**
- **`make check`:** all checks passed on the committed tree.
  - Python: library 771, backend 1681, door scenarios 217 of 217, tools 166.
  - TypeScript: library 554, API 932.
  - UI: jsdom 892 tests in 48 files; browser 270 tests in 31 files.
  - `check-ui`: "frontend bundle matches its source".

author: tennashi
body:
## Why
With Vim's keys, fix text typed in the chat without relying on the mouse or the arrow keys. Until now, Normal mode in an input had only `i` `a` `I` `A` and Esc, with no movement or editing. This is the third step in making inputs a Vim line editor.

## What
- **Cursor.** The Normal mode cursor sits on a character and is drawn as a block in the accent color. Leaving Insert with Esc puts it on the character before, as in Vim. Closing hints or the command line with Esc does not move it.
- **Keys.** Expressed as an `Edit` (Move, Delete, Change, Yank, Put, Undo, Redo) and its range, a `Span` (up to a motion, the whole line, `iw`, `aw`). Aliases are the same values (`x` is `dl`, `D` is `d$`, `s` is `cl`, `S` is `cc`, `Y` is `yy`).
  - Move: `h` `l` `w` `b` `e` `0` `^` `$`
  - Delete: `x` `X` `d{motion}` `dd` `D` `diw` `daw`
  - Change: `s` `S` `c{motion}` `cc` `C` `ciw` `caw`. These enter Insert mode. `cw` goes to the end of the word, as in Vim.
  - Copy and paste: `y{motion}` `yy` `Y` `p` `P`. What is deleted or copied goes to the clipboard. Linewise text is told apart by its trailing newline and goes in the line below or above. In a single-line input, it goes in as one line.
  - Undo and redo: `u` and Ctrl-R. These use the history from #343.
  - Counts: `3x`, `2dd`, and so on.
- **Where it works.** The chat, goal, sketch, and rename inputs, and the inputs on the settings and a project's card (`FORMS`).
- **Where the code is.** Editing lives in `ui/input/draft/normal.rs` (`Draft::edit_normal`). For word movement, `stage/code/cursor.rs`, made for the code viewer, moved to `vim/cursor.rs` and is shared. Inputs receive it through the `vim::EditText` and `ui::input::Settle` actions.
- **Fixed the expectations of 3 existing tests.** One used `x` and `0` as examples of "keys that do nothing" in the chat's Normal mode, and one described the cursor after Esc as "between characters". The new expectations match what the same keys do in real Vim.

## Verification
- Unit tests in `draft/normal.rs`: the position after Esc, motions, `x` and `d`, `dd` and `p`, `c`, `y` and `p`, `u` and Ctrl-R.
- `normal_mode_edits_the_chat_s_input_as_vim_edits_a_line` in `tests/vim.rs`: presses `dw` `u` `$x` `ciw` `yw` `p` `dd` in the chat's input. Also checks that closing hints with Esc does not move the cursor. This check failed with the fix removed.
- `cargo test -p cox --lib --test vim --test window --test chats --test code`: all pass. clippy and fmt are clean too.
- Not yet tried in the real app (for example, how the block cursor looks).
