author: dkhalizov
body:
## Summary

The release parser misread or missed several release-name shapes, usually getting the release type wrong: single episodes read as season packs, multi-season packs read as one episode, multi-episode names cut down to their first episode, and some daily episodes and non-English season packs with no identity at all. This PR fixes each shape in the parser crate only. It targets `release-0.22.3` directly, as #437 did.

Fixes #472

Regression tests reproduced each defect before the fix. On a local comparison over about 900 release-name shapes, 68 more shapes now parse as expected, and no shape that parsed correctly before is misread now.

| # | Shape | Before → after | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Separate season and episode markers: `S03.E05`, `S15 E06`, `S1-E1`, `S01.Ep06`, `S01.E.01`, `Season 1 - Episode 01`, `Season 01 Episode 05` | season pack, no episodes → one episode | The split-season reader only accepted a bare number after the season. A new `episode_marker_at` helper reads an `E` / `Ep` / `Episode` marker (fused or as its own token) and is used by the split and season-keyword readers. The season-pack reader declines when such a marker follows the season. |
| 2 | Zero-padded fused season ranges: `S01-05`, `Season 01-07`; explicit `Season 01 - Season 07` | `S01-05` → S01E05, `Season 01 - Season 07` → season 1 only → multi-season pack | New `season_range_after`. Deliberately narrow: a bare end counts only when a zero-padded two-digit start is fused to a larger two-digit end by a hyphen with no spaces. Unpadded `S4-07` and spaced `S01 - 05` still read as episodes; existing tests pin `S4-07` and `S3-01` as episodes. See decisions below. |
| 3 | Repeated episode markers: `S03E01.S03E02`, `S02E09 E10`, `2x04.2x05`, `2x04x05`, `[02x01-x02]`, `S6.E1-E3`, `Episode 05-06`, `S42 Ep10718 - Ep10720` | first episode only (or season pack / no identity) → every episode | New `extend_repeated_episodes`, called after the first marker. A hyphen fills the range and other separators list the episode, matching the existing `E01E02` list semantics. Each episode must exceed the previous one and keep the season. A bare number needs a fused hyphen, so the #423 spaced-number rule is unchanged. `2x04x05` is read as a fused list. Role scoring for standard-episode identities now accepts a season or episode marker in any position instead of assuming the first token is the episode, because split forms put the season first. |
| 4 | Hyphenated `WEB-Rip` / `WEB-RIP` with no streaming-service tag | source `WEB-DL` → `WEBRip` | `WEB` followed by a hyphen and `RIP` is read as one source in the beam metadata step and in the independent technical-metadata recovery (the path used for unknown-facet and movie-shaped parses). |
| 5 | Daily air dates: `2011 04 18`, `2018_06_22`, `2012.16.02`, `04.28.2014`, `140722`, `5th Mar 2025`, `2015.09.07.Part2` | no identity (or date without part) → daily date, with part | Space- or underscore-separated dates need matching separators and two-digit month and day, and apply only when the name has no episode marker anywhere (new `has_episode_marker`), so `2016 02 25 S20E142` stays S20E142. Day and month swap only when the middle number cannot be a month. `parse_fused_daily_date` now also accepts six-digit `YYMMDD` (read as 20YY); it backs off the same way, so `221208 Show A ep34` stays S1E34. Its other caller only adds a date role, and checksums are 8 characters, so the two do not clash. An ordinal day is accepted beside a month name. A fused `Part2` after a date now sets the daily part. |
| 6 | Non-English season words: `Saison3`, `SAISON.1`, `Stagione.3`, `Temporada 10`, `Sezon 3`; Spanish chapters `Cap.201`, `Cap. 101`, `Cap.1901` | no identity → season pack, or season and episode from the chapter | The lexer normalizes `SAISON`, `STAGIONE`, `TEMPORADA` and `SEZON` (alone or fused to digits) to `SEASON`, so every existing season rule applies. Raw title spans used for identity matching are unchanged, and a season word with no number stays a title word (`La Saison des Pluies S01E02` is still S01E02). In a chapter number, the last two digits are the episode and the rest the season (S2E1, S1E1, S19E1). `CAP` before a 3-4 digit number gets an episode-marker role, the season-pack reader declines when a chapter is present, and a season word followed later by a chapter takes the chapter's numbering (`Temporada 2 [Cap.1901]` → S19E1). |

Measured parser output on the base commit and on this branch:

| Name | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Show.A.S03.E05.720p.HDTV.x264-Grp` | season pack [3] | S3 E5 |
| `Show A - Season 1 - Episode 01 (720p).avi` | season pack [1] | S1 E1 |
| `Show A S01-05 WS BDRip X264-Grp` | S1 E5 | seasons 1-5 pack |
| `Show A Season 01 - Season 07 BluRay 1080p x264-Grp` | season pack [1] | seasons 1-7 pack |
| `Show A S4-07 [1080p]` | S4 E7 | S4 E7 (unchanged) |
| `Show.A.S03E01.S03E02.720p.HDTV.x264-Grp` | S3 E1 | S3 E1, E2 |
| `Show.A.2x04x05.720p.BluRay-Grp` | no episode identity | S2 E4, E5 |
| `Show A - S42 Ep10718 - Ep10720` | season pack [42] | S42 E10718-E10720 |
| `Show.A.S01E01.1080p.WEB-Rip.x264-Grp` | WEB-DL | WEBRip |
| `Show.A.S01E01.720p.AMZN.WEBRip.x264-Grp` | WEB-DL | WEB-DL (unchanged, see below) |
| `Show A 2011 04 18 Guest Name HDTV XviD-Grp` | no identity | date 2011-04-18 |
| `Show.A.2012.16.02.PDTV.XviD-Grp` | no identity | date 2012-02-16 |
| `Show_A_04.28.2014_hdtv.x264.Grp.mp4` | no identity | date 2014-04-28 |
| `Show.A.140722.720p.HDTV.x264-Grp` | no identity | date 2014-07-22 |
| `Show A 5th Mar 2025 1080 (Grp)` | no identity | date 2025-03-05 |
| `Show.A.2015.09.07.Part2.720p.WEBRip.x264-Grp` | date 2015-09-07 | date 2015-09-07, part 2 |
| `Show.A.05.06.2024.720p-Grp` | date 2024-06-05 | date 2024-06-05 (unchanged, see below) |
| `Show A 2016 02 25 S20E142` | S20 E142 | S20 E142 (unchanged) |
| `221208 Show A ep34[1080p60 H264].mp4` | S1 E34 | S1 E34 (unchanged) |
| `Show.A.Saison3.VOSTFR.HDTV.XviD-Grp` | no identity | season pack [3] |
| `Show.A.Stagione.3.HDTV.XviD-Grp` | no identity | season pack [3] |
| `Show A [Sezon 3] [1080p] [WEB-DL] [H264]` | no identity | season pack [3] |
| `Show A - Temporada 2 [HDTV 720p][Cap.201][AC3 5.1]` | no identity | S2 E1 |
| `Show A - Temporada 2 [HDTV 720p][Cap.1901][AC3 5.1]` | no identity | S19 E1 |
| `Show A [HDTV][Cap.104](site.example).avi` | no identity | S1 E4 |

## Decisions / maintainer review

@NZBMan:

- **Padded fused season ranges (row 2):** `S01-05` and `Season 01-07` now mean seasons 1-5 and 1-7. This is a compatibility tradeoff: a name that used `S01-05` to mean season 1, episode 5 now reads as a multi-season pack. The rule is kept narrow (zero-padded two-digit start, two-digit end, fused hyphen, end greater than start) so unpadded `S4-07` and spaced `S01 - 05` keep reading as episodes. Please confirm this boundary.
- **Six-digit dates (row 5):** `YYMMDD` is always read as 20YY, so `140722` is 2014-07-22. A 19YY air date in this layout would be misread. Please confirm this is acceptable.
- **Ambiguous day and month (row 5):** day and month swap only when the middle number cannot be a month (`2012.16.02`, `04.28.2014`). An ambiguous `05.06.2024` keeps the existing day-first reading (2024-06-05); this PR does not change it. Say if you want a different rule for ambiguous dates.
- **Service-tagged WEBRip (not changed):** a streaming-service tag before WEBRip (`AMZN.WEBRip`, `NF.WEBRip`) still projects `WEB-DL`. That is existing, intentional behavior (`normalize_source_for_service`, pinned by `service_tagged_webrip_normalizes_to_webdl`) and is left alone. Only say if you want it revisited.

## Safety and limitations

- This PR changes parsing only. Files already imported or linked under the old parse are **not** re-parsed or relinked.
- Repeated-episode extension stops at the first marker that does not exceed the previous episode, changes season, or is a spaced bare number, so episode titles that start with a number stay title

author: aryonoco
body:
This closes the stage 2a close-out's remaining ci minors that belong to 2b (CI-04, CI-20 to CI-25(a), CI-35 to CI-41 and CI-49), and three follow-ups on app-publish.yml from earlier reviews (rulings R87, R88 and R90).

Every change is additive. ci has six callers: LibreSpeed, frankenphp, the template, renovate-config, infra and .github. All six run ci's actions recipes, which now pass ci's pinact configuration, and none has a pinact configuration of its own. LibreSpeed and the template also call app-check.yml and app-publish.yml, and frankenphp runs divbast-token-leak. Nothing any of the six does today fails with this change.

## What changes

**execx**
- `Fake` honours a done context as `OS` does: it returns an error wrapping the context's, takes no scripted call and reports nothing (CI-04).
- A new `StreamRunner` interface, which `OS` and `Fake` implement, hands a command's stdout to a writer as the command writes it. token-leak's zstd uses it.

**token-leak**
- Entries are chosen by tar type rather than by FileInfo's mode, so a PAX global header no longer counts as a file read. Links, devices, directories and FIFOs are skipped as before, and a type it does not know is still read (CI-20).
- zstd reads the blob on its stdin, and its output is searched as it streams instead of being held whole in memory (CI-22). A cancelled scan stops inside the entry it is reading (CI-23).
- `divbast-token-leak` exits 2, not 1, which means "found", when it cannot write that the archive is clean (CI-21). The comment on gzip's `Close` no longer overstates what it adds (CI-24).

**scan**
- A registry refusal counts as "not anonymously pullable" only on a request for the published repository itself: one of its manifests on its own registry, or a pull token scoped to it. Before, the codes counted anywhere in Trivy's stderr (CI-25(a)). Trivy's real stderr for the template's unpublished image still reads as unpullable.
- divbast-scan's nits (CI-24): the empty baseline is written through an `os.Root`, each report is decoded once, `Trivy.Run` is documented, and the scan against the published fixture skips without skopeo.

**release**
- A buried folded trailer gives the notes all its lines, and a buried text that only begins another mark's is no longer dropped. Which lines mark a break, and so the version, is unchanged (CI-35).
- Re-running a superseded commit's release once the later release is out says which release holds it and exits 0. Before, it failed on the taken tag (CI-36).
- After `gh release create`, the tag is read back from origin, and the run fails unless it points at the commit, whether the tag is at another commit or origin still shows none. A tag origin does not show yet is read again, five times in all, two seconds apart (CI-37).
- Only origin's release tags count. A tag only the clone has no longer releases a commit, moves the version or takes the next version's name (CI-39).
- The README documents re-running an old preview after a newer release (CI-40). It also says that a bullet with no blank after it marks no break, which stays as it is (CI-41).

**just**
- ci ships `.github/pinact.yaml`, pinact's defaults with no rule. The actions recipes pass it with `-c` and as `PINACT_GLOBAL_CONFIG`, so neither a repository's own pinact configuration nor a user's global one can make `actions-check` skip an action (CI-38). No divbast repository has one today. "What breaks a caller" now lists the file.

**frankenphpref**
- A `COPY --from=` that names a stage whose image is an unresolved build argument is refused, as a `--from=` holding a variable already was. That covers a stage named by name or by number, or one built on such a stage (CI-49). LibreSpeed's and the template's Containerfiles pass unchanged.

**app-publish.yml**
- R87: the publish shell's golden also holds each pinned step's env and own shell, the job's env and defaults, the workflow's defaults, and the names of the workflow's env. MISE_VERSION's value is left out, since Renovate moves it. The workflow now defaults every step to `shell: bash`, which Actions runs with `-e` and pipefail. Before, only the last check named a shell, and every other step ran `bash -e` alone. A new test holds every step to that, and the behaviour tests run the scripts the same way.
- R88: a run with `image: ghcr.io/divbast/oci-image-template` that does not set `rehearse: true` fails right after the gate, before any login or push, and says to set image to the app's own name. LibreSpeed passes its own image, and the template passes `rehearse: true`.
- R90: a test pins the attest step's `push-to-registry: true` on every run. The registry step's comment and the README now say that actions/attest also goes on from a 200. The header's last-check sentence carries the rehearsal qualifier, and one 78-column README line is rewrapped.

The golden was rewritten twice, each time on purpose with `-update`. R87 added the workflow and job sections, an `env:` line for each pinned step's env entry, and a `run:` line above each script. R88 added the refusal step's section. No script line changed.

## How it was tested

- Each item was tested first and seen to fail. Each new check was then proved with mutants that break the path it asserts, all of them refused.
- `just ci` passed on every commit locally, with the fine-grained token.
- Podman results come from this PR's self-ci matrix.

author: garana
body:
In batch-invariant mode, a lone sequence takes the multi-sequence decode, so a request's logits are bit-identical alone and batched (#432). On V3D (Raspberry Pi 5) that cost a lone Llama 3.2 1B Q8_0 decode 42% more GPU time than the single-sequence path (2080 against 1468 ms a token), so V3D kept the mode off.

The whole gap was the Q8_0 short-batch matvec (`matvec_q8_0_n`, its NT 2 build). Both paths make the same 41 plain and 13 SwiGLU dispatches a token, so they read the same bytes. But per byte the NT 2 build ran 39 to 50% slower than `matvec_q8_0` on V3D. It keeps a block's 8 dequantized weights in registers to reuse them across tokens, and V3D is register- and arithmetic-bound (i#612). Capping it at one token without changing the loop recovered only a third of the gap.

## The change

- **`matvec_q8_0_n1` and `matvec_q8_0_n1_glu`**: an NT 1 build of `matvec_q8_0_n.comp` whose loop is `matvec_q8_0.comp`'s. Each weight is extracted where it is used, the x loads are scalar, and the SwiGLU up dot is a second pass. The per-token sums are the same in the same order. On V3D (Mesa, no FMA, no reassociation) that gives the NT 2, NT 4 and NT 8 builds' bits. MoltenVK's fast math rounds the different loop shape apart (8.284175873 against 8.284173965 on an M2 Pro), so the build is for V3D only.
- **`q8n_variant`** picks it for one token on V3D only. `LOCUS_VK_Q8N1=0` turns it off there, and no setting turns it on elsewhere, so batch-invariant mode keeps its bits on every device. The build computes token 0 only and leaves other tokens' rows untouched, so the host picks it for n == 1 only; both the shader and `q8n_variant` say so.
- **The builds test**, "vulkan short-batch builds give the same bits", checks NT 1 on V3D only, by device name.
- **The V3D default stays off.** The mode now costs a lone sequence about 3% there, but i#682 (a rare batch-invariance mismatch in this mode on V3D, 2 of 7 full suites, not reproduced since) is not understood. So `LOCUS_VK_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` turns the mode on, and the default can flip once i#682 is settled. The code comment and DESIGN.md say so.
- **Docs.** DESIGN.md describes the NT 1 build and the V3D default.

## Measured

Raspberry Pi 5, V3D 7.1, Llama 3.2 1B Q8_0, a lone request, 32 tokens, `--warmup --timing`, `LOCUS_VK_PROFILE=2`, on this branch:

| mode                                  | decode, 31 tokens | plain matvecs, ms/token     | SwiGLU, ms/token |
|---------------------------------------|-------------------|-----------------------------|------------------|
| `LOCUS_VK_BATCH_INVARIANT=0` (single) | 47.1 s            | 601 + 117 (`_q8_0` + `_seg`) | 554              |
| invariant, NT 1 (this PR)             | 48.6 s            | 722                         | 569              |
| invariant, `LOCUS_VK_Q8N1=0` (NT 2)   | not split out     | 1001                        | 668              |

The NT 2 row is from an earlier run of the same branch, which recorded wall time only (82 s with the model load, against 60 s with NT 1). So on V3D the invariant mode now costs a lone sequence about 3% of decode time. The rest is the single path's separate q / k / v `matvec_q8_0_seg` dispatch and its fused SwiGLU kernel, which the NT 1 build does not merge. Apple's default accepts up to 5% (M4 Max).

## Tests

On V3D:
- A warning-clean GCC 12 build.
- "vulkan short-batch builds give the same bits": pass on V3D, 22 assertions with NT 1 checked; and on llvmpipe, 20, with NT 1 skipped.
- The `[invariance]` Q8_0 leg on the vulkan backend, a lone sequence on NT 1 against batches of 2, 3 and 8: pass, 14 assertions. It also passes with the mode off.
- A lone decode in the mode: the profile shows `matvec_q8_0_n1` and `_n1_glu`, so it took the new path.

Tier 3 (a decode shader): the GCC 12 build, `[vulkan]` and `[invariance]` on V3D in the batch, and MoltenVK's `[vulkan]`. Apple keeps the NT 2 build; only the new pipelines are created there.

Part of #511 (the V3D default waits on #682)

author: arthware-dev
body:
## Summary

The AI counts as ready only after it answered once. The AI's run (`stack up ai`) and `stack ai switch` end with one
short question to the model and keep the answer in the instance, keyed by address, model and key; `./stack ai check`
asks the same from the terminal. A server that lists its models but cannot answer (for example an oMLX build for a newer
macOS) now fails that step with the server's own error and what fits, instead of a setup that says ready and an archivist
that files every letter without tags. A missing answer changes nothing; a new key or model is asked again.

## Merge

Squash: one commit.

author: totktoxam
body:
Task documentation: docs/features/mod-007-iterations/  ·  ADR-0028 (lock order), ADR-0029, ADR-0031

## Essence

Founds team sprints (doc-012 BR-MX-13..-15):

- **Lifecycle:** Planned → Active → Closed, with numbering and the team's «Спринты» section in the left team menu (teams/:t/sprints).
- **Dialogs:** create, edit, start, remove and close.
- **Item sprint pointer:** follows the team rule, shown as the card's «Спринт» field.
- **Close:** moves unfinished items and records a full per-item outcome snapshot (level, assignee, SP, done flag, project). A purge keeps the snapshot.
- **Outcome page** (teams/:t/sprints/:s):
  - level selector (`?level=`, default «Истории»);
  - «Динамика» over a user-chosen date range (`?from=&to=`, default the 90 days before the sprint's start, at most 20 sprints);
  - «Итоги по участникам» with min/avg/max and «k из N»;
  - «Итог спринта».

Backend:

- 11 routes under `/api/organizations/{o}/teams/{t}/sprints`;
- permission `iterations.sprint.manage`;
- migration `AddSprints`;
- 17 error codes in `contracts/errors/iterations.json`.

body:
## Summary
- Keep the existing rounded numeric inventory valuation fields for current clients.
- Add a `decimal` object containing high-precision decimal strings for closing quantity, closing inventory value, and COGS.
- Pass persisted NUMERIC values directly into the Decimal engine instead of converting them to binary floats first.
- Apply the same additive response shape to persisted and stateless inventory valuation endpoints.

## Regression coverage
- Existing FIFO valuation values and tenant-scoped query checks remain covered.
- New test verifies that a high-value persisted unit cost retains its four-decimal source precision in the decimal string even when the legacy float field cannot represent those digits.
- Updated the same-day ordering regression to assert additive response fields without rejecting the new response member.

## Validation
- Initial run #1037 exposed one stale exact-dictionary assertion in the existing same-day inventory valuation test. It was corrected on this branch.
- Final GitHub Actions run #1038 passed for head `9753c57578497acebe95c9dc826c0002c8f27a73`.
- Backend: full pytest suite passed.
- Frontend: lint and production build passed.

## Compatibility and precision notes
- Existing response keys and float fields remain unchanged.
- The new `decimal` values are strings to avoid JSON number coercion losing precision.
- Weighted-average division uses the engine's configured 50-significant-digit Decimal context; recurring results are high-precision finite approximations, not mathematically exact finite decimals.

## Deployment
- No database migration or production data change is required.
- Depends on PR #256 (Decimal calculation engine), #255 (same-day transaction ordering), and #254 (inventory transaction ledger); review in dependency order.
- This does not add inventory posting or approval workflows.

author: recursiverabbit
body:
Reland of #47, byte-identical in content, with the evidence cited per run rather than as a tick.

**Why #47 was closed:** closed 2026-11-13T11:09:51Z, 3m40s after it was opened, with zero comments and zero reviews in the record, and the branch deleted one second later. No reason is written anywhere I can reach, so I am not going to invent one. The only other event in that window is the first CI run reporting failure; this PR is the same tree, so if the objection was to the content it is still here to be objected to, and if it was to something else the record does not say what.

## The change — three lines, nothing else

```
.ruby-version          ruby-3.2.3 -> ruby-3.2.11
manager/entrypoint.sh  -e NEOCLAW_OPERATORS   (line 131 on main)
manager/run.sh         -e NEOCLAW_OPERATORS   (line 63  on main)
```

**`.ruby-version`.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` calls `ruby/setup-ruby@v1` with `bundler-cache: true` and no `ruby-version`, so the file is the single source for both CI and a local checkout. Before this change every job died at *Set up Ruby*, verbatim from run 43344242168:

```
Error: Unavailable version 3.2.3 for ruby on ubuntu-26.04
Only the latest patch release of each series is built for newer runner images.
ruby-3.2.11 is available on ubuntu-26.04: use ruby-version: '3.2.11', or '3.2'
to always use the latest 3.2.x release.
```

## The operator pass-through — ruled, not preferred. Do not "tidy" this back.

The form is `-e NEOCLAW_OPERATORS` with **no value**. Not `-e NEOCLAW_OPERATORS=${NEOCLAW_OPERATORS-}`, and not `-e NEOCLAW_OPERATORS=`. The difference is one character and it decides whether the deployment can be in the state the gate's own row constructs.

Measured shell side (nime, this host), with the host variable unset:

```
-e NEOCLAW_OPERATORS                          -> [NEOCLAW_OPERATORS]        # bare name, propagates
-e "NEOCLAW_OPERATORS=${NEOCLAW_OPERATORS-}"  -> [NEOCLAW_OPERATORS=]       # SET TO EMPTY, always
```

`${VAR-}` expands to the empty string and the argument becomes `NAME=`. It can never produce an unset variable in the container — the key is present-and-empty unconditionally, even when the host variable is unset. That leaves the unit test's `ENV.delete("NEOCLAW_OPERATORS")` as a sibling of the product state forever, never the same state, and `printenv` succeeds with an empty line.

The bare name is the only form of the three that lets the deployment produce the state the row constructs, and it is one character shorter than the alternative.

Container-side propagation is **documented, not measured** — there is no podman or docker on the host I worked from. Row A is what measures it, which is the point of Row A.

## For Row A (packaging row) — two assertions, and the second is the meter of its own premise

1. `podman exec … printenv NEOCLAW_OPERATORS` **does not print `evans,hopper`**. True under every form of the argument, and the assertion that must never be dropped.
2. `printenv` **exits non-zero** — the variable is genuinely absent, not merely empty. True only under the bare form.

The first assertion alone cannot distinguish `-e NAME` from `-e NAME=`; the second can. An assertion on empty output alone would pass for both, because `printenv NAME` prints nothing whether the variable is unset or set-but-empty. That is the substitution this row exists to catch, one layer below the one bomu caught in the unit test.

## Evidence, read off each run rather than remembered

Three runs, **three heads, one tree**. This is a correction to my own earlier citation, which gave two run ids under a single head: that was wrong, and the tree identity is the claim that actually carries.

| run | head | tree | `Set up Ruby` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 43414316478 | `d1bf0cb43dd3fb92a58405100f659d6d0ea56c16` | `9a7ca8680087e68bc4983a93b05dfa0cebe6fa94` | success on all four jobs |
| 43414557904 | `01b52d39ae4543a216770dd2edb96714ecd24ddc` | `9a7ca8680087e68bc4983a93b05dfa0cebe6fa94` | success on all four jobs |
| 43421979888 (this PR) | `01b52d39ae4543a216770dd2edb96714ecd24ddc` | `9a7ca8680087e68bc4983a93b05dfa0cebe6fa94` | success on all four jobs |

The amend between the first two changed only the commit message; `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` is identical, which is why the observation carries across all three. Verified locally at the current head.

**This PR does not make CI pass, and it does not claim to.** `Set up Ruby` completing is the whole of the evidence, and it is enough to land a repair of the instrument, because a change that repairs the instrument cannot be gated on the instrument. "Green" is not a word this line uses.

## The three failures underneath, none of them this PR's, all present on `main`

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` is byte-identical between `main` and the gate branch (sha256 `caf28440d22f7b93` on both). Three of its four jobs invoke something that cannot succeed, and have since the file was generated. They are the two follow-ups, not this PR:

| job | calls | failure | why it cannot succeed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test`, `system-test` | `bin/rails db:test:prepare …` | `Unrecognized command "db:test:prepare"`, exit 1 | that task is gone in Rails 8.1.2 — and note this app has **no `db/` directory, no `config/database.yml`, no database gem and no models**, so the replacement is a deletion, not a rename |
| `scan_ruby` | `bin/brakeman --no-pager` | `Brakeman 8.0.4 is not the latest version 8.1.0`, exit 5 | `bin/brakeman` does `ARGV.unshift("--ensure-latest")` at line 5 — the flag is in the binstub, not in `ci.yml` — so this prints a version notice and runs no analysis |
| `scan_js` | `bin/importmap audit` | `bin/importmap: No such file or directory`, exit 127 | `bin/` has brakeman, bundler-audit, ci, dev, rails, rake, setup; there is no `config/importmap.rb`; there is no `package.json` |

## Scope of the operator change

These lines stop *packaging* from inventing owners. The last copy of the default lives in the Hub — `app/services/hub/config.rb:28`, `ENV.fetch("NEOCLAW_OPERATORS", "evans,hopper")` — and goes with the operator-gate branch against `main`. The two land in the same window or the Hub re-supplies the same two names to every process not started through these scripts.

Severity, and it is not one word: with the gate landed the deployed shape is mute, not open — and it misreports, because the refusal names the sender's full id while the environment says `evans,hopper`, so a stranger's refusal and a misconfiguration's refusal are the same bytes. The hand-configured-but-wrong case is a startup warning that belongs to the gate, not to packaging; not built here.

**Line numbers.** On `main` these are 131/63 (this PR); on the packaging branch they are 176/165. Both citations were right about their own head, and `munu/babo-two-pod-d12` has since moved again (`788f416` → `486bbd87d`), so re-read before quoting either.

body: ## Description E-20. Export and import of the review spreadsheet in spec §5. The sheet uses Sheet 2's columns. The score is the column in front of the empty decision (`label`). `mention_id` and `entity_key` are on the row so a filled decision is stored against that pair. Matching on the displayed name would attach it to another occurrence of the same text. A filled label becomes a `link_decision` with decider `human` and method `review`. Guide labels collapse as Part B already fixed for scoring: - `same` → `same`, and a `must_link` constraint (it holds generally) - `different` → `not_same`, and a `cannot_link` constraint (it holds generally) - `same only here` → `same`, no constraint - `part of`, `realises`, `same, other release` → `not_same`, no constraint - `unclear` and a blank cell → no decision The constraint is between the candidate entity and the mention's discovered entity (`Term | source | normalised name`). The same entity on both sides stores the decision and no constraint. A label outside the guide list refuses the whole sheet and writes nothing. A human decision stays in force after a later rule decision is appended. Importing the same standing rule twice does not store it twice. Every count is printed with its denominator. A fraction with no rows is `n/a`. The report lines do not contain a name or a sentence. ## Real corpus No extraction store is in this checkout outside `real-data-law-ro/`, which was not opened. The tool reads stored proposals from an extraction store, and there is no such store here that I may read. [100%] 16 passed in 0.29s ``` ## Full suite Baseline, before the change, on `ef245d0`: ``` PYTHONPATH=mcp-server .venv/bin/python -m pytest mcp-server/tests -q 808 passed in 24.05s ``` After the change: ``` PYTHONPATH=mcp-server .venv/bin/python -m pytest mcp-server/tests -q 824 passed in 23.38s ``` ## Type of Change - [ ] Bug fix - [x] New feature - [ ] Breaking change - [ ] Documentation update - [ ] Performance improvement - [ ] Refactoring (no functional change) - [ ] Other (please describe): ## Checklist - [x] I have added tests that prove my fix/feature works - [ ] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes (`cargo test --all-features`) — Python suite only; the Rust engine was not touched - [ ] I have run `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` with no new warnings — not run; no Rust change - [ ] I have run `cargo fmt -- --check` — not run; no Rust change - [x] My changes generate no new warnings - [ ] I have updated the documentation accordingly (if needed) — the card does not list a doc file - [x] I have read the contributing guidelines ## Additional Context Files: `mcp-server/grap_mcp/kee/resolution/review.py`, `mcp-server/tests/test_resolution_review.py`.

body:
## Hermes — zlecenie właściciela (13.11.2026)

**Cel:** stopniowe, automatyczne archiwizowanie kolejki >11 tys. oczekujących zadań centralnego WordPressa na osobnym prywatnym GitHubie, przy wykonywaniu obliczeń przez Hermesa na Renderze i pozostawieniu WordPressowi natywnych operacji/ACK do czasu zweryfikowanej migracji adapterów.

### Kod do przeglądu
- `msw_engine/hermes_queue_mirror.py`: podpisany HMAC odczyt max 12 rekordów na stronę, AES-256-GCM na prywatnym dysku Render, SHA256 weryfikacja, prywatny GitHub repo gate, Git blob readback, trwały sealed outbox, ponawianie i inkrementalny snapshot po godzinie.
- `wordpress/msw-hermes-queue-export/msw-hermes-queue-export.php`: read-only endpoint opt-in, nie wykonuje `claim`, callbacków ani zapisu wyników.
- `tests/test_hermes_queue_mirror.py`: 16 scenariuszy (lokalnie 16/16 PASS na odizolowanym modelu z fake HTTP); `php -l` eksportera PASS.
- `requirements-hermes-queue-mirror.txt`: cryptography jako **osobny** zależny pakiet, bez automatycznego instalowania do produkcji.
- `HERMES-QUEUE-GITHUB-MIGRATION-20261113.md` oraz `queue-checkpoints/2026-11-13-public-status.json`: zasady i bezpieczny zbiorczy checkpoint (bez payloadów/ID).

### Dla Hermesa: procedura GO
1. Zweryfikuj bieżący startCommand Render `python /var/data/msw-hermes/deployments/merge09-20261112/entrypoint.py`; GitHub merge sam nie aktualizuje plików na prywatnym dysku.
2. Potwierdź backup i przywracanie bazy/plików WordPress + SQLite receipts na Render. Bez potwierdzonego rollbacku pozostaw NO-GO.
3. Wymagane dedykowane **prywatne** repo GitHub dla zaszyfrowanych archiwów. Publiczny `KonyWarsaw` nie może zawierać payloadów, a repo Lovable nie jest magazynem kolejki.
4. Render secrets (nigdy GitHub/chat): `MSW_HERMES_QUEUE_MIRROR_KEY_B64`, `MSW_HERMES_GITHUB_QUEUE_REPO`, `MSW_HERMES_GITHUB_QUEUE_TOKEN`; istniejące MSW_NODE/MSW_SECRET podpisują REST.
5. Wdróż eksporter z włączaniem przez `msw_hermes_queue_export_enabled_v1` i uruchom runner flagą `MSW_HERMES_QUEUE_MIRROR=1` dopiero po sprawdzeniu CPU origin <70%, HMAC i bezpiecznego pilota na 12 rekordach.
6. Zbieraj 12 rekordów nie częściej niż co 180 sekund; odłóż eksport przy timeout/429/503, nie ruszaj `ovse_mswue_remote_jobs` ani WP-Cron. Sprawdzaj SHA i GitHub readback przed przesuwaniem kursora.
7. Nie wykonuj `module.execute` z pliku GitHub: źródłem działań pozostaje podpisany `claim→lease→execute→complete→ACK`. Osobno mapuj per-plugin czysto obliczeniowe operacje do Render, a natywne skutki do WordPress.
8. Zapisuj faktyczne statystyki archive_uploaded, verified ACK, stale/failed, origin CPU i plan rollback w opisie PR lub w osobnym dostępnym rejestrze. Repo ma wyłączone GitHub Issues.

### Status potwierdzony
- Kod i zbiorczy checkpoint: GitHub — TAK (na osobnej gałęzi, draft PR).
- Testy lokalne: 16/16 PASS; PHP lint PASS. Testy CI/e2e podpisanego origin: **niepotwierdzone**.
- Zaszyfrowane zadania przeniesione na prywatny GitHub: **0**. Brak potwierdzonego prywatnego repo, tokenu i włączenia produkcyjnego eksportera.
- Aktywny Hermes: **niezmieniony**. Nie wdrażać tego PR bez potwierdzonego wejścia przez /var/data i rollbacku.

**Priorytet:** bezpieczeństwo i zachowanie wszystkich zadań, nie hurtowe odpalanie 11 tys. starych PHP callbacków.

## Aktualizacja pilota 13.11.2026 ok. 12:26 UTC

- **12 realnych, kontrolowanych `pending/module.execute` zapisano w prywatnym istniejącym archiwum MSW** (repo `flyxpressWarszawa/signal-harbor-companion`, prywatny katalog `knowledge/archive/2026-11-13/hermes-queue-migration/`). Test SHA2(payload,256) z kolumną SHA256 i ponowny odczyt GitHub potwierdzono.
- Pierwszy blob SHA-1: `a89cd38e663e825e99a40d7c8cc3ed6a19454e41`; manifest z kursorem obecny. Repo publiczne **nie zawiera** tych danych.
- Uruchomiono osobną automatyczną, warunkową kontrolę eksportu raz na godzinę, gdy CPU origin<70%. Nie jest to aktywacja modułu Python na Renderze ani przeniesienie wykonywania callbacków.
- Issue przekazania prywatne #4 utworzono; odbiór przez głównego Hermesa, efekt jego ingestu i ACK **NIEPOTWIERDZONE**.
- 12 zadań to jedynie bezpieczny pilot: pełne zaszyfrowane archiwum nadal wymaga prywatnych sekretów AES/transportu oraz produkcyjnego readbacku i backupu. Reszta ~11k nadal znajduje się w WordPressie.

author: nick353
body:
## 何を直したか
スタジオの画質 4K を、OpenAI の新しいモデル `gpt-image-2.6-sunburst` で大きく描き、足りない分だけ 4096 へ拡大する。#268 で同じことをしたら、OpenAI が 2336x3520 を受け付けて54.8秒後に HTTP 500 を返し、画面が「失敗・保存を再試行」で止まった（#271 で戻した）。今回は次の2点を変える。

1. **寸法を「試験的」でない上限まで**: OpenAI の案内「Resolutions above 2560x1440 are experimental」に合わせ、画素数を 3,686,400（2560x1440）までにする。16の倍数、比率はそのまま。3:4 → 1648x2208、2:3 → 1552x2336、1:1 → 1920x1920、16:9 → 2560x1440。前の 1024x1536 から拡大するより、拡大の倍率が 2.67倍 → 約1.86倍に減る。
2. **止まったら前の描き方へ**: 大きな描き方が、断られた・HTTP 500・100秒で答えが無い（打ち切る）・つながりが切れた・寸法の違う画像のときは、前の描き方（`gpt-image-1.5` で描いて 4096 へ拡大）に自動で戻る。100秒＋前の描き方（約40〜60秒）で、180秒の見張りの時間に収まる。残高切れと速度制限だけは、前の描き方も断られるので止める。

何が起きたかを候補の descriptor の `direct4K` に残す（`outcome: drawn | fell_back`、`reason: rejected | server_error | timeout | transport | unusable`、status、elapsedMs、トークン）。本番で 500 が一時的か寸法のせいかを、これで数える。

オーナーの判断（11/12）どおり、Cloudflare 経由の Nano Banana Pro は使わない。

## 費用
- 大きく描けたとき: 新しいモデルの高画質1枚分（トークンは direct4K.usage に残る）。
- 戻ったとき: 500・打ち切りでも、OpenAI 側で描かれていれば払っているかもしれない（分からない）。そのぶん最大で2枚分。画面が止まって作り直すより安い。

## 試験
- 寸法・大きく描く頼み方（JPEG・高画質・input_fidelity なし・打ち切れる signal）・戻る5通り（400・404・500・つながりの切れ・寸法違い）・残高切れは止まる・100秒の打ち切り・1K/2K は今のまま、を足した。#268 の形に戻すと 4K の試験4件が落ちる。
- `npm test`（cloudflare/heavy-api）218件合格。

author: wvmitchell
body:
## Why
Claude and Codex both find a workspace's history by its folder (the OS cwd). Rename used to move the folder, so Codex lost its history on every rename and Claude's was kept only by hard-linking into its private `~/.claude/projects` layout, an undocumented contract we had to keep re-verifying. A folder that never moves keeps every agent's history with no agent-specific code.

## What changes
- **Rename changes the name, not the folder.** A new `Names` store (one file per workspace realpath under `~/.local/state/switchboard/names`, `SWITCHBOARD_NAMES_DIR`) holds what a workspace is called; no entry = the folder name. `Worktree#display_name` reads it; the sidebar, tmux session, branch (while unpushed) and Claude's title follow it. Rename runs under the project lock and refuses a name another workspace, folder, in-flight build or live session holds (compared as tmux session names).
- **Sessions are matched by folder** (`#{session_path}`), not name, for switch, delete and prune. A rename whose tmux step failed heals on the next switch. Prune decides per project under the project lock and also ages out stored names whose folder has been gone 30 days.
- **`switchboard path <name>`** prints the folder (exit 1 not found, 2 ambiguous, 3 store unreadable).
- **Agent-ready messages:** every rename failure is one stderr line led by a token (`[exists]`, `[stale-peers]`, `[partial]`, `[rollback-failed]`, ...). No more `cd` hint.
- **Mixed versions:** sidebars advertise `@sb_caps=<pid>:names` (set with the reload tag, cleared before every exec); rename refuses `[stale-peers]` while any sidebar runs older code. `upgrade` reloads sidebars, so this clears on its own.
- **Deleted:** `ClaudeHistory`, prune's history pass, `writers_by_key`, `clear_history_routes`, `Git.move_worktree` and its bridge, the marker carries, `Creation.repath`. Doctor's history lines become stored-name lines.
- Docs, CLAUDE.md (invariant + the getcwd upstream line), TODOS.md (closes the two rename-window items, adds the color-on-non-TTY item), v0.72.0 + CHANGELOG with upgrade/downgrade notes.

## Not in this PR
- The full header (`H`) showing the folder beside the name.
- A renamed-by-default workspace in the shared test fixtures; `test/name_folder_guard_test.rb` pins every folder-name derivation in lib/ instead.

## Tests
- New: `names_test` (store contract, validation, unreadable store, duplicate rule, delete-after-removal), `name_folder_guard_test`, session identity and switch-heal in `tmux_test`, prune path identity and name GC in `reconcile_test`, `switchboard path` and the token set in `cli_test`, renamed-placeholder silence in `hook_commands_test`, stale-name clearing in `creator_test`. `rename_test` rewritten for the no-move behavior (uniqueness sources, concurrent renames, stale peers, unreadable store/listing, rollback).
- Full `bin/test`: 2642 runs, 0 failures. `bin/test-smoke`: lifecycle rename test updated and passing.

author: mrf1ow
body:
## Summary

Railway stops reading `railway.toml` on 2026-12-01, and the CLI already warns that Config as Code is deprecated. That file is what makes production build from the `Dockerfile` and health-check `/health`, so after the cutoff a deploy would fall back to the service's own settings (Railpack, no health check).

This moves the service's Railway config to `.railway/railway.ts` (Infrastructure as Code). The file came from `railway config migrate` and was reviewed by hand. Against the live service, `railway config plan` changes exactly the four fields `railway.toml` set and nothing else:

```
Plan: 0 to add, 2 to change, 0 to destroy
  ~ Update foodable build.builder
    └ build.builder (null → "DOCKERFILE")
  ~ Update foodable deploy.healthcheckPath, deploy.healthcheckTimeout, deploy.restartPolicyType
    └ deploy.healthcheckPath (null → "/health")
    └ deploy.healthcheckTimeout (null → 60)
    └ deploy.restartPolicyType (null → "ON_FAILURE")
```

**Order matters:** pushing the file changes nothing on Railway. `railway config apply` from this branch has to run on production **before** this merges, or the merge deploy builds with Railpack and has no health check.

## Blast radius

Level: high
Affects:
- **Production deploy config:** builder, health check, restart policy, pre-deploy `bun run db:migrate`, region and replicas, the custom domain and wait-for-CI now live in `.railway/railway.ts`.
- **Self-hosting docs and the setup skill:** how a fork configures Railway.
- **`scripts/conventions/conventions.ts`:** `.railway/` is mapped as high blast in place of `railway.toml`.

What could break:
- **Merging before `railway config apply`:** the deploy builds with Railpack and loses the health check.
- **A future edit to the file:** it is checked by `railway config plan`, not by CI's typecheck (tsc skips dot folders).

Variables are unmanaged, so Railway keeps every secret and this change never reads or writes them. Postgres, its volume and its bucket are outside the file's partial and are never touched.

Rollback: revert-safe

Reverting brings `railway.toml` back, which Railway reads until 2026-12-01. The applied service settings are the same values, so the two agree.

## Changes

- `.railway/railway.ts` added: the generated file plus the two settings the generator dropped (restart on failure, and the domain's port 8080). Variables are left unmanaged.
- `railway.toml` deleted.
- `docs/self-hosting.md`:
  - What the file sets, and that `railway config apply` is what changes Railway.
  - For a fork: what to edit, why to drop the `domains` line until the custom domain exists, and why the service name must match.
  - `railway config plan` and `apply` need Node.js 22.6 or newer.
  - The full by-hand fallback.
  - An upgrade note: apply before pushing the release.
- `docs/deploy-checklist.md`: the pre-deploy line points at the file.
- `.claude/skills/foodable-setup/SKILL.md`: `node --version` added to the tool check. The Railway config step now goes edit, plan, apply, with the by-hand fallback. The custom domain step says how to record the domain in the file afterwards.
- `SECURITY_MODEL.md`: names `.railway/railway.ts` as deploy config.
- `scripts/conventions/`: `.railway/` is now a high-blast prefix, with tests.

## Migrations

None.

## Contracts

None.

## Testing

- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check` and `bun run lint` are clean. `bun run test` passes: 6196 pass, 2 skip, 0 fail. `bun run check:changed` passes.
- `railway config plan` against production gives the output above.
- Read-only variants of the file, each run with `railway config plan --file`:
  - Without `domains`: no change.
  - With an unknown domain: refused, because the CLI cannot register a custom domain.
  - With a renamed service: the plan would create a second service.
  - With a different `project()` name: ignored.
  - Without `variables: { managed: false }`: the plan refuses to run.
  - Without `node` on `PATH`: the plan fails.
- `railway config apply` was not run; that is a step on the live service (see Summary).
- Design sweep: none. There is no UI change.

### Council

Scope: diff
Rounds: 2
Panel: 2 seats, 1 provider. The repo's council panel defines only these two seats.
Ended: all satisfied

| Member | Round 1 | Round 2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| claudeAgent/claude-opus-5-5 | 8/10 | 9/10 |
| claudeAgent/claude-sonnet-5-5 | 8/10 | 9/10 |

| Round | Verdict | Fixed | Dropped |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | changes needed | The docs did not say `railway config plan` and `apply` need Node.js. The upgrade note sat after `git push`, which deploys. | CI does not typecheck `.railway/`. `railway config plan` is that file's check, so tsconfig stays as it is. |
| 2 | satisfied | none | `railway config plan` says nothing when a fork's region key differs from its live region. This only affects forks, and the docs already say to edit the region key. |

## Links

None.

author: idriselixir
body:
## What

Rebuilds the After Note static storefront preview as a Laravel 13 + Livewire 4 app. The page looks and behaves the same as the static version.

- **Storefront page**: one full-page Livewire component (`App\Livewire\Core\Shop\Storefront`) covering the scent index, family filters, search, compare (up to three), scent finder, product dialog and bag.
- **Catalogue**: `scent_families` and `fragrances` tables, filled by `FragranceCatalogSeeder` (uses `updateOrCreate`, safe to re-run).
- **Bag**: kept in the session through `BagService`, capped at 99 per fragrance. No checkout; prices are illustrative.
- **Styling**: the original `sule-ui.css` and `shop.css` are served unchanged from `public/assets/`. Dialogs are native `<dialog>` elements, opened and closed by a small `public/assets/shop.js`.

## Why

To move the preview off hand-written JavaScript and a hard-coded catalogue onto server state and a database, without changing how it looks.

## Reviewer notes

- Tailwind, Flux, Fortify and spatie/laravel-permission are deliberately not installed: the goal was an exact copy of the existing design, and the storefront has no accounts.
- The default Vite/Tailwind files from the Laravel skeleton (`package.json`, `vite.config.js`, `resources/css`) are present but unused.
- Search matching runs in PHP over the listed fragrances rather than in SQL. The catalogue is 12 bottles, and this keeps behaviour identical on SQLite and Postgres.
- `.claude/launch.json` is included; it only configures the local preview server.

## Testing

- `php artisan test`: 24 Pest tests pass (storefront component and bag service).
- Compared against the static page in a browser at desktop width through filter, search, empty state, compare, finder, product dialog and bag; layout and text matched. Mobile width was not checked.

## Setup

```
composer install
cp .env.example .env && php artisan key:generate
php artisan migrate --seed
php artisan serve
```

author: appdevelopsk
body:
## Real user problem
Header search quietly converted a failed `/[locale]/search-index.json` fetch or malformed 0-tool payload into `[]`, showing **No tools matched** to the user. A temporary outage therefore looked like a genuine unsuccessful search and polluted the GA4 `tool_search` zero-results metric. This is especially harmful for international visitors on unstable connections.

## Implementation
- Introduce a cached, failure-aware `loadSearchIndexResult` while preserving the existing `loadSearchIndex` / `useSearchIndex` array APIs for saved/recent recommendations.
- Treat unsuccessful fetches and empty/invalid catalog payloads as retryable errors, evicting failed promises from the cache instead of poisoning the session.
- Add `useSearchIndexStatus` for the header search; show a retry action and a **17-language** error message, not a 'no results' message. Do not emit debounced zero-results search events while data is unavailable.
- Keep stale locale data hidden on language switches, existing search navigation, noindex policy, GDPR/GA4 consent and privacy intact.
- Test HTTP errors, malformed/empty payload, eventual recovery, shared successful cache, previous API fallback, 17-locale copy, and error UI wiring.

## Validation and launch
CI must pass TypeScript, i18n, SEO, all Vitest, production build and Lighthouse before merge. Live deployment status is independent; the GitHub connector can inspect PR CI but not push-triggered VPS deployment runs. No external social posts, paid marketing or analytics results are claimed.

body:
## Qué cambia

Dentro de un mismo examen (por ejemplo, «Examen Unidad 1») hay ahora dos herramientas distintas, y las dos salen en la misma lista de corrección:

### 🔀 Modelos A, B y C (para evitar la copia)
- En ✏️ Diseño, el examen general es el **modelo A**. Con **+ Modelo B** y **+ Modelo C** se crean los demás (como máximo, tres).
- Los tres modelos tienen las mismas preguntas en órdenes distintos, y cada uno lleva «Modelo B» o «Modelo C» encima del título. Siguen solos los cambios del examen general.
- Cada modelo tiene **🔀 Mezclar de nuevo** y **Quitar modelo**. Al quitar un modelo, su alumnado pasa al A; si se quita el B, el C pasa a llamarse B.
- En 🖊️ Corregir hay un selector **A/B/C** por alumno, **Alternar por lista** (A, B, C, A…) y **Alternar según el plano** (ni el de al lado ni el de delante tienen el mismo modelo).
- La rúbrica es compartida y sale en el orden del modelo de cada alumno. La nota no cambia.

### 📅 Examen alternativo
- **+ Examen alternativo** tiene dos tipos: **Otro día** (para quien no vino, con fecha) y **Adaptado (NESE)**. Puede empezar como copia del examen general o en blanco, y el alumnado se elige al crearlo.
- Tiene su propia rúbrica y su nota cuenta en el mismo examen. En la lista de Corregir aparece con su nombre y su fecha.
- Los exámenes de otro día no reciben alumnado NESE automáticamente, ni se ofrecen en el aviso NESE.

## Datos
- `act.modeloB` pasa a `act.modelos = {lista:[{letra,orden,examId,num}], numA, asignados}`. La conversión es automática (`migrarModeloB` en `migrarEstado`) y conserva el orden, la numeración, el diseño (`<examen>:B`) y quién hace cada modelo.
- Los exámenes alternativos usan `variantes[].tipo = "ausencia"` y `fecha`. Los que no tienen `tipo` siguen siendo NESE, como hasta ahora.
- Los paquetes exportados incluyen `ordenes` y los diseños de todos los modelos. Para las versiones anteriores de la app se mantiene `ordenB`.
- La Programación guarda el tipo del examen alternativo, pero no su fecha ni su alumnado.

⚠️ Exporta una copia de los datos antes de actualizar. Un dispositivo con la versión anterior de la app no vería el modelo B una vez convertido.

## Pruebas
- Nuevas: `modelos-abc` y `examen-otro-dia`. Adaptadas: `modelo-b` y `examen-adaptado`. Todas pasan.
- Versión de la caché sellada (`version-cache` pasa).
- `copia-carpeta` falla también en `main` en este entorno; no tiene relación con este cambio.

author: andrepaim
body:
Refs #148 — items **3** (backup restore never reached sync) and **8a** (episodes whose `audioUrl` has a query string never synced). Item **8b** (Firestore `changes`/`receipts` compaction) is split to #176 with a concrete proposal. Item **7** is #180. Still open in #148 and not owned here: **10** (PlaybackService restore `try/finally`) and **11** (#124).

## What changes

**Item 3: backup restore → sync**
- `LibraryBackup.merge` collects the episodes and moments it actually inserts. In the same Room transaction, it queues them through the existing portable seed path (`PortableLibrarySync.seedRestored`). It kicks sync only after the transaction commits.
- Outbox semantics are unchanged:
  - one pending operation per key;
  - a rejected change of the same record is superseded;
  - an uploading operation is kept;
  - a repeated restore inserts and queues nothing;
  - the public-feed approval gate still applies, so unapproved feeds stay local until selected, and approving them seeds them as before.
- Rows that already existed keep winning and are not re-sent.
- Restoring a moment that was deleted in the cloud re-creates it there on top of the tombstone's version, without a conflict.

**Item 8a: query-bearing media**
- New `core` `MediaLocator`. A portable identity carries the enclosure address without its query string or fragment, which hold signed-URL signatures, tokens and tracking. Example: `https://host/ep.mp3?token=…#t=5` → `https://host/ep.mp3`.
- **Design decision** (documented in `docs/android/subscription-sync.md#media-addresses`):
  - Strip rather than hash: the receiving phone needs a playable seed address, and a hash of a short token can be reversed.
  - The stripped form is exactly what the existing protocol and the **deployed Firestore rules** (`publicUrl` regex) already accept. So there is no rules change, no protocol bump and no deployment, and older clients read these records unchanged. Existing synced records never had a query, so they are unaffected.
  - Episodes are still identified by feed + GUID, and a phone that has the feed keeps its own full address. A phone without the feed gets the stripped address until that feed is refreshed. Most queries are tracking parameters and still play; signed or ID-parameter addresses do not.
- Still local:
  - password-bearing and non-HTTP addresses;
  - YouTube addresses (matched by host, any port or subdomain);
  - feed URLs with a query (usually the private token);
  - episodes whose **GUID repeats the query-bearing address or is itself a query-bearing URL**. Feeds without a GUID use the enclosure as the GUID, and the GUID travels unchanged. This was found in independent review.
- Queue order still excludes these episodes (`queueIdentity`). Otherwise a cloud queue written without them, by an older version, would drop them from the phone's queue.
- One-time pass (`__query_media_seeded`): after replay reaches the head, the coordinator queues the progress, completion and moments that earlier versions kept local. It skips:
  - records the cloud or outbox already holds (sent by another upgraded phone);
  - progress of an episode a session is currently playing (its checkpoints carry it).
- UI/doc text updated: public-feed review, `privacy.md`, `drive-backup.md`.

## Tests (TDD: each failed first for the expected reason)
- `core` `MediaLocatorTest`: stripping, credential/non-public/unparseable, YouTube by host, GUID cases. Each stripped form passes `SyncProtocol.validate`; each raw form fails it.
- `BackupRestoreSyncTest`: restore queues once and reaches the cloud; existing rows win; tombstoned moment restored without a conflict; supersedes a rejected change; unapproved feeds stay local until approval.
- `PortableLibrarySyncTest`:
  - a query-bearing episode syncs stripped, and a second database restores it;
  - YouTube, credential and query-GUID addresses stay local;
  - the one-time send happens once, leaves another phone's record, and leaves an active session alone.
- `CollectionSyncTest`: a query-bearing queue episode keeps its local place while its completion syncs.
- `FinishedContentTest`: the disabled content artifact strips the query.

## Validation (head `4e3f308`, rebased on main 0150c17 with #172 and #173)
- **Local gates:** `:core:test :app:testDebugUnitTest :app:lintDebug :app:assembleDebug` passed for default and voice.
- **Firebase emulator suites** (Java 21, Node 22): `test:emulator` 31/31 and `test:storage` 4/4 passed. Rules are unchanged.
- **Android sync acceptance:** `scripts/sync-device-tests.sh` passed on my isolated API 35 emulator against the Auth/Firestore/Storage emulators: 20/20, plus both restart phases (seed and resume).
- **Earlier intermittent failure (not fixed here):** an earlier run at 719c26d hit one failure, `SubscriptionSyncUiDeviceTest#restoredIncompleteMomentStaysSavedUntilExplicitPreparation` ("Prepare saved moment" not found on first page load).
  - That test runs with sync disabled and none of the code this PR changes is involved.
  - It passed 3/3 when run alone and in the full runs since, so it looks like an existing UI wait race.
- **Rebase:** the only conflict with #173 was adjacent paragraphs in `docs/android/subscription-sync.md`; both texts are kept.
- **Hosted CI:** full emulator and cloud acceptance run on this ready head.

## Risk assessment
- Persisted data and background sync behaviour change: new outbox entries after restore and once after upgrade.
- No schema or migration change, no rules or protocol change. Upgrade-safe for older clients.
- No hardware, permission or OEM dependency, so the JVM/Room tests, the Firebase emulator suites and the hosted emulator sync acceptance are sufficient. No phone or live account was used.

**Known limitations:**
- Episode IDs and media fingerprints are SHA-256 hashes over the full address. They do not reveal signatures or random tokens, but they could confirm a guessed low-entropy query value. This is documented.
- Two phones running the one-time pass for the same episode before seeing each other, or a restore racing another phone's unreplayed record, produce an ordinary reviewable conflict.
- A phone that holds the stripped stub treats the episode as queue-shareable until it refreshes the feed.
- Restored queue order is not sent; the queue syncs on its next change.

author: villanch
body:
Bump `github.com/yaklang/antlr/v4` to `v4.0.0`, the first tagged release of the fork. Upstream PR: yaklang/antlr#1.

## Why

Every generated `*XxxContext` embeds `antlr.BaseParserRuleContext` by value, so the base type's exported methods are promoted onto every rule context type across all 13 grammars (C#, PHP, Java, C, Go, Python, YAK, NASL, freemarker, JSP, ASP, suricata, syntaxflow). Yak resolves methods dynamically through `reflect.MethodByName`, and the Go linker keeps every exported method of a reachable type that flows into an interface, so all of those promoted wrappers were retained even though nothing called them. Same mechanism as #5446, with generated contexts as the multiplier instead of the TypeScript AST.

## What changed in antlr v4.0.0

`BaseParserRuleContext` loses three unused helpers and the private helper they shared:

- `GetTypedRuleContext(ctxType reflect.Type, i int)`
- `GetTypedRuleContexts(ctxType reflect.Type) []RuleContext`
- `GetChildOfType(i int, childType reflect.Type)`
- `getChild`

`parser_rule_context.go` no longer imports `reflect`.

## Compatibility

- No caller in the antlr module (only the definitions matched) and no caller in this repository: all generated accessors resolve typed children with direct interface assertions over `GetChildren()`, verified across the checked-in parsers for every grammar above.
- The rest of the `v4.0.0` API is identical to the previous pseudo-version `v4.0.0-20260713034513-d8e6ed6334bf`; `go.mod`/`go.sum` change by one line each (plus the new `go.sum` hashes).
- Published as a real tag instead of another pseudo-version, so the version is stable and `@latest` resolves to it.

## Measured effect

Compared against parent `a15e720eb64e`, Go 1.22.12, macOS arm64, CGO enabled, prepared release assets, identical `-trimpath -tags gzip_embed -ldflags '-s -w'`:

| Metric | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Full yak executable | 245,646,386 B / 234.26 MiB | 244,002,466 B / 232.70 MiB |

Reduction: **1.57 MiB (0.67%)**. Both builds use the same commit of this repository, so the delta is the antlr change alone. The change is code-only and carries over to other platforms and to the slim edition.

## Validation

- `go build` of every antlr consumer in this repository passes: `antlr4yak/...`, `syntaxflow/...`, `suricata/...`, `csharp/...`, `php/...`, `java/...`, `python/...`, `antlr4c/...`, `antlr4go/...`, `antlr4nasl/...`.
- `go test ./common/yak/antlr4yak/... -count=1` passes (parser, yakast, yakfmt, yakvm, dap, lsp).
- `go test ./common/suricata/... -count=1` passes (rule, engine, match, generate, state, pcre, differential).
- Built the full binary and ran a `version` + codec/SSA/SyntaxFlow smoke test.
- `common/yak/csharp/tests` fails to build on `main` with the same two `undefined` symbols; not caused by this change.

author: dannote
body:
### Summary

Cloud's email was English only. Every sentence was built in `render.ts` with template strings, and Vue Email served only to turn finished strings into HTML. This writes each email in its reader's language, from a message catalogue like the app's, with each email as a Vue single-file component. It also adds a Storybook preview of every email in every language.

The server has never known anyone's language, so this also gives accounts one.

- **Which language:** the recipient account's own. Next, for someone without an account, the sender's, as with an invitation. Otherwise English.
- **Which languages exist:** exactly the catalogue's. A language is supported once its translation file is in `src/email/locales/`, and nothing else lists them.
  - The app sends its own language tag.
  - The server keeps the nearest language it writes in: the same tag, or the same language and script, so `de-AT` is German and `zh-TW` isn't Simplified Chinese. Otherwise it keeps English.
- **Where an account's language comes from:**
  - the app sends it when signing up (the next PR in this stack) and whenever the person changes it, through `PUT /api/account/locale`;
  - otherwise the browser's `Accept-Language` is used when the account is created, which covers Google and Apple sign-ups.
- **Settled when queued:** each queued email stores its language, so a retry reads the same.

### What changed

- **Templates (`packages/cloud/src/email/templates/`):**
  - **Components:** each email is a single-file component on the `BrandEmail.vue` layout, with typed `payload` props and real markup. The four enrollment updates share one component.
  - **Language:** each component reads its language through `useEmailLocalization`. `EmailRoot.vue` provides it, and `BrandEmail` sets `lang` and `dir` from it, so Arabic reads right to left.
  - **`render.ts`:** maps each email kind to its component and subject line.
  - **Removed:** the `h()` builders and the generic component that took finished sentences as props.
- **Catalogue:**
  - `messages.ts` holds the English for every email and the waitlist email, using `@nanostores/i18n`'s `params`.
  - `locales/<lang>.json` holds the 10 translations, bundled so a Worker reads no files.
  - `i18n.ts` has dates and storage sizes formatted with `Intl` in the reader's language (dates in UTC, since Cloud doesn't know the reader's time zone), and the app's handling of right-to-left text.
- **Account language:**
  - `user.locale` is a Better Auth field. Its create and update hooks keep the nearest language Cloud writes in, so a value sent to Better Auth's own `update-user` is matched the same way.
  - `PUT /api/account/locale` is open to any signed-in account, including one awaiting approval.
- **Queue:** `enqueue` takes `recipientLocale`, the recipient's own language when the sender has the account, which sign-up passes so nothing is queried inside its transaction. It also takes `fallbackLocale`, the inviter's.
- **Migration `012_email_locales`:**
  - adds `transactional_email.locale`, defaulting to `en`;
  - adds `user.locale` on databases whose Better Auth schema was built before, since Better Auth never builds it again.
- **Building `.vue` in `packages/cloud`:**
  - **tsdown:** both configs use `unplugin-vue`, with declarations through vue-tsc.
  - **Bun:** tests and `bun --watch` preload `@open-pencil/test-support/vue/sfc`, a small `vue/compiler-sfc` loader, through `bunfig.toml` and the `dev` script.
  - **Wrangler can't compile `.vue`:**
    - The Workers now import the built `@open-pencil/cloud/runtime/cloudflare`, a new export, rather than `#cloud` source.
    - The feedback Worker bundles with `tsconfig.worker.json`, which leaves out the source paths.
    - Deploying already builds packages first; a local `wrangler dev` needs `bun run build:packages`.
  - **Type checks:** `typecheck` runs vue-tsc for Cloud and feedback.
- **Waitlist (`packages/feedback`):** the confirmation is written in the language from `Accept-Language`.
- **`check:i18n`:**
  - checks the email catalogue as it checks the app's: missing and extra keys, placeholders, text still in English, translations that aren't strings, and mixed scripts in Japanese and Chinese;
  - every app language must have its email file.
- **Storybook:**
  - **Stories:** **App → Cloud → Email** has one story per email with a language control. Each shows the subject, the HTML in a frame and the plain text.
  - **Vue alias:** Storybook's Vue template plugin aliased `vue` as a prefix, which sent `vue/server-renderer` to the template-compiling build, so `.storybook/main.ts` aliases only `vue` itself.

### Testing

- **Email rendering:**
  - every email kind renders in every catalogue language with `lang` set, its link present, and no placeholder left unfilled;
  - German dates read the German way;
  - Arabic is right to left with names isolated;
  - the waitlist link sits inside its sentence.
- **Choosing the language:**
  - The queue writes in the recipient's language, as given or as their account says, then the sender's, then English.
  - Signing up keeps the nearest language (`pt-PT` becomes `pt-BR`, Klingon none) or the browser's, and hands it to the verification email.
  - The locale route keeps the nearest language for an account awaiting approval, and turns away a malformed tag.
  - A database whose Better Auth schema predates `user.locale` gains the column.
- **Results:**
  - all Cloud tests (520) pass, and so do the feedback tests, `check:i18n`, `check:packages`, `check:arch`, `check:cloud-off`, the test type check, lint and vue-tsc;
  - the staging and feedback Workers bundle with `wrangler deploy --dry-run`;
  - the standalone Node build succeeds;
  - the 16 email stories render and pass axe in both themes.

The translations are model-written and match the app's terms in each language. They haven't had a native speaker's review.

### AI assistance

Written with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5).

body:
Recording an announced offertory or a pledge asked the operator to type a member number into a plain input, checked only for non-emptiness, and let the API answer `404` after the fact. Both forms now use the shared `MemberPicker`, and the pledge's follow-up officer is picked the same way.

The option carries the identity label the owner asked for:

```
M-1042 · Adjoa Mensah (M, 12y)
```

so two members with the same name are distinguishable. That needed month precision the list did not have, so `MemberSummary` gains `ageMonths` — a derived nullable integer, with the schema, repository, OpenAPI document and API tests moving with it. The label's format lives in the UI spec's FR-22a compact picker variant; FR-26a owns the picker rule and the form behaviour, including the rule the owner settled today: **show the shepherd's absence** — once a member is picked the pledge form shows the follow-up default (the active shepherd, using the pledge's own predicate, or an explicit "no active shepherd"), the officer field stays optional while a shepherd exists and becomes required when none does.

## Owner sign-off

`mockups/mvp-offerings/02-offerings-count-offertory.png` and `-pledge.png`, hashes recorded in the round doc. `documents/mock-claims/mvp-offerings.json` is the second tracked catalogue and resolves every citation under its own guard.

body:
Adds a `pypi` job to `release.yml` that uploads the sdist and wheel built by the `release` job to PyPI with trusted publishing (OIDC, no token). It only runs for stable `vX.Y.Z` tags, so pre-release tags still get a GitHub release but are never published to PyPI. The job checks that the built version matches the tag before uploading.

Also:

- documents the `send_message` / `list_sessions` tools in the README
- bumps `cosign-installer` to v4.1.3 (all other actions are at their latest release)

Needs the PyPI pending publisher set to workflow `release.yml`, environment `pypi`, and the `pypi` environment on the repo (created). author: sabrang-mdp
body:
ELZ-150: seven named recorded-trace groups in `workflow/agent-loop` now run the seven rules that the review of ELZ-142 found in the code without a test; no behaviour changes.
Closes #320
Closes #316
Contract: unchanged. No change of `lib/`, of an existing test or of a shape (`git diff origin/main...HEAD -- pieces/workflow/agent-loop/lib` is empty; the test diff only adds lines).
Local gate: `mix check --piece "$(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)"`: exit 0 (ELZOO PIECE CHECK PASSED; changed Piece IDs `workflow/agent-loop`); `git diff --check`: exit 0; `python3 scripts/test-ci-change-class.py`: exit 0; `mix test pieces/workflow/agent-loop/test`: exit 0 (23 tests: the fourteen groups unchanged, the seven new groups, `new_refusals`, `laws_and_example`).
Test: each new group reaches its rule through `step/3` only, with literal neutral maps and requests written by hand.
- `declaration_over_state_bound`: a host listing with one description of 55,608 bytes puts the state at exactly 65,536 bytes and is accepted; one more byte is refused with `[declaration refused: state_over_bound]`, the loop stays open, every member of the state outside the open request is equal, and the next request declares the old tools.
- `repeated_id`: the second kept use of an `id` in one turn is left out with `repeated_id`, gets no action, no echo and no tool result; the `id` of a proposal that was left out is not taken.
- `over_call_bound`: 65 proposals give one request with 64 actions; proposal 65 is left out with `over_call_bound`.
- `validator_disagreement`: a proposal with no tag whose arguments the schema of the tool refuses is echoed, gets the notice `[tool call not run: validator_disagreement]` and no action; the other call of the turn runs.
- `not_resolved`: a proposal with no tag for a name that no entry holds, and one for an own name on two sources, get `[tool call not run: not_resolved]` and no action; the next request echoes neither and holds each notice as content.
- `request_not_built`: a spec member that `build/2` refuses at the first model call gives `stopped`, `request_not_built` with `turns` 0; a turn that no request of `max_request_bytes` holds gives it with `turns` 1; the state is closed after each.
- `run_ended`: from one open state of each phase of the README table (new, model, tools, stores) it gives the closed state and no request; the input that the phase reads gives a request before it and nothing after it.

Negative controls, each a temporary edit of `lib/elzoo/agent_loop.ex`, run with `mix test pieces/workflow/agent-loop/test` (exit 2), then reverted. In every run the named group is the only one of the 23 tests that fails:
1. Rule 6 of "Declarations" accepts instead of refusing (`else: {accepted, next}`): `declaration_over_state_bound` fails (a `stopped` finish comes where no request is expected). Also `<=` to `<` in that rule: the same group fails (the exact fit is refused).
2. The operand `new_id` of `keep` is always `true`: `repeated_id` fails (the repeated call gets an action).
3. `@max_calls` 64 to 63: `over_call_bound` fails (63 actions).
4. The answer of `ToolRegistry.check/2` is not read and its clause is removed: `validator_disagreement` fails (the call gets an action). Also the tag `validator_disagreement` to `not_resolved`: the same group fails.
5. The tag `not_resolved` to `unresolved`: `not_resolved` fails.
6. The reason `request_not_built` to `model_stopped`: `request_not_built` fails.
7. `run_ended` taken out of the closing inputs (`kind in ["cancel"]`): `run_ended` fails (the state stays open).

Upstream: the ready Contracts as they are on main: `ToolRegistry.resolve/2` (`:unknown`, `{:ambiguous, _}`), `ToolRegistry.check/2` (`{:error, {:validator_disagreement, _}}`), `ToolRegistry.refresh/3` and the snapshot form (the listing of a source is kept as given); `PromptAssembly.build/2` (`:invalid_input` for empty role instructions, `:over_limit` when one unit is left); `PatternStep.decode/1` (the typed `run_ended` input, at most 64 actions in one request); OTP `term_to_binary` with `[:deterministic, {:minor_version, 2}]` as the state measure.
Assumptions: none new. Decisions that the body left open: the seven group names; the evidence text says "twenty-one named groups" and lists them; `declaration_over_state_bound` tests the exact boundary, so its literal 55,608 depends on the term encoding of the test fixture (the group asserts the 65,536 bytes itself); `not_resolved` covers the resolutions `unknown` and `ambiguous`, not `removed`; `run_ended` asserts the closed state form that the README documents. Every rule was reachable through the public function and matches the README and the body of #301, so issue #316 got no comment.
Limits: finite scenarios, not a universal proof. The negative controls are not committed and are not named in `piece.json` or the README, which change only in the count and the list of the groups.
Shared paths: none (index file of AGENTS.md section 3 only: `docs/plans/release-plan.json`, the `manifest_sha256` of the row `workflow/agent-loop`; `mix elzoo.ledger` and `python3 scripts/check-roadmap.py --write` changed no generated file).
Friction: a negative control that only replaces the `check/2` call does not compile: the build treats warnings as errors and the type checker reports the clause that can no longer match. The control for rule 4 removes that clause too.

author: tripathiarpan20
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"tripathiarpan20"} -->
_Requested by **Arpan** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01PaHpegnWa8rEqHBFMbB7u4?thread=cmsg_01PaHpegnWa8rEqHBFMbB7u47gQb7EhawmXm8E2mut5hTR)_

## Why

Round 1 of the Muse Spark Open relaunch was won by a patch that OKC's judge later failed, and an operator disqualified that miner with `campaign.disqualify`. The leaderboard moved to the runner-up, but the round 1 page kept showing the disqualified submission as the scored winner. That is by design on the backend: a round's entries are the round's own record and a later disqualification only adds a `disqualified` event to the submission. The page had no way to say so.

## What changes

The round page reads the campaign's submissions and marks every entry the round **scored** whose submission's latest state is `disqualified` today:

- its row keeps the `SCORED` chip, gains a "disqualified later" note next to it, and its score is struck through;
- the Leader tile's hint reads "won by …, disqualified later" when that entry is the round's winner;
- the Winner row in the sidebar gets the same note.

The round's verdict, score, top score and outcome stay as recorded. Entries the round itself disqualified are untouched, since their row already carries the round's reason.

## How

- `src/lib/api/later-disqualified.ts`: `disqualifiedAfterRound(entries, submissions)` returns the submission ids to mark.
- The page fetches `getAllCampaignSubmissions` only when the round has a scored submission, in parallel with the campaign. Like the campaign lookup it is decoration: a failure marks nothing and never breaks the page.
- No API change. `latest_state` on `GET /v1/campaigns/{id}/submissions` already carries the later verdict, and it stays `disqualified` after a waiver, which only restores the miner's future eligibility.

One thing to know: a submission scored in one round and disqualified by the harness in a later round is marked on the earlier round too. That is accurate, it was disqualified after that round.

## Validation

- `vitest run`: 324 passed, 2 skipped (new: `later-disqualified.test.ts`, `round-entries.test.ts`).
- `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint src` and `prettier --check .` are clean.
- Checked in the browser against the mock API with the mock round's winner set to `disqualified`: the row, the Leader tile and the Winner row all show the note.

1) New `subassembly_parameters()` on Arch entity data returns a subassembly's input parameters: name, display name, description, value (integer, double or string), the kind field, named choices of integer parameters, and the definition index.
2) The parameter set is read field by field right after the subassembly shape: `BL 0, BL 0, 6 bits`, then integer, double and string lists, each preceded by its count. 3) The item texts are taken from the record's text stream in item order (name, display name, description, an empty string, then each choice's name and display name, or a string parameter's value), starting after the shape codes.
4) The shape reader now also reports where the body continues after the area list; shape output is unchanged.
5) A unit test reads one item of each kind from a hand-built bit string.

author: krystophny
body:
[Width bisection](https://github.com/itpplasma/milca/blob/df87d5f8dc99dc2679030cde2a0296a47092746b/src/mhd/island_diagnostics.f90#L320-L357) labels libration by continuous geometric helical-angle range, which shrinks islands whose lobes occupy unequal geometric angles. [Return-section accumulation](https://github.com/itpplasma/milca/blob/5a6e63248cf24bad5e78af15acddb94d1e175041/src/mhd/island_diagnostics.f90#L319-L406) now classifies circulation by a finite-duration residual poloidal range above $2\pi$, assuming same-lobe returns and a lobe confined to an angular interval narrower than $2\pi$. The residual angular advance, after removing the expected signed full rotations, must be smaller than half a turn in magnitude. [Fixed-step tracing](https://github.com/itpplasma/milca/blob/5a6e63248cf24bad5e78af15acddb94d1e175041/src/mhd/island_diagnostics.f90#L90-L106) also reaches its requested endpoint when a phase span is requested.

The synthetic pendulum's analytic full width is $W=12.7004\,\mathrm{cm}$. Under angular deformation, the earlier code reports 11.1357 cm; the corrected width differs from the analytic value by less than 1 micrometre. The finite-duration and tolerance changes remain sensitivity estimates.

![Native pendulum widths against the analytic separatrix](https://box.sloppy.at/aafc8.png)

The native pendulum regression passes. The six affected native checks are pending. [Queue statuses](https://github.com/itpplasma/milca/blob/5a6e63248cf24bad5e78af15acddb94d1e175041/ci/run.sh#L17-L26) acknowledge policy without running these tests.

No non-public code of others was used or in context.

Chris&AI

body:
## Unified MahsaNG integration (replaces every previously open MahsaNG PR: #13, #14, #15, #16, #17)

**Target:** `master` • **Source:** `integration/unified-roadmap-20261113`. This single PR aggregates all five open workstreams without merging to `master`.

### Included workstreams
- **#13:** Prevent account/profile selection from silently switching to different credentials at an identical endpoint; includes Kotlin and source contract regressions.
- **#14:** Reject stale JNI live-delay completions after service stop, new run or selected-profile change.
- **#15:** Configurable TCP-only Quick/Balanced/Diagnostic presets, honest protocol/transport eligibility, English/Persian settings and tests.
- **#16:** Capped 1–16 atomic bulk-TCP workers and bounded user-facing concurrency choices (default 8).
- **#17:** Run/revision/method-owned *review-only* multipass failure evidence with explicit pause/stop state and finite work limits; **no scheduler, automatic profile deletion or destructive actions**.

The base commit is #17’s latest head `b50aa98292da2641cc3e79e694d5a46847aadae1` (which already includes #15 and #16). Six non-overlapping exact blobs from #13 and #14 are overlaid as one integration commit `9b130267d37b5a3dd2558f85abf268af71c3a2b8`. Source/test snapshots are preserved; no workflow checks were disabled.

### Gates
- **Require green full native Android/JVM/ABI/emulator CI on this exact integrated head**, not merely independently passing PR runs.
- Review security-sensitive core stop, credentials, TCP false-failure handling and diagnostics; do not claim live tunnel validation from unit/emulator tests.
- Physical-device start/stop/reconnect, IPv4/IPv6 routing, DNS/leak, binary provenance and signing review remain release gates.
- This PR is **draft**, with no default-branch merge or production distribution authorized.

### Superseded PR handling
**Consolidation completed:** #13–#17 were closed as superseded (not merged into `master`), with links here and their discussion/history preserved. Duplicate consolidation PR #19 had the identical Git tree and was also closed as superseded. #18 is the sole canonical MahsaNG PR; full integrated CI and device gates still apply.
