author: sfmskywalker
body:
[Claude] On behalf of @sfmskywalker.

Part of #4229 (round 4, the BPMN spike). Third of the stack: based on #4332 (`agent/claude/kernel-r4-bpmn-2`), which is based on #4328. Merge those first, then retarget this to main.

## What it changes

- `sim/BpmnSim.cs` (new): BPMN instances in the simulation's mix with `--bpmn` (40 % of outside choices in BPMN-only mode; with `--native`, Native takes 40 % first and BPMN takes 40 % of the remainder, or 24 % overall), the token checks, a reference run without faults, and `--bpmn-mutations`.
  - The mix: the seven processes of `BpmnCases` (#4332) `b-fault` (a fork whose one branch fails with no boundary: it must end Faulted with the other branch's job stopped) and `b-race` (an event-based gateway between a message catch and a timer catch: the loser is stopped, so a stopped catch's subscription is checked), with random inputs, started from outside (retried within the window) or handed to an owner in memory; messages for `b-early`'s catch, now and then twice, half of them to a catch that waits when one does (in the 200,000-seed run 559,386 were published before their catch and 12,602 to a waiting one); terminates from outside, to root instances (a terminated child fails its parent's call, which then faults by BPMN's rules). The simulation's own faults are unchanged, and its generic controls (suspend, resume) reach BPMN instances too. Boundary timers race the jobs on the simulation's clock, so both orders occur.
  - The checks, against the committed rows after every action, and at the end:
    - **G1 token conservation**: the interpreter's work in flight (`ActiveWork`), the host's ledger and the kernel's work (row jobs, pending timer messages, subscriptions, child rows or their start messages) are one set, both ways; and from the child's side, a running child of a BPMN instance is its parent's live call, or a terminate is on its way to it.
    - **G2 a join fires at most once per round**: no arrival token is consumed by two firings, no firing is journalled twice, and at the end the joins fired match a run without faults (the loop's join three times).
    - **G3 a join fires on what it may**: a parallel join on exactly one arrival per inbound flow; an inclusive join on distinct inbound flows.
    - **G4 completion exactly when no live token remains**: a Finished row has no live token, no ledger entry and no interpreter work; at idle every BPMN instance started has finished (or was terminated from outside); only `b-fault` and instances whose job or child the kernel parked may fault, and any other fault is reported with its code.
    - **G5 no token outlives its cancelled scope**: no cancelled token keeps a stopped handle; a row the model ended (Finished or Faulted) keeps no job, subscription or timer; a row terminated from outside keeps no job or subscription (its pending timers arrive later and are dropped: the kernel's terminate does not recall them); a cancelled child was stopped by its parent's call or its parent was terminated.
    - **G6** (extra) a finished root instance's variables equal a run alone without faults (the timer-first run where a boundary timer won).
  - The model's deliberate flaws (`BpmnFlaw`), each with the check that must catch it; `--bpmn-mutations` counts a catch by another check as a miss: `KeepStoppedWork` (G1 or G5), `NoLateReport` (G5), `KeepSubscription` (G1 or G5), `StaleTokens` (G1 or G5), `ReuseHandles` (the kernel's I9, or G1: two units, one job id), `ResurrectArrivals` (G4's unexpected-fault clause: the interpreter finds arrivals left at a join that can never fire and faults the instance with `bpmn.join.deadlock`; the mutation harness also accepts G2), `NeverEnd` (G4), `LoseChildOutput` (G6), `KeepChild` (G1: a stopped call's child is not terminated). No host flaw makes a join fire twice (G2) or on the wrong flows (G3) without breaking the interpreter, which the spike runs unchanged: those two guard the interpreter and the journal.
  - An instance whose job the kernel parked (on trial when too many owners were lost, FINDINGS section 7, rule 3) faults with that job's error; the checks count it, and a caller whose call failed because of it, as an innocent bystander for I14, and still check how the host ended it (G1, G5, and G4: it must end Faulted, not run on at idle). A row the kernel parked itself is recognised by its fault text as well as by the parked set. Found by `--bpmn --native`, seed 6706 of 1,000 actions, the one seed of the gate runs that reaches it: that branch (a job's error) is run; the caller branch (a call failed by a kernel-parked child) and the recognition by fault text are traced, not run (no seed in the gates reaches them).
- `models/Bpmn`: the flaws, and a journal entry for a job's error (`e handle error`).
- Shared files, small: `sim/World.cs` (the config fields, the model in each worker, the generator's share, a hook when an act is applied so a replay without the generator knows what was started), `sim/Checks.cs` (the checks in `Check`, `Meet` and `End`; the BPMN model may hold subscriptions), `sim/Program.cs` (`--bpmn`, `--bpmn-flaw`, `--bpmn-mutations`, the summary), `sim/Kernel.Sim.csproj`.

## What it does not change

No kernel code (`src/`), no store, no other model. Without `--bpmn` the generator draws nothing extra: every existing seed replays unchanged (run below). No invariant is loosened; the I14 path above only adds BPMN instances to the parked set, in `sim/BpmnSim.cs`, and `b-fault` instances that end Faulted are marked as expected to fault.

## Gates

Run, without `--bpmn`, on main (`a3eb06e851`) and on this branch before the last merge of #4332's fixes (the shared files have not changed since): **identical output, times aside** (`diff` of the two logs).

```

author: bindreams
body:
Closes #292.

Scopes each service's `environment:` to the variables it reads, as bare passthrough keys, and removes `env_file:` from every compose file. Variables now reach a service through one channel, and an unset variable stays absent in the container.

- `compose.yaml`: portal, mta and provisioner list their variables explicitly (portal: `Settings` fields; provisioner: its entrypoint variables plus the 14 DNS provider variables). nginx gains `EDGE_TRUSTED_CIDRS` and `EDGE_REALIP_HEADER`, which `EDGE_PROFILE=generic` reads. `SECRET_KEY` is `${SECRET_KEY:?...}`, so a missing `.env` still fails every compose command.
- `e2e-mta-real.compose.yaml`: the mta no longer carries the provider variables it never read.
- `portal/tests/test_compose_env_scoping.py`: derives each service's read set from source (`Settings.model_fields`, the entrypoints, `postern-dns`'s `newProvider`, `nginx/render.sh`) and checks the resolved output of the real Compose CLI. Shared compose-test helpers move to `_compose.py`.
- Docs, `example.env`, `CLAUDE.md`: delivery contract (UPPER_SNAKE_CASE names, shell overrides `.env`, only documented names are passed) and an upgrade note.

Upgrade note: services now receive only the variables they read; if you put DNS provider credentials or `SMTP_PASSWORD` in `.env`, consider rotating them. Check that `.env` names are upper-case, that none of these names are exported in the deploying shell, and that you do not rely on undocumented variables reaching a container.

Verification: `test_compose_env_scoping.py` 16 passed. The rest of the non-e2e suite has the same 82 failures and 10 collection errors with and without this change (Windows host: `fcntl`/`mkfifo`, path separators, shell scripts); CI is the gate for those. The `e2e-mta-real` edit has no CI job.

author: jamesponwith
body: ## What changed Telling filtered UDP from a slow host takes a 5 s QUIC probe (`PROBE_DEADLINE`). `phux attach --ssh HOST` pays it on every attach before `attaching through ssh instead`. An attach to a registered `ssh://` host pays it twice: `promote_direct_route` probes the saved direct route, then the bootstrap probes the per-attach listener. - **Every probe notes its outcome** (`enroll::probe_within`, which every QUIC probe goes through). One that gets no answer at all writes `UNIX_SECONDS HOST` to `udp-unanswered` in phux's state directory. One that connects removes the host. Entries expire after 24 h. Refused or TLS errors are not UDP evidence and are not recorded. - **`phux attach --ssh` / registered `ssh://` attach**: when the ssh host (`ssh -G` hostname) is remembered, it skips bootstrap and probe and falls back at once. It prints `UDP to HOST went unanswered on a recent attach; checking it again in the background for next time` and then the same `attaching through ssh instead` line. Meanwhile a background thread runs a silent bootstrap (BatchMode through phux's master, stderr not copied to the TUI's terminal) and probes the listener. If UDP answers, the memory is cleared and the next attach rides QUIC. - **Registry upgrade** (`promote_direct_route`): skips the probe when the entry's QUIC candidate is remembered. `host add` and `host renew` still always probe, so rerunning `host add` after opening the port works right away. - `remote_target.rs` was over the file-size limit, so the QUIC-upgrade code moves unchanged to `remote_target/quic_upgrade.rs`. - docs/ssh.md documents the memory and how to clear it. The docs/remote.md troubleshooting entry is updated. Rune isn't affected: a Rune window dials an `ssh://` machine straight through the ssh lane and never probes QUIC (`Transport::Ssh` in `phux-client-runtime`), so it never waited. ## Timings Measured live: a throwaway local sshd, with UDP filtered by pointing `HostName` at TEST-NET `192.0.2.10` while ssh reaches sshd through `ProxyCommand nc`. The remote phux runs on a dev profile in a temp home. The time is from exec to the fallback line and the TUI's alternate screen, on a PTY. | `phux attach --ssh fvm`, UDP filtered | before | after | |---|---|---| | first attach | 5.17 s / 5.22 s | 5.77 s (records the host) | | next attaches | 5.17 s / 5.22 s (every time) | 0.07 s, 0.07 s | Registered `ssh://` host (from the code path; not timed live): before, two 5 s probes (~10 s). After: the first attach after a filtered `host add` skips both probes, because `host add`'s own probe of the ssh host's route recorded it, and later attaches skip both. A host that no probe has recorded yet pays one probe, and the bootstrap probe is then skipped. ## Verification - New unit tests (`enroll/unanswered.rs`): a timed-out probe is remembered for a day; an answer forgets it; entries expire; a route is keyed by its host (`HOST:PORT`, `[v6]:PORT`, `quic://…`). - New e2e `attach_over_ssh_skips_the_probe_for_a_host_udp_left_unanswered`: seeds the memory for a host whose UDP works. The attach falls back with no probe, the background recheck clears the memory while the TUI runs, and the next attach rides QUIC. - `cargo test -p phux --test lifecycle_e2e ssh_bootstrap -- --ignored`: 6/6 pass. - `just crate-check phux`: pass. `just docs-check`: pass. - `scripts/check-file-tokens.sh --base $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)`: pass. ## Left out - I didn't race the stdio lane against the first probe. Switching a running TUI between lanes is a much bigger change, and the memory removes the wait from every attach after the first. - The memory is keyed by host, not by network. After moving from a filtered network to an open one, the first attach still goes through ssh. Its background recheck then clears the memory, so the second attach uses QUIC. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

author: luizstsantos
body:
## Release 3.3.2

Merging this pull request releases **3.3.2**:
- `Cargo.toml` changes on `main`, so **Tag release** tags the merge commit `v3.3.2`;
- the release and image workflows publish the GitHub release and `ghcr.io/luizstsantos/noar:3.3.2`, and move `3.3` and `latest` to it.

Why 3.3.2 (PATCH): the notes have only a `### Fixed` section, and there is no new migration since v3.3.1. No API field, setting or playlist format changes; the `elapsed` of the playout status now has the right value after midnight.

## Fixed: the Player's progress stood at 0:00 after midnight (`1d840e00`)

Reported on the Player: at 08:27 on the 13th, with the 12th's playlist still on air, the clip on air showed `0:00 of 53:34` and did not move.

The playout status (`get_data_map` in `backend/app/src/player/utils/mod.rs`) counted the time into the clip on air as the clock minus the clip's begin. The clock starts again at 0 at midnight, but playlist times run on past 86400 until the day start. With a day start later than midnight, a clip of the day still on air after midnight came out most of a day below 0, and the Player shows a negative position as `0:00`. A clip or a scheduled event that ran over midnight did the same.

`seconds_since()` reads a begin more than half a day ahead of the clock as before midnight. A clip that starts a moment early still counts a moment below 0, as before. The `elapsed` of `GET /api/control/{id}/media/current` and of the data sent to an external task come from the same status. Three unit tests, one with the reported case (begin 07:33 + 86400, clock 08:27:10: 54:10).

## Fixed: Up next was empty during the last program of the day (`851ec6b9`)

**Up next** only looked in the playlist on screen, so during the day's last program it showed `—`. When nothing of the day on air comes after the program on air, the Player now reads the next day's playlist, names its first program with the same lookup the guide uses, and shows it at its time (the day start, a day later). It reads it again every minute while it is needed, since that playlist can still be edited.

The grouping of clips into programs moves out of the programmes store into `groupClips()`, so the next day's first program is grouped like the programs on screen.

`qa/e2e/tests/player-next-day.spec.ts` answers the two playlists and the status stream itself and saves nothing; the name lookup is the real one. It passes with the change and fails without it (Up next shows `—`).

## Checks run

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --no-default-features --all-targets -- --deny warnings` (Rust 1.99.1), on `851ec6b9` | pass |
| `cargo test --no-default-features` (container with the packages of `validate.yml`), on `851ec6b9` | 810 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored (the ones with a stated reason) |
| `vue-tsc`, ESLint, Prettier, `vite build` | pass |
| `qa/e2e/run_staging.py` (debug build) with the new test | 60 passed, the 3 header tests skipped as designed |
| The same e2e run with the interface change taken out | the new test fails: Up next shows `—` |
| `npm ci && npm run build`, ESLint, `npm audit --audit-level=high` (release commit `84f33970`) | pass |
| `qa/architecture/check.py`, `.claude/scripts` unit tests | pass |
| Migrations since v3.3.1 | none |
| CI on `84f33970` | pass |

Not verified:
- The progress bar on a channel really on air after midnight: the staging runner never starts the channel, so the browser test answers the playout status itself; the elapsed value is covered by the unit tests.
- Whether the 12th's playlist on air at 08:27 on the 13th is expected: that depends on the channel's day start, still to be confirmed.
- The soak was not run again: these changes touch the status shown to the Player, not the output.

author: erkkimarkus
body:
Smaily could not see which stores run the WooCommerce plugin, on which Smaily account and plugin version, with which features switched on, or whether each connection still works, so nobody knew who had what installed or which installations had quietly broken.

The plugin now sends the installation report that Smaily's subscription service defines (contract installation-report-v1). The report goes only while a Smaily marketing account is connected, authenticated with that account's API credentials in the header, and carries the site address, versions, accounts, features, and each connection's status as an error code with its last sync time — never customer, order or admin data. An Action Scheduler action sends a snapshot five minutes after a settings save and once a day, and retries only when the service cannot take the report in now. A Campaign Intelligence disconnect or a save that clears a Smaily account sends a `disconnected` event before the credentials go, and deactivation sends a `deactivated` event; both go once and never block. The two HTTP clients now record each connection's last answer for the report. A must-use guard on the wp-env sites keeps tests and dev sites from ever reaching the receiver.

Refs CON-290

body:
## Değişiklik ve gerekçe

ML-29: Hesapların eklenmesiyle her anı ve fotoğraf işlemi yalnızca oturum sahibinin verisiyle çalışır. Kararlar ve yeni endpoint yazarken uyulacak kurallar ADR-0003'te.

- **Ortak oturum filtresi:** `/api/v1/auth/` dışındaki tüm `/api/v1` istekleri, controller çalışmadan önce geçerli oturum ister. Eksik, geçersiz, iptal edilmiş veya süresi dolmuş token `401 INVALID_SESSION` ve `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` alır. Oturumsuz istek bilinmeyen yola gitse de 401 alır; rota bilgisi sızmaz. Token doğrulaması mevcut `AuthService.me` ile yapılır; auth dosyaları değiştirilmedi.
- **`@CurrentUser`:** Controller'lar kullanıcı kimliğini yalnızca oturumdan alır; istemciden gelen `ownerId` kullanılmaz.
- **`OwnershipGuard`:** `requireMemory` (okuma), `lockMemory` (yazma; anı satırını transaction boyunca kilitler) ve `requirePhoto` (fotoğraf sahipliği bağlı anı üzerinden). Yabancı ve var olmayan kaynak aynı `404 MEMORY_NOT_FOUND` / `PHOTO_NOT_FOUND` gövdesini alır.
- **Statik dosya sunumu kapatıldı:** Test, Spring Boot'un `static/` altındaki bir dosyayı oturumsuz 200 ile sunduğunu gösterdi. `spring.web.resources.add-mappings=false` ile kapatıldı; fotoğraflar yalnızca korumalı endpointlerden dönecek.

## İlgili issue / Trello kartı

ML-29 (bağımlılık: ML-03, ML-04, ML-27)

## Doğrulama

- `.\gradlew.bat test bootJar` → BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 56/56 test geçti, atlanan yok.
- Yeni testler (gerçek PostgreSQL ve HTTP):
  - Oturum: token yok / bozuk / çıkış yapılmış / süresi dolmuş → 401; geçerli token kullanıcıyı çözer; bilinmeyen yol oturumsuz 401, oturumlu 404; health ve register açık.
  - Sahiplik (iki hesap): B, A'nın anısını ve fotoğrafını kimlikleri bilse de okuyamaz, değiştiremez, silemez; A'nın verisi değişmez. Yabancı kaynak yanıtı, var olmayan kaynakla birebir aynı. Başka anının fotoğrafı 404 PHOTO_NOT_FOUND.
  - Şema: `owner_id` zorunlu, kullanıcıya bağlı ve indeksli; fotoğraflar indeksli `memory_id` ile anıya bağlı.
  - Statik dosya: düzeltmeden önce 200, sonra 404.
- Birlikte çalışma: PR #13, ML-07 (`feature/ml07-sprint1`) ve bu dal yerelde birleştirildiğinde dosya çakışması yok, 61/61 test geçiyor (ML-07 anı testleri dahil).

## Bilinen eksikler

- `OwnershipGuard` henüz gerçek anı endpointlerinde değil, test endpointleriyle doğrulandı. Detay, güncelleme, silme, fotoğraf ve harita kartları ADR-0003'teki kuralları uygulayacak.
- ML-07 merge edildikten sonra `MemoryController`, kullanıcıyı `auth.me` yerine `@CurrentUser` ile alacak şekilde sadeleştirilecek; şu an oturum iki kez okunur ama davranış doğrudur.

- [x] Gizli bilgi ve yerel SDK yolu içermiyor.
- [x] İlgili testler çalıştırıldı; atlanan yok.
- [x] Mimari karar ADR-0003 ile belgelendi.

author: guilhermefeitosa66
body:
## UX and performance epic, 2026-11 (desktop)

One branch for the seventeen desktop issues of the November review (openemux-ops/research/ux-performance-2026-11), one commit per issue, in the order the work landed. Every issue stays open for the maintainer's review; each carries a comment with what changed and how to test it. Nothing here is merged by the branch itself.

### Performance (899, 900, 901, 902, 903, 905, 907, 908)
- 899/900 — grids start dormant and wake one page from the viewport; a torn-down page returns its heap (`malloc_trim`); `cards_built` counted. 3000-game All page: main-thread CPU 1.76 s → 0.28 s, settle 2.96 s → 0.77 s, RSS 437 → 234 MB (r2, cold).
- 902/903 — cartridge composites rendered from pixels at the display scale, cached on disk and pruned by housekeeping; the shadow baked into the composite, no CSS filter; the AppImage tries the GPU renderer behind a crash probe.
- 907 — artwork resolved once per entry, a priority decode pool (a card on screen jumps the queue), colour and favourites stamps with a TTL.
- 905 — `save_config_soon()` debounces gesture setters (0.4 s), flushed on close, shutdown and before a launch; `session.json` no longer fsyncs.
- 901 — one-pass scan, a `<CONSOLE>.meta.json` index, incremental start-up rescan by directory mtimes.
- 908 — only pickable cores in the deferred sweep (opt-in for all), one `CoreCatalog` per process with a JSON cache warmed on a worker.

### UX (904, 906, 909, 910, 911, 912, 913, 914, 915)
- 904 — launch on a worker with a "Starting…" card state and a Stop banner; a cached shader index; cheap bar-asset checks; "Played X for N min"; a BIOS alert with "Open BIOS settings" and "Launch anyway".
- 906 — incremental search, words in any order, scope placeholder and "Search everywhere", an empty state, Enter and Escape.
- 909 — the library opens before any download; cores on demand at launch; offline notice with Retry; "Choose your ROM folder" first; a covers offer after the scan; the tour waits for games.
- 910 — Recently played page with play time captions; the app opens on it; "Resume where I left off" with a badge and "Start fresh".
- 911 — BIOS warnings on the sidebar row and the console page, re-checked after imports, core changes and transfers.
- 912 — console display names everywhere, the folder id in the tooltip.
- 913 — a game details dialog (menu, Alt+Return, the pad's X).
- 914 — TV mode (F11/Guide), controller glyph families with a swap preference, an on-screen keyboard on Start, shoulder jumps on All. Reduced scope: text glyphs in keycaps, no icon set; no right-stick letter jump; the 26 px measurement left to human QA.
- 915 — accessible names, roles and positions on the cards and their buttons; transitions follow `gtk-enable-animations`.

### Decisions worth a look
- Start-up lands on Recently played when there is history (over the stored view, issue 383).
- The gamepad's X opens the details dialog instead of the popover; Start opens the on-screen keyboard instead of confirming.
- 904's end-of-game wording replaced `toast.finished`; the optional "hide the window while a game runs" preference was not built.
- The first boot's offline failure path is gone with the gate: a package without bundled cores says so at the first launch of a game instead.
- Screenshots of the site and the manual were not refreshed (the refresh-screenshots pass redoes the whole set).
- Two keyboard fixes came out of recording the video, both in the last 914 commit: Escape in TV mode used to bring the sidebar back as a full-screen page (the collapsed split view pops on Escape first), and Enter or Space on a focused card launched nothing on any branch (the GtkListItemWidget cell drops both keys before the grid's controller saw them). Both handlers now run in the capture phase.

### Known: one whole-suite run in the devbox ended with harness failures
- Every touched module passes alone under coverage, `test_window` passes alone (403 tests), and the host run of the entire suite (`unittest discover`, 5940 tests) passes. One run of the entire suite inside the devbox (GTK 4.22, one process) ended with 403 `test_window` and 7 `test_welcome_assistant` failures, all in `WindowCase.setUp`: the throwaway library read back empty and its playlist index came back unparsable right after being written. Bisecting it was cut short by the host's GPU hanging (the NVIDIA driver timed out and every process that opened its render node froze in the kernel, the devbox's Xvnc included), so the cause is not confirmed; the shape points at a leaked thread, timer or patch from an earlier module writing into the next test's home. CI's windowed split is the arbiter here; if it reproduces, the first failing test after a green `test_x11_windows` is where to look.

### How to test
- `make devbox-tests` (the suite is at 100% on the touched modules under coverage); test book scenarios RT-1028 to RT-1045, plus the updated RT-021, RT-022, RT-034, RT-062, RT-003, RT-316.
- The perf numbers: `tools/perf/gen_library.py` + `tools/perf/library_bench.sh` (`tools/perf/README.md`).
- A video of the desktop flows is in the maintainer's `~/Videos/openemux-epic-ux-perf/`.

author: 0xtlt
body:
A metafield used without `.value` now acts as its value, as it does on a store. `{% if product.metafields.custom.show_badge %}` with `false` hides the badge, `== 'gloss'` matches, and `metaobjects.faq.values | sort: 'question'` sorts instead of raising "cannot sort values of incompatible types".

## What changed

- `MetafieldDrop` gives its value (`to_value`) for the types whose value is a text, a number, a boolean or a date: `single_line_text_field`, `multi_line_text_field`, `url`, `id`, `number_integer`, `number_decimal`, `boolean`, `date`, `date_time`. So `if`, `unless`, `==`, `>`, the math filters, `sort`, `where` and `sum` read the value. `{{ f.finish | size }}` gives the length of the text.
- The `date` filter reads the time a drop stands for, so `{{ f.day | date: '%d.%m.%Y' }}` formats a `date` metafield.
- References, lists, `json`, `color`, `money`, `rating` and measurements stay the metafield: the report only shows the scalar types. Printing, `| json`, `.value`, `.type`, `metafield_tag` and `metafield_text` are unchanged.

The issue's repro now prints Shopify's output line for line:

```text
a|C|D|E|F|G|H|J
43|3.0|05.03.2026
2,3,1|Do you ship to Belgium?|6
```

## Shopify sources

- The report's observations on a development store (`shopify theme dev`, 2026-11-13).
- [Liquid reference, `metafield`](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/liquid/objects/metafield): `value` is the string, number, boolean or date of each type. The page says nothing against a metafield standing for its value, and its deprecated types already "return the metafield value directly".

## Tests

`a_metafield_without_value_compares_filters_and_sorts_as_its_value` (`crates/theme/tests/render.rs`) runs the repro's checks. It also checks that printing, `json`, `.value` and `.type` are unchanged, and that a `color` stays the metafield. fmt, clippy (`-D warnings`), `cargo test --workspace --locked` and the JS tests pass.

CHANGELOG `Unreleased` lists this as a breaking change: a theme test that relied on a `false` metafield being truthy gets the other branch.

Fixes #74

author: agent7898
body:
## Why
The wave 2 tester 3 run (wash, wallet, admin) through the real UI found these bugs. Antigravity's PR #14 script had reported 57/57 Pass, but it checked results through the API with conditions that couldn't fail.

**Security**
- **Self-approval:** cleaners and washing centers could approve themselves and set their own rating. The "manage own profile" policies allow every column, and no trigger guarded them.

**Wrong messages and screens**
- **Wash bells:** the notify trigger checked `progress = 'confirmed'` before the terminal statuses. A cancelled, rejected or completed wash therefore told the customer "Wash slot approved — pay now", and "Wash completed" never arrived.
- **`/washes`:** an ended wash still showed **Confirmed**, with Pay and Cancel buttons, because only `status` changes when a wash ends.
- **Fake Withdraw buttons:** on the cleaner and wash-center dashboards they only showed a success toast; no request was made. Earnings there were `price × 0.85`, under a made-up "15%" label.

**Broken features**
- **Referral link:** it pointed to `synchoo.in/join`, a route that doesn't exist. The **Invited Friends** list was always empty because profiles RLS hides other users' rows.
- **Revenue & Fees:** `admin_revenue_aggregates()` always failed (it read `commission_rental_pct` and similar, which don't exist), so the tab showed a client-side estimate at made-up rates.
- **Broadcasts** said "sent" even when the insert failed.
- **Payouts:** "Mark paid" with an empty reference did nothing, with no message.

## What
- **Migrations**
  - **`0009_wash_partner_guard_and_notify_order`:**
    - `tg_guard_wash_partner_verification` on `cleaners` and `wash_centers`. An end user's new row is forced to `pending` with a zero rating. Status and rating are kept on update, except that editing a rejected profile resubmits it to `pending`. Admins and `verify_cleaner()` / `verify_wash_center()` are unaffected.
    - `tg_notify_wash_booking` checks terminal statuses first, and each message fires only on the change that causes it. Claiming a job no longer re-sends "Wash slot approved".
  - **`0010_my_referrals`:** `my_referrals()` SECURITY DEFINER returns only the caller's own referrals.
  - **`0011_fix_revenue_aggregates`:** platform revenue is the sum of each paid booking's stored `commission_amount + service_fee`; provider payouts are paid `withdrawals`.
- **Frontend**
  - **Dashboards:** Withdraw buttons open `/wallet`, where the real withdraw form is. Earnings use `provider_earning`.
  - **`/washes`:** an ended wash shows its real status and no Pay or Cancel.
  - **Referrals:** the link is `<origin>/auth?mode=signup&ref=…` and the list comes from the RPC.
  - **Broadcasts** throw on errors, and an empty UTR shows `Enter the payment reference (UTR)`.
- **Removed:** `scripts/execute_all_tests.py`. It recorded passes that couldn't fail (`refund == X or status == 200`, plus ten unconditional passes), could `ALTER TABLE … DISABLE TRIGGER` on the database, and wrote to `local/test wave 2/…`, a folder that doesn't exist. Nothing references it.

## Testing
- Backend: 33 passed. New: `test_wash_partners_cannot_approve_themselves`, `test_cancelled_wash_is_not_told_to_pay`, `test_my_referrals_lists_only_my_friends`, `test_revenue_aggregates_use_stored_commission`. The sentinel is now 97 functions and 86 triggers.
- Frontend: 205 passed; `tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- Ran the full tester 3 suite through the UI on a fresh database: **55 Pass, 0 Fail, 2 Blocked**. The two Blocked cases need a person to finish a Razorpay test payment.

## Not in this PR
- Revenue & Fees' per-category commission editor saves to columns that don't exist. Whether to add per-category commissions or keep the single rate in Fees & settings is a product decision.
- The cleaner's "proof photos" are a hard-coded stock image, not an upload.
- Broadcasts go only to the first 100 profiles and ignore the chosen audience.

After merging, run `python manage.py migrate` in `backend/`.

author: fw-bot
body:
Issue:
----------------------------------------
HR administrators without the administration rights get an access rights error when linking an employee to a user.

Steps to reproduce:
----------------------------------------
- Log in as an HR administrator without administration rights
- Open an employee without a related user
- Set a related user and save
- An access rights error is raised

Cause:
----------------------------------------
Linking the user sets the user's partner as work contact, which recomputes the work email and mobile from it.

When saving, we send them to `_inverse_work_contact_details()` gets triggered and writes them on the user's partner. Then we require the write access even if no value changes.

Solution:
----------------------------------------
Only write the email or phone number when they differ from the contact ones, and skip the write when nothing changed. This is specifically the case when changing the user, as `_compute_work_contact_details()` already computes them from the contact.

## Why

The web host styles a link whose children are only text and images as a text link. It gets `color: var(--exact-accent, AccentColor)` (blue on a Mac) and `text-decoration: underline` on hover and focus. On this site that drew blue underlines, first in the sidebar, then in the crumbs of #470 and the header links of #451. Both PRs, now on `main`, put their links' contents in a `row`. This PR fixes the two such links still on `main`, and adds a browser test so that it does not happen again.

## Scope

- `docs/site/components/article.contract`: on the not-found page, the "Go to …" link and the "Did you mean" links hold their contents in a `row`, as the sidebar's links do.
- `docs/site/tests/browser.test.mjs`: one new test for each of `/`, `/recipes/website`, `/learn/website-recipe` (the not-found page) and `/_components`. The test forces `:hover` and `:focus-visible` on every link view (`#exact-root a[data-view][href]`) with the DevTools protocol's `CSS.forcePseudoState`. It fails when a link's computed colour is the accent or its `text-decoration-line` has `underline`, and it names each such link. It skips links inside running text, because the host underlines those on purpose.
- The first version of this PR made `tools/link-check.ts` the first step of `bun run build`. This version removes it, so the build is the same as on `main`.

## Tradeoffs

- The review found two faults in `link-check.ts`. It read indentation, so it failed links that the host does not style (with a `role` or a `buttonStyle`), and it passed links whose text is under `if`, `else`, `for` or a component. The browser test reads the styles that the host applies, so it has neither fault.
- The test checks 4 of the 150 pages. Together they show every kind of link the site draws: the header tabs, the sidebar, the crumbs, On this page, Previous and Next, the footer, the home cards, the not-found suggestions and the link cards. A new kind of link on another page is not checked until one of these pages shows it.
- The "Go to …" link shows only until the app redirects to the new path (`app.contract` lines 308 and 309), so the test cannot hover it. It has the same `row` as the "Did you mean" links, which the test checks.
- `CSS.forcePseudoState` is a Chromium call. The suite already runs on Chromium (`suiteBrowser()`).
- On the two fixed links, the text has its own underline in the text colour, which covers the host's blue one. The page does not look different.

## Blast Radius

The not-found page, and the browser suite (`bun run test:browser`), which gets 4 tests of about 0.2 s each.

## Verification

Main is at `9ef3e064ae`, which has #451 (`4aaf3b9fab`), so these runs include it.

- `bun run build` in `docs/site`: exit 0, 150 pages, 237 internal links, 0 broken.
- `bun exact.mjs test web`: 32 passed, 0 failed.
- `bun test ./tests/browser.test.mjs` after the build: 37 pass, 0 fail.
- The new test with `main`'s `article.contract` (the old links): the `/learn/website-recipe` test fails and names `/recipes/website`, `/learn/contract-for-humans` and `/learn/contract-for-humans/run-an-app`. The other three pass.

No screenshots, because nothing on these two links looks different (see Tradeoffs).

author: nordmanndev
body:
The owner went through the independent review of `main` @ `6d6d84a` of 2026-11-04 point by point and decided what LUI would do before the freeze (epic #39). The decisions are written down — ADR-0023, ADR-0024, ADR-0025, ADR-0026 — and ADR-0026 lists the points of the review that were **declined**, by name, so that a later contributor cannot take one of them up and break the promise.

But the surface of 0.1.0 is nowhere written down **against** the review: a reader cannot tell which point of the review produced which member, what the later decisions did to a point of the review, and what the two changes that came after the review do to the surface.

**The change.** ADR-0063 with the table: every point of the review — the ones that were decided and the ones that were declined — the decision, and where it stands in 0.1.0 today: the type or the member that carries it. Every line is checked against the code, not against the memory of it.

**Four points of the review were taken up again afterwards.** Three of them were decided differently, because the world of the library moved: the catalog became the entry point (ADR-0033), the index learned no types (ADR-0035), and the typed view replaced the untyped facade (ADR-0044) — the untyped facade of the owner's addition of 2026-11-05 is not part of the API. One of them was decided the way the review wanted it: **A.3**, the route named in the call (ADR-0062). And two changes came after the review entirely: the typo distance became an enumeration (ADR-0054) and the uniqueness of a text was given to the data (ADR-0055).

**A row of the freeze that had become untrue.** ADR-0026 says of A.2 that the name `LuiServicesBuilder` stays. The type is gone with the entry point — a guard says so. The decision of the owner still holds; the sentence that carries it names a type that no longer exists. ADR-0026 gets a dated note, and the table carries the truth.

`docs/api.md` stays the member-by-member list — the record is the provenance, and the documentation of the library and the papers of the work stay apart, as `docs/README.md` says.

**No change to the public API.**

author: smaug123
body:
Stage 7 of the sema-interning plan (#543, `docs/sema-interning-plan.md`): `Ty`'s named paths become ids in the env's name table.

## What changes

- `Ty::Named` and `Ty::Project` now carry a `TyPath`, which is a `PathId` interned when the type is built. Cloning a nullary type no longer allocates, and comparing two paths compares integers.
  - `TyPath` is public and opaque, with no `Ord`. Read it back with `segments(env)`.
  - Building a type (`Ty::named(env, …)`, `TyPath::of`) and rendering one (`render(env)`, `render_fsharp(env)`) take the env the type belongs to, the same way `Def::spelling` does.
- Inference's project-type maps are keyed by `TyPath`: `project_types`, `ProjectRecords`, `sealed_project_types` and `PrecedingTypes`' earlier-file types.
  - A file's contribution sorts its records by the paths' text.
- Outside sema the changes are minimal and mechanical:
  - Hover passes the fold's env to its two type renderings.
  - Completion spells the receiver path through that env.
  - corpus-diff's `parse_canonical` reads FCS text into a table of its own.
  - The LSP's incremental-against-cold inference test now re-keys the warm fold onto the cold env's table (`test_support::names::rekeyed_inference`).

## Lockstep and oracles

Both oracles below were written first and passed against the string-keyed `Ty`.

- **Lockstep:** under `interning-reference` in a debug build, a `TyPath` carries the segments it was built from. Construction, reads, equality, `is`, and both renderers assert that the id agrees with them. The renderers are checked against `ty/reference.rs`'s string-form renderers.
- **`ty::spelled_form`:** a property over generated types, with decoy-filled tables. It checks four things:
  - converting to and from the string form is the identity;
  - two types are equal exactly when their spellings are;
  - a path `is` exactly its own segments;
  - both renderings match the string form's.
- **Interning-order test:** now covers inference. A generated two-file project and the corpus sample are each inferred against two tables, and must publish the same rendered types and the same fold after re-keying.

## Planted bugs, each caught and reverted

1. Interning under the parent: caught by the construction check, in 146 cases.
2. A project type rendered without its first segment: caught by the property and the render lockstep, in 9 integration cases.
3. `is` answering for a prefix: passed every test at first. Caught only after I added the `is` property.
4. Re-keying without receiver types: caught by the interning-order whole-fold comparison.
5. Records sorted by arity only: caught by `body_edit_preserves_full_inference_reuse`.

## Counts (`sema_counts`, `parse_counts`; instructions and allocations per source byte)

| | before (`7cf250bd`) | after |
|---|---|---|
| `infer_file` instr/B | 173.3 | 158.6 (−8.5%) |
| `infer_file` allocs/B | 0.128 | 0.093 (−27%) |
| `resolve_file` instr/B | 861.0 | 860.8 |
| `resolve_project` instr/B | 868.9 | 867.3 |
| parse instr/B | 509.9 | 510.7 (code unchanged) |

## Output

Output is byte-identical. I extended 6c's whole-corpus dump with each directory's implementation files inferred as one project: node, binder and export types, 6,748 file inferences, the signed pass included. The dump is the same before and after.

The string keys 6c left over from 5a (`repr_access_root`/`case_repr_roots`, `exported_value_paths`/`exported_case_paths`) are resolver paths, not `Ty` paths. The plan now files them with 5a's not-converted list.

author: unfunco
body:
Stacked on #35.

## Summary

The cluster referenced its two roles but not their policy attachments, and nothing tied it to the log group, so Terraform was free to create all of them at once. That allows two failures:

- EKS starts building the cluster before its role can manage EC2, or on destroy the policies are detached while EKS still needs them to remove the cluster's network interfaces and security groups.
- EKS creates `/aws/eks/<cluster>/cluster` itself, with no encryption or retention, and the apply then fails because the log group already exists. On destroy the log group can be deleted first and recreated by the still-running cluster, which orphans it.

`aws_eks_cluster.this` now has an explicit `depends_on` for the log group and both sets of policy attachments, as the provider documentation recommends.

## Validation

- `terraform fmt -check -recursive`, `terraform validate` and `terraform test` (3 passed) passed.
- Ordering can't be asserted in a mocked plan and no apply was run against AWS.

author: fr0ster
body:
## Problem
`AnthropicProvider` passed the pipeline's OpenAI-shaped tools verbatim. Anthropic rejects them: `HTTP 400 tools.0: Input tag 'function' found using 'type' does not match …`. Every agent step that carries tools failed with "LLM unavailable (no response from model)". Found in a local cloud-llm-hub run on `claude-opus-5-5`.

## Fix
Follows https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/define-tools and https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/handle-tool-calls.

- **Tools.** OpenAI or MCP shape becomes `{ name, description, input_schema }`. No `tool_choice` is sent, so the default `auto` applies; Opus/Sonnet 5.5 and Fable 5.x return 400 for `any`/`tool`.
- **Assistant tool calls.** They become `tool_use` blocks. Malformed arguments are sent as `{ _unparsed_arguments }` and no longer throw.
- **Tool results.** They become `tool_result` blocks. All results answering one assistant turn go into **one** user message, first and in `tool_use` order, with any text after them. Results with unknown ids become plain text.
- **Responses.** `tool_use` comes back as `toolCalls` with `finishReason: 'tool_calls'`, which is what the pipeline checks. Streaming emits `{index, id, name, arguments}` deltas.
- **Errors.** HTTP errors keep their status and Anthropic error type.
- Text-only messages stay plain strings.

## Verified on the live API (claude-opus-5-5)
1. Streamed turn: two parallel tool calls with correct arguments; `finishReason: tool_calls`.
2. Both results sent back in one message: the final answer quotes both (`end_turn`), via `chat` and `streamChat`.
3. Text between the two results: still merged correctly; `end_turn`.

## Tests
- anthropic-llm: 51 pass, 0 fail.
- Build and root typecheck are clean.

Codex review: APPROVE (two rounds: malformed JSON arguments; merging results across interleaved text).

author: silentlie
body:
## PR #31: Variable Locks

Builds on merged PR #30's conflict-aware edit history and PR #29's trusted game-init primitive-edit opt-in.

### Semantics and safety
- Add bounded, bridge-session exact-path locks for existing editable Store primitives only (128 paths / 32 KiB).
- Locks protect only this inspector's explicit Edit, Undo and Redo endpoints. They do not patch Store objects, acquire Python locks, intercept game scripts or prevent Ren'Py from changing variables during gameplay.
- Add authenticated `PUT /api/v1/locks` lock/unlock actions. HTTP workers validate primitive arguments and queue them; target validation and lock changes execute on the Ren'Py interaction thread.
- Lock/unlock metadata does not mutate game values or advance the game-state generation. Inspector writes to a locked path return HTTP 423; blocked Undo/Redo leaves the history stack unchanged.
- Lock state clears on load, rollback, unclassified generation invalidation, bridge restart and editing disablement. Explicit edit/undo/redo preserve unrelated locks.
- Editing and locks remain disabled by default; no browser endpoint enables either capability.

### UI
- Show a padlock beside locked Store variables in the virtual tree.
- Add contextual Lock/Unlock controls to the primitive editor and explain that locks do not freeze gameplay.
- Explain HTTP 423 in Edit and Undo/Redo flows.

### Tests and packaging
- Python 2/3 typed-path validation, Unicode paths, idempotence, bounded count/byte budgets and reset semantics.
- HTTP auth, game-thread queue ownership, locked Edit/Undo rejection, unrelated-history preservation, script-write noninterference and lifecycle resets.
- Browser E2E for lock/unlock, tree state, edit rejection and Undo rejection; real Ren'Py 7/8 default-deny checks.
- Add the lock manager to the closed installer manifest and build v0.7.13 Ren'Py 7/8 preview ZIPs.

**Draft until all Python, browser, dual-engine SDK lint, real-engine E2E and preview-package CI jobs pass.**

## What
`MuseBar.send` gets a `useRef` guard alongside the render-time `busy` check.

## Why
`busy` (`muse.asking || creating || holding`) is read from the render closure. A second submit in the same frame (keyboard Enter plus a send-button tap, or a double tap) sees it as still false.

author: ondrejmacko-it
body:
## Co se mění a proč

PR #10 a #11 vznikly souběžně z `main` a kolidovaly ve dvou souborech. Tento PR je spojuje a dokončuje body, které v #10 zbývaly. **Nahrazuje #10 a #11**, ty lze zavřít.

**Z #10:** bezpečné zveřejňování akcí (potvrzení dopadu změny, „Ukládám…“), K doplnění v harmonogramu, Nahradit pravidelný termín, správa témat s archivací (migrace `0006_topic_archive`), Přehled podle role, stavy termínů, Zahodit návrh změny, zápis po výměně nahrávky.

**Z #11:** oprava resetu formulářů (`submitKeepingValues`), odlišení týdnů, úpravy pro Mac a iOS, rozložení na iPadu a telefonu.

**Řešení konfliktů:** dialog akce si nechává ruční odeslání z #10 (drží hodnoty a navíc ověřuje dopad změny), ostatní formuláře používají `submitKeepingValues`. V `globals.css` platí obě sady pravidel.

**Nově dokončeno:**
- **Stáhnout zveřejněný zápis.** Publikum zápis přestane vidět, vedoucí ho má zpět jako návrh a může ho zveřejnit znovu. Z pozvánky zmizí odkaz na zápis. Smí jen ten, kdo s nahrávkou pracuje.
- **Koho se zrušení dotkne.** Dialog zrušení ukáže skupinu, která akci vidí ve Wiki, a hosty pozvánky, kterým Kalendář pošle storno. Upozorní, že se zahodí rozpracovaný návrh změny.
- **Stín původního termínu.** Když návrh přesouvá zveřejněnou akci, organizátor vidí v harmonogramu i původní termín, který kolegové dál vidí.
- **Průvodce měsícem.** Tři kroky nad harmonogramem organizátora: Termíny, Témata a vedoucí, Zveřejnění, každý se stavem a počtem.
- **Rada ke stavu.** V detailu akce je pod stavem věta, co má organizátor udělat (návrh, chyba Kalendáře, chybějící pozvánka, probíhající synchronizace).
- **Pořadí polí v dialogu akce.** Typ, termín, Téma, Vede a Publikum jsou nahoře. Název v plánu a Kontrolor zápisu jsou ve sbaleném „Další nastavení“, které se otevře samo, když jsou vyplněné jinak než výchozím způsobem nebo když je v něm neplatné pole.
- **Režimy ukázky na Integracích.** Pruh s ukázkovým časem a režimy je i na stránce Integrace, na telefonu tam zůstává vidět.
- Texty z #10 psané tykáním jsou sjednocené na vykání jako zbytek UI.

## Jak to ověřit

- [x] Lint, typová kontrola, testy (108 ze 108) a build.
- [x] Přístupy: nové serverové akce ověřují roli na serveru. Stažení zápisu smí jen vedoucí a kontrolor (účastník `forbidden`, kolega mimo publikum `not_found`), dopad zrušení jen organizátor. Původní termín přesunu se posílá jen organizátorovi. Kryje `tests/dokonceni.test.ts`.
- [x] Diff zkontrolovaný. Bez tajemství, neveřejných podkladů a produkčních dat.
- [x] Integrace: vše běželo v simulaci.

Průchod v prohlížeči (Chromium, lokální PGlite):
- Organizátor, vedoucí a účastník na šířkách 1280, 820 a 390 px: Přehled, Harmonogram (Měsíc i Seznam), Zápisy, Témata, Integrace, Správa a detail akce bez vodorovného posunu stránky.
- Přidat akci na 390 px: neúspěšné zveřejnění bez tématu nechá zvolený Typ i Publikum.
- Nové funkce na 1280 a 390 px: pořadí polí a Další nastavení, dopad v dialogu zrušení, průvodce měsícem (i prázdný měsíc), rada u návrhu, pruh režimů na Integracích. Přesun termínu jako návrh ukáže stín původního termínu.
- Vedoucí nahrál nahrávku, zveřejnil zápis a stáhl ho. Účastník potom zápis nevidí.

**Neověřeno:** skutečné Safari (WebKit) na Macu a iPhonu. Živý test proti Googlu, tedy i storno a odebrání odkazu na zápis ve skutečné pozvánce. Úkol „Nahrajte audio z dnešní akce“ v prohlížeči (v ukázkovém čase není vidět). body:
## Permanent instruks skærpet — policy + værktøj (13.11.2026)

Brugerens fornyede permanente instruks er nu skrevet ind i `master/README.md` som en bindende blok med otte punkter og en tabel, der mapper hvert punkt til den kontrol, der håndhæver det.

**Skærpelser, der nu blokerer (før: advarsel eller 60 %):**
- **Kultur 100 %** — alle virksomhedens egne udtryk i `jd/<Stilling>_kultur.txt` skal genfindes i dokumentet (var 60 %).
- **Dybde 110 tegn blokerende** — intet krav må besvares overfladisk (var blokerende under 60, advarsel under 110). `--allow-thin` findes til ældre dokumenter.
- **Ny blokering: kandidat-først åbning** — første afsnit må ikke begynde med »jeg er/har/kan/vil/søger«, »som person«, »min baggrund« osv.

**Efterkontrol:** #241 make:net, #242 Rigshospitalet, #243 AHH og #244 Elos Medtech består alle de skærpede regler — 100 % kultur, 20–21/20–21 rækker på ≥110 tegn og arbejdsgiver-først åbning.

**Test af den nye åbningskontrol:** et syntetisk dokument med »Jeg er en passioneret og ambitiøs leder…« bliver nu afvist med både åbningsfejl og rosord.

body:
<!---☝️ PR title should follow conventional commits (https://conventionalcommits.org) -->

### 🔗 Linked issue

#2461

### ❓ Type of change

<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->

- [ ] 📖 Documentation (updates to the documentation, readme or JSdoc annotations)
- [ ] 🐞 Bug fix (a non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] 👌 Enhancement (improving an existing functionality like performance)
- [x] ✨ New feature (a non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🧹 Chore (updates to the build process or auxiliary tools and libraries)
- [ ] ⚠️ Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)

### 📚 Description

This PR adds a `Carousel` primitive. Nuxt UI's `UCarousel` wraps Embla and hands its instance to users, so every Embla major (v9 renames most of the API) becomes a breaking change for us, and shadcn-vue is in the same spot since it's built on Reka too. With a native primitive the whole surface lives under Reka's semver, with no dependency and the same accessibility and SSR behaviour as the other components.

The viewport is a real scroll container with CSS scroll snapping, so it renders and scrolls with touch, trackpad and keyboard before hydration. Once mounted it measures the snaps and adds mouse and pen dragging, `loop`, `align`, `slidesToScroll`, `containScroll`, `dragFree`, `skipSnaps`, `fade`, `autoHeight`, wheel paging, `autoplay` and `autoScroll`. It follows the APG carousel pattern: roledescriptions and slide labels, a rotation control, a pause on hover and when keyboard focus enters, and reduced motion respected. The item padding and negative content margin gutter that Nuxt UI and shadcn-vue use lines up on every snap.

It started as #3171 on `v3`, and this is the port to `v2`'s patterns, with plain `update:modelValue` and `update:playing` emits like the other `v2` primitives. Nuxt UI v5's `UCarousel` was validated against the `v3` build, not this one yet. It's marked Alpha in the docs. The browser tests need real pointer and wheel events, so this also adds the `mouseDrag` and `wheelAt` Playwright commands `v3` already has.

author: matymeatboy
body:
Makes the repository usable as a **skill** for putting link-cable play online in a native port, a decompilation build or a static recompilation, and for porting a GBA game to a native program, with everything ShiningSource (Shining Soul II) established. Not to be merged without review.

## What is in it

- **`SKILL.md`** (name `gbanocable`): the method in order for online play (read the game's link code → seam → transport → relay/rooms/seats/rules → departures, outages, reconnect, barriers, join in progress → test rig → what to state as not verified), the order of work of a native port, and a table "which chapter changes which decision".
- **New chapters**
  - `docs/09` anatomy of a Multi SIO game: the block (state bytes vs. event bytes), the lobby, the stop-and-wait message layer, message kinds by role, the barrier and its unnumbered tokens.
  - `docs/10` the direct transport and the reliable ordered message channel: why lockstep was wrong for this game, the packet in words, one order through the host, the 40-frame reach and the hole that froze players, the fix.
  - `docs/11` departures and reconnect: standing characters, who is given up and when, revival with replay, when replay is impossible, the host, barriers and the world map, the lock-out decision and its alternative.
  - `docs/12` join in progress: what a late program lacks, the anchor at a map set-up, the steps, what was measured, what is open.
  - `docs/13` the relay: rooms hashed with ROM + rules number + transport, seats and tokens, protocol, hardening, test knobs (loss, lag, jitter, outage).
  - `docs/14` the recomp playbook: each of the above without source.
  - `docs/15` the mechanisms of a native port, each with its check and its limits (compile gate and patch list, memory at real addresses, x32 / arm64_32 images, bridge, thunks, BIOS and division, frame boundary, line renderer and hashes, wide picture, flicker bench, sound, audio reserve, pacing, picture skipping, saves, determinism, ARM-only C, crash reports, what applies to a recomp).
  - `docs/verified-lessons.md`: trigger / mechanism / check / limits.
- **Corrected chapters** 03-08 where later experience contradicts them ("always do packet slots first"; telling the game the truth about a departed player; pacing to the monitor; the first Shining Soul II transport is marked as superseded).
- **`games/shining-soul-2.md`** and an extended `games/TEMPLATE.md` (link style, seam, transport, message kinds by role, barrier, departure behaviour, porting status, test status).
- **Reference code**: `reference/src/gnc_direct.c` (+ header): state blocks handed over as they arrive, one reliable ordered message channel through the host, holes stepped over. Written fresh for this repository, generic, MIT. `reference/tests/test_direct.c`: 2-4 simulated players over a lossy in-process link with outages.
- **`tools/relay.py`**: `--outage SEAT:START:LENGTH` (cut a player off for a while) and `--max-datagram`, with unit tests.
- README ("Try it in ten minutes"), ROADMAP, CONTRIBUTING (how to add a game sheet and a verified lesson), references.

## Tests run (Windows x86-64, clang 23 from llvm-mingw, Python 3.14)

```
cc -std=c99 -O2 -Wall -Iinclude src/gbanocable.c tests/test_sim.c -o test_sim && ./test_sim       -> all ok
cc -std=c99 -O2 -Wall -Iinclude src/gbanocable.c tests/test_check.c -o test_check && ./test_check -> all ok
cc -std=c99 -O2 -Wall -Iinclude src/gnc_direct.c tests/test_direct.c -o test_direct && ./test_direct
  3 players, player 2 away 300 frames                 order once fresh   (4 holes stepped over)
  3 players, player 2 away 300 frames, no hole fix    order once FROZEN  (the check fires)
  all ok
./test_direct --no-hole-fix                           -> FAILED ..., exit status 1 (as intended)
python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p "test_*.py"  -> Ran 19 tests, OK
```

## What is not verified, or is inference

- Every ShiningSource figure quoted is from scripted headless players on one machine with a relay that simulates the network; none is from a real network. The chapters say so per figure.
- `docs/14` (recomp playbook) and section 13 of `docs/15` are a method derived from the port; no static recompilation has run these steps. The "local peer" variant of the message channel and the "write the standing character's block so it satisfies the check" idea are untested inferences.
- `docs/13`: that the C relay's token is visible to other members of a room is read from its code, not tested.
- `docs/12` describes an uncommitted prototype of the port.
- `gnc_direct` leaves out giving a player up, revival after that, rooms and join in progress; its test certifies the transport's contract with simulated players, not a game.

body:
Here is everything you need to know about this upgrade. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ✳️ tailwindcss (4.3.3 → 4.3.5) · [Repo](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss) · [Changelog](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
Release Notes

4.3.5

Fixed

  • Canonicalization: improve performance in projects with many functional variant values (e.g. a matchVariant plugin with thousands of values) (#20663)
  • Don't crash or create a fallback with the wrong color for a color-mix(…) without a color interpolation method (e.g. color-mix(var(--color-red-500)) or color-mix(currentcolor 50%, transparent)) (#20658, #20666)
  • Ensure @tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi loads instead of hanging forever (e.g. with NAPI_RS_FORCE_WASI=error or in WebContainers) (#20667)
  • Remove as: '*.css' from the @tailwindcss/turbopack setup in its README, because it breaks CSS modules (#20660)
  • Ignore <!-- and --> between top-level rules in CSS instead of throwing or swallowing the next rule (e.g. a { color: red } --> b { color: blue }) (#20665)
  • Ensure @tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi detects changed and new source files after the first scan (e.g. in WebContainers) (#20487)
  • Prevent type errors with skipLibCheck: false caused by imports of unshipped modules in the @tailwindcss/node type declarations (#20632)

4.3.4

Added

  • Add @tailwindcss/turbopack, a Turbopack loader for using Tailwind CSS with Next.js (#20367)

Fixed

  • Ensure watch mode detects changes to symlinked @source files whose real paths aren't otherwise scanned (#20356)
  • Ensure variants using @scope wrap generated utilities instead of nesting inside them (#20369)
  • Ensure nested @scope rules preserve their scoping semantics when flattened (#20369)
  • Preserve declarations directly inside @scope by wrapping them in :where(:scope) (#20369)
  • Ensure generated utilities include a space in empty var() fallbacks (e.g. var(--tw-blur,) → var(--tw-blur, )) (#20373)
  • Canonicalization: convert arbitrary breakpoint and container query variants to named equivalents (e.g. max-[64rem]:flex → max-lg:flex) (#20380)
  • Prevent @tailwindcss/vite from crashing on every edit under Vite's experimental bundledDev mode (#20379)
  • Ensure @tailwindcss/oxide falls back to WASM on platforms without native bindings (#20383)
  • Extract class candidates from Ruby %w and %W literals using angle brackets or custom delimiters (e.g. %w<flex>, %w|flex|), including in Slim and Haml templates (#20387)
  • Preserve whitespace in --default(…) values in functional @utility definitions (e.g. --default(box alphabetic) no longer becomes boxalphabetic) (#20392)
  • Ensure automatic source detection respects negation-based .gitignore files (e.g. /* followed by !/… patterns) (#20397)
  • Ensure root theme('…') namespace lookups in JavaScript plugins and config files return the full namespace object instead of the value of its DEFAULT key (#20399)
  • Skip ignored directories when generating watch globs instead of walking their contents on every rebuild (#20408)
  • Drop invalid UTF-8 candidates during class detection (#20389)
  • Prevent @tailwindcss/vite from forcing full-page reloads for scanned files that Vite does not handle as modules (e.g. .php files) (#20414)
  • Canonicalization: don't merge utilities that reference different theme variables set to CSS-wide keywords like unset (#20417)
  • Don't generate utilities when a modifier is used that would otherwise be silently ignored (e.g. rounded-sm/[5], shadow-sm/foo, stroke-2/50) (#20419)
  • Preserve and,

JAR-317. Project manager agents could change .github/ (CI workflows run with repo secrets), and the protected-path check was case-sensitive, so .Claude/settings.json or .GitHub/workflows/x.yml slipped past on Windows/macOS.

body: ## Что сделано На сайт добавлен раздел «Журнал»: список `/journal` и отдельные страницы `/journal/`. Вёрстка на тех же токенах, шрифте STIX Two Text, шапке и подвале, что и остальные внутренние страницы. Пункт «Журнал» стоит предпоследним в навигации — и в шапке на десктопе, и в мобильном меню: Портфолио, Этапы, Цены, О нас, Журнал, Контакты. В подвале отдельного меню страниц нет: там соцсети, адрес и ссылка на политику конфиденциальности. Реальных статей в коммите нет. Пока папка `content/journal` пустая, список открывается и пишет «Пока в журнале нет статей». Страница с `noindex`, чтобы пустой раздел не попал в поиск. Ссылку в меню не прятал: в задаче она нужна в навигации, а пустое состояние спокойное и в том же языке, что и остальные страницы. Как только появится первый markdown-файл и пройдёт сборка, `noindex` снимется сам, карточки выстроятся от новых к старым, по 12 на страницу (`/journal/page/2` и дальше). ## Стек Статический сайт без фреймворка и без npm-зависимостей. Node-скрипт `scripts/build.js` собирает HTML, `onreza.rules.toml` делает чистые URL, Onreza отдаёт `dist/` как статику. Журнал встроен в эту же сборку: свой мини-парсер markdown в `scripts/lib/journal.js`, без новых пакетов (workflow деплоя не делает `npm install`). ## Как добавить статью Файл `content/journal/.md` и картинки в `images/journal//`. Подробно: `content/journal/README.md`. В шапке файла: `title` (SEO ``), `description`, `h1`, `excerpt`, `date`, `cover`, `coverAlt`. По желанию `updated` и `draft: true` (черновик на сайт не попадает). В теле: абзацы, `##` / `###`, ссылки `[текст](/portfolio)`, картинка отдельной строкой `![подпись](/images/...)`, список, блок `:::faq`. Из FAQ собирается FAQPage JSON-LD. Дальше `node scripts/build.js`. На каждую статью — свой HTML с уникальными title и description, canonical, Open Graph и Article/FAQ JSON-LD. Картинки не кропаются: `width: 100%`, `height: auto`, `object-fit: contain`. На карточках и в статье видны оба края кадра, пропорция сохраняется. Sitemap в репозитории нет (`sitemap.xml` не найден), поэтому журнал в него не добавлялся. Когда карта сайта появится, в неё нужно включить `/journal` и `/journal/<slug>`. ## Деплой на Onreza Автодеплой уже настроен, этот PR в `main` не влит. - Пуш в `main` запускает `.github/workflows/deploy-onreza.yml` (`workflow_dispatch` тоже есть). - Джоба: Node 20, `npm run build`, установка CLI `nrz`, `nrz deploy --prod`. Нужен секрет `NRZ_TOKEN`. - `onreza.toml`: `build.command = "npm run build"`, `output_directory = "dist"`, `deploy.compute = "static"`. Проект `studio1903`, id `019f3811-6c1d-7dc0-8789-87bab5a69cc1`. - Сборка пишет `onreza.rules.toml`. Для журнала сейчас одно правило: `/journal` → `/pages/journal.html`. Правила статей и `/journal/page/N` появятся при сборке, когда будут файлы. - Вручную: `npm run build`, затем `nrz deploy --prod`. ## Проверка `node scripts/test-journal.js` — разбор markdown, экранирование, пагинация 12, JSON-LD, черновики, отсутствующий файл картинки. author: carloseduardolourenco
body:
## Resumo
A chamada por token digitado passa a ser por **QR code projetado**, com ciclo curto, confirmação pelo celular do aluno e revisão do professor. O código digitado continua funcionando para quem não tem câmera.

## Professor
- Abre a chamada escolhendo **turma**, **tempo do QR** (15, 30, 45 ou 60 s) e **limite de presenças** (automático = alunos com matrícula ativa, ou personalizado para dias com poucos alunos)
- **Janela de projeção** com apenas o QR, o código e o contador, para compartilhar na aula. A lista de presença fica só na tela dele
- Quando o tempo acaba, a chamada **fecha** e só reabre se ele clicar em **Renovar QR**, que gera um código novo
- **Finalizar chamada** mostra as faltas e as presenças em análise, com os botões **Aceitar** e **Recusar**

## Aluno
- Lê o QR (ou digita o código), faz login se precisar e tem **3 minutos** para confirmar
- A leitura feita antes do login não se perde
- Vê na hora se a presença foi **registrada**, ficou **em análise** ou foi **recusada**, com o motivo

## Regras
| Tipo | Quando | Resultado |
|---|---|---|
| Recusa | Tempo de confirmação esgotado, chamada finalizada, sem matrícula ativa, presença repetida, limite atingido | Não grava |
| Em análise | Mesmo celular de outro aluno; localização negada, imprecisa ou fora do raio da instituição | Grava e o professor decide |

- Só a **distância até a instituição** é guardada, nunca as coordenadas do aluno (LGPD)
- O limite é conferido com `select_for_update`, para dois alunos simultâneos não passarem juntos
- O **painel de desempenho** passa a contar apenas presenças **confirmadas**

## Banco de dados
- `Chamada`: `ciclo_segundos`, `renovacoes`, `finalizada_em`
- `Registro_de_Presenca`: `situacao`, `motivo`, `origem`, `distancia_m`, `dispositivo`. As presenças que já existem ficam como **confirmadas**
- Novo model **`Instituicao`** (latitude, longitude, raio aceito e precisão mínima), ligado à `Turma`. Por enquanto é cadastrado pelo `/admin`. Turma sem instituição faz chamada normalmente, só sem conferir a localização
- Migrações: `chamada/0005` e `turmas/0006`

## Commits
- Campos do ciclo do QR, da situação da presença e da instituição
- Regra de registro da presença (`chamada/servicos.py`)
- Telas do professor (painel da chamada e projeção) e do aluno (confirmação e resultado)
- Estilos no padrão visual do SIMAP
- Testes

## Como testar
```bash
python manage.py migrate
python manage.py test --settings=SIMAP.settings_test

author: saagedal
body:
Reading a Direct2D image back into software memory dereferenced a null bitmap when the graphics device had been lost or was out of memory, crashing the app. `readFromDirect2DBitmap` now returns `false` in that case, which every caller already handles.

## Changes

- **juce_graphics** (`modules/juce_graphics/native/juce_Direct2DImage_windows.cpp`) — `readFromDirect2DBitmap` returns `false` when `Direct2DBitmap::createBitmap` returns null for the CPU-readable bitmap, when `CopyFromBitmap` fails, or when `Map` fails or gives no data. Previously the result of each was used unchecked.
- **juce_graphics** — the readable bitmap is now mapped once, up front, in `readFromDirect2DBitmap`, and unmapped by a `ScopeGuard`. `TexturePixelData` is given the mapped rectangle instead of mapping the bitmap itself in `initialiseBitmapData`, so its `Releaser` is gone. The conversion runs in its own scope, so the source image is released before the bitmap is unmapped.

## Notes for review

- `createPersistentBackup` already turns `false` into `State::outdated`, and the overload that builds a new software image returns an empty pointer. So a failed readback skips the backup and the content is redrawn, instead of crashing.
- Mapping up front was needed so that a failed `Map` can also be turned into `false`. Inside `initialiseBitmapData` there was nothing to return it to, and a null `mapped.bits` would have reached the pixel conversion. `TexturePixelData` is only ever created here for this single read-only conversion, so moving the map out of it changes nothing else.
- Our Acoustica build crashed through `Image::multiplyAllAlphas` → `Direct2DPixelData::applyEffectInArea` → `createPersistentBackup`, but the fix is in the shared readback, so every path that reads a D2D image back benefits.

## Testing

Untested: not built, and not run against a lost device. Reproducing it needs a removed or exhausted GPU device, for example from a driver reset during playback with a meter open.

## Related

Sentry NATIVE-DX (Acoustica 8.0.1, Windows): `EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION_READ / 0x0` in `readFromDirect2DBitmap`, called from the correlation meter's Lissajous image.

author: tonypinkevych
body:
## What changes

- **A calm answer card.** The calculator shows the sum as it was read in a small, faint line, over the answer in big numbers. Enter says **Copy**, which is what it does.
- **A faint unit.** A `number` block takes `unit=`, the part of its shown value to draw faint, such as `₴`, `mi` or `days`. Any spot can use it, on a card or a sheet. `PROTOCOL.md` lists it.
- **`openspot calc solve` prints `unit=`.** It gives the currency symbol, the unit of a measure, the word of a span and AM or PM. When the Mac writes a currency only as its code, the answer uses the symbol of its home country, such as `4 544,63 ₴` in place of `4 544,63 UAH`, and bitcoin uses `₿`.
- **Powers read as math.** `2^64` reads back as `2⁶⁴` in the caption.
- **Old rates are a card too.** The caption names the day of the rates and how old they are, in the tone that warns.

## Simpler after review

- **One name per idea.** The word that Enter shows is `openTitle` everywhere. The big number of a block is `number` in code, as in the protocol; "metric" is only the mark of a widget.
- **One answer type.** The date reader returns a `CalcAnswer`. A failure of the rates is thrown as `CalcRateFailure`, which prints its own `status=` line, and old rates are the fact `ratesAreOld`.
- **Facts as fields.** `calc solve` prints the day of the rates as `rates=`, so the spot reads fields and cuts no text. A number keeps its unit inside its control.
- **One view of a number.** `SpotNumberView` draws a number on a card and on a sheet.
- **One rule for a unit.** A currency takes its formatter's symbol, a time its AM or PM, and a measure or a span its title without the number its formatter wrote.

## Checks

- `make verify` passed after each commit.
- A pixel diff of renders before and after the simplifications shows 0 differing pixels: three number views, and the nine real calculator cards.
- Nine real answers were rendered through `Openspot render --card large`: currency, sum, a long number, units, a date, a span, a time zone, bitcoin and old rates.
- The ring and the Copy footer are proven by tests, not seen in the running panel. The faint AM was not seen, because the Mac uses a 24-hour clock.

## Summary

Constitution 1.14.0 -> 1.15.0 implementing PO S54-PO-4 (S54-R11). Docs-only; no application code or workflows changed.

### a. Main merge gate (R4)
- Old: "before any merge to `main`, require three independent executed successful full CI attempts on the exact PR head."
- New: "require one executed successful full CI attempt on the exact PR head (a `pull_request` run, or one `workflow_dispatch` run under the existing dispatch-validity rules)."
- Per-attempt validity rules retained (required jobs, executed steps > 0, PR/head/merge tuple, merge-tree T == T' recheck, fail-closed, infra reruns never counted). Count references replaced consistently (docs-only paragraph now one full `workflow_dispatch` run; Supplementary merge gates now "verifies the counted run").
- Added: a test failure that passes on rerun is a flake, recorded and reported, still needing one clean counted run.

### b. AI review clause (R2)
- BLOCKING = P0/P1, or any finding about security, authorization/RLS, data loss/corruption, money math, privacy, a failing/missing test for changed behavior, or a spec/FR contradiction; fixed in the current round with a test.
- NON-BLOCKING = P2/P3, nitpicks, style, refactors, "consider" suggestions; not fixed in the PR, reply once "Deferred to backlog: <backlog id>", append to `~/.lifter/backlog/review-deferred.md`, then resolve the thread (satisfies "answer it with evidence").
- Uncertain severity decided by the architect and recorded, never silently downgraded.
- At most two AI-review rounds per PR (one provider per round); blocking findings left after round two go to the PO for decision.

### c. Standing approval (R5)
- Existing clause retained; coverage extended to docs-only PRs and PRs at the R2 two-round cap after the PO's decision.
- Always-explicit-PO-command exclusions: `.specify/memory/constitution.md`, `.github/workflows/**`, branch protection, secrets handling, production configuration, open PO-DECISION-NEEDED.
- Constitution PRs always require the PO's exact-SHA command (unchanged).

### d. Spec Kit (R6)
- Analyze reruns required only when FR/SC/acceptance requirement text changes; code/test-only review fixes do not require a re-dated Analyze.
- Clarify/Analyze zero open CRITICAL/HIGH findings unchanged.

- `**Version**: 1.15.0 | **Ratified**: 2026-10-27 | **Last Amended**: 2026-11-13 (S54-PO-4; S54-R11)`

author: seeshuraj
body:
## Why
At 2,000 accounts per college the grading queue returned every submission with full text plus one extra request per row, the users page downloaded every account, the landing page downloaded every dashboard, and every open tab polled notifications every 30 s.

## Server
- `GET /api/instructor/submissions?limit=` → `{ items, total, nextCursor }`, keyset-paged newest first, `status` (pending|graded|all) and `courseId` filters, `file_count` and `course_name` included. Without `limit`: at most 500 pending rows (older clients).
- `GET /api/admin/users?limit=` → `{ items, total }` with server search (`q`, LIKE wildcards escaped) and `role` filter. New `GET /api/admin/users/role-counts`.
- Migration `20261113130000_grading_queue_paging.sql`: `submissions.submitted_at` NOT NULL (it already defaults to `now()`) and a partial index for the pending queue per college.

## Client
- Grading queue: 25 per page with "Load more"; the per-row file-count request is gone (was N requests per dashboard load).
- Users page: debounced server search, role filter, 50 per page, Previous/Next.
- Course management fetches instructors only; admin dashboard uses role counts.
- **Lazy pages:** every signed-in page loads on first visit; recharts is its own chunk. A stale chunk after a deploy reloads once instead of a blank screen.
- **vercel.json:** `/assets/*` cached 1 year immutable, `index.html` revalidated, missing assets 404 (no longer rewritten to HTML), HSTS / nosniff / referrer policy.
- **Notifications:** poll the unread count every 60 s only while the tab is visible; fetch the list when the count rises or the panel opens.
- **Bug fix:** "mark all read" used PATCH against a POST route and never worked.

Every client accepts the old array response too, so Vercel deploying before Render is safe.

## Tests
3 new paging tests (84 total here, passing). CI runs typecheck and build.

## Rollout
Merge → apply the migration → Render Manual Deploy.
