body:
**Gestapelt auf #811** (Auswahl „Bestehendes Concept“). Bis #811 gemergt ist, zeigt dieser PR auch dessen Commit; neu ist hier nur `ce588545`. **Enthält eine Migration.**

Concept → Positionen → Erstellung (Dominique 13.11.2026: „Das sind meine Gerichte, die dort hinterlegt sind. Ich müsste jetzt auf Umwegen die Gerichte anlegen lassen.“).

**Befund**
Der Fan-out eines Concepts (`fanoutConceptInvention`) zählte nur die leeren Positionen, rief `kiDivergenzConcept(Anzahl)` und ordnete die erfundenen Skizzen der Reihe nach zu. Ein eigener Gerichtstitel an der Position ging nie in den Prompt. Die Kette dahinter passt aber schon: Skizze (Titel + Beschreibung) → geplanter Gericht-Schritt → Freigabe → Gericht in der Position. Es fehlte nur der Einstieg für die eigene Skizze.

**Was sich ändert**
1. **Vorgabe an der leeren Position:** neue Spalten `dish_brief` (Gerichtstitel) und `dish_brief_note` (Notiz) an `foodalchemist_concept_slots`. Eigene Spalten, nicht `title`: der ist das Anzeige-Label und wird bei Hand-Anlage mit dem Gangnamen gefüllt, als Vorgabe gelesen entstünde ein Gericht namens „Vorspeise“.
2. **Fan-out:** Position mit Vorgabe → Skizze 1:1 mit geplantem Gericht-Schritt, ohne KI-Aufruf (Vorschlag-Gate wie bisher: gebaut wird erst nach der Freigabe). Nur Positionen ohne Vorgabe gehen an `kiDivergenzConcept`; die Vorgaben stehen dort als Kontext `vorgaben_im_menue` („steht schon im Menü, nicht wiederholen“). Stehen an allen leeren Positionen Vorgaben, wird die KI gar nicht nach Ideen gefragt. „A | B | C“ wird zum Komponentenplan des Bauplans.
3. **Wortlaut (Entscheid Dominique):** nach dem Bau bleibt die Vorgabe als Kundenwording der Position stehen; ein schon gepflegtes Wording gewinnt. Der interne Name folgt der Namensregel.
4. **Bestand zuerst (Entscheid Dominique):** gibt es ein **freigegebenes** Gericht mit demselben Namens-Token-Set (das Kürzel in eckigen Klammern zählt nicht), heißt der Schritt „Aus Bestand: …“. Die Freigabe des Schritts übernimmt es in die Position, gebaut wird nichts. Entwürfe und nur ähnliche Gerichte zählen nicht als Treffer.
5. **Eingabe an drei Stellen:** Concepter (leere Position, Titel und Notiz), Leitstelle (Plan-Panel „Menü-Aufbau“ mit Vorgabe je Position und „Position hinzufügen“), MCP (`concept_slots.POST`/`PUT` nehmen `dish_brief` und `dish_brief_note`, `concepts.GET` liefert sie). Schreiben nur im Besitzer-Team und nur an einer leeren Position.

**Struktur**
Neuer `ConceptVorgabenService` (setze / planeVorgaben / setzeGericht / uebernimmBestand / bestandsGericht), Traits `ManagesSlotVorgabe` (Concepter) und `PlanGerichtVorgaben` (Leitstelle), zwei Partials. Grund: `PlanningCascadeService`, `Planung/Index`, `Concepter/Editor`, dessen View und `ConceptService` stehen auf ihrer Größen-Basis. `PlanningCascadeService` sinkt um eine Zeile (Basis 3518 → 3517 gesenkt), die anderen bleiben gleich. `MaterializeConceptIdeaJob` bekommt die Bestand-Weiche vor dem Bau.

**Migration:** `2026_12_26_100000_add_dish_brief_to_foodalchemist_concept_slots` — zwei nullable Spalten, additiv, kein Backfill.

**Tests**
- Neu: `tests/Feature/ConceptGerichtVorgabeTest.php` (14 Tests): setzen/löschen; nicht an belegter Position, nicht im geerbten Concept; Fan-out gemischt (Vorgabe + Erfindung, die KI wird nur nach einer Idee gefragt); nur Vorgaben (kein KI-Aufruf); Freigabe startet den Bau; Wortlaut wird Kundenwording; Bestand zuerst inklusive Übernahme; Bestand nur freigegeben und namensgleich; Leitstelle, Concepter und MCP.
- Lauf über 100 Dateien (grep auf PlanningCascadeService, IdeenService, MaterializeConceptIdeaJob, Concepter\Editor, Planung\Index, concept_slots.POST/PUT, concepts.GET, concepter- und planung-Views, plus Wächter PolicyTest, Spec77bBereicheTest, UiRegelnTest, DateigroessenWaechterTest, Spec84SichtWaechterTest, Spec84ServiceEigentumWaechterTest, EnumStatusVergleichWaechterTest, Spec84ToolListeTest, McpToolsTest): 1227 Tests, 1226 grün, 1 rot.
- **Der eine rote Test kommt nicht aus diesem PR:** `Spec84FehlertypenTest` schlägt bei `src/Tools/PlanungSessionPostTool.php:117` an (`str_contains($ex->getMessage(), 'nicht gefunden')`), eingeführt mit #806. Die Datei ist hier unverändert.
- Keine volle Suite. Der echte KI-Weg (Ideen-Prompt mit `vorgaben_im_menue`, Bau des Gerichts) ist nur verdrahtet getestet, nicht gegen einen echten Provider.

**Offen (nicht in diesem PR):** „Rezeptur erstellen“ für vorhandene Gerichte ohne Komponenten folgt als eigener PR.

author: vazarkevych
body:
## Features and Changes

`GrowthBook` never read sticky bucket assignments from `Context.StickyBucketService`. An instance held only the documents handed over on the context and the ones it saved itself. A user seen before by another instance, or in an earlier process, was therefore hashed again, and could change variation once the experiment's weights changed, which is what sticky bucketing exists to prevent. `GrowthBookClient` was not affected: it reads the service on every evaluation.

Assignments are now loaded from the service, as `refreshStickyBuckets` does in the JS SDK:
- when the instance is built;
- when features are loaded, or returned by remote evaluation;
- when the attributes are updated or merged, so switching to another user loads that user's assignments.

How loading behaves:
- What the service returns is merged into the documents already held, which take precedence, as when an assignment is saved. Documents handed over on the context may not be in the service, and an assignment saved while the service was being read is not in its answer, so replacing the held documents would lose both.
- Unlike JS, the documents handed over on the context are not written back to the service on construction, since that could overwrite newer assignments another instance saved.
- A service that cannot be read is logged at warning level and leaves the held documents as they are, so a store outage cannot stop an instance being built or evaluating.

## Testing

- `StickyBucketRefreshTests`: an assignment stored by another instance survives a weight change; updating or merging to another user loads that user's assignment; loading features loads the assignments they need; documents handed over on the context are kept, and merged with a stored document for the same user; a service that throws does not stop construction or evaluation. Four of the seven fail on main, and removing the merge, the error handling, the load on construction or the load after `LoadFeatures` each fails its own test.
- All sticky bucket tests, including the spec fixtures, still pass.
- Full suite passes in Debug, Release and on one core.

author: neotoma-agent
body:
## Summary

Regular-expression patterns supplied in schemas and rendering rules are now validated and evaluated through one shared helper, `src/services/safe_pattern.ts`. The helper bounds pattern length, subject length, pattern shape and evaluation time, and never reports a match for a pattern it refuses.

Three places used to compile such patterns directly:

- field constraints (`constraints.pattern`)
- derived-entity conditions (`matches_any_pattern`)
- rendered-page conformance rules

All three now go through the helper. Schema registration refuses patterns whose shape the helper recognises as unsupported, and returns the rewrite guidance as a structured `hint`.

**What guarantees the bounds.** The time limits (per check, per store request and per rendered page, below) apply on every path and are the guarantee. The registration shape rules are a conservative first filter that catches common shapes. Some uncommon forms are not caught at registration and are bounded only by the time limits.

## What is bounded

| Bound | Value |
|---|---|
| Pattern length | 256 characters |
| Subject length | 10,000 characters (rendered-page rules: 1,000,000, since they check whole page bodies) |
| Evaluation time per pattern | 100 ms |
| Evaluation time per store request | 1,500 ms, shared by constraint and derived-condition checks (see below) |
| Group nesting depth | 20 |
| `matches_any_pattern` patterns per condition | 16 |
| Patterns per schema (constraint patterns plus condition patterns) | 64 |
| Rendered-page rules evaluated per page | 32, within a shared budget of about 1,000 ms (checked before each rule, so the last rule can add up to one per-check limit) |
| Flags accepted on a rendered-page rule | `i`, `m`, `s`, `u` |

## What registration refuses

`register_schema` and `update_schema_incremental` refuse the common forms of these categories, over HTTP and MCP. The list is not exhaustive of every spelling; forms that are not recognised are bounded by the time limits instead. The response is `400 SCHEMA_VALIDATION_FAILED` over HTTP, or an `error` object with `error_code: "SCHEMA_VALIDATION_FAILED"` over MCP. The `message` contains `is not accepted` and names the field (or the derived-entity condition and pattern index). The rewrite guidance is in `hint` (`details.hint` over HTTP), and `details.refusal` names the kind: `shape`, `length`, `syntax` or `count`.

- **Backreferences** (`\1`, `\k<name>`). Remove the backreference and match the repeated text with an explicit group.
- **Common nested variable quantifiers**: a quantifier inside a group that is itself repeated without bound, or more than 5 times. Use a bounded count on the inner part, for example `(\d{1,3},){1,32}` instead of `(\d+,)+`.
- **Common repeated alternations whose branches begin the same way**, or that include an empty branch. Make the branches distinct, or remove the repetition around them.
- **Length and structure limits**: more than 256 characters, groups nested deeper than 20, unbalanced groups, an unterminated or nested character class.
- **Count limits**: more than 16 patterns in one condition, or more than 64 patterns in one schema.

Syntactically invalid patterns were already refused and still are. A syntactically invalid `matches_any_pattern` entry keeps its earlier substring fallback.

The rules also err on the cautious side: a few harmless patterns that nest quantifiers will be refused and need a bounded rewrite.

This narrows what registration accepts, so it ships with a legacy-payload fixture (`v0.28.x/register_schema_repeated_group_pattern`, `rejected` with a hint assertion) and a compatibility entry in `tests/contract/legacy_payloads/CHANGES.md` for the release's **Breaking changes** section.

## Behaviour for schemas that are already stored

- **Stored schemas keep loading.** Load-time validation checks pattern syntax only, as before. The new shape, length and count rules apply when a schema is registered. Conditional stores and cleared-fields snapshot reads on a type whose stored schema holds a now-refused pattern continue to work; tests cover both.
- **Activating an older stored schema version does not re-run the registration rules.** Its patterns stay time-bounded at evaluation.
- **`update_schema_incremental` on a schema that already holds such a pattern hits the same `is not accepted` error, even when the edit is unrelated to the pattern**, because the edit registers a new version of the whole schema. Rewrite the pattern in the same edit or first.
- **At evaluation, each sink fails safely:**
  - Field constraint: the value is rejected with "has a pattern constraint that cannot be evaluated safely", followed by a pointer to rewrite the pattern in the schema and register the updated schema. An over-long value is rejected with a message stating the limit. A warning is logged naming the field, entity type and schema version, never the pattern.
  - `matches_any_pattern`: the refused pattern is ignored and never matches. A warning names the entity type, schema version, rule, condition and pattern index.
  - Rendered-page rule: the rule is skipped, which means it does not apply to that page, whether it is a `require_present` or a `require_absent` rule. A warning names the rule code and index. This matches how malformed rules were already handled. A stored `conformance_policy` holding a refused pattern is skipped this way through the publish path; the policy's other rules still apply (test included).

## Per-request budget for store requests

Each pattern check is limited to 100 ms, and a store request runs many checks (one per entity per constrained field, plus derived conditions). Each store request (REST, MCP and the conditional path) therefore shares one evaluation budget of 1,500 ms across all of its constraint and derived-condition checks:

- A pattern that exceeds the per-check limit is remembered for the rest of that request and is not run again.
- Results for short values are remembered per request, so a value checked twice (for example under the `warn` policy, or in the conditional path) is evaluated once.
- When the budget is spent, remaining pattern-checked values are rejected with a message saying the request's evaluation limit was reached and suggesting fewer entities per request. Remaining derived conditions do not match.
- Log lines for an unusable pattern are written once per request, not once per entity.

Tests store many entities against a stored schema whose patterns run past the limit, over REST and MCP: a shared pattern is evaluated once and the request finishes quickly; many distinct such patterns stop at the budget (about 1.5 s) and every constrained field is rejected. With the budget disabled the same test takes about 3 s, which the test's bound catches.

## Cost of a normal batch

Measured with a script (not committed) on the development machine, 200 entities with 2 patterned fields each (400 checks of ordinary patterns), median of 20 runs:

| | Time per batch |
|---|---|
| Direct compile-and-test, before | 0.05 ms |
| Through the helper, after | about 13 ms |

That is roughly 32 microseconds per check, almost all of it the per-evaluation time limit. Compiled patterns are already cached inside the evaluation context; that is not where the time goes. The added cost is small next to the database writes for the same batch, and is capped per request by the 1,500 ms budget. A faster path for short values was considered and not taken, because the time limit is what bounds the shapes the static rules do not recognise.

## Known limits

- Rendered-page rules are tenant data on a `conformance_policy` entity and have no store-time validation; they are checked only at evaluation. Follow-up: store-time validation of rendered-page rules (tracked separately).
- The static rules are heuristics. The evaluation time limits are what bound anything they do not recognise.
- Follow-up: stricter quantifier parsing at registration, in a separate PR from branch `fix/patte

## Why

`falls` is still red on the owner's PC after #450. Every table number matches the cloud's: cells, ground, held, the depths, and the lake below at 1 m (`dry_cell_depth 256000`). Even so, all 5 falls count as dry on Windows. The PC check never posted the dry fall's own drop, top, way or the level below it, so it was impossible to tell whether fallsNear's sum or the test's decision is what differs.

I checked the cloud's raw sum for fall 0: the lip is point (19, -2), ground 300 cm, depth 5356; the point below is (20, -2), ground -100 cm, depth 256000. That gives a drop of 3.02092 m, and the bed plus 1 m of water puts the level below at exactly 0.

## What

- On a dry fall, the test now redoes fallsNear's sum from the table, using `cell()` and `groundCm()` for the lip's point and the point the fall heads to. It logs both points' ground and depth, plus the drop and top this sum gives.
- `tools/ci/pc_checks/falls.json` posts the existing dry line's way x/z, drop, top and below level, and the new table line's numbers. I checked these regexes against a forced dry run in the cloud: way 1 0, drop 3.02092, top 3.02092, below level 0, lip 300/5356, below -100/256000.

Reading the next PC run:
- If the table sum gives 3.02092 m while the fall says 4.02, the fault is fallsNear's arithmetic on MSVC.
- If both say 4.02, the fault is in a value the hashes don't cover.
- If the fall's drop is 3.02 and it still counts as dry, the fault is the test's decision.

author: vudigapranav
body:
Resolves #8493.

`JsonRequest.replace(data=..., dumps_kwargs=...)` serialized the new `data` with the original request's `dumps_kwargs`, while storing the replacement options on the new request. It now serializes with the replacement options when they are passed (with the same `sort_keys=True` default as the constructor), and keeps using the original ones otherwise. `replace(dumps_kwargs=...)` without `data` keeps the existing body, since the original data isn't stored; the new options apply to later `replace(data=...)` calls.

Tests in `tests/test_http_request_json.py` cover the issue's `Decimal`/`default=str` case, replacement options overriding the original ones (`ensure_ascii=False`, `{}`, `None`), and `dumps_kwargs`-only replacement. They fail on master and pass with this change. `tox -e py -- tests/test_http_request_json.py` and `tox -e pylint` pass; `tox -e mypy` reports 3 errors in `scrapy/spiders/sitemap.py` / `tests/test_spider_sitemap.py` that are already on master.

author: evil88332115-png
body:
head：`7ebeacc`（分支 `wp3/fw-advisory`，已併入 main cc7d101）。

韌體 SBOM 的公告比對（D-043 (1) 的 Intel 部分，加上 D-051）：Intel 微碼依 Intel 公開的微碼發佈資料離線比對；Intel CSME 元件加上 NVD 的 CPE。每份韌體 SBOM 的報告都有「公告比對」一節。比不到的一律寫「資料庫沒有資料，以廠商公告為準」，沒有任何結果代表「沒有漏洞」；`dumpling:vuln-assessment` 維持 `NOT_ASSESSED`。NVIDIA vBIOS 的比對（D-043 (1) 的另一部分）不在這個 PR。

## Intel 微碼（`tools/cra/fw_advisory.py`、`tools/cra/intel_ucode_releases.py`、`tools/cra/data/intel-microcode-releases.json`）
- 資料表由 `intel_ucode_releases.py` 從固定來源產生，CI 不連網：
  - 來源：`intel/Intel-Linux-Processor-Microcode-Data-Files` 的 `releasenote.md`，tag `microcode-20261110`、commit `d71fe4e2f0f70a49ebbac7f2c7e915f181361974`、sha256 `338b556b…11f3`。
  - 涵蓋 45 個 release、920 個表格列。
  - 資料表的 sha256 固定在 `TABLE_SHA256`；`verify` 可以從固定來源重現資料表。
- 結果有四種：
  - `affected-candidate`：較新的 release 列了 INTEL-SA，列成候選。候選只到 release 層級，不一定影響這個 CPUID，待人審。
  - `older-no-sa`：有較新的 revision，但那些 release 沒有列出公告。
  - `up-to-date`：等於資料表裡的最新 revision。不代表沒有漏洞，以 Intel 公告為準。
  - `NOT_ASSESSED`：資料庫沒有資料，以廠商公告為準。
- 候選可以多列，但不能漏列，也不能把較舊的微碼標成 up-to-date，所以另外處理了：
  - 「New Disclosures Updated in Prior Releases」表：revision 不高於列出的版本，就列成候選（how=disclosed）。
  - 20250812 那段散文（releasenote.md:346）：用一份明確、可重現的人工對照（`PROSE_RULES`，記行號與一句原文）納入 ADL／RPL／SPR／EMR／MTL／ARL 的 key；同 F-M-S 但原文沒提的 key 加註。
  - 同 F-M-S 有交集的遮罩在之後的 release 還有更新時，舊遮罩不標 up-to-date，改成 `NOT_ASSESSED`（`superseded-platform-mask`）。
  - 退版（revert）的歷史會加註。
- 授權：`releasenote.md` 沒有明確授權。資料表只取事實性欄位（tag、日期、INTEL-SA 編號、F-M-S、遮罩、revision、Processor 代號），不抄原文，只有人工對照引用一句。PROVENANCE 已寫明。
- 加了 `.gitattributes`，資料表不做換行轉換，避免 sha256 不符。

## Intel CSME 的 CPE（D-051）
- NVD 的 product 是 `converged_security_management_engine_firmware`（2026-11-13 查證）。NVD 的版本只有三段，所以 CPE 只放前三段，並註明 NVD 資料不完整，最新的 CSME CVE 設定停在 2022 年。
- `dumpling:cpe-basis` 只有兩個值：
  - `listed`：版本清單寫明是 CSME。
  - `inferred`：family 讀不出來，major 在 11～30 之間。報告寫明「family 是由版本推定，比對結果待人審」。
- 不帶 CPE、記 `dumpling:cpe-gap` 的情況：major 小於 11 或大於 30、讀不出版本、清單寫 ME／TXE／SPS。
  - **版本清單對同一個版本寫了不同的 family（例如 CSME 和 TXE）時，也不推定、不帶 CPE，標 ATTENTION。這條比 D-051 更保守。**
- 臨時 DT 沒有開 NVD 來源，所以這個 CPE 只對 Grype 有用；報告寫明。

## AMD 平台
AMD 的微碼、PSP 韌體、AGESA 元件都加上 `dumpling:advisory-match=NOT_ASSESSED`，依據是「AMD-SB 規則表還沒做，資料庫沒有資料，以 AMD 公告為準」。報告照實寫「AMD 微碼已解析 N 份，沒有做公告比對」。PSP 目錄解析沒有執行時寫 GAP。

## 報告與 CI
- `fw-inventory.md` 每份都有「公告比對」一節。
- CI 摘要表的「微碼公告比對」欄：`pipeline/lib/firmware_advisory_cell.py`，多個映像時逐份列出。
- DT 報告的摘要標籤改成中性，並寫明 AMD 元件的狀態。

## 公開樣本結果（資料表 microcode-20261110）
| 樣本 | 結果 |
|---|---|
| Protectli VP46xx | 微碼 3 份都是 affected-candidate，各 14 個 SA；ME 14.0.47.1558，CPE `…:14.0.47`（inferred） |
| NUC11 | 000806C2 是 affected-candidate（24 個 SA）；000806C1 是 up-to-date；ME 讀不到，沒有 CPE |
| NovaCustom V540TU | 000A06A4 是 affected-candidate（10 個 SA）；ME 18.0.10.2285，CPE `…:18.0.10`（inferred） |
| ASUS B550M（AMD） | 沒有 Intel 微碼；AMD 元件 98 個都是 NOT_ASSESSED |

四個樣本的 `firmware-expect` 全部 OK：Protectli 11、NUC11 2、NovaCustom 2、B550M 3。

## 驗證（PR 前的預驗）
- 獨立驗證代理一共複驗了四輪，**做到 d8a20ec**：
  - 5bddbf8：不通過，4 項。
  - 03b33cd：不通過，3 項。
  - d8a20ec：不通過，2 處 AMD 文字。
  - d8a20ec 那一輪確認了核心比對：獨立 oracle 對真表 2417 個案例、隨機小表約 21 萬個案例都是 0 差異；四個樣本的結果逐行對過 releasenote.md 的行號；資料表可以重現；D-051 的邊界（10、11、30、31）正確。
- **7ebeacc 是作者自己看的 diff**，沒有再派驗證代理。這一輪修了那 2 處 AMD 文字，把 CI 欄邏輯抽成可測的模組，加上 family 矛盾時不推定、`.gitattributes`，並補了測試。
- 本機：C2 pytest 638 passed、`tests/test_firmware*.py` 177 OK、public-check 與 provenance-check OK。
- CI（7ebeacc）：tests 43451689061、firmware 43451693975 綠；firmware-expect B550M 3／3、Protectli 11／11、NUC11 2／2、NovaCustom V540TU 2／2 OK（OVMF 沒有 expected）。

## 已知限制
- 資料表只涵蓋 Intel 的 Linux 微碼套件，不含 BIOS 專用與 OEM 的 revision。表會變舊，重新產生是人工步驟（notes 有寫步驟）。release notes 缺 4 個 tag 的段落（notes 有列出）。
- 候選只到 release 層級，沒有讀 INTEL-SA 頁面的受影響處理器清單。
- TXE／SPS、AMD-SB、AMI-SA 的公告比對（D-043 (2) 規則表）還沒做。供應商 SBOM（kind: sbom）的公告比對一節，等 `wp3/supplier-normalize` 合併後再補。

author: oneisnotprime
body:
## What is here

**Counts in the data:** 288 verbs, 168 adverbs (all `manner`), 42 quantity nouns, plus about 60 adjectives that set or multiply `plural_count` or `pack_size`.

**Verbs and adverbs** (shared `verb.ts`, `castVerb`)
- `<adverb> <verb>` can now be spelled: QUICKLY RUN, FOREVER FLY, SLOWLY FLY.
- The adverb rule:
  - When an adverb sets or changes an effect property (the `effect` group plus `extends_duration`), it changes the verb itself. Examples: duration, cast_time, restores.
  - `effect_multiplier` is the strength the verb's own ops apply at, the same grading comparatives use (a multiplier becomes `f ** m`, an added amount becomes `a * m`). It also multiplies `restores`.
  - Any other property the adverb sets or changes is added to what the verb does to the body, for as long as the verb lasts.
- One adverb per verb, using the verb's `adjective_slots`.
- These are refused with clear messages: an adverb on its own, an adverb before a noun, an adjective before a verb, and two adverbs on one verb.
- A verb whose `effect_target` is `touched` and that has an event property (`destroys_target`, `transfers_ownership`, `moves_target`) now acts on the picked target through `happen`: DELETE, STEAL, BUY, CAPTURE, GRANT, GRAB, PULL, SUCK, SEND.
- A verb that would do nothing is refused before any letters are spent.
- `steal` now names the contested properties in its refusal, instead of always saying "stealth".

**Plurals and numbers** (shared `plural.ts`, `phrase.ts`)
- `pluralize` and `singulars` handle -s, -es, -ies and -ves, plus an irregular list.
- **CATS** gives `plural_count` cats (3 by default) and costs the extra S. A singular comes as its `pack_size`, so **WOLF is a pack of 4**.
- Number words set how many: adjectives such as TEN, and quantity nouns such as THOUSAND, MILLION and DOZEN used in front of a noun. Quantity nouns act exactly like adjectives and take the adjective slot.
- When a plural form is also a word in the data:
  - The plural rule wins if that entry has the same archetype as its singular: ROADS, LEGS and FALLS are several roads, legs and falls.
  - The entry's own data wins if its archetype differs: MEN and PEOPLE are groups.
- Plurals of events, fields and sky words are refused.
- **How counts are represented (this is not a cap):**
  - Up to 12 spawn as separate creatures or things.
  - More than 12 become one creature or thing with a `count`. Its integrity, mass, damage and letter output are multiplied by the count (shared `massed`, `Spelled.count`, `Player.count`, `Thing.count`).
  - Terrain is laid once, with its area multiplied by the count.
- The client labels show counts, e.g. `ANT ×1,000`.
- `stampTerrain` no longer loops over tiles outside the map, and `nearestWalkable` checks only the edge of each ring. Before this, spelling MILLION LAKES stalled the room.

## What is not done (added to TODO.md)
- `cast_time` is not a delay yet.
- REPEAT (`duplicates`) still does nothing.
- 37 verbs change only properties the engine does not read yet (CLIMB, DIG, VOTE, POLISH...).
- held, companion and mount verbs, and touched verbs without event properties, still land on the caster.
- SEND pulls its target to you instead of sending it away.
- An instant verb (HEAL) does not carry an adverb's body effects.
- WOLVES gives 3 wolves but WOLF gives 4 (a data issue).

## Testing
- `npm run typecheck` is clean.
- `npm test`: shared 96, server 32, client 1, all passing. The full suite ran twice.
- New tests:
  - shared: pluralizer; adverb rule; every verb cast with every adverb onto a body.
  - server `verbs.test.ts`: QUICKLY RUN (15 s instead of 30, speed 14.1 instead of 10), refusals, CATS, TEN WOLVES, THOUSAND ANTS (one swarm, ×1000 stats), MILLION ANTS and MILLION LAKES (slowest tick under 50 ms; MILLION LAKES answered in about 90 ms), and all 288 verbs cast (287 do something).
- Fixed a flake already on main in the NET test in `status.test.ts`: a miss could fail it, 2 runs in 15.
- Headless Playwright check: QUICKLY RUN, CATS, TEN WOLVES and THOUSAND ANTS show the expected labels and toasts, with no console errors.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body: ## Summary Adds the base for autonomous runs (`src/karry_agent/autonomy/`, `/api/autonomy/*`) and a phase-1 two-device setup (worker phone + monitor phone, no orchestrator yet). Everything is experimental-gated: `/api/autonomy`, `/monitor`, `/companion`, `/device-sw.js` are in `EXPERIMENTAL_PREFIXES`, so production returns 404 unless `KARRY_EXPERIMENTAL_FEATURES=1`. ``` plan_subtasks(instruction, budget_tokens=2000) -> one subtask per list item; oversized pieces are split by sentence, then by character -> "それをもとに/上記を使って…" depends on the previous item (backward-only, so acyclic) -> kind = video | image | research | general AutonomousRunner.execute(run_id) loop: refresh signals -> skip tasks whose deps failed -> ready = deps done gate.review() each task (allow / deny / hold) -> re-check signals under lock -> mark running + attempts++ -> SAVE -> run up to max_workers in parallel -> SAVE each result -> default_merge (or merger) builds one ordered final_output ``` - **Resume / loop guards:** state is saved before and after each subtask (`JsonRunStore`, atomic 0600 files under `KARRY_AUTONOMY_DIR`). A run found in `running` is a crashed worker, so `resumes++`. Limits: `max_attempts`, total executions, `max_resumes`, `deadline_seconds`. Runs are not auto-resumed on restart; `POST /runs/{id}/resume` is explicit. A `stop` sent to an idle run finishes it immediately. - **Existing features kept:** `general`/`research` call `AgentCore.run`; `image`/`video` go through the existing `_execute` task-chat path (requires `session_id`). - **Monitor hooks:** hash-chained JSONL `AuditLog` (optional HMAC, secrets masked), `KARRY_MONITOR_URL` events/review, `KARRY_MONITOR_POLICY_FILE`, `X-Monitor-Token`. Anything unreadable/unreachable puts the run on **hold** (fail closed). - **Paired devices (`autonomy/devices.py`, `static/monitor.html`, `static/companion.html`):** ``` POST /api/autonomy/devices/enroll {role: worker|monitor, name, password=KARRY_DEVICE_ENROLL_PASSWORD} -> HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie karry_device (Path=/api/autonomy); server keeps only sha256(token) in devices.json (0600) worker: POST /device/heartbeat (whitelisted status fields) PUT /device/frame (JPEG/PNG/WebP magic, ≤600KB, only while sharing) monitor: GET /overview (devices, runs, events) GET /devices/{id}/frame POST /devices/{id}/revoke + existing /runs/{id}/signal, /audit ``` Cookie-authenticated writes require `X-Karry-Device: 1` (CSRF). Enrollment failures are throttled via `user_login.throttled`. Neither device can create runs; there is no remote control of the worker. Screen preview uses browser `getDisplayMedia` (desktop browsers); mobile browsers show an "unsupported" notice — Android mirroring needs a native MediaProjection app (next phase). Both pages ship a web manifest + service worker so they can be added to the home screen. - Limitation: in-process locks assume a single worker process; Render's disk is ephemeral (see `docs/autonomy.md`). Tests: `tests/test_autonomy.py` (13) and `tests/test_autonomy_devices.py` (7: one-step enrollment/hash-only storage/restart, throttling and fail-closed, heartbeat/frame validation and role boundaries, CSRF header, revoke, page headers/manifests, experimental gate). Full suite: 1271 passed. body:
## What

go_web's download page (`/d/:token`) now renders the purchase props for four shapes it used to hand to Rails:

- **Reviews:** `purchase.review` is `ProductReviewPresenter#review_form_props` for `original_product_review`, which is the review on the true original purchase for a membership. A review with an editable video still goes to Rails, because its thumbnail URL is an Active Storage variant.
- **Custom fields:** `purchase_custom_fields` lists the post-purchase fields that have a custom field, mapped to their node type.
  - Boolean types are cast as `PurchaseCustomField#value` casts them, and other types read as strings.
  - File fields list each attachment's name without its extension, its size, and its upcased extension, using `ActiveStorage::Filename`'s sanitizing.
  - Checkout fields, which were most of these, render as `[]` as in Rails.
- **Calls:** `purchase.call` has the start time, the end time, and the call URL when it's present.
- **Memberships:**
  - `purchase.membership` mirrors the subscription's state methods (`alive?(include_pending_cancellation: false)`, `ended?`, `charges_completed?`, `cancelled_or_failed?`, `alive_or_restartable?`, `in_free_trial?`).
  - `receipt_purchase_id` and `has_invoice` follow `receipt_purchase`: the last successful charge that isn't refunded or charged back, unless it's a gift or was bought under another email.
  - A recurring charge's license is its original purchase's, as in `Purchase#license`.

These shapes still go to Rails, each with its own reason:

- a free charge outside a trial (`free_membership_purchase?` prices the next charge through `renews_free?`);
- a purchase whose subscription row is missing (Rails raises);
- a recurring charge of a licensed product without an original purchase (Rails raises);
- a custom field file whose name isn't valid UTF-8 or whose extension isn't ASCII.

Existence checks for the review, custom field and call rows stay in the page's one data query, so pages without them run no extra reads.

## Why

The download page isn't routed to go_web yet. These four fallbacks are common real shapes, and porting them keeps go_web's page identical to Rails' for those buyers before any traffic moves. Builds on #9151.

## Before/After

No UI change; the download page has no traffic on go_web.

- **Before:** a download page with a review, a custom field, a call or a subscription goes to Rails.
- **After:** go_web renders it with the same props as Rails.

## Test Results

- `go vet ./...` and `go test -race ./...` in `go_web/` pass, and the MySQL-backed downloads and delivery tests pass locally.
- **`TestTheReviewFormShowsThePurchasesReview`:** checks no review, then a review, then an anonymous one with a message. An editable video goes to Rails, and a rejected video doesn't.
- **`TestPostPurchaseCustomFieldsRenderTheirValuesAndFiles`:** checkout fields and fields without a custom field are left out. Covers a long answer with no value, a checkbox, and file fields, including a multi-dot name and a dotfile.
- **`TestACallShowsItsTimesAndLink`:** the times, and a blank URL rendered as `null`.
- **`TestAMembershipsPageDescribesItsSubscription`:**
  - the membership hash;
  - the receipt following the latest paid charge and skipping refunded, failed and other-email charges;
  - cancellation by the seller, a free trial, and a pending cancellation by the buyer;
  - a free charge going to Rails.
- **`TestACompletedInstallmentPlanCountsItsCharges`** and **`TestARecurringChargeShowsItsOriginalPurchasesLicense`** cover installment plans and recurring licenses.

author: rif
body:
Branch: docs/rfc8-read-only-journal-rows

---

RFC 8 §2.5 and §8.1 say what the engine does once its journal turns read-only: it refuses every sync, whatever the journal's `Sync` answered, and it retries a removal whose record was durable before the transition, answering `ErrDelay` with `DelayJournal` until the reopen. #3885 built both. No conformance row checked either one. Epic 7 also still left the read-only half of `journal_sync_failed` out of scope, saying the journal had no read-only state. It has had one since #3866 (T6.6).

**RFC 8 (#3926)**
- §15.2's read-only journal row now checks both behaviours, under both causes:
  - With a write staged and nothing unsynced, the group commit commits nothing, even though the journal's `Sync` answers nil.
  - A stable commit gets the same answer as a write.
  - A truncate whose record synced before the transition answers `ErrDelay` with `DelayJournal`. Its guard stays held, the store is not called, and reads return the truncated size. The truncate completes after the reopen.
- §11.2's journal-sync row names the refused sync and the retried removal next to the writes, citing §2.5 and §8.1.
- The §15 tables name no tests, so the rows don't either. The unit tests from #3885 are `TestTheGroupCommitCommitsNothingOverAReadOnlyJournal`, `TestAStableCommitOverAReadOnlyJournalAnswersItsCause` and `TestATruncateSyncedBeforeTheJournalTurnedReadOnlyIsRetried` (`pkg/block/engine/readonly_test.go` on `feat/storage-v2`). They cover all of the new row except the truncate completing after the reopen, because the reopen is not built (epic 6, open point 8).

**Epic 7 (#3898)**
- The read-only carve-out is gone from out of scope, R34, D10 and T7.3's rows. T7.3 now plans both halves of `journal_sync_failed`, and #3885 is listed as one of its dependencies.
- §9 point 1 records the state on `feat/storage-v2`. The drain in `loss.go` raises the condition for every failed-window event not found at open, and a read-only journal publishes its failed records as such events. So this half needs no code of its own. What it still lacks is its assertion: `TestRFC8B_JournalSyncFailed` (#3940) covers only the failed-window half, and the fixture has no way yet to turn the real journal read-only. Both remain T7.3's work under #3590. Estimates are unchanged.

Merges on develop first and is cherry-picked onto `feat/storage-v2` with the next batch.

Closes #3926
Closes #3898

body:
## Resultado
Correções da auditoria aplicadas na branch `fix/auditoria-monografia-seguranca-agenda`.
Base: `01193e795d6e8c92a496b0042263a9dad76d95b1`.
Revisão proposta: `7ab84de2aebc9450d5d260cde805e760df5cde6b`.
**Sem merge, deploy, alteração de variáveis ou migração do Neon de produção.**

## ATENÇÃO: migração antes da publicação
Esta PR altera o schema e rejeita tokens antigos sem versão. **Não integrar com auto-deploy ativo antes de planejar a migração.**
Fazer backup, ensaiar em homologação e executar com o código desta branch:

```bash
python -m app.backend.migrate --check
python -m app.backend.migrate --apply
```

A primeira operação só verifica; a segunda altera o schema. Requer a role proprietária e a extensão `btree_gist`. A migração é aditiva e transacional no PostgreSQL, preserva registros e recusa sobreposições/datas inválidas/e-mails duplicados sem corrigi-los automaticamente. Após publicar, é necessário novo login, não recriar os usuários.

Nunca apontar `TEST_POSTGRES_URL` para produção: a suíte recria tabelas em bancos descartáveis. Os detalhes estão em `docs/auditoria-codigo-20261113.md`.

## Correções implementadas
- Autenticação em todos os endpoints do assistente; escrita legada `/assistant/agendar` desativada com 410, sem reservar por nome de paciente.
- Gestor inicial sem senha padrão nem promoção silenciosa; redefinição explícita com revogação de tokens.
- Segredo obrigatório, HS256, validade limitada a 480 minutos, estado ativo e limitador persistente de tentativas de login.
- Interseção de intervalos protegida no serviço e no PostgreSQL por exclusion constraint; geração em lote atômica e idempotente para intervalos idênticos.
- Fallback automático PADRAO para falha de carga/predição, resultado inválido e timeout do classificador; uma tarefa pendente por processo, sem acumular threads.
- Remarcação pelo chat com seleção e confirmação; mantém a consulta original até a transferência atômica.
- CPF com dígitos verificadores, datas reais, edição autorizada de e-mail/telefone, ativação de usuários/profissionais e telas de contato/gestão no Django.
- Modo simplificado com duas vagas por página e uma instrução; modo padrão com até seis; escolha explícita de preferência de linguagem.
- Avaliação com F1 macro, matriz de confusão, versões, hash do corpus e previsões por linha.
- Documentação técnica atualizada e relatório antigo preservado como histórico.

## Validação concluída
### Backend — execução 43456086429
https://github.com/Vinicius-Oliveira-R/Desenvolvimento-de-uma-Assistente-Virtual/actions/runs/43456086429

**234 testes aprovados; zero falhas, erros ou testes ignorados.** Inclui PostgreSQL 16 descartável para concorrência de geração, bloqueio de reserva, constraint de interseção e migração de schema antigo sem perda de registros. Existem avisos de depreciação de dependências no log (766); não foram ocultados.

### Frontend — execução 43456086511
https://github.com/Vinicius-Oliveira-R/Desenvolvimento-de-uma-Assistente-Virtual/actions/runs/43456086511

As duas etapas (`frontend` e `postgres`) concluíram com sucesso: diagnósticos de configuração, verificações Django, testes de login/interfaces, sessões/migrações em PostgreSQL temporário e geração de estáticos. A suíte Django contém 65 testes; configuração/diagnóstico acrescenta 37 testes.

### Modelo
Corpus: 118 exemplos sintéticos (58 IDOSO / 60 PADRAO).

## Limites e providências externas
- Se a senha padrão histórica foi utilizada, redefini-la; remover o valor do script não altera a conta cadastrada nem apaga o histórico Git.

author: tskarhed
body:
## What

When a dashboard or snapshot fails to load while the page is captured by the image renderer, the page now sends the failure reason over the renderer's message channel, as `REPORT_RENDER_COMPLETE` with `success: false` and an `error` of `{ status, message }`.

Before, a missing dashboard never sent a message. With `reportRenderBinding` on, the renderer waited the full 30 second readiness timeout and the request failed with a 500.

`DashboardVersionError` is skipped, because it triggers a reload rather than ending the load.

## Compatibility

`sendRenderComplete(success)` is unchanged when no error is given. Outside a capture the binding doesn't exist, so the call does nothing.

An older renderer ignores the new fields. It treats the message as "ready" and returns an image of the error page after about 1.5 seconds, instead of timing out.

## Related changes

Three independent changes make up the full behavior, and they can merge in any order:

- grafana/grafana-image-renderer#1083: the renderer returns 424 with the reason.
- This PR: the dashboard page sends the failure reason.
- grafana/grafana#137839: Grafana recognizes the 424 instead of turning it into a 500.

## Testing

- New `sendRenderComplete.test.ts`, and two tests in `DashboardScenePageStateManager.test.ts` for a dashboard and a snapshot that fail to load. Removing the new call makes them fail.
- Run end to end on a Grafana 13.4 image built from this branch, with `reportRenderBinding` on and the renderer from grafana/grafana-image-renderer#1083: a missing dashboard failed after about 1.5 seconds instead of 30.

author: laurajoyhutchins
body:
## Git reconstruction loop

This PR adds four complementary Rust paths under the existing `excession reconstruct` CLI:

- **`git`**: replay exact source blob/mode identities, declared dependency closures, contract introduction, and actual two-parent Git integration against pinned commit objects.
- **`git-evidence`**: independently re-audit existing build-provenance and REA records in SQLite, bound to exact contract/checkpoint source closures. Missing bindings remain explicit.
- **`git-oracles`**: with mandatory `--trusted-local true`, replay independently supplied executable oracles against clean, exact Git checkouts. Verify program/script hashes, bounded outputs, expected stdout, and joint integration behavior. Persist scoped observations in the existing evidence store. **Not sandboxed.**
- **`git-synthesize`**: generate real candidate Git histories from a pinned target and declared dependencies/contracts in an *isolated output repository*. For two independent contracts, construct parallel commits and a genuine two-parent merge. Validate generated plans with the existing structural verifier, select capability-introduction and joint-oracle obligations, and preserve counterexample hints.

The synthesis interface is documented in `docs/GIT_RECONSTRUCTION_SYNTHESIS.md` with versioned seed and counterexample JSON schemas; `docs/GIT_RECONSTRUCTION.md` and `docs/GIT_RECONSTRUCTION_ORACLES.md` cover the replay layers.

### Evidence boundary

Exact tree equality is structural, not proof of program behavior. Build/REA receipts do not attest execution. A finite passing oracle is a bounded observation, not universal equivalence. Generated synthetic commits are *not* recovered upstream chronology. The dependency/contract graph is caller-declared and may be incomplete. Counterexamples passed to synthesis are caller-supplied hints, **not authenticated failures**; source-identical histories cannot repair a failure against the unchanged final tree.

No source checkout is rewritten. `git-synthesize` writes only to a new directory outside the source repository; `git-oracles` requires explicit trusted-local consent and external isolation for untrusted code.

### Verification

- Baseline four-layer implementation passed exact-head GitHub workflows before synthesis was added.
- Pinned Rust 1.99.1 toolchain restored locally; new synthesis Rust module compiles and passes strict Clippy in a standalone type-checking harness; formatting checks pass.
- New integration tests exercise real rootless Git commits, a true two-parent merge, exact tree equality, counterexample retention, dependency cycles, and unsafe output refusal.
- The latest full GitHub CI on the synthesis branch is being checked; **do not merge until exact-head Verify and all required workflows pass**.

author: vudigapranav
body:
Resolves #1639.

`serveStatic` now evaluates `If-Match` and `If-Unmodified-Since` before the existing `If-None-Match` / `If-Modified-Since` check, as RFC 9110 §13.2.2 orders them, and responds `412 Precondition Failed` when they fail:

- `If-Match` uses strong comparison: `*` passes, a weak ETag never matches, and a missing ETag fails.
- `If-Unmodified-Since` is only evaluated when `If-Match` is absent; an invalid date is ignored.

The check lives next to `isCacheMatch` in `src/utils/internal/cache.ts` as `isPreconditionFailed()`. Tests in `test/static.test.ts` (node and web) cover each case; they fail on main and pass with the change. `pnpm lint` and `pnpm typecheck` pass. In the full `pnpm vitest run`, only `test/bench/bundle.test.ts` (defineHandler bundle 7045 > 7040) fails, and it fails the same way on main locally.

Not included: the `cache-control: no-store` header nitro adds on its 412, since h3 error responses don't carry headers set on `event.res`.

author: stekperepolnen
body:
### Changelog entry

Add `data_migration: "full"` to the Walle API to move VDisks off a host before allowing maintenance.

### Description for reviewers

`POST /cms/api/walle/v11/tasks` accepts the optional string field `data_migration: "full"` and passes it as `EvictVDisks: true` in the existing CMS permission request. Other values return HTTP 400. Omitting the field keeps the existing Walle behavior.

Eviction uses the same CMS checks and configuration as `/cms/api/permissionrequest`, including validation of the action and the single-host restriction. Walle rejects the option for `prepare` and `deactivate`, which do not send a CMS permission request.

The task returns `in-process` while permission is pending and `ok` when CMS allows maintenance. `GET /cms/api/walle/v11/tasks/{id}` checks the saved CMS request. Task lookup, listing, and deletion also handle eviction requests retained after approval.

The shared CMS recheck handler also preserves pending eviction actions after a failed check. For example, disabling eviction while a task is pending used to clear its actions without granting permission. Walle could then report inconsistent status and fail to delete the task. Preserving the request allows retry and cancellation through either API.

Tests follow the existing `VDisksEviction` and `DisabledEvictVDisks` scenarios. They also cover HTTP validation, dry run, task lookup/listing/deletion, and retry or cancellation after an error.

Validation: `git diff --check` passed. The targeted CMS eviction and Walle tests could not run on macOS: the build fails while linking bison because `ld64.lld` rejects `--allow-multiple-definition`.

session: GitHub Support

## Summary

Three regex graders in the eval case `plugins/session-flow/evals/recall-reports-tried-kept-reverted/` fail correct answers on wording. The eval passes on #15920 hit this on both sides of a compare (before and after), so it is a property of main and was found before any change was under test.

This changes graders of an existing case, and that is not moving a goalpost:

- The failed answers are correct. Each one says the token bucket was tried and reverted for dropping requests during bursts, says the sliding window is kept, cites SHAs, and says the PR and tracker skills were unavailable. They are quoted below.
- The fix lands on main, so both sides of any later compare use the same graders.
- Every existing failing sample of the three graders is still rejected, along with the wrong answers two independent reviews found. Calibration figures are under Verification.

The real answers that failed:

- Sonnet before, run 3, failed `tried-kept-reverted`, `unavailable-prs-named` and `unavailable-tracker-named`:
  > **Other sources:** I searched git. The `/source-control:pull-request` and `/work-items:track` skills aren't available here, so I searched neither closed PRs nor the tracker.
  >
  > **Answer:** Yes. The in-memory limiter was already replaced once, with a token bucket, and that was reverted because it dropped legitimate requests during bursts. A sliding-window limiter then replaced the in-memory one and is current.
- Sonnet after, run 2, failed `unavailable-prs-named` and `unavailable-tracker-named`:
  > - **Pull requests and tracker:** `/source-control:pull-request` and `/work-items:track` aren't available here, so closed PRs and tracker items weren't searched.

## Fix

Only `case.yaml` and `samples/` under this one case directory change, plus a changelog fragment. No skill text, prompt or other case changes.

- **`unavailable-prs-named`, `unavailable-tracker-named`:** both are now model-graded (`type: llm`, `focus: last_message`), with the same names and `arm: with-only`.
  - Each passes only if the reply says its source (closed pull requests through gh or the pull-request skill; the work-item tracker) could not be searched or was not searched, and reports no result from that source.
  - A statement about the other source, about code not yet in a branch, or about a narrower check left undone while results are reported is a FAIL.
  - Why not regex: two regex rounds each closed the tested strings and let the next phrasing through, because a pattern cannot tell which noun a negation belongs to, or see that another clause reports a search that returned results.
- **`tried-kept-reverted`** is split in two:
  - `cites-commit-and-burst` (regex, `arm: both`): a 7 to 40 character hex commit id holding a digit is present, and "burst" is mentioned. A pattern decides both without knowing which approach a statement is about. `names-both-attempts` already checks that both approaches are named.
  - `token-bucket-reverted-sliding-window-kept` (`type: llm`, `focus: last_message`, `arm: both`): passes only if the reply says the token bucket was reverted because of bursts and the sliding window is the one kept, and nothing in it (a closing summary included) says the token bucket is current, kept, in use, or re-applied after its revert.
  - Why: the relaxed regex at the previous commit passed "The token bucket was reverted in a1b2c3d because it dropped requests during bursts, but it later replaced the sliding window; it is current.", which main fails. A regex cannot tell which noun "current" or "reverted" belongs to; this wrong answer is now a must-fail sample of the judge, which failed it in every run.
- The case keeps its regex and tool graders (`git-searched`, `names-both-attempts`, `cites-commit-and-burst`), so it is not judge-only.

Samples:

- `cites-commit-and-burst`: 5 must-pass and 5 must-fail, checked offline by the validator.
- `token-bucket-reverted-sliding-window-kept`: 8 must-pass and 25 must-fail calibration samples. Every earlier `tried-kept-reverted` sample carries over to the grader that owns its judgment. New must-pass: three correct phrasings the regex rejected (the token bucket and "is current" in one sentence, where "is current" belongs to the sliding window). New must-fail: the wrong answer above, the token bucket restored, re-adopted or remaining in use after the revert, the two approaches reversed, both named with no outcome, a revert reason other than bursts, an answer to a different question, and an empty answer.
- `unavailable-prs-named`: 14 must-pass and 35 must-fail calibration samples.
- `unavailable-tracker-named`: 12 must-pass and 17 must-fail calibration samples.
- Both criteria count a read that was attempted and failed as could not be searched, and a search that returned a count, zero included, as a search that ran.
- Every earlier sample of the two graders carries over. The new ones are the real answers above, the wrong answers both reviews found, and correct phrasings the regex rejected.

A `bump: none` changelog fragment is included, because `scripts/check-changelog-fragments.sh --check-required origin/main` requires one for any change under `plugins/session-flow/`.

**Added cost per eval run:** two opus judge calls per with-arm run of this case for the `with-only` graders, plus one per run in either arm for `token-bucket-reverted-sliding-window-kept` (`arm: both`). In calibration that was about 0.02 USD per run at list price, including the reproduction call.

The samples added since are replies that ran the read and reported it failed (must-pass), seven cross-source wrong answers, a zero-count search, an empty answer per grader and an answer to a different question.

author: new-usemame
body:
Refs #2921.

**Problem.** On a library kept on an NFSv4 share, changing a book's author to an author with no folder yet failed with `[Errno 524]` on every file and on the folder, and the edit reported "Rename title ... failed".

**Cause.** `move_files_on_change` called `shutil.move(book_folder, new_author/new_title)`. The new author folder did not exist, so `os.rename` failed with ENOENT and `shutil.move` copied the whole book with `copytree`/`copy2` instead of renaming it. That copy ran `copystat`, which writes back every extended attribute. NFSv4 exposes `system.nfs4_acl` for reading but refuses writing it (errno 524), so each file and the folder failed after their data had already been copied. The helper's own `copytree` fallback failed the same way.

**Fix.**
- `cps/services/file_move.py` gains `move_path`. It creates the destination's parent first, so a move inside one filesystem is a plain rename (no copy, nothing to fail on). Only when the rename is refused (another filesystem) does it copy, and a folder copy that fails part way is removed so the old folder stays the only copy.
- The copy keeps times, permissions and each extended attribute the destination accepts, one at a time, and skips the ones it refuses (`copy_metadata_best_effort`). `copy_with_metadata_fallback` now uses it too, so its data-only fallback also keeps times and mode.
- `move_files_on_change` uses `move_path` for the folder move.

**Tests** (`tests/unit/test_move_book_dir_refused_metadata_2921.py`, committed before the fix):
- a move to a new author completes when metadata copying is refused (red on main with the reporter's exact log lines, helper:1711/1717/1763);
- a move to a new author on one filesystem is a rename (same inode; red on main, which copied);
- a move that must copy (rename refused with EXDEV) keeps data and mtime, keeps an accepted `user.*` xattr and skips `system.nfs4_acl` raising 524 (Linux only, where shutil copies xattrs through `os.*xattr`; red on main in the Linux image).

**Checked by hand** in the `:dev` image with real syscalls: a move to a new author on one filesystem kept the inode (main: new inode, a copy), and a real cross-device move from a tmpfs to the overlay kept the bytes, the mtime and a real `user.origin` xattr and removed the source.

I could not reproduce an NFSv4 server here, so the 524 itself is simulated in the tests from the reporter's measurements.

**Review.** An independent fresh-context review passed it and exercised the data-safety paths (copy failing part way, existing destination, case-only rename). From its low findings: a folder destination is now refused, a parent folder created by a failed move is removed, and a test covers the rollback (it fails when either cleanup is removed). Symlinks inside a book folder are copied as links, the same as `shutil.move` did.

author: esteira-iplan[bot]
body:
DEV-579 · issue no It's a Plan: DEV-579 (projeto DEV, raia MCP Server). Relacionado ao CHATR-167 (item B17).

## O que mudou

`handle_errors` (`src/tools/multi_step_service/core/base_workflow.py`) é o decorator de todo nó de todo workflow do `multi_step_service`. O `logger.error` dele imprimia `traceback.format_exc()`, cuja última linha é `str(exceção)`. Exceção de domínio embute o valor que a provocou (`InvalidInscricaoError` leva a inscrição imobiliária na mensagem), e inscrição, guia e CDA não têm formato nem rótulo que a barreira de `src/utils/log.py` redija: o valor saía em claro.

Agora o log leva `_traceback_sem_mensagem(e)`: os frames (arquivo, linha, função, linha de código-fonte) e o tipo qualificado de cada exceção da cadeia (`__cause__` e `__context__`, respeitando `from None`), sem `str(exceção)`. Serviço, nó e `user_id` (redigido pela barreira) continuam na linha.

A resposta ao agente **não muda**: `status = "error"`, `error_message = str(e)` e a `AgentResponse` já preparada pelo nó é preservada. `error_message` é o contrato do tool com o LLM, usado igual por todos os workflows, e não é log.

## Critérios e provas

- Valor embutido na exceção não vai para o log, em todo workflow (o ponto é único): `test_inscricao_da_excecao_nao_vai_para_o_log` usa a `InvalidInscricaoError` real com inscrição sintética, pelo decorator real, com a barreira de log instalada, e confere o stderr do sink de produção e um sink de teste.
- Exceções encadeadas (`raise ... from`, contexto implícito) também não vazam a mensagem; `from None` omite o contexto: três testes.
- O log continua diagnosticável: serviço, nó, tipo de cada exceção e o frame do nó (`in informar_inscricao`) presentes.
- Resposta ao agente inalterada: `test_resposta_ao_agente_nao_muda`.
- Teste falha antes: com o `base_workflow.py` da `main`, os 4 testes de comportamento falham com o valor sintético no log; com a mudança, 7/7 passam.

## Verificações

- `uvx ruff@0.15.5 check .` e `uvx ruff@0.15.5 format --check .`: ok
- `uv run pytest --cov=src --cov-report=xml` (ambiente do `ci.env`, sem Redis local): 2143 passed, 23 skipped

Sem migration, sem contrato novo. Rollback: revert do merge.

author: gecube
body:
## What

The ECR provider now warns at start about a lifecycle policy below the instance prefix that can expire or archive what Lajstrom needs.

- **When and which repositories:** a bounded sample at start. EnsureRepository's repositories are not used. The provider's first successful `Capabilities` starts one check, once per provider, in the background, bounded to a minute; in `serve` that first call is the registry probe at start. It delays no caller.
  - `DescribeRepositories` lists the repositories below the prefix, as `ListRepositories` does.
  - `GetLifecyclePolicy` reads at most 20 of them, spread evenly over their names in order.
  - Why not EnsureRepository: a repository Lajstrom creates with `CreateRepository` gets no lifecycle policy. The ones worth reading are those that exist already, and the publish path gains no call.
- **Parsing:** the policy JSON (`rules[].rulePriority`, `description`, `selection.tagStatus`, `tagPatternList`, `tagPrefixList`, `countType`, `countNumber`, `countUnit`, `action.type`). Repositories with the same policy text share one line per rule.
- **Warning** (`WARN`) for a rule with `tagStatus` `tagged` or `any` (or a status the check does not know), with the action `expire` or `transition`:
  - The line names the rule and the sampled repositories that have it.
  - A version's tag can be any string, so every tagged rule can take versions.
  - `reservedTags` says which of Lajstrom's own forms the lists select: keep-tags `_keep.sha256.*`, the npm journal `_j*`, hashed tags `_h*`, `sha256-*`.
  - A policy that does not parse is a warning too.
- **Untagged-only rule: info, not a warning.** This departs from the brief. ECR keeps an image a manifest list references while the list exists, and expires a referrer only within 24 h of its subject's deletion or archival ([evaluation rules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/LifecyclePolicies.html#lp_evaluation_rules)). operations.md already calls untagged-only rules the safe configuration. A warning there at every start would flag the configuration we recommend. Making it a warning is a one-line change if the maintainer prefers.
- **Soft failure, once:**
  - `AccessDeniedException` on `GetLifecyclePolicy` ends the check with one line at info: `ECR lifecycle policies not checked: the credentials may not call ecr:GetLifecyclePolicy …`, `action=ecr:GetLifecyclePolicy`.
  - `LifecyclePolicyNotFoundException` means no policy, and a repository deleted meanwhile is skipped.
  - `catalog: false`, a failed listing or another error each give one line and end the check.
- **Docs:** `docs/registries/ecr.md` gets `ecr:GetLifecyclePolicy` as an optional statement of the IAM policy (not part of the policy #19 measured) and a section "Lifecycle policies". The package doc mentions the check.

Size: 570 lines added, but 235 are `lifecycle_test.go` and 50 are docs. The code is one unit (`lifecycle.go` plus a few lines in `provider.go`), so there is no natural cut.

Not done: the lifecycle policy of a repository creation template, which ECR applies to the repositories it creates on push (`createOnPush: true`). Reading it needs `ecr:DescribeRepositoryCreationTemplates`; it would make a small follow-up. Such repositories are read once they exist, if they fall in the sample.

## How tested

- `TestLifecycleRuleCatches`: untagged, any, an unknown status, `*`, prefixes, keep-tag, `sha256-` and journal patterns, and that `.` in a pattern is literal.
- `TestCheckLifecycle`: five repositories below the prefix and one beside it. Checks:
  - one warning for the policy two repositories share, naming both, with priority, description, count and action;
  - an untagged rule at info, and the archive (`transition`) rule of the same policy at warning;
  - a policy that does not parse;
  - the summary line;
  - no call for the repository outside the prefix.
- `TestCheckLifecycleSkipped`:
  - `AccessDeniedException`: one info line naming `ecr:GetLifecyclePolicy`, after exactly one call;
  - throttling;
  - `catalog: false`;
  - the listing denied;
  - no repository, which logs nothing above debug.
- `TestCheckLifecycleSample`: 100 repositories over four pages give 20 `GetLifecyclePolicy` calls, spread evenly.
- `TestCapabilitiesChecksLifecycleOnce`: three `Capabilities` calls against a fake `/v2` run one check.
- `TestDataPath` (through the AWS SDK against a fake HTTP endpoint): the check's `DescribeRepositories` and `GetLifecyclePolicy` go over the wire, and the warning names the rule decoded from `lifecyclePolicyText`. The test now waits for the check, so its call list stays deterministic.
- Mutations checked: treating `untagged` as harmful, or `LifecyclePolicyNotFoundException` as an error, fails the tests.
- `make check` green.
- Not run against ECR or moto: no live account, and no containers. `go vet -tags integration` of the ECR package and the facade passes. In `TestIntegrationMoto` and `TestIntegrationECRLive` the check now runs in the background, and it only logs. With the IAM policy #19 measured, the live test's check stops at the refusal, with the info line.

Closes #665

author: chrisgleissner
body:
## Summary

Four recurring CI flakes. Each fix is a separate commit. Only flake 3 could be demonstrated as a failing-to-passing change locally; flakes 1, 2 and 4 could not be reproduced on this host (see each section).

Open items: the CI rates of flakes 1, 2 and 4 are unknown until the next CI runs. `coordinator/src/db.rs` changes by 5 lines (flake 2); the branch `fix/coordinator-writer-stall` also edits that file.

## Flake 1: `ui-features.spec.ts` "mission activity humanizes events" (Firefox desktop)

Cause (not reproduced as a failure): the "Terminal opened" and "Terminal closed" rows are live-only. The mission page publishes them when its session pane has loaded (a lazy chunk), opened the terminal WebSocket and received the status and close frames. The test did not wait for that chain and relied on the default 10 s expect timeout. Measured at 1 CPU with 6 workers in the Playwright image, the wait after the Activity panel appeared was up to 5.1 s (40 runs). A slower runner can exceed 10 s.

Rate: 0 of 30 (1 CPU, 4 workers) and 0 of 40 (1 CPU, 6 workers) before the change. 0 of 48 after, over four browser projects.

Change: the test waits for `#terminal-status` to reach `data-state="ended"` (60 s timeout) before it asserts the rows. That state is reached after both events were published.

## Flake 2: `coordinator/tests/db_lock_burst.rs`

Cause: the test asserted that no call held the database connection for 500 ms. A Windows runner measured 553 ms under load. Hold time depends on the host. Locally the longest hold was 18 ms idle and 263 ms with four busy loops (40 runs), so the failure did not reproduce.

Change: `Db::lock_stats` gains an `acquisitions` counter, incremented in `Db::c()` (5 lines in `db.rs`). The test asserts at least one and at most three acquisitions per request, and that fewer than `n` callers waited at once. The longest hold is printed only. A call that retried or took the connection twice raises the count above the bound.

## Flake 3: slow database call fails the Python certificate test

Cause: the coordinator prints `slow database call <name>: N ms` on stderr when a call takes 500 ms or longer. The test fixtures took the first stderr line as the listening line. On a loaded Windows runner `cursor_key` took 624 ms during start-up, so the warning came first and the fixture assertion failed.

Change: `read_listening_line` reads stderr until a line contains the URL; `tests/distributed_harness.py` `restart` uses it too. The warning is still printed.

Rate: a wrapper binary that prints the warning before `serve` fails the test 1 of 1 before the change and 0 of 1 after.

## Flake 4: screenshot baselines depend on load timing

Cause: the screenshot specs waited only for fonts. A capture could land before the status reads finished, which changed the Inbox badge (`13+` or `15`) and the row counts.

Change: `api.ts` sets `data-requests` on the root element to the number of requests in flight. The Inbox badge carries `data-partial`. `settle()` in `web/e2e/redesign/harness.ts` waits for no request in flight, no `data-partial="true"` and no `aria-busy="true"` (outside buttons), checked twice around two animation frames. `screenshots.spec.ts`, `site-shots.spec.ts` and `redesign/evidence.ts` call it before capturing.

Verification: `screenshots.spec.ts` on `chromium-mobile` in the Playwright v1.64.1 image at 3 CPUs: 144 of 144 pass with the existing baselines. No baseline was regenerated.

## Checks

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --test db_lock_burst --test hardening`, `mypy`, `web npm run typecheck`, `tests/test_distributed_integration.py` and `tests/test_distributed_crash.py`, `trail check`.

author: alvinwquach
body:
## Done / Next step

- Done (part 1 of 2): the hosted-database half of the AG-10 red-team suite, `apps/hosted/db/__tests__/red-team.test.ts`: 11 cases pass (each fails closed) and 1 `it.todo`, plus the docs page `docs/hosted/agent-red-team.md` (linked from docs/nav.ts) and an internal changeset. Test-only: no migration, guard, allowlist, lint or dependency rule, test baseline, role or table is touched.
- Next step: part 2 (branch `test/ag-10-red-team-mcp-writer`, stacked on this one because it extends the same docs page): page-text injection through the MCP tools, malformed hosted answers, MCP oversized input, MCP cost cap and kill switch, the writer's replayed and edited approvals, and the receipt chain's replay and edit.
- No case failed open: no finding to report.
- Auto-merge NOT enabled (the orchestrator decides after the case list).

## What a user can now do

Run one named test per attack against the hosted agent path and see that each is refused with nothing written, and read on one page which control stops which attack.

## Docs first

- [x] Docs page: docs/hosted/agent-red-team.md (table of cases, threat and control; how to run, with the real output)
- [x] The tests are the output shown on that page

## Promises

- [x] Requests to a checked site are still GET or HEAD only (no request is made; tests use a local database)
- [x] No key or webhook address appears in any output (agent tokens are built at run time and are invented)
- [x] Exit codes unchanged

## Changeset

- [x] `.changeset/test-ag-10-red-team-suite.md`: `none` (internal)

## Changelog

(1h) A red-team test suite for the hosted agent path: eleven attacks (double approve, replay, edited draft, cross-tenant token and more) must each be refused with nothing written.

Section: Reliability
Time-Spent: 1h

## Cases, the ADR-0014 threat, and the existing control that stops each

Real Postgres 16; skipped without `GAUGELINE_TEST_DATABASE_URL`, required in the CI `hosted-db` job. No case reads the clock (limits are counted by the database).

| Case (test name starts with) | Threat | Existing control that stops it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| passing fixture: a registered agent drafts for its own site | all | (shows the agent works, so the refusals below are not vacuous) |
| double-click approve (5 concurrent approvals) | T4 | unique index `decisions_one_choice_per_draft` (0005); `decide()` reports the winner; one apply job |
| replayed approval (approve again, decline after, raw insert) | T3 | the same index; decisions append-only (`refuse_change`, 0002) |
| approval of an edited draft (UPDATE after approval, edit after approval) | T5 | drafts append-only (0002); the database hashes the payload at the decision (0005); `verifyApplyJob` refuses another text |
| cross-tenant token (draft into B's site, B's finding, read B's draft, B's site pending, B's runs) | T6 | organisation taken from the token's registry row in `agent_insert_draft` / `agent_list_pending` / `agent_list_runs` (0012, 0014) |
| revoked agent, and an unknown token | T10 | only an active registry row is recognised; `revoked` wins; deny row logged (0012, 0013) |
| cost-cap breach (over the day's ceiling, negative, over 10^12) | T7 | `private.agent_authorize` cost check before the call; refused call not counted (0013) |
| runaway loop (third call in a 2-call window) | T7 | per-agent rate limit (0013) |
| oversized input (51 findings, payload over 16 KiB, 201-character token) | T7, T9 | `agent_insert_draft` 50-finding cap, payload size check (0005), token length bound (0012) |
| malformed tool output (unknown key, wrong type, bidi control, line break, bare string, null) | T9 | per-kind shape check in the database (0005) |
| kill switch (database global switch; `GAUGELINE_AGENTS_OFF` = `1`, empty, `true`, garbage) | T7, T12 | `private.agent_switches` (0013); `agentsOff` read at every call in `createAgentDrafts` before the database is called (#395) |

## Pending (`it.todo`), listed here instead of weakening anything

- **expired token** (T10): the registry has no expiry on an agent token (`public.agents` has no `expires_at`; AG-02 chose revoke, `disabled` and the 30-day idle flag). The control the ADR's list implies does not exist, so this is a todo and a decision for the owner, not a pass. The nearest existing expiries (the 72-hour approval and the draft's 72-hour pending window) are covered in part 2 and by existing tests.

## Findings

None. Every case failed closed on the first run, and each has a passing counterpart (the active agent in the first case, the kill switch removed, the rate limit's first two calls), so a refusal is not a broken fixture.

## Tests

- 11 passed, 1 todo, on Node 22 and Node 24, against Postgres 16.15 locally. `scripts/__tests__/check-docs.test.ts` passes; `pnpm docs:check`, `pnpm docs:build`, `prettier --check .`, `adr:check`, hosted `tsc` and eslint on the new file are clean. (Full `pnpm lint` ran out of memory on this loaded machine; CI is the authority.)
- The suite does not depend on AG-05 traces or AG-06 receipts.

## Sources

- ADR-0014 (docs/adr/0014-agent-safety-model.md), section 1, T2 to T12 "Planned: AG-10 case ...": the case list and the threat each covers. [repository]
- Migrations 0002, 0005, 0012, 0013, 0014 and `apps/hosted/agents/draft.ts`: the controls named above (the comment at the top of each file states the rule; the existing tests `inbox.test.ts`, `agent-policy.test.ts`, `agent-reads.test.ts`, `agent-registry.test.ts` pin them). [repository]
- Batch AG row AG-10: "Each must fail closed." [repository]
- No library call was added; the suite uses `postgres` and vitest as the neighbouring tests do. Nothing external was read: uncited for any framework behaviour.

## Architecture notes

- Chosen: one test file per package, named `red-team.test.ts`, with one `it` per attack, over a single cross-package file. The hosted app does not depend on the writer and the MCP package does not depend on the hosted app, so a single file would need cross-package relative imports. Cost: the suite is found by name (`pnpm exec vitest run red-team`), and the docs page is the index.
- Chosen: assert the absence of a write by counting rows (`drafts`, `decisions`, the job queue's `Map`) before and after, over only checking the error text. A refusal that also wrote a row would otherwise pass. Cost: a case needs a committed call, so cases share one database and count differences, not totals.
- Chosen: register agents with a direct insert as the migration owner (as `inbox.test.ts` does), over the person-login `register_agent` path, to keep the file small; the registration door has its own tests.
- Data structures: a `Record` of named agent tokens (looked up by name, not array position); cost in integers (micro-units), as the policy does.
- Cost: one more Postgres-backed test file (about 3 seconds) in the `hosted-db` job.

author: heinvv10
body:
Brief "Fixes to existing tools" (isaflow-mcp-tools-20261113): three MCP tool fixes, plus literal `general_ledger` search.

1. **`list_bank_transactions` `description_contains` was ignored.** `getBankTransactions` has an account-only branch (a `bank_account_id` with no status). That branch never applied the search in its rows query or its count query. It now does, in both.
2. **`general_ledger` returned `universeTotal` 0 when the filters matched nothing.** The unfiltered window count was read off the first returned row. When no row came back, it reported 0 for a window that held lines.
   - It is now read separately (`gl/generalLedgerUniverse.ts`), using exactly the universe CTE's predicate.
   - This was not a date or timezone boundary.
3. **`bulk_allocate_bank_transactions`: one R0.00 line rolled back the whole batch.**
   - Zero-amount lines are now skipped as `zero_amount` and reported in `skipped`; the rest of the batch allocates.
   - The dry run reports the same skip, and idempotency is unchanged.
   - Two existing suites had used a zero line as their rollback fault. They now use a supplier refund with no credit to cover it.
4. **`general_ledger` `search` is a literal substring.**
   - `%`, `_` and `\` are escaped, with an `ESCAPE` clause.
   - A new shared helper, `src/lib/sqlLikeLiteral.ts`, now also serves `list_bank_transactions`.
   - The GL stream's row shaping moved to `generalLedgerStreamRows.ts`, bringing the service from 300 to 263 lines.

**Tests**
- Integration, on throwaway clusters:
  - `mcp-list-bank-tx-description-contains` 6/6
  - `mcp-general-ledger-universe` 8/8
  - `mcp-general-ledger-search-literal` 5/5

body:
## What does this change?

Adds the full WAX Hub 2.1.0 project: source, build scripts and docs for the Android app and the new Linux desktop app.

- **Rescue & recover**: scans 34 places across 27 WAX contracts for value still held for an account: leftover deposits, unclaimed packs and auction results, farm and vault stakes, open orders, claim links, unlocked token locks, unstake refunds and voting rewards. Each item gets a one-tap action that returns it. Coverage and how each lookup was checked are in `CONTRACTS.md`.
- **Contract console**: call any action on any WAX contract with forms generated from its ABI, or browse any table. Includes ready-made tasks, per-field help, and a typed confirmation for account-takeover actions.
- **Guided Creator studio**: collection → schema → template → mint → sell, with explainers, presets, previews, airdrop minting and a NeftyBlocks drop builder.
- **Drops tab**: shows live, claimed drops instead of old test drops. Collection search works on partial names. Load more paging is fixed.
- **Linux desktop app** (`desktop/`): Electron, packaged as an AppImage and a .deb. Sandboxed, with no Node.js access for web content and a loopback-only file server; wallet sign-in pop-ups are allowed but every other link opens in the system browser.
- **Android release hardening**: version 2.1 (versionCode 3), WebView remote debugging and mixed content disabled.
- **Other fixes**: plain-English errors, account menu (no accidental sign-out), Android back button, NeftyBlocks and AtomicHub pack claims, older Alcor orders now listed, wide-screen layout.
- **Repo setup**: README, SECURITY, CHANGELOG, CONTRACTS, `docs/BUILDING.md`, third-party notices, `.gitignore` (blocks keystores and password files), CODEOWNERS (`@SquishEyez`), and PR and issue templates.

Release binaries (APK, AppImage, .deb, `SHA256SUMS.txt`) aren't committed. They go on the v2.1.0 GitHub Release.

## Why?

To publish WAX Hub as a free, open-source app, and to give people a way to recover assets stuck in contracts whose websites have shut down.

## How was it tested?
- [x] Android: the APK built from this exact source was signed with the release key. Signature verified (v1, v2, v3). The manifest was confirmed as 2.1 / versionCode 3 with an independent parser.
- [x] Linux desktop: the app was run under a virtual display against live mainnet data. Checked that the page has no Node.js access, outside links are blocked from opening in the app, and requests for files outside the app return 404. The .deb was installed with `apt` and launched from its installed location.
- [x] Browser (`android/dist/web`): the Wallet, Drops, Rescue, Creator and Console screens were exercised against live WAX mainnet data, with no page errors.
- [x] `./build.sh` was run from a clean copy of this repo and built everything successfully.
- [ ] **Not yet tested:** signing a real transaction with WAX Cloud Wallet or Anchor. Please do a small test (e.g. send 0.1 WAX) on Android and Linux before publishing the release.

## Checklist
- [x] No private keys, keystores, passwords or API tokens are included (scanned before pushing)
- [x] Transactions still show a confirmation summary before signing

author: marlon-costa-dc
body: ## Summary Adds the process deadline the flext-infra ADR-032 admission needs. Reviewer conditions (orchestrator): it is the smallest possible addition, reuses the existing supervisor and its broadcast with no second stop path, and uses the native one-shot kernel timer with no thread. - `u.Cli.process_deadline_scope(deadline: p.Cli.ProcessDeadline | None)` arms `signal.setitimer(ITIMER_REAL, …)` on the main thread `termination_grace_seconds` before the deadline. The SIGALRM handler calls the installed SIGTERM forwarding of the supervisor, so every owned lifecycle stops its process group (signal-wave workers included). It then raises `SystemExit(c.Cli.PROCESS_TIMEOUT_EXIT_CODE)`, so the interrupted lifecycles reap their children through the existing `except BaseException` → `_finalize_lifecycle` path. - `TimeoutError` was rejected: it subclasses `OSError`, and the supervisor converts `OSError` into a failed result instead of an interruption. The first runtime proof caught this. - `u.Cli.process_deadline_expire()` ends the active scope now through the same handler, from any thread. With `deadline=None` nothing is armed. ## Evidence - Runtime (fixture `tests/fixtures/process_deadline_holder.py`, real child under `u.Cli.run`): `deadline 6` → rc=124, child gone. `expire 600` → rc=124, child gone. `expire 0` (no deadline) → rc=124, child gone. - `make gen` / `make fmt` / `make fix` in the lane are no-ops after generation. `CHECK_PHASE=primary make check` reports lint 0 and pyrefly 0. The commit hooks passed. Consumer PR: the flext-infra fix-forward of #2370 (removes the Timers and the `os.kill` calls on its own pid) follows once this lands. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Adds a process deadline scope to the runtime utilities that stops the owned process tree at a deadline, reusing the existing supervisor so no second stop path is introduced. **How it works** - `u.Cli.process_deadline_scope(deadline: p.Cli.ProcessDeadline | None)` arms the native one-shot `setitimer(ITIMER_REAL, …)` on the main thread `termination_grace_seconds` before the deadline; without a deadline nothing is armed. - The `SIGALRM` handler forwards SIGTERM to the installed supervisor forwarding so every owned lifecycle stops its process group (signal-wave workers included), then raises `SystemExit(c.Cli.PROCESS_TIMEOUT_EXIT_CODE)` so the interrupted lifecycles reap their children on the way out. - `u.Cli.process_deadline_expire()` ends the active scope through the same handler from any thread. - `TimeoutError` was avoided because it subclasses `OSError`, which the supervisor converts into a failed result instead of an interruption. - Runtime fixture tests cover an expired deadline, on-demand expiry from a worker thread, and a deadlineless scope; all exit with status 124 and the child gone. Written for commit f0a5ed6080b8b59255088f36a49dd19630a12b63. Summary will update on new commits.
