author: mchwalek
body:
Fixes Trello [#33 The Trouble with Triads - missing fires](https://trello.com/c/vvXZfttw/33-the-trouble-with-triads-missing-fires).

## Problem
The 3DS caps all particles at 256 (128 in stereo); PS2 LCS has a 750 pool (`SLES_541.35` `0x1cc6b0`) with no budget. Fires and the flamethrower are pure particles (CARFLAME/FLAME/FIREBALL). After the Trouble with Triads warehouse blast and while ballots burn in Friggin' the Riggin', smoke and other fires filled the cap, so new flames were refused and fires (or the flamethrower) vanished.

## Fix (`stories/src/renderer/Particle.cpp`)
- The cap stays at 256 (128 stereo). A first attempt raised the pool to PS2's 750, but that cost ~2 fps (12 -> 10) in the warehouse scene.
- When the cap is full, CARFLAME/FLAME/FIREBALL replace the oldest smoke particle (CARFLAME_SMOKE, then FIREBALL_SMOKE, then SMOKE).
- The flamethrower (FIREBALL) may also replace the oldest CARFLAME/FLAME, so it stays visible among many fires. Fires never replace each other.
- Other effects are refused at the cap as before. Stories only.
- AGENTS.md landmine #46 and a particle-pool note in the `ps2-lcs-decompilation` skill.

## Validation
- `scripts/tests/test_3ds_fire_particle_budget.py` (5 cases: oldest smoke replaced, fallback order, refused without smoke, flamethrower replaces oldest flame, stereo halves).
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_*.py'`: 70 OK.
- `scripts/build.sh relcs` builds. On hardware: fires visible and frame rate back near pre-fix in The Trouble with Triads.

## Risks
- With the flamethrower in a big fire, the fires lose their oldest (nearly faded) flames first.

body:
## What

The first M3 clause module of A7 (§11: `common`, then the three J14 heads, then the rest).

- **New `1-formats/deed/spec/abnf/clauses/common.abnf` v1.0.0 (DRAFT).** It is a library of rules, not a profile. It defines:
  - `str-list` and `str-list1`;
  - `chora-uuid8` and `lc-variant`, moved from `anchor.abnf` unchanged;
  - `date-string`: YYYY-MM-DD, with month 01–12 and day 01–31 in the grammar; the real-calendar check is SEMANTIC, for the linter;
  - the A7 §7.1 affirmation members `:affirmed`, `:affirmed-by` and `:expires`, with the J4 note: required by default, and a relaxation is authorised and reported.
- **`anchor.abnf`** now borrows these rules instead of defining them. Its accepted language is unchanged.
- **The differential** compiles `common.abnf` with the other modules. Because no clause uses the date and affirmation rules yet, it holds them to explicit accept and refuse lists.
- The differential README and the DEED-GRAMMAR-SPEC references list the new module.

## Why one definition

The differential concatenates every module into one apg-js grammar. A rule defined in two modules would collide, and later modules (the J14 heads, descriptiles, edicts and `CLADE.deed`) all need dates and the chora id.

## Checks run

- `bun differential.js --cases 1500`: PASS. The gate is lenient on 0 variants and stricter on 0.
- Mutation check: loosening `date-month` to `2DIGIT` makes the differential fail on `"2026-13-01"` and `"2026-00-10"`.
- `deed_lint.js --anchor-fixtures`: OK. `deed_lint.test.js`: 204 tests, 0 fail.

## Not in this PR

- No `deed_lint` profile yet: nothing reads the affirmation members until the `descriptile-deed` head (J14) lands, and that is the next PR.
- No change to `deed.abnf`, licences or SPDX.

body:
## Problem

The mobile quick-note shortcut was added in #2 as a 48px `rounded-2xl` tile positioned `right-4`. The add-entry FAB is 56px wide at the same `right-4`, so:

- the tile's centre sat **4px left of the FAB's axis** — it looked like it was sitting beside the `+` instead of above it;
- the rounded square didn't read as the floating "balloon" that was asked for.

## Fix

- Wrap the shortcut in a **56px-wide stack** (`w-14 flex justify-center`) that matches the FAB, sharing its `right-4` / `sm:right-8` offsets → both centres align on one axis at every breakpoint.
- Make the button a **true circle** (`rounded-full`, 48px) with a frosted glass surface (`bg-white/55`, `backdrop-blur-xl`, `saturate-150`), keeping the dot indicator, hover lift and safe-area offset.
- `pointer-events-none` on the transparent wrapper so it can't intercept taps on page content.
- Added a visible `focus-visible` ring for keyboard users.
- 12px vertical gap to the FAB and to the quick-action pills is unchanged, so nothing overlaps.

```
        [ Add entry / Transfer ]     ← FAB menu
        [  ○  ]                      ← note balloon (centred)
        [   +   ]                    ← add entry
```

## Verification

- `npm run build` in `frontend` — passes (PWA, 16 precached entries).
- Dev server serves the component; `PUT /api/accounts/:id/note` still round-trips.
- CSS confirms `w-14` → `3.5rem` for both wrapper and FAB, `right-4` → `1rem` for both, `rounded-full` → `9999px`.
- Frontend-only change, no backend touched.

author: dial203
body:
## What

Whoop states a respiratory rate on every scored sleep (`/v2/activity/sleep`, `score.respiratory_rate`). OW kept it only in the sleep health score's `components`, which no summary reads, so every Whoop night reached `/summaries/sleep` with `avg_respiratory_rate` empty. On 2026-11-13 the sleep hub showed 12.5 br/min for a WHOOP 5.0 on its direct road and nothing for the same strap through OW.

- `whoop/coverage.py`: new `SLEEP_SCALAR_SERIES` (`respiratory_rate` → `SeriesType.respiratory_rate`), added to `TIMESERIES`.
- `Whoop247Data.save_sleep_data` now keeps the record `create_or_merge_sleep` returns and calls `_save_sleep_scalars`. That writes a `respiratory_rate` sample stamped at the sleep's start with `SessionValue(record_id=…)`, so the summary reads it as the provider's figure with scope `sleep`, the same way Oura's `average_breath` arrives. The write runs in a savepoint, so if it fails the sleep is still kept.
- When sleeps merge into one record, only the segment that ends the record writes its figure. The record then carries the figure of the sleep its recovery was scored on, whatever order the segments sync in.
- The resting HR needed no change. The recovery's `resting_heart_rate` was already filed on the sleep and published as `resting_heart_rate_bpm`. `avg_heart_rate_bpm` stays empty for Whoop because Whoop sends no heart-rate samples. The sleep hub's reader is fixed separately.

## Stored nights

`scripts/data_migrations/resync_whoop_sleep_respiratory_rate.py` runs from `scripts/start/app.sh`, once per instance (data_migration). It queues one historical `sync_vendor_data` for each active Whoop connection that holds sleep. Each re-pull starts a day before that connection's earliest stored sleep and is limited to that connection with `connection_ids`. `is_historical=True` leaves the live cursor unchanged. Re-saving is idempotent: sleeps are matched on Whoop's id, and samples are unique per source, series and instant.

Why the stored components aren't copied over directly: Whoop sleep scores carry no data source. On a profile with two Whoop accounts (a 4.0 and a 5.0 worn together, which is the case on the study account), a score can't be told apart from the other strap's at the same wake time. A re-pull files every figure under the account that measured it.

The decision is recorded in `docs/fork/DECISIONS.md`. `DIVERGENCE.md` is generated and was not regenerated here.

## Tests

- `tests/providers/whoop/test_whoop_sleep_vitals.py`: two Whoop accounts on one user each get their own `avg_respiratory_rate` and `resting_heart_rate_bpm` (provider figure, scope `sleep`). A sleep with no respiratory rate reports none. A re-sync keeps one figure per sleep. The first and third tests fail on `main` (`None == 12.5`, `0 == 1`).
- `tests/scripts/test_resync_whoop_sleep_respiratory_rate.py`: one re-pull per account from its own earliest sleep. Revoked accounts, accounts with no sleep and other providers are skipped. A dry run queues nothing.
- Full backend suite run locally: 5686 passed, 3 skipped. `ruff check` and `ruff format` are clean. `ty` was not available in this environment.

## After deploy

Check the app log for `resync_whoop_sleep_respiratory_rate: queued N Whoop history re-pull(s).` After the Celery tasks finish, `/summaries/sleep?filter_by_priority=false` should show `avg_respiratory_rate` on Whoop rows.

author: swhitt
body:
## What

Fixes the `DKRQuickJoinLifecycle` flake. It failed #101's first CI round on `macos-15-intel`, and the diagnostics from #96 finally showed where it stops: host ICE connected, client stuck at checking with no remote candidate.

`create_peer` registers a route only after `create_offer_channels`, but the first `createDataChannel` already starts negotiation on an SDK thread. So the OFFER could leave first, and a fast ANSWER plus its candidates hit `handle_signal` before the route existed and were dropped. Nothing retries until the 30 s reaper. The test waits 20 s.

- Queue a route's OFFER, ANSWER and CANDIDATE on the peer, flush them in order once it's registered
- Lifecycle test holds the first offer construction open at stage 6. Without the fix that fails every run with the same dump as CI, with it the hold ends in 0 ms
- `quick_join_transport.cpp` added to `scripts/pinned-drifted-bases.txt`

## Pattern checklist

- [x] First-party changes are in-place edits under `runtime-recomp/`, `modding/` or `scripts/` (no new `patches/<name>/`)
- [x] Third-party changes are `*.patch` files registered in `patches/manifest.json` (n/a)
- [x] Guest hooks only via `guest-hooks/hooks.toml`; symbols only via `symbols/*.toml` (n/a)
- [x] New settings, launcher pages and owned services are registered, and their contract docs are updated (n/a)
- [x] `netplay/legacy_identity.hpp` updated (reviewed by both owners) if simulation, wire or owned-service behaviour changed (n/a, same messages on the wire, only when they leave changes)
- [x] Tests added or updated; `python scripts/check.py --suite all` passes locally (ran `guard,tooling`, `DKRQuickJoinLifecycle` 35 times, `DKRQuickJoinTransport`, `DKRExperimentalQuickJoin` and `DKRDirectSession`. Not the full host suite)
- [x] Platforms considered: shared transport code, nothing platform specific. Tested on macOS arm64 only.

## Risk

It's the netplay transport, so worth a careful read. Signals are queued under `mutex_` and sent outside it, same locking the callbacks already did through `send_signal`. A construction that fails now never sends its OFFER (before it could leave and the peer got retired anyway).

I didn't reproduce the CI failure without widening the window, so "this was the flake" is an inference from the matching dump. I think players could hit it too, but rarely: the ANSWER has to get back while the client is still creating the other four channels, and the cost is a stall of up to 30 s, not a failed join.

author: itkadr-git
body:
## Fact
Candidate 1.6.9-rc.2, 13.11.2026: task OPE-13017 was created straight in `blocked` with blocker OPE-13014, no assignee, `blockerMetadata = {"previousStatus":"todo"}`. The blocker is `done`. The stale-block sweep failed on it on every pass (board log level 40, "stale block sweep failed for one task", `errorKind: sweep_failed`, HttpError 422) and the task stayed blocked. The operator unblocked it with `PATCH {status:"todo"}` (200).

## Cause
The block has a named reason (the edge to the blocker), so the sweep chose `in_progress`. `issueService.update` refuses it: `server/src/services/issues.ts`, `patch.status === "in_progress" && !nextAssigneeAgentId && !nextAssigneeUserId` -> 422 "in_progress issues require an assignee".

## Changed
- `sweep.ts`: the target status is `todo` when the task has neither an agent nor a user assignee (re-read under the row lock), otherwise `in_progress` as before; a bare block still goes to `todo`. The system comment and the attention signal for such a task name the dead reason.
- The failure warning carries `errorMessage`: the service's fixed refusal sentence for a 4xx HttpError (plain words, up to 120 chars); other errors still log no text.
- Change fragment `docs/myrmidon/changes/stale-block-unassigned.md` (EN/RU).

## Tests
`sweep.myrmidon.test.ts`: unassigned task with a done blocker goes to todo and the edge is removed; assigned one still goes to in_progress; `describeStaleBlockSweepFailure` expectations extended (existing ones not weakened). Not run locally (CI only).

## Check on prod
After rollout, create a task in `blocked` with a closed blocker and no assignee (or wait for one): the next sweep moves it to `todo`, with a system comment "returned to todo without assignee"; no "stale block sweep failed" warnings with `errorStatus: 422`.

author: mchwalek
body:
Fixes Trello card https://trello.com/c/QMJjVaBT ([Friggin' the Riggin'] missing tutorial text).

## Problem
During the cutscene where Toni enters Phil Cassidy's Fully Cocked Gun Shop, the top-left help text never appears.

## Cause
The mission prints `NEDS419`/`NEDS420` with `PRINT_HELP_ALWAYS`. On PS2 the `*_ALWAYS` help opcodes set a flag (`CHud::mAlwaysAllowHelpText`) that keeps help visible in widescreen. reLCS left that line as a TODO, so `CHud::Draw` hid the help box whenever widescreen was on.

## Fix (ported from PS2 `SLES_541.35`)
- The four `*_ALWAYS` help opcodes set the flag (PS2 handlers `0x2746d0`, `0x27472c`, `0x2f32b8`, `0x2f3314`).
- `CHud::Draw` only hides help in widescreen while the flag is clear, and clears it when the fade-out ends (`~0x242840`-`0x242a60`).
- `SetHelpMessage(nil)` clears the flag (`0x23f094`).

Other `main.scm` messages that use these opcodes will now also show in cutscenes, as on PS2: `HELPB`, `CLOTHB`, `HELPC`, `VIC4_A3`, `VIC4_A4`, `HELP58`, `DONS4H1`, `DONS4H3`, `VIC3_H1`, `TT1_A0`, `FERR_SK`.

Stories only.

## Validation
- `Hud.cpp`, `Script9.cpp` and `Script10.cpp` compile with the `scripts/build.sh relcs` flag set.
- Not yet tested on hardware.

author: datawav
body:
Closes #3799.

Every switch, link and action row on the settings subpages now has a 24 dp leading icon. This also covers chat and DM details, conversation notification settings and the per-person notification override. Rows that already lead with an avatar or a progress indicator keep that.

## What changed

- **One helper.** `SettingsLeadingIcon(icon, modifier, tint, testTag)` draws every row glyph at 24 dp with no content description. The title already names the row, so screen readers don't hear it twice.
  - It dims through the same `LocalSettingsRowEditable` signal as the row title, so disabled and busy rows grey the icon at Material's 0.38 alpha on every screen.
  - Destructive rows pass the error tint.
  - The hub keeps its `settings.icon.*` test tags.
- **`leading` is now required.** `SettingsSwitch`, `SettingsLink` and `SettingsAction` no longer default `leading` to `null`, so a new row can't quietly ship without an icon. The only production `null` is the App updates row, which keeps its existing rule: it shows its update emblem only in the prominent state.
- **Icons.** The new drawables are Material Symbols, outlined. Direction-dependent glyphs set `autoMirrored`. No glyph repeats within a group. The read-aloud Engine row uses the memory chip glyph instead of a microphone.

## Tests

- `SettingsLeadingIconCoverageTest` checks that every row has a leading icon, that no glyph repeats within a group and that icons stay out of the accessibility tree. It runs on Appearance (including the preview rows), group and DM notification settings and the per-person override.
- `SettingsComponentsSemanticsTest.leadingSlotDimsWheneverTheRowRejectsActivation` checks that switch, link and action rows mark the leading slot as non-editable when they are disabled or busy, and that the dim alpha matches the title's.
- `GroupAdvancedSettingsIconsTest` still passes, including its RTL check. Its three goldens were re-recorded along with the others.
- Re-recorded the Roborazzi goldens for the affected settings, details and notification screens, then reviewed them in light, dark, AMOLED and RTL.

## Docs

The manual release guide drops the inventory anchors for the per-screen icon helpers this replaces. SET-001 now checks the leading column, and `SettingsLeadingIconCoverageTest` is registered in `docs/invariant-gates.md`.

## Overlap

#3791 also changes `AccountKeysScreen`, `SettingsLayout` and the `profile_keys_*` and `settings_screen_*` goldens. Whichever PR merges second needs to rebase and re-record those goldens.

author: mchwalek
body:
Fixes Trello: https://trello.com/c/3KYmuUFv/6-dead-meat-sneaking-mechanics-not-working-at-all

In Dead Meat's sawmill hide-and-seek, the mission script (MAC4) picks Casa's next hiding spot with `IS_CHAR_WANDER_PATH_CLEAR`. reLCS read the target point from params 0..2 (ped handle, x, y) and the height tolerance from param 3 (z), so the check always failed, no hiding spot was ever found and Casa stayed crouched even after spotting Toni. On PS2 he sprints off when he sees you, which is why you have to sneak up from behind.

## Changes
- `stories/src/control/Script7.cpp`: use params 1..3 / 4, as PS2 does (`SLES_541.35` `0x185210`, case `0x515`).
- `stories/src/core/World.cpp`: `CWorld::IsWanderPathClear` now matches PS2 `0x17bde0`: the LOS is level at the lower Z (`min.s`), and ground probes are capped at `maxSteps` (re3 used `Max`).

Spotting (`HAS_CHAR_SPOTTED_PLAYER` -> `OurPedCanSeeThisOne`) was checked against PS2 `0x1d33d8` and is identical, so it is unchanged.

Stories only. miami has the same handler and `Max` bug, left untouched.

## Validation
- `scripts/build.sh relcs` builds.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_*.py'`: 65 tests OK.
- Not tested in-game yet.

## Risk
The `IsWanderPathClear` change also affects ped wandering (`Ped.cpp`) and ped attractors (`PedAttractor.cpp`, `maxSteps` 0 now means LOS only); both now follow PS2's behaviour and are more permissive than before.

author: tskarhed
body:
## What

Grafana now recognizes `424 Failed Dependency` from the image renderer, which the renderer sends when the page it was asked to capture reports that it could not load, such as a missing dashboard. The reason is the response body.

Before, only 408 and 429 were recognized, so a 424 became a generic error and the caller got `500 "Rendering failed."` without the reason.

- `PageLoadError` carries the reason.
- The HTTP client turns a 424 into a `PageLoadError` for image, PDF, and CSV rendering. The body is read up to 1 KiB.
- `RenderHandler` answers it with 424 and the reason in the error page title.

## Compatibility

Nothing changes until a renderer sends a 424. Alerting does not retry a page that fails to load, because only timeouts count as retryable there.

## Open points

- Rendering metrics still count the new error as `failure`. A separate outcome would keep missing dashboards out of the service failure rate. That is a metric change, so it is left for review.
- Callers outside this repository that match on rendering errors may need to handle `PageLoadError`.

## Related changes

Three independent changes make up the full behavior, and they can merge in any order:

- grafana/grafana-image-renderer#1083: the renderer returns 424 with the reason.
- grafana/grafana#137838: the dashboard page sends the failure reason.
- This PR: Grafana recognizes the 424.

## Testing

- Client tests against an `httptest` server for the image and CSV paths, the 1 KiB cap, an empty body, and a 500 that must not be treated as a page error.
- Handler tests for 424 with the reason, and for other errors still returning 500.
- Removing the new code makes the new tests fail.
- `golangci-lint` was not run, because it was not available in the environment.

author: jacobloader
body:
Part 2 of "resident REPL improvements" I've used so agents can quickly try speculative tactic applications without recompiling the whole file (extends from #770, which kept files warm but doesn't isolate a single line)


Agent description:

The interactive LSP tools re-elaborate everything after the edited line for each candidate. With AUTOFORM_TACTIC_BACKEND=repl (default lsp), one long-lived REPL per project (servers/repl/resident.py) imports a file's header once, project modules included, elaborates the text before the target declaration once while it is unchanged, replaces the target line with sorry and runs each candidate as a REPL tactic step on that goal. A candidate is closed when the REPL's kernel check of the goal completes, or else when the declaration elaborates with it written in. Lines sorry cannot stand in for, declarations with other errors, and failures of the REPL process fall back to the language server, and the result says so.

Each distinct list of import lines is checked once with Lean's header parser (a new public run_header_parser in servers/repl/core.py), on a thread beside the REPL's own import, so it adds no latency. A header Lean reads differently, or a module or prelude header, falls back. The header environment is keyed on the .olean files of every project module below the header, so a rebuild of any of them restarts the REPL; a module changed since its last build is used as built and named in the result, as lean_diagnostic_messages reports stale imports rather than building them.

A candidate that overruns its budget kills the process. A process group that cannot be verified gone blocks the next start (which falls back) and makes close() raise, so the resource cache retries it. stderr keeps only its last 2000 bytes. Memory is checked after each batch against AUTOFORM_RESIDENT_REPL_MAX_GB (default 8), and at most once a second within a batch against 1.5 times that, so a restart mid-batch happens only far past it.

Tests: tests/test_resident_repl.py runs a fake REPL and header parser; tests/test_real_resident_repl.py runs the pinned upstream REPL in the real REPL CI job. Latency on a 391-line tbscv file, four candidates per call, before and after these checks: 70-79 ms warm in both; 3.2-3.7 s after an edit above the target in both; cold and header-change calls (23-41 s) are dominated by the Mathlib import in both.

## Premise

- **User:** who needs this: a consumer project, an agent step, or a maintainer.
- **Problem:** the measured problem: a reproduction, a run, or a count.
- **Replaces:** the behavior, command or doc this replaces.
- **Deletes:** what this removes, or why nothing can go.

A new command, flag, schema or JSON key, UI paradigm, or skill rule needs a
design note in its issue first; link it here.

## Checks

- [ ] Tests for new behavior, docs for changed APIs, a CHANGELOG line.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make test` pass.

body:
## Problem and resulting behavior

First of four pull requests that give the dark theme its new HUD look. The look was settled option by option in a throwaway branch; this series writes it into the stylesheets that own each component, so nothing of that experiment (selectors, overrides, sample content) reaches `main`.

This one covers the run view's two panels and the text in them, in dark:

- **Panels.** Both reply boxes share one panel rule set: an octagon edge that brightens toward its corners, a fill of faint scan lines and a bloom, and a halo. The halo is a shadow, and the edge and fill are on layers of their own, so typing or streaming redraws only the text.
- **Panel names.** A small tab on each panel's top edge names it: Agent, User. The reply panel's edge, fill and tab light up while the caret is in it.
- **Text.** Share Tech Mono in a paler blue with a soft glow. Headings are in the same face, told apart by size and colour; bold text and headings are thickened by a stroke, since the face has one weight. Heading levels four to six are now styled too.
- **Scan lines** are drawn in whole screen pixels, so they look the same at every zoom. `theme/screen-row.ts` keeps that unit current.
- **Shell.** Fine ticks along the top and bottom edges, with more room above the header and below the footer.

The buttons, the overview, Environment, dialogs and the message log follow in the next three pull requests; until the last one lands, dark is a mix of old and new.

**Light is unchanged**, with one exception: a numbered list's numbers were cut off at the panel's left edge in both themes. The list is now indented far enough to show them.

## Issue and scope

Requested directly by the maintainer.

## Validation

**Full E2E must pass in CI before merging.**

- `npm run typecheck`, `eslint`, and the whole native suite (`npm run test:electron`): 316 passed.
- Dark screenshot baselines regenerated (`--update-snapshots=changed`) and each new image reviewed. The light baselines pass untouched.
- New tests: the panel names are shown in dark and hidden in light; the scan lines' unit stays one screen pixel after a zoom change. The font test now expects Share Tech Mono in the dark HUD.
- Two existing tests raced a layout they had not waited for, and the new spacing made them lose now and then (the first failed once in CI here). The image viewer test now waits for the preview to load before opening the viewer, which takes its size from the preview. The footer screenshot test now waits for the footer to place its buttons after the last resize. Each passes 20 of 20 repeats.
- Compared against the reference look at 140% zoom on a virtual display: both panels and the shell match it pixel for pixel; the light run view is pixel-identical to `main`.
- Not run locally: the backend lifecycle tests and the package check (CI runs them).

author: chanjdaniel
body:
A market's table assignment now stores where it stands, and the back end alone owns and serves that state.
Publish results and going live are refused until a table allocation has really been run, and the screens read the served state instead of working it out themselves.

## Why

An organizer could assign one vendor to a table by hand, press Publish results and publish the market with no allocation ever run.
Every other approved vendor then read "You did not get assigned" on their vendor page, though nobody decided that: the solver never ran.
Nothing stored where the assignment stood, so the product could not tell hand assignments alone from an allocation: each reader worked it out from the rows, their hand-placed flags, `madeFrom`, `resultsPublished` and the phase, each in its own way.

The reproduction, `back-end/tests/test_publish_needs_a_run.py`, drives the routes: two approved vendors, one pinned by hand, then Publish results, the move to market days, and the other vendor's read.
Against `dev`'s back end it fails as the bug does:

```
{'publish': (200, None), 'move': (200, []), 'phase': 'market_days', 'other vendor': ('open', 'not_assigned')}
```

On this branch publish answers 409 with the pins-only sentence, the move answers 409 naming `assignment_computed` and `results_published`, and the other vendor's read carries no outcome.

## What Changed

- **The stored state.** `assignmentObject.state` is `none`, `pinned` (tables assigned by hand only) or `run`, and a run always records what it was made from (`madeFrom`).
  Publish results stores the assignment revision it stood on (`assignmentObject.publishedRevision`).
- **One owner.** `back-end/assignment/lifecycle.py` is the only writer of the assignment's rows, state and `publishedRevision`, and serves `allocation` on the market read: `none`, `pinned`, `current`, `stale`, `published` or `changed_since_published`.
  Publish results, the go-live guards, assigning, the rules lock and the closed review all ask it.
  The applicant-facing reads (the vendor page, the rejection rules) keep reading `resultsPublished` on purpose: they ask whether applicants were told.
- **A read that survives a rollback.** The stored state is trusted only while it agrees with the rows and `madeFrom`; otherwise it is derived by the migration's rule, with one warning naming the market by id, and a market read never fails on it.
  An allocation stored before runs recorded `madeFrom` reads as a run with a legacy marker, `{"legacy": "before-fingerprints"}`, which is never out of date, so existing markets read as they do now; a hand edit of such an allocation stores the marker too, so it never turns into pins only.
- **The refusals.** Publish results and publishing the market are refused on pins only ("Only tables assigned by hand are stored. Allocate tables first: allocating keeps them and assigns every other approved vendor, so each applicant is told whether they have a table."), and on an allocation run then freed to nobody.
  Nothing allocated, an out-of-date allocation and results already published keep their sentences.
  Allocate tables stays refused after results are published; assigning, moving, swapping and freeing a seat by hand stay allowed.
  A free that frees nothing still answers 200 with `removed: 0`.
- **After results are published.** The seat dialog says what the vendor's page tells them and that nothing is sent to them, and the history entry of a free, move, swap or assignment says it came after results were published, naming the table the vendor's page had shown on a free or a move.
  Older entries read as before.
- **The front end reads the server.** `front-end/src/utils/assignPhase.ts` is deleted: the screens read the served `allocation`, `assignRefusalReason`, `publishWaitsReason` and transition blockers.
  The phase rail never offers a remedy the server would refuse, a stale allocation's fix on the rail is Allocate tables, and Assignments takes "the allocation is settled, assign seats by hand" from the served go-live blocker, not from the phase.
- **E2E.** `results-wait-for-the-allocation.spec.ts` gains the pins-only case, and the new `a-change-after-results-says-so.spec.ts` publishes through the product, then frees and moves a seat.
  Two specs published on hand assignments alone and now run an allocation first (`allocateThenFreeEverySeat`): `the-stats-headlines.spec.ts` and `the-market-on-a-phone.spec.ts`.
  `seedStoredAssignment` stores a legacy run, and the two `phase-state-machine.spec.ts` walks through Offers and `the-closed-review-says-why.spec.ts` keep writing their state into the database, since no route reaches it.
- **Docs.** A new node, [the assignment's lifecycle](docs/implementation/modules/assignment-lifecycle.md), [ADR 0026](docs/adr/0026-the-assignment-stores-its-state-and-publish-needs-a-run.md), two glossary terms in `CONTEXT.md` (Pins only, Changed since results), an `AGENTS.md` index line, and the nodes the change touches.

## Release

Once this release is deployed, run the migration, a dry run first:

```
MONGODB_URI='<URI>' .venv/bin/python migrations/migrate_assignment_state.py --dry-run
MONGODB_URI='<URI>' .venv/bin/python migrations/migrate_assignment_state.py
```

It sets each live market's state, the legacy marker where the rule says so, and `publishedRevision` on published markets, printing each market by id and a count.
It is safe to run again, and should be run again after any roll-forward past a rollback.
Nothing waits on it: an unmigrated market reads correctly, so there is no boot marker.
`docs/OPERATIONS.md` and `docs/RELEASING.md` carry the same lines.

## Risk Assessment

Medium.
Product behaviour changes on purpose: a market in Assignment holding only hand assignments can no longer publish results or go live until tables are allocated, and the rail sends its organizer to Allocate tables; an organizer used to that path meets a refusal that says what to do.
Every other path reads as it did: an allocation stored before this change reads as current through the legacy marker, published markets read as published, and each refusal's existing sentence stands.
The deploy needs no migration first, since the read derives the state an unmigrated market lacks, and a rollback is safe: the release before ignores the new keys, and when rolled forward again the read repairs whatever it wrote, as does the next write or the migration.
The new keys are written beside the existing ones inside `assignmentObject`, never replacing it, and every write still holds what it read (`write_market`).
The migration writes only `state`, `madeFrom` (the legacy marker) and `publishedRevision`, holding what it read, and is tested on live, archived, published and being-deleted markets, against a real MongoDB too.

## Testing

- Back end: `scripts/real-mongo-test.sh` at this PR's head, 9222 passed (the whole back-end suite with the real-MongoDB tests, none skipped); `python -m pytest tests/` alone, 8545 passed and 674 skipped, at the head the team review passed.
- The table test, `back-end/tests/test_the_allocation_table.py`, drives every one of the 36 (allocation, event) pairs through the routes, with real runs and a real publish, and asserts the answer, the served `allocation` and that the stored state agrees with the rows.
- Front end: `npm run test:unit`, 271 files, 4913 tests; `type-check`, `lint`, `lint:css` and `format:check` clean.
- `python3 scripts/knowledge_graph.py check`: 0 errors; `drift --base origin/dev`: 0 warnings.
- E2E: each changed or new spec passed alone on a freshly seeded stack (`results-wait-for-the-allocation`, `a-change-after-results-says-so`, `phase-state-machine`, `the-closed-review-says-why`, `the-stats-headlines`, `the-market-on-a-phone`); the whole suite is CI's `e2e` shards on this PR.

## UI check

Captured on the worktree's own stack with fixture data alone: before on `dev` (2a222c2f), after at this PR's head, at 390, 768 and 1440 px; the tiles below are one width each.

author: ruguevara
body:
## What

Player and Studio open `.taym` files ([ruguevara/taym](https://github.com/ruguevara/taym)): AY tunes with timer effects (PWM, sync-buzzer, samples). A TAYM opens as a PSG clip with timers, and the AY chip plays each timer's register writes at their own sample, between frames.

- **Engine**: the taym C timer engine (`third_party/taym` submodule) runs inside `AYChipPlugin` (`ChipTimers`), on the chip's cycle timeline.
- **Wire**: timer commands travel as CCs on one MIDI channel per timer after the chip's four (`TimerCC`). The bank of lanes and actions never travels as MIDI: the clip registers it and the chip looks it up by number (`TimerBankRegistry`).
- **Clip**: `ClipTimers`, a `TIMERS` child of the PSG clip's state. `editFormatVersion` is not bumped: an older app plays the frames without the effects.
- **UI**: timers drawn as notes in the clip; a `⚠` in the AY panel for commands the chip cannot play; a stopwatch on driven scopes (Viz mode and rendered video too); a timers switch per channel; the frame hover lists the running timers, and now opens with Time / Frame / Bar and names each pitch's nearest note with cents.

Design as built: `docs/design/timer-fx.md`.

## For the reviewer

- Plain PSG playback is byte-identical to `develop` (WAV and PSG compared before the merge).
- Atarized rendered through uZX correlates 1.00000 with the taym Python reference over 180 s.
- `develop` is merged in; that merge moves `third_party/zxtune` to develop's commit.
- Built and tested on macOS/Clang only. GCC and MSVC are unverified until CI runs.
- No screenshots attached.

## Tests

Full suite, 718 tests, passing locally. New groups: `TimerCC`, `ChipTimers`, `AYChipTimers`, `ClipTimers`, `TaymFile`, `TaymImport`, plus hover and timer-note cases in `PsgClipPainting`.

author: zhach1
body:
Refs #161.

## Problem
`init` runs `bootstrap/install-third-party-skills`, but its `/ralph/skills` bind was read-only. `shutil.move` crosses filesystems from `/tmp`, then its fallback copy fails against that mount. The install script returns an incomplete stack with a traceback.

## Change
- `compose/docker-compose.yml`: only the trusted one-shot `init` mounts the skills checkout writable. Hermes and Chat keep read-only mounts; no agent sandbox gains a writable skills mount.
- `bootstrap/install-third-party-skills`: when Git metadata is unavailable inside `init`, refuse to replace any existing **unstamped** target instead of mistaking a tracked first-party skill for an untracked install. Preserve same-pin idempotency and the offline-tolerant warning policy.
- Focused tests pin the mount boundary and the no-Git collision/no-op cases; infrastructure and operations docs describe the trusted init exception and `--check` recovery. No third-party content is vendored.

## Validation
- Both new regression tests failed before implementation, then passed.
- `python3 evals/test_third_party_install.py`: 8 passed; `ComposeFileTests`: 8 passed.
- Board wiring 8, profile config 61, notifier approvals 92, review-loop 30 pass. `evals/check-skills-public` public-only scan, Compose config parsing, `git diff --check`, and local scope check pass.
- No live `init` or real pinned upstream fetch was run for this PR; CI will exercise the pinned fetch on a public runner.

## Assumptions
- `init` is trusted one-shot setup; its RW bind covers the whole skills tree, not only third-party paths. Agent-facing Hermes and Chat mounts remain RO. A compromised Hermes orchestrator already has a documented Docker-proxy bind risk; this PR does not claim to close it.
- First-party skill directories do not carry an installer `.third-party.json` stamp; without Git metadata, an existing unstamped directory must fail closed.

## Other observations
- The installer's existing pin-upgrade path removes an old stamped directory before moving the replacement, so a crash between those operations is not atomic. Unchanged; outside #161's mount failure.

## Rollout
After owner review/merge, run `init` on each instance using that instance's current checkout and verify the pinned skills plus `--check`. No live service or volume change is included in this PR.

# Pull Request

## Closing issue

Fixes #54

## Summary

`SpreadsheetModel.evalCondition` turned both sides of a comparison into numbers with `Number()`, so any text became `NaN`. Because `NaN === NaN` is false, `=IF(A1="yes", ...)` always took the false branch, `<>` was always true for text, and `AND` / `OR` / `NOT` (which use the same function) gave the same wrong answers. When either side is not a number, the two sides are now compared as case-insensitive text, as other spreadsheets do. When both sides are numbers, nothing changes, including an empty cell compared with `""`.

## Type of Change

- [ ] feat - New feature
- [x] fix - Bug fix
- [ ] docs - Documentation only
- [ ] style - Formatting, no code change
- [ ] refactor - Code restructuring without behavior change
- [x] test - Add or fix tests
- [ ] build - Build system or dependency changes
- [ ] ci - CI/CD pipeline changes
- [ ] perf - Performance improvement

## Changes

- `packages/core/src/spreadsheet-model.ts`, `evalCondition`: if either side is `NaN` as a number, compare `String(left).toLowerCase()` with `String(right).toLowerCase()` using the same operator; otherwise compare the numbers as before.
- `packages/core/src/__tests__/spreadsheet-condition-text.test.ts` (new): 8 tests. Text `=`, case-insensitive `=`, `<>` and `!=` on equal text, two text cells, `AND` / `OR` / `NOT`, text never equal to a number, and the existing numeric comparisons (`=10`, `<>10`, `>=10`, `="10"`, empty cell `=""`), which are unchanged.

## Testing

| Pass after | same at `b03b5f1` | PASS: 8 passed, exit 0 |

| CI Build | `pnpm run build` | PASS: exit 0 |
| `pnpm lint` (template) | `eslint src ... --max-warnings 0` | FAIL, not from this change: the same 70 warnings in `src/`, which this PR does not touch (`git diff --stat 4dc1c97 HEAD -- src` is empty) |
| Core package types | `cd packages/core && tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` | 2 errors, both in the untouched `spreadsheet-model-extended.test.ts` (lines 273, 282), the same 2 on `4dc1c97`; none in the changed files |
| Whitespace | `git diff --check HEAD~1` | PASS |

- [x] Unit tests pass (`pnpm test`)

## Additional Notes

Text comparison ignores case, as in Excel, LibreOffice and Google Sheets, so `"Paid" = "paid"` is true. `<` and `>` on text compare alphabetically, again ignoring case. A text cell is never equal to a number (`"abc" = 0` is false); before, it was also false, but for the wrong reason.

author: dancsi
body:
In `pivot`, the `aggregate_function` reads the values through `pl.element()` (and counts them with `pl.len()`). Each pivoted column replaced every `pl.element()` and `pl.len()` in that expression with the column's filtered values, including those inside a nested `list.eval`, `arr.eval` or `cumulative_eval`, where they refer to the evaluated values instead. So `aggregate_function=pl.element().first().list.eval(pl.element() * 10)` raised "named columns are not allowed in `eval` functions", and the same expression works in `group_by().agg()`. The replacement now stops at the evaluated expression of an `eval`.

I used AI to implement this change and its tests.

author: alexprudhomme
body:
## Jira

https://coveord.atlassian.net/browse/KIT-6626

## Motivation

When the answer to an action that opens no turn, such as `restoreState`, re-created a surface that an earlier turn drew (`createSurface`, `replace: true`, same surface id), the surface moved to the session's latest turn. In the multi-surface sample, going Back to an earlier search grid restored the search on the server, but the page then lost its grid and switched to the assistant layout.

The bug shows up now because Agent Gateway keeps only the latest search surface of each view (agent-gateway ADR-010, KIT-6268). Since that change, `restoreState` on an earlier surface gets a full `createSurface` with `replace: true` instead of a diff.

## Root Cause

An action that opens no turn has its answer recorded with the latest turn (ADR-018). `deriveOwnerTurnIds` gave each surface to the turn whose activities held its latest `createSurface`, so recording a re-created surface with the latest turn moved the surface to that turn.

## Changes

- **Design:** a surface keeps the turn that first created it for as long as the renderer stream holds it. A later `createSurface` for that id, from any run, replaces the surface in place but doesn't move it. Only a `deleteSurface` frees the id, and a `createSurface` after that belongs to the turn that sends it. A surface the initialization created, such as the session shell, stays in no turn.
- **Loading placeholders don't change:** a placeholder is still listed only while the run that last created it streams, and `abandonedPlaceholderIds` uses that same run. `session-surfaces.ts` now tracks two maps: the owner turn, used to group surfaces by turn, and the creator turn, used to decide whether a placeholder is still streaming.
- **No-catalog creates:** a `createSurface` without a catalog doesn't count, because neither projection draws it. The first `createSurface` with a catalog decides the owner.
- **Rejected options:**
  - Keeping the owner only for answers to actions that open no turn would need a new, persisted marker on the public `Activity`.
  - Recording the answer with the turn that owns the surface would contradict ADR-018's rule that an action's run is recorded with the active turn. It would also put operations ahead of later turns' operations in the activity log.
- **Doc change:** the `TurnResponse.surfaces` TSDoc used to say a surface "a later turn creates again under the same id belongs to that turn". It now says such a surface stays with the turn that first created it. The README and `docs/architecture.md` say the same.
- **Changeset:** a patch for `@coveo/thermidor`.

## Validation

- **New session test:** turn 1 draws a search surface and turn 2 draws an answer. Then a `selectPage` that opens no turn gets back a `createSurface` for the search surface, which must stay in turn 1. The test failed before the fix: turn 1 ended up with `[]` and turn 2 with both surfaces. It passes now.
- **`session-surfaces` unit tests:**
  - The two tests that encoded the old rule are rewritten for the new one: a turn re-creating an earlier turn's surface, and a turn re-creating the initialization's shell.
  - New tests: a create after a delete belongs to the new turn; a no-catalog create doesn't take ownership; a re-created placeholder is listed while its run streams, both turn to turn and from the initialization's shell, and is abandoned once that run ends.
- **Automated checks:**
  - `@coveo/thermidor`: 447 unit tests, `tsc --noEmit` and `test:dts` pass.
  - demo-schema-react: 612 unit tests pass.
  - demo-multi-surface-react: 61 unit tests and the typecheck pass.
  - `pnpm lint:check` passes.
- **Browser check:** demo-schema-react against prod (`--mode=demo`). I searched "kayak", selected Barca Sports, then searched "surfboard".
  - Browser Back sent `restoreState` for turn 1's kayak surface, and the gateway answered with a full `createSurface`. The kayak grid stayed in turn 1 with Barca Sports selected, and the surfboard grid stayed in turn 2.
  - Forward did the same for the surfboard surface.
  - A question to the agent landed under turn 3.
  - The only console errors were a `favicon.ico` 404 and a 409 `AGENT:ACTION_IN_FLIGHT`, which the session retried.
  - No turn drew the session shell.
  - The browser check ran on a build from before the no-catalog guard, which this flow doesn't touch.

## Checklist

- [x] PR title follows [Conventional Commits 1.0.0](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) format (`fix(<scope>): <description>`)
- [x] [Added a changeset](https://changesets.dev/guide/getting-started) (`pnpm changeset`) if modifying public package source code

author: blarghmatey
body:
### What are the relevant tickets? N/A ### Description (What does it do?) Bots in other apps can't see what a learner told MIT Learn about their interests and available time. This writes three profile fields to the learner's shared memory (the Hindsight service, through ol-llm's memory interface) when the learner saves their profile, including during onboarding: - topic interests, education level and time commitment, one note per field; saving again replaces the note and clearing a field deletes it - nothing identifying goes into a note or its key (no name, bio, headline, images or certificate records) - only the learner's own request writes, exchanging the session token APISIX forwards in `X-Access-Token`; a staff edit of someone else's profile writes nothing - a memory outage or a forget in progress is logged and the profile save goes through Memory is on only where `OL_LLM_MEMORY_BACKEND` is set, which today is QA (https://github.com/mitodl/ol-infrastructure/pull/6934).
Implementation details
- `profiles/memory.py` holds the note text and keys, and `ProfileViewSet.perform_update` calls it with the note fields present in the request (read before saving, since `ProfileSerializer.update` pops `topic_interests`). `completed_onboarding` isn't writable through the API, and onboarding saves through the same `PATCH /api/v0/profiles/me/`. - Keys are `profile-topic-interests`, `profile-current-education` and `profile-time-commitment`; the backend stores them as `mit-learn.`. - ol_llm is imported inside the functions that use it, so it stays off the boot path (`main/boot_imports_test.py`). ol-llm's configuration moves from `vector_search/encoders/litellm.py` to `main/llm.py` so the memory path and the embeddings encoder configure it the same way. - `SyncMemory` runs on a per-thread event loop. Under ASGI a request's sync code runs on a thread that ends with the request, so the loop and its HTTP clients are closed after the writes. - ol-llm moves from 0.0.7 to 0.0.14 with the `memory` extra (opik 2.2.94 to 2.2.143, adds hindsight-client 1.2.0). - The token is held only for the call. Failures are logged by exception class only.
### How can this be tested? `pytest profiles/memory_test.py main/boot_imports_test.py` covers the write, replace, delete, staff-edit, missing-token, outage, fenced and partial-failure cases on ol-llm's in-memory backend. `profiles/`, `main/` and `vector_search/` pass locally on the 0.0.14 lock, and `learning_resources/` passed against a local 0.0.14 build before it was published (its 5 StarRocks integration tests need a live StarRocks and errored). Not yet checked against the deployed Hindsight. After the QA deploy, a profile save should produce `mit-learn.profile-*` documents in that learner's bank, and no "Profile notes were not written" warnings in the mit-learn logs. ### Additional Context - Not measured: how long a Hindsight retain takes in QA. Each save that touches these fields makes one token exchange and up to three retains in the request, each bounded at 10 seconds. - Not in this PR: forgetting a learner's memory when their MIT Learn account is deleted. That needs the platform admin client delivered to mit-learn's Celery workers, which is new ol-infrastructure work. https://claude.ai/code/session_01FGZebDqcuBXJ9WPJzGWLaa

author: mdvermeer
body:
Adds an optional way for a module port to see which error the modem returned for a request. Today a failed request only yields CELLULAR_PKT_STATUS_FAILURE; the +CME ERROR: <n> line is logged and discarded, so a port can't distinguish "file not found" from any other failure.

Changes:
- CellularAtErrorResponse_t (received, truncated, line[CELLULAR_AT_ERROR_RESPONSE_MAX_LENGTH]) in cellular_common.h, and an optional trailing pErrorResponse member on CellularAtReq_t. Existing brace-initialised requests get NULL and are unaffected.
- _Cellular_AtcmdRequestTimeoutWithCallbackRaw resets the caller's struct before the request is validated (so a rejected request can't leave a stale result behind), attaches it to the context for the lifetime of the request and detaches it on every exit path (including timeout), so a late response can never write to a caller's stack buffer.
- _Cellular_ProcessLine copies the error final result line into the attached struct (bounded, null terminated, truncated set if it didn't fit) under PktRespMutex. A comment at the capture point documents the pre-existing window in which a late error line from a timed-out request can be attributed to the next request.
- CELLULAR_AT_ERROR_RESPONSE_MAX_LENGTH config default (48).
- Fixed the pre-existing swapped arguments in the "Modem return ERROR" log line (it printed the command under the "line" label and vice versa).

The library doesn't interpret the line; that's left to the port (see the BG770 PR, which maps +CME ERROR: 405 to CELLULAR_FILE_NOT_FOUND for AT+QFCRC and AT+QFDEL).

Tests (test/unit-test, CMock/Unity, run in the firmware "tests (hw-v2)" Drone step):
- Fixed the existing suites so they pass against this fork's sources (Cellular_ATStrtoui mock with the real range checks, prefix removal in _Cellular_ParseRegStatus), and removed a dead "return NULL token" knob from the URC handler mock.
- 5 new pkthandler tests (58 → 63): captured, detached on timeout, detached on send failure, reset on a rejected (NULL command) request, request without an error response.
- 6 new pktio tests (49 → 55) driving the real _Cellular_ProcessLine: +CME ERROR captured, plain ERROR captured, max-length line, truncation, not written on OK, error without an attached struct still reported.
- The pkthandler tests that pass a NULL data pointer now pass a data length of 0 to match.

Motivation: field BG770A units that lose their UFS certificate files (BinSentry/firmware PR#405).

author: stixaly
body:
Refs #757 (v1-required).

**Bug.** `POST /api/jobs/{id}/finalize` checked that the job existed, not its status. It rebuilt the bundle of a job that was uploaded, queued or processing, and could mark it completed under the worker. A job deleted just before the rebuild gave a 500, and one deleted during it gave a fictive success. Reproduced on the unchanged code: **10 of the 12 new tests fail** (`200 == 409`, `500 == 404`, `200 == 404`). The 2 that pass are the allowed states.

**Fix** (`api/worker.py`, `api/routes/jobs.py`):
- `re_run_final_stages` raises `FinalizeRefused` from its first read, before any build, for `uploaded`, `queued` and `processing`.
- The publication UPDATE carries `AND status NOT IN (...)`. When it writes nothing, the status is read again: gone gives 404, refused gives 409, otherwise the existing "newer build" and "overtaken" paths run. `_stored_newer_build` has the same guard.
- The route answers 409 with a text (not the Stage 5 verdict). The web client then shows it as an ordinary error, because it reads only a body with `validation: "invalid"` as a refused bundle.
- 404 replaces the 500 and the fictive success. `contract/openapi.json` gets the 404, a compatible change.

**Tests**:
- `tests/test_finalize_status_guard_757.py` (13): the matrix of 3 states × quick and full with nothing written, the allowed states, a claim during the rebuild where the worker keeps the job, deletions before and during the rebuild with no file coming back, and the worker resuming after a refusal.
- `test_bundle_builds` asserted the old fictive success and is corrected.
- Five `test_worker` tests built a job left in `processing`; they move to `reviewing`.
- 48 related test files pass; ruff, mypy and `contract.py check` pass.

Docs: `docs/api.md` (the finalize row and the internal errors table).

body:
Scoping only. No model was fitted, no run was made, no spend.

## Why

The frequency/severity fair test is finished, and **both of its arms are TabPFN**. So the programme can say "fine-tuning helps" and still cannot answer the question a pricing team asks: does TabPFN beat a GLM or CatBoost built the way an actuary builds one?

Until that exists, every headline is a comparison between two TabPFN configurations. The row-scaling arm closed the last internal-validity question (the cap did not manufacture the frequency Go; the severity null survives at every claim), so this is the comparison that can change the conclusion rather than defend it.

## What is in here

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `docs/experiments/fair-test-freq-sev/baseline_method_specification.md` | The configuration, sourced: Poisson-log + case-study GLM1 encoding; CatBoost Poisson/RMSE; the measured facts below |
| `docs/experiments/fair-test-freq-sev/ACTUARIAL_BASELINE_PREREGISTRATION_2026-11.md` | Statistic, per-target floors, decision rule, fixed vs free |
| `docs/plans/597-actuarial-baseline.md` | Order of work |
| `GLOSSARY.md` | **Actuarial baseline** defined as a `Method`, never an `Arm` |
| `docs/REPORT_REGISTRY.md` | The specification's row |

## The decisions this encodes

Settled with the owner before writing: all four targets; `B_ft30` as contender with `A_raw` alongside; **full fold pool** primary with the fair test's 10,000-row sample as sensitivity; per-target registered floors (2/4/2/2); statistic `r = (M(baseline) − M(TabPFN)) / M(baseline)` so positive means TabPFN is better; per-target verdicts only, task means descriptive; three seeds uniformly; literature feature engineering for the baselines; lognormal severity only; intercept-only anchor.

## Three things the research changed

All measured, not remembered:

- **sklearn has no `offset`.** The GLM must use `ClaimNb/Exposure` with `Exposure` as weight, which is the offset model exactly (verified to 2.8e-14). Weighting the count by `Exposure` instead gives different coefficients.
- **CatBoost 1.2.10 has no Gamma loss** — it raises at fit. Tweedie is the only Gamma-adjacent option, and neither is scored on the registered metric, so both are dropped.
- **`src/metrics.poisson_deviance` is a total, not a mean.** It differs from sklearn's by the test-row count — a quoting trap.

## A correction worth flagging

The case study is **doi:10.2139/ssrn.3164764**, Noll, Salzmann & Wüthrich (three authors). An earlier draft of this work cited arXiv `2003.11984`, which is a differential-geometry paper by an unrelated author; that id is gone. The specification cites the verified DOI.

## Risk this buys, stated up front

**The comparison can lose.** If the GLM beats fine-tuned TabPFN on French frequency, the headline changes from "fine-tuning helps" to "fine-tuning helps TabPFN lose by less" — more useful, but not what the current write-up implies, and the documents quoting +11.84% would need a dated restatement rather than a footnote.

Verification: `doclinks`, `docstatus`, `citation` and `verdict` pass locally.

Refs #597

Human NPCs, the dead and player-controlled animals don't count. Ecology `find_site` skips crowded sites, allowing for the largest herd. Every mating (deer, cattle, pigs, boar, goats, sheep, bison, wolves and bears) is cancelled in a crowd, on top of each species' own limit of 5 of its kind.

body:
## Summary

**Payment settings** on **Payments** › **Payment methods** now holds every payment provider the tenant has, on the RPCs #5516 added: a card per provider with its status, what it sells, its credentials, its webhook URL, **Save**, and **Remove**, and **Add a provider** for the ones it does not hold yet. Adding one leaves the others as they are, so the warning that switching deletes the other provider's credentials is gone. A server of the previous release answers `ListTenantPaymentProviders` with `unimplemented`, and the page then shows the single-provider form as before.

![Payment settings holding Stripe and PAY.JP: a card for each with the Ready status, what it sells, Remove, Currency, Enable payments, its credentials, its webhook URL, and Save.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b5d908e4-71a3-4008-a7d0-c9d009c7fd7b)

The storefront still sends every checkout without a provider until #5518 lets the reader choose, and the server refuses such a checkout while more than one provider is ready. Testing therefore goes one provider at a time, with **Enable payments** off on the others, which is what **Testing before going live** now says.

## Changes

- `TenantPaymentProviderList` replaces the single form when the server answers the new list. Each card says **Ready**, **Incomplete**, **Disabled**, or **Removed**, and what the provider sells: episodes, volumes, coins, and tips, plus subscription plans on the first ready provider that takes recurring payments, which is how the server picks the plan provider.
- **Currency** on a card or in the add form offers only the currencies that provider and every other provider the tenant has not removed charge in, or only the locked one; a provider that can charge in none of them says why instead.
- **Remove** asks for confirmation and posts from a form of its own, so no typed credential is sent with it. A removed provider stays as **Removed** with **Add back** and **Delete**; **Delete** says when the server keeps it because it is still needed. Additions and removals report in a toast, since they change the cards beside the form.
- `addTenantPaymentProviderAction`, `saveTenantPaymentProviderAction`, and `removeTenantPaymentProviderAction` share the validation of the existing save, clear the payment settings tag, and clear the site tag the currency is read from.
- The credential fields, the currency, the enable switch, and the webhook URL move to `payment-provider-fields.tsx`, which the single-provider form uses too.
- `@publira/api-client/admin/payment` exports the payment service's messages, so the mapper `Pick`s the list response rather than restating it, and `TenantPaymentProviderSettings` joins `admin/types`.
- Strings in every `locales/*.json`.
- **Choosing a payment provider** in `docs/en/4-console/4-selling-episodes.md` describes the cards, the shared currency, and what each provider sells, and a new **Removing a provider** section covers removal, adding back, and deletion. **Subscription plans** no longer says choosing PAY.JP deletes the Stripe credentials. Both pages are brought in line in every translation.
- New `selling-episodes-providers.png` shot of a tenant holding both providers, taken on the analytics tenant the documentation setup already holds so that no shot changes the tenant counts the Platform Console's dashboard shot shows. The Stripe and PAY.JP setup shots are regenerated for the add form, and the selling page's shots below **Payment settings** are taken again, since the section above them changed height.
- The E2E helpers that set up Stripe use **Add provider**, and `admin.payment-settings.spec.ts` adds PAY.JP beside Stripe, removes it, adds it back, and turns it off, checking `tenant_payment_providers` each time.

## Upgrade notes

None.

## How to Test

- `pnpm preflight`
- `pnpm build --filter @publira/web-admin`
- `task e2e:test -- tests/admin.payment-settings.spec.ts tests/admin.purchases.spec.ts tests/admin.subscription-plans.spec.ts tests/storefront.checkout.spec.ts tests/storefront.subscriptions.spec.ts tests/admin.coin-settings.spec.ts tests/storefront.coins.spec.ts --no-deps` against a freshly seeded E2E stack: 34 passed.
- `task e2e:test -- --project=docs-screenshots-setup --no-deps`, then `task e2e:test -- tests/admin.selling.docs-screenshots.spec.ts tests/platform.tenants.docs-screenshots.spec.ts --project=docs-screenshots --no-deps --update-snapshots -g "providers a tenant holds|dashboard's tenant counts|selling episodes"` regenerated the selling shots and left the dashboard counts as committed, and `tests/storefront.tips.docs-screenshots.spec.ts`, which uses the shared Stripe helper, matched its images.
- On a local stack, Stripe and then PAY.JP were added from the console, PAY.JP was removed, kept on **Delete**, and added back.
- The rest of the E2E suite is left to CI.

## Checklist

- [x] I used a Conventional Commits style PR title.
- [x] I tested my changes locally.
- [x] I updated docs if needed.

Fixes #5517

## Ce que ça fait

Les **tickets par coin de cuisine** (ADR 0100 §9), **sans impression** : il n'existe ni commande du site ni imprimante choisie (ADR 0099 §5).

- `lib/menu-options/tickets.ts` (pur, testé) : un ticket « CUISINE » avec la somme, ou un ticket par coin sans prix (« TICKET 1/3 · PIZZA ») et un ticket « CAISSE · TOUT » en option. Prénom en très grand sur chaque ticket, retrait en entier (« SANS SALADE », jamais « SANS » seul), supplément « Oui » écrit « + FRITES ». Un plat sans coin va au ticket « CUISINE » : jamais perdu, même au-delà de 8 coins.
- `menu_items.kitchen_zone` (coin proposé d'après la famille du plat, modifiable) : `zones-save.ts` + route `app/api/admin/menu/options/zones` (le serveur nettoie, vérifie l'appartenance des plats, dit clairement si la migration manque).
- `components/admin/menu-options/KitchenTickets.tsx` : écran « Ce que le cuisinier reçoit », exemple bâti sur les vrais plats et les vrais choix du restaurateur.
- Migration `docs/migrations/20261113-2300-menu-item-kitchen-zone.sql` ; ADR 0100 §9, CONTEXT.md (« Coin de cuisine »), CLAUDE.md.

## Bouclier (ADR 0065)

Scène observée : maquette v7 validée (étape « Ce que le cuisinier reçoit », ticket avec prénom en grand) ; écran vérifié dans le navigateur avec des réponses simulées (coins, aperçu, erreur d'écriture), 0 px de débordement à 390 / 768 / 1440. Le défaut « + OUI » vu à l'aperçu est corrigé et testé. **Rien n'a été imprimé ni essayé sur de vraies données.**
Trace laissée : table `menu_zone_setups` (propositions de coin gardées, changées, vidées) et requête 9 de `suivi-options-menu.sql`. Seuil : moins de 2/3 des propositions gardées, la table famille → coin (`ZONE_OF`) est à revoir. Échecs visibles à l'écran (« Détail pour l'équipe »).
Échos suivis : ADR 0100 (§9, « restent ouverts »), CONTEXT.md, CLAUDE.md, mesures. Le choix « un ticket par coin ou un seul » n'est pas enregistré : il le sera avec la commande du site. Jeu de caractères des imprimantes thermiques (accents, « œ ») à tester sur le matériel choisi. Aucun écran membre ni site touché.

## À faire après fusion

Appliquer **à la main** dans Supabase `20261113-2300-menu-item-kitchen-zone.sql` (idempotente). Sans elle, l'écran s'ouvre mais l'enregistrement répond « pas encore activés » et n'écrit rien.

## Vérifié

`tsc --noEmit` ; `npm test` 1722 / 1722 ; `check:naming` ; rendu 390 / 768 / 1440.

author: mbkkt
body:
The open `[post-merge]` and bug-hunt issues, triaged against main at 008723f24: this fixes the crashes, restart failures, transaction races and wrong results among them. PostgreSQL-compatibility gaps and features stay open; the items that need a decision are listed at the end.

**Crashes and internal errors.** A GROUP BY whose key holds an ARRAY killed serened when an aggregate failed while partial results were merged (#2162): `RowOperations::CombineStates` shifts the row-location vectors in place, and the cleanup destroyed the states through the shifted vector; they are shifted back when a combine throws. A checkpoint crashed on a merged in-memory search piece that filled a row group (#2164): that piece is a written segment and is read through its column file like any other. EXECUTE of a statement prepared over a view or function that was dropped meanwhile crashed (#2170.4): it rebinds. `SELECT -x` under `integer_overflow = 'wrap'` raised "Monotonic arg annotation violated" over a column holding the type's minimum (#1651), see below.

**Restart failures.** After SET NOT NULL, another ALTER of the table, DROP NOT NULL and a checkpoint, serened aborted at every start (#2152.1): the catalog history folds the NOT NULL pair away while every ALTER logged its table's constraint oids by position. Constraints are now catalog parts with names and oids, an ALTER logs only the oids of the constraints it creates, and its replay matches them by name. A sequence handed out used values after a checkpoint and a restart (#2152.2): compaction kept the last logged value instead of the highest. A table whose CHECK or struct-field DEFAULT called a function of another database or one found through search_path could not be replayed (#2092.1, #2092.3): the function is qualified.

**Transactions and races.** Each of these committed both transactions; the later commit now fails with 40001, as a single session's statement would: a foreign key created while another session drops or renames its key (#2152.4), a sequence or view created in a schema another session drops (#2152.5), a trigger that writes to a table another session drops (#2153.4). The commit checks are the dependency index's: each new or changed catalog part records what it depends on, and COMMIT checks those against what committed after the transaction's snapshot. Two transactions that each inserted one primary key committed it twice when the first wrote again after its INSERT (#2152.3): the checked state now moves only when every key the transaction holds was checked against it. ALTER TABLE and CREATE INDEX no longer wait for transactions that wrote the table (#2152.6 hung when two of them waited for each other's writers); a writer whose rows predate the change fails at COMMIT. A role committed while another session published the role cache could be missing from it: the cache is labelled with the catalog version its snapshot holds. An immediate-mode BEGIN pinned another session's `read_duckdb` reader, so its ATTACH failed (#2167), and a catalog listing with and without `include_hidden` in one query could crash serened (#2166).

**Foreign keys at statement end.** Each INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE operator checked foreign keys when it finished, so a statement that wrote a child before its parent failed where PostgreSQL succeeds: `WITH c AS (INSERT INTO child ...) INSERT INTO parent ...`, and COPY FROM DATABASE, whose INSERTs run concurrently and made `copy_database_foreign_keys.test` flaky in CI. Unique keys are still checked when the operator finishes; reference keys and the removed keys another table still references are checked once the statement's operators finished (a new `Transaction::OnStatementEnd` in the fork). The checks do the same work as before, at the end of the statement instead of the operator.

**Wrong results.**
- ON CONFLICT took another session's uncommitted unique index as an arbiter (#2152.7), and a unique index on `(team, lower(email))` as unique on `team` (#2152.8).
- EXECUTE reused a plan checked for another role after SET ROLE (#1677) or resolved under another search_path (#1680); a plan records both and is planned again when either differs.
- An UPDATE of a table with a `REFERENCING OLD TABLE` trigger failed an assertion (#1822).
- A table accepted a constraint name it already had (#2084.2); RENAME COLUMN of a referenced column left the foreign keys naming the old one (#2153.2, part of #1440); INTERVAL keys took `1 day` and `24 hours` for different values (#2153.1); a key on a NOCASE, NOACCENT or ICU-collated column took `a` and `A` for different values (#2153.10); OWNED BY NONE left a serial sequence owned (#2153.3); SET SCHEMA after ALTER TYPE of a serial column moved its sequence twice (#2153.7).
- COPY FROM DATABASE copied a referencing table before its parent (#2153.8), and dropped object owners and sequence ownership (#1732).
- NOT over a `::min_match` or `::boost` group returned rows whose UNIQUE column, read only through its key, is NULL (#2153.5): the index has no NULL rows for such a column, so the negated group is not claimed, as a negated key lookup already was not.
- A multi-statement Query analyzed each statement before the earlier ones ran, so a later statement could not see a table an earlier one created (#1695).
- A regex run followed by single characters counted bytes instead of characters (#2132, serenedb/re2#16); approx_quantile turned a DECIMAL input into an integer and left the range of all-negative inputs (#2135).
- `integer_overflow = 'wrap'` held only in the arithmetic kernels while the optimizer solved comparisons and split `SUM(x + C)` as if integer arithmetic could not wrap, and EXECUTE ran a plan made under the other mode (#1650, #1651, #1654). The mode is now part of how integer `+ - *` and unary minus are bound: under wrap they cannot error and claim no monotonicity, so every rewrite that needs exact arithmetic skips them, and EXECUTE rebinds after the mode changes.
- `pg_replication_origin` listed the origins as last committed instead of as the transaction sees them (#2085).
- EXECUTE failed when a parameter of an index condition was NULL (#1683): a strict predicate over a NULL value is NULL at EXECUTE, as the binder makes it for a literal, and matches no row.
- A distance selected without a limit or radius dropped the rows whose vector is NULL (#1679); a distance written before BM25 or ts_offsets took the scan's score from them (#2070).
- `LIMIT (SELECT 2.5)` returned a row less than `LIMIT 2.5`, and a bigint-maximum LIMIT from a subquery or parameter failed (#2116.1, #2116.3).
- A statement with a data-modifying CTE answered as the CTE: `WITH c AS (INSERT ... RETURNING x) INSERT INTO t ...` sent the outer INSERT's count as a row, and `WITH c AS (INSERT ...) SELECT 42` sent no row.
- `CREATE DATABASE "Repro_Db"` failed while `repro_db` existed (#1657): attached database names are case-sensitive, as in PostgreSQL.
- ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING dropped one of two rows with a NULL unique key and a row that conflicted only with another proposed row that was itself skipped, and DO UPDATE and INSERT OR REPLACE silently kept one of two rows proposing a key (#2153.9): the binder made every upsert a MERGE INTO over DISTINCT ON the proposed rows, which also joined the whole table. DO NOTHING and full-row INSERT OR REPLACE are now an INSERT that decides each row in order against the rows the transaction sees, through the key term dictionaries the unique check reads, and against the keys the statement proposed before it; RETURNING, the row count and foreign keys see only the inserted rows, and a key proposed twice under REPLACE or DO UPDATE fails with 21000 as in PostgreSQL. DO UPDATE and partial REPLACE stay a MERGE INTO without DISTINCT ON. Without a conflict target every unique key arbitrates, unique expression indexes included, and DO NOTHING on a table without a unique key inserts every row. The plain INSERT keeps its operator. Each key is probed once (the statement-end

author: amir-faghihi
body:
Developer API keys require a bounded creation window when listing invoices or invoice items, but the OpenAPI references omit the required query parameters. This leaves integrators receiving HTTP 400 without enough information to construct a valid request.

Document `created__gte` and `created__lt`, timezone requirements, inclusive start and exclusive end, and a positive window of at most 31 days. Add UTC request examples, guidance for fetching longer history, and HTTP 400 descriptions to the general, A440, and Bullbustin references.

## How to verify

1. Open each reference at `/openapi/`, `/a440/`, and `/bullbustin/`. Expand the organization invoice and invoice item list operations. Confirm both creation parameters appear as required with timestamp examples.
2. Confirm each operation explains the timezone requirement, the 31 day maximum, and the inclusive start and exclusive end.
3. Check the example request uses both parameters with UTC timestamps spanning one day, and that the HTTP 400 description explains invalid or missing windows.

body:
## What changes

**Dashboard theme**
- Neutral greys with white as the highlight replace the amber accent and the zinc tint; one typeface throughout.
- Cards are a shared flat surface (`.dashboard-card`): no outlines or nested panels, a small label over a bold figure. Applied to Files, Storage, Users and the Repositories pages.
- Sidebar: larger items, a filled pill for the active section, grouped labels, and a profile row with sign-out at the bottom. The top-right avatar now shows only below `lg`, where the sidebar is hidden.
- The rule under the page title is removed.

**Storage page**
- Recomposed as three stat cards, a wide card with the usage bar, then bucket and details cards.
- The pixel bars keep their color: they read the accent preference through `--dashboard-accent`, captured before the dashboard turns the highlight white.

**File list**
- Selecting an entry no longer inserts a row above the list. The selection actions take the place of the column labels inside the header row, so nothing shifts. On narrow screens the actions show icons only.

**Ghost mascot**
- `GhostMascot` replaces the empty-folder illustration, and `GhostLoader` / the flying ghost replace the spinners for upload preparation and the upload progress panel. It is an original drawing, not the MetalForge asset it was inspired by.

**Login page**
- `LedMatrixBackground`: a full-screen wall of red-orange cells with drifting streaks and the Aeralyth mark lit in the cells. It renders one pixel per cell on three small canvases that CSS scales and masks into cells, runs at about 14 frames per second, pauses when the tab is hidden, and is static under reduced motion.
- `LoginCard`: dark glass framed by a ring of cells with two travelling lights, a pointer glow, and staggered entry.
- The old gradient backdrop, its noise image and the two feature lines are removed. "Welcome back" (used by the image smoke test) is unchanged.

**Dependencies** (separate commit)
- Lockfile updated within the declared ranges (Next.js 16.4.6, Biome 2.6.7, Vitest 5.1.0, Tailwind 4.3.5, @hpke/core 1.10.1 and others).
- The @hpke/core update changes the vault worker bundle; its archive and manifest are committed with it. `biome.json` moves to the 2.6.7 schema.

## Verification

- Locally: `npm run lint`, `tsc --noEmit`, the full Vitest suite (740 tests) and `npm run worker:verify-release` pass.
- Every dashboard page and the login page were viewed in `next dev` against a stand-in API with invented data, at desktop and phone widths. The upload indicators were viewed in a standalone preview of the real components, since the stand-in API cannot run an upload.
- Not run locally: production build, backend and database suites. This PR is merged without waiting for CI at the owner's request; the `master` CI run gates the Railway deploy.

## Not included

- The invite page and the public share-link page keep their previous look.
- Dialogs and menus pick up the new colors but were not individually reviewed.

author: scylark
body:
Adds `/rider-panel/method/`, a walk-through of how the Rider Panel works as a process. It doesn't report any study's results.

## What it covers
- **The design principle:** code decides what each agent can come across, and the agent decides what to do about it.
- **The structure:** a nine-layer map that links to each section, then a funnel showing what decides each narrowing step.
- **Population and agents:**
  - the synthetic population and its public data sources
  - the in-market cohort, an example agent record and how life stories are written
- **The season:** weather, calendar and market.
- **Channels and exposure:**
  - how shortlists are built
  - each route and what sets its reach
  - the reach cap and the fixed random draws shared across runs
  - the brief each agent gets, with its fixed output format
- **Running a study:** monthly decisions, then the run types, from baseline to price, channel, earned media, AI visibility, rerun and swap.
- **Validation:** checks set before any results, ranges from re-sampling, and scaling to the real market.
- **Brand data:** a brand's own data can replace an assumption, calibrate the panel or validate it against a past launch. A table maps nine kinds of brand data to the layer each one improves.

## Kept out of search
- The robots tag reads `noindex, nofollow`. `Base.astro` gains a `nofollow` prop for this.
- The page is listed in `astro.config.mjs`, so the sitemap leaves it out.
- Nothing on the site links to it.

## Checks
- The build passes.
- On a 390px phone there's no sideways page scroll, and the tables scroll within their own width.
- The copy has no ', and' joins, no X, Y and Z lists and no em dashes.

## Summary
These changes follow from the audit of llms.txt, llms-full.txt, schema.org, breadcrumbs and orphan pages, which scored 82/100 on the live site.

  - every page's summary;

  - "UK Amazon prep partneri";
  - "Tilbury ~30 dakika" (measured ~20 min);
  - "Amazon … Dartford: yakın erişim" (not verified).
- **New check:** `npm run seo:llms` (`scripts/audit-llms.py`) fails if a sitemap URL is missing from either file, if the date is older than 45 days, or if a banned claim appears.

### Organization / LocalBusiness
