author: peter-mega
body:
Atlas task **1772accd-f5ea-4d12-a9ad-f55083114084** · applies WEB Director ruling comment **87a71011-723e-5c57-9bbe-ba7dbc933f2d** (bounded scope).

## What changed
- **Budget removed** (acab823): no `estimatedBudget` state, label, validation, focus, error, options, lead key or event metadata. ISO / CMMI / Not sure yet each send `qualified: true`; no budget disqualification reason.
- **Intro, both forms:** "Tell us your certification goal." No other copy changed.
- **Canonical field rules:** new `src/lib/fields.ts`, **byte-identical** to `Landing-Pages-Websites/lp-starter@a9beaa6` `src/lib/fields.ts` (blob `5a23e486`, sha256 `d25400ba6ee08423f81f50a3dda98d6bd8d110952edfd99f0618799aeeedfe89`). FormCard and `useMegaLeadForm` both import it. This removes the forked email regex, the NANP regex and the phone formatter that truncated input to the first 10 digits.
- **§4c:** names are trimmed, required and limited to 200 characters. The certification must exactly match a declared option. Validation and focus cover every field in DOM order, and `noValidate` stays on with the form's own inline errors.
- **§4 attributes:** email gets `inputMode`, the canonical `pattern`, `maxLength=254`, `spellCheck`, `autoCapitalize` and `title`. Phone gets `tel-national`, the canonical `pattern` and `title`, and no `maxLength`.
- **§6:** Enter is handled on keydown (textarea, select, button, link and IME composition are excluded), and an `onSubmit` backstop calls `preventDefault`. Both go through the same validator. The submit button is still a `type="button"` direct send, and there is no `requestSubmit`.
- **§7:** `inFlightRef` stays set after a confirmed lead. The thank-you is committed before tracking runs, and each MegaTag and dataLayer call is isolated, so a tracker exception can't turn an accepted lead into a failure or allow a duplicate POST.
- **Hook (narrow):** imports the shared functions, validates a nonblank phone *before* reducing it to 10 digits, and adds the canonical email check and domain-only lowercasing. It is not rewritten.

## Optional-phone exception (task-specific, per ruling)
Phone stays **optional** in both forms (`aria-required="false"`, no `required`). Only a genuinely blank phone skips validation. A nonblank invalid value fails in the UI and in the hook and is never sent as `""`. firstName, lastName, email and certificationSought stay required. This is not a fleet-default change.

## Unchanged
Endpoint, customer/site/source IDs, attribution, form identifiers, event names (`form_submit`, `qualified_lead`), event payload keys (minus budget), MegaTag/GTM/Ads/CTM config, routing, thank-you copy, CSS and layout (apart from removing the field), dependencies and lockfile.

## Evidence (full set in `tasks/1772accd-commandtec/`)
- `npm run build` exit 0. LP Lint v2: ALL CHECKS PASSED.
- Byte preservation: 47 of the 48 protected files are sha256-identical. The one mismatch is `useMegaLeadForm.ts`, which the ruling put in scope.
- Fixture `run-fixture-r2.cjs`: **367/367** on this branch; 140/367 on round-1 HEAD.
  - Coverage: both forms × 3 certifications × blank / `+1 (555) 555-0100` / `5555550100`.
  - Rejections: empty or undeclared cert, empty or 201-char names, the full email matrix (length limits, U+212A), and the full phone matrix (N11 in area and exchange, national and +1; foreign, overlong, letters, extensions, fictional numbers).
  - Hook guard checks.
  - Failure responses, each with 1 POST, 0 events and a working retry: HTTP 400/500, `ok:false`, missing `ok`, `null`, `ok:"true"`, invalid JSON, network error.
  - Delayed response with 5 clicks and 5 Enters gives 1 POST. A same-tick double click gives 1 POST.
  - MegaTag or dataLayer throwing still ends in success with no duplicate POST.
  - Enter and backstop boundaries.
- **The fixture is transport-isolated** (fake fetch, MegaTag and dataLayer). It does **not** prove live backend persistence or third-party delivery.
- Authored destinations per confirmed lead: MegaTag `form_submit` ×1 + `qualified_lead` ×1, and dataLayer `form_submit` ×1 + `qualified_lead` ×1.
- Static DOM/a11y on the built HTML is clean. **Browser screenshots unavailable (bootstrap gap):** the controller will capture native 390×844 and desktop evidence and confirm real accepted-lead persistence. The estimated hero submit bottom at 390×844 is about 770px (828 before the field removal).

## Follow-ups (out of scope)
- `src/app/privacy-policy/page.tsx:127` still lists "Estimated budget" (another route; copy is frozen).
- Safari can send an IME-confirm Enter with `keyCode 229`. The canonical §6 boundary checks only `isComposing`, so this is noted upstream rather than forked.

## Round 3: optional-phone boundary (`9be0a84`)
Completes director ruling 87a71011-723e-5c57-9bbe-ba7dbc933f2d: a genuinely blank phone is accepted, but nonblank invalid input must never become an empty, accepted phone.

**Defect:** canonical `formatPhone("()" | "---" | "tel:")` returns `""`, and `isValidPhone` of the raw value is false. The phone `onChange` stored `formatPhone(raw)`, so that input became blank and skipped the optional-phone check. Separately, the hook rejected a whitespace-only phone even though the UI treats it as blank.

**Fix (2 files, +25/−9):**
- `src/components/FormCard.tsx`: `displayPhone` adapter at the phone `onChange` only. When canonical formatting would erase nonblank input, the raw text is kept. Whitespace-only still collapses to blank.
- `src/hooks/useMegaLeadForm.ts`: `normalizeOptionalPhone` uses the same trim-based blank check as the UI. A blank phone is sent as `""`. Any other value is validated before it is reduced to digits, as before.
- `src/lib/fields.ts` **unchanged**: sha256 `d25400ba6ee08423f81f50a3dda98d6bd8d110952edfd99f0618799aeeedfe89`, byte-identical to the lp-starter pin. It reuses `formatPhone`, `isValidPhone` and `phoneDigits` with no validator fork.

**Tests:** transport-isolated fixture with the real FormCard, hook and fields code, and fake fetch, MegaTag and dataLayer. It is not live persistence and sends no real leads.
- New R3 suite `run-fixture-r3.cjs`: **410/446 before the fix** (36 failures, all from this defect), **446/446 after**.
- The R3 suite is 366 unchanged R2 assertions plus 80 new ones, covering both forms and the hook:
  - 14 punctuation-only inputs (`()`, `---`, `tel:`, `(`, `( ) -`, …). Each stays visible, fails validation, sends 0 POSTs and 0 events, and focuses phone.
  - Blank and whitespace-only phones, which are accepted with `phone: ""` sent.
  - A phone typed character by character starting with `(`, and a phone backspaced to empty.
- The 367th R2 assertion is replaced, not carried over: R2 expected the hook to reject `"   "`, and the new cases now require it to accept it and send `""`. The unmodified R2 suite therefore scores 366/367, and that case is its only failure.
- All other R2 behaviour still passes: valid `+1` display and digits, failed response with no conversion, Enter key, and rapid-click.
- Next build, LP lint v2 and `tsc --noEmit` all pass.

**Reviews:**
- Simplify: one readability edit, early returns in `displayPhone`.
  - Skipped consolidating the blank-or-valid rule shared by `validateField`, `buildLead` and the hook, because those are outside the bounded scope.
- Code review: two findings, both not adopted.
  - Not adopted: making a deletion blank the field. With that rule, pasting `()` over an existing number, or typing `-` over a selected digit, would silently become blank, which the ruling forbids. **Known trade-off:** backspacing `(5` leaves `(` visible with the phone error until it is deleted too. It is never silently accepted.
  - Not adopted: rejecting non-string `formData.phone`. This is not a regression: the old code also ran `String()` on any truthy value, and FormCard always sends a string.

**Upstream follow-ups for lp-starter (not this PR):**
- `formatPhone` should return the input unchanged when it contains no digits but is not blank, which is what its

author: clintongormley
body:
## What this does

`scripts/dashboard-browser-purity.test.ts` is a check that runs in CI. It makes sure the code the admin dashboard sends to the browser never pulls in server-only libraries (the database layer, `drizzle-orm`, `hono`, Node built-ins). It only checks the files on its list, and the files those reach.

Five venue-service files that the dashboard loads in the browser were not on the list. So if someone added a server-only import to one of them, the check would catch it only indirectly, through another listed file, or not at all. This change adds all five:

- `src/dashboard/season-tint.ts` and `src/dashboard/live-queries.ts`. These two were the backlog entry this closes.
- `src/routing.ts`, which `apps/dashboard/src/widgets/folder-made-at.ts` imports.
- `src/hours-occurrences.ts`, which `apps/dashboard/src/widgets/attendance-proposal-dialog.ts` imports.
- `src/hours-types.ts`, which `packages/staffing/src/dashboard/staffing-month.ts` imports.

The pre-merge review found the last three. The comment at the top of the check now names them, and says which venue-service entry is still left off (see the comment below). The check's case count goes from 250 to 282, all passing.

The backlog entry, in `docs/backlog/ci.md`, and its index line in `docs/backlog.md` are deleted.

## How it was checked

For each file, I added a forbidden import (`import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";`) to the top of it for a moment and ran the check with `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/dashboard-browser-purity.test.ts`:

| File with the planted import | Check before this change | Check after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `season-tint.ts` + `live-queries.ts` | 2 failed, both reaching `season-tint.ts` indirectly; nothing caught `live-queries.ts` | 6 failed, including `live-queries.ts` itself |
| `routing.ts` + `hours-occurrences.ts` | 2 failed, both reaching `hours-occurrences.ts` indirectly; nothing caught `routing.ts` | 6 failed, including each file itself |
| `hours-types.ts` | 7 failed, all indirect | 9 failed, adding the file itself |
| none (all files restored) | — | `Tests  282 passed (282)` |

## Review

The light path: this is a CI check with no product code, so there was no simplify reviewer. A Codex run-it reviewer reran every count in the commit message and found `routing.ts` unlisted. A convention reviewer asked for the left-off entry to be written down in the check itself. A second reader, of the fixes, found `hours-types.ts`.

Nobody approved this work in advance. The campaign watcher queued it from the backlog on 2026-11-13.

body:
Partial build of `openspec/changes/records-change-held-for-approval`: task 1.1 (the declaration).

## Done
- **1.1** `gate.change` in the `x-openregister-approval-chains` dialect: `gate: {change: {properties, on, exempt}}`. New `Service/Task/ChangeGateDeclaration` reads it (empty `properties` gates any change; absent `on` gates `update` only; `on` limited to `create`/`update`; `exempt` group list). `ApprovalChainAnnotationInstaller::compile()` carries it onto the template as `changeGate`. A malformed gate, or an entry that gates both a transition and a change, does not compile (logged), so it fails closed like any other misconfigured chain. Chains without `gate.change` compile exactly as before (golden test unchanged). Row added to `scripts/component-map.csv`.

## Left, and why
- **2.1–2.4, 3.1–3.2** (holding the write as a `pending-<n>` draft, 202/409 answers, gated create, task sequence and apply/discard on decision): these need draft promotion from `records-draft-versions` (its tasks 2.x and 3.1 are not built yet; only `DraftService` create/update/list/discard exists). Holding a write with nothing that can apply it later would lose approved changes, so this waits for that dependency.
- **4.1** UI panel and e2e test, **4.2** buildiq issue, **4.3** docs: depend on the above; e2e/browser work is not done in this pass.

## Tests
- `tests/Unit/Service/Task/ChangeGateDeclarationTest.php` (5 tests): absent, full, defaults, exact matching of properties/operations/exempt groups, 9 malformed shapes.
- `tests/Unit/Service/ApprovalChainChangeGateCompileTest.php` (4 tests): gate compiled onto the template field for field, transition+change refused, malformed refused, transition-only chain unchanged.
- Each new test file was seen to fail against a broken subject line.

## Suite before/after
The full unit suite needs a Nextcloud server checkout, which was not available here, so tests ran with a minimal bootstrap (vendor autoload + OCP from `nextcloud/ocp`). With vs without this change:
- ApprovalChain compile golden, gate listener, advance listener and advance guards tests: all pass, both.
- `tests/Unit/Architecture`: 2364 tests OK, both.
- `tests/Unit/Service/Task`: 754 → 759 tests, the same 40 errors before and after (bootstrap-related), no new failures.
- phpcs clean on the new file (the installer keeps its one existing class-level warning); phpstan: no errors on both changed files.

How it was proved: `pnpm check` (typecheck, 324 tests, build), then the real app in `pnpm dev:demo` and `pnpm dev:fake` (throwaway `MESH_UI_USER_DATA_DIR` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `--password-store=basic`) driven over the DevTools protocol for screenshots, the Day / Week toggle, scenario switches and Retry.

## Done when

- **Matches the mockup in `pnpm dev:demo` and `pnpm dev:fake` in light and dark.** Screenshots below (Gruvbox Hard). Demo shots at 1480 px wide to compare with the mockup; the Week shot is at the default 1200 px window, where rows wrap their detail line instead of truncating.
- **Loading, empty and error states.** Empty: `demo.scenario.set {"scenario":"empty_network"}` (usage shows `-` and "No activity in this window.", Top devices and the heatmap the same sentence, Profiles "No profiles yet..." with a disabled Add a profile, eeros with flat sparklines). Offline: `network_offline` (Offline, "Last seen 12 min ago", the "Maple Street is not reporting..." note with Troubleshoot, gauges muted) and `eero_offline` (Weak link, "Garage is offline", Garage row Offline). Loading and error: the demo backend answers instantly and `demo.scenario.set` has no slow or failing scenario, so these come from `pnpm dev:fake` against a scratch copy of the fake eero server with its scenario switches: requests to `data_usage`, `profiles` and `app_events` answering 500. While the client retried, the page showed the loading layout (hero filled, `-` figures, unlabelled gridlines, blank rows at normal height, an empty heatmap); after that each section showed its own note ("Couldn't load profiles. eero answered 500 ...") with Retry while the hero and eeros kept working. Clearing the switch and pressing Retry brought every section back.

## Screenshots (demo and fake eero server, invented data)

Demo, dark: ![demo dark](https://github.com/pkkid/mesh-ui/blob/assets/M1.14-screenshots/01-demo-dark.png?raw=true)

Demo, light: ![demo light](https://github.com/pkkid/mesh-ui/blob/assets/M1.14-screenshots/02-demo-light.png?raw=true)

Week range, light, default 1200 px window: ![week](https://github.com/pkkid/mesh-ui/blob/assets/M1.14-screenshots/03-week.png?raw=true)

`eero_offline`, dark: ![eero offline](https://github.com/pkkid/mesh-ui/blob/assets/M1.14-screenshots/04-demo-eero-offline-dark.png?raw=true)

`network_offline`, dark: ![offline dark](https://github.com/pkkid/mesh-ui/blob/assets/M1.14-screenshots/05-demo-offline-dark.png?raw=true)

`network_offline`, light: ![offline light](https://github.com/pkkid/mesh-ui/blob/assets/M1.14-screenshots/06-demo-offline-light.png?raw=true)

`empty_network`, dark: ![empty](https://github.com/pkkid/mesh-ui/blob/assets/M1.14-screenshots/07-demo-empty-dark.png?raw=true)

Fake server, dark: ![fake dark](https://github.com/pkkid/mesh-ui/blob/assets/M1.14-screenshots/09-fake-dark.png?raw=true)

Fake server, light: ![fake light](https://github.com/pkkid/mesh-ui/blob/assets/M1.14-screenshots/10-fake-light.png?raw=true)

Loading (fake server, uncached network while queries are in flight): ![loading](https://github.com/pkkid/mesh-ui/blob/assets/M1.14-screenshots/11-fake-loading-dark.png?raw=true)

Errors (fake server answering 500): ![errors](https://github.com/pkkid/mesh-ui/blob/assets/M1.14-screenshots/12-fake-error-dark.png?raw=true)

## Decisions

- **Shared pieces live in `OverviewView.tsx`** (row list, header link, per-section error note with Retry, `ComingSoonButton`, `useNow`), since the story's file list has no extra file. Disabled buttons sit in a `span` with the tooltip because disabled buttons take no pointer events.
- **Status and cause** come from `network.health`: an offline eero or a `weakLink` eero turns the hero to Weak link with "Garage has a weak link" / "Garage is offline" linking to eeros; a network offline shows Offline and "Last seen ...".
- **Gauges.** One `speedtest.history` call (default limit) gives the latest result and, when no plan speed is set, the gauge max (best result in history rounded up to 100 Mbps), plus a small "Set your plan" link to Internet. The latest result falls back to `internet.get` `lastSpeedTest`.
- **Usage.** Hero, totals, busiest bucket and "so far today" are the `usage.get` fields; the renderer only formats them. Zero bytes in the window reads as missing (`-`), matching the chart's empty sentence. Week says "busiest day Wednesday". The By eero share bar and the eero sparklines use the same `usage.get {scope: "eero", range: "day"}` query, so on Day it is fetched once. Colours are `entityColors` by eero id, so the bar, legend and sparklines agree.
- **Heatmap.** `usage.get {scope: "network", range: "week", cadence: "hourly"}` gives hourly points; the renderer places each in its weekday row and hour column in the network time zone (layout only) and the Heatmap component scales to the peak. The tooltip reads "Mon 20:00" with the share of the busiest hour. The page doc says "core normalises to 0..1"; the command does not, and the chart kit's Heatmap already scales, so no core change was needed.
- **Profiles.** Today's usage per profile is `usage.get {scope: "profile", range: "day"}` `todaySoFar`. A scheduled profile shows its next-change schedule ("Homework 4:00 PM to 6:00 PM"). A paused profile shows "3 devices paused": the model has no pause time, so the mockup's "Paused 25 min ago" is not possible yet.
- **Top devices** is `usage.breakdown {range: "day", by: "device"}`, first five with any usage; icons come from the device type in `device.list`, which also gives "31 online now". The device icon map lives in `TopDevices.tsx`.
- **Clock and date labels** use `Intl.DateTimeFormat` in the network time zone; `format.ts` has no clock formatter yet.
- **Bridge mode** hides Profiles, Top devices and Pause a profile, adds a note at the top, and the last row becomes eeros, busy heatmap, activity.
- **Layout breakpoints.** Two and three columns from `lg`; eero sparklines narrow below `xl` so names fit in the default 1200 px window.

## Self-review

The delegated Sol review could not start (`parent_not_active`: this worker session cannot delegate), so I did a careful self-review. Self-testing caught and fixed a duplicate React key in the share bar while `eero.list` was still loading, and a `0 B` hero on an empty network (now `-`); the review pass hoisted per-point date formatters.

## Open

- `demo.scenario.set` has no slow or failing scenario, so loading and error states can only be shown in fake mode. A `slow` and an `errors` demo scenario (in `src/core/demo/scenario.ts`) would make them reachable in demo; worth a line at M1.R.
- A shared network-time-zone clock formatter in `src/core/format.ts` would replace the `Intl` calls here and on later pages.
- Device type icons will likely be needed again by M1.15 Devices; a shared map would avoid two copies.
- `docs/ux/pages/overview.md` says the heatmap is normalised in core and lists "Paused 25 min ago"; both differ from the commands as built (see Decisions).

body:
**Changement de structure, pas un réglage : à fusionner seulement avec l'accord du concepteur.**

## Ce qui change
- **Fournisseur de graines** (`src/jeu/graines.ts`) : toutes les graines viennent d'un seul endroit. En local, mêmes valeurs qu'avant (partie au hasard, match regardé 1, 2, 3…, autres matchs 1000 + 7 × journée + camp).
- **Arbitre de match** (`src/match/arbitre.ts`, `arbitreLocal.ts`) : il calcule chaque mi-temps et en produit le **film** (`src/match/film.ts`, format documenté en tête du fichier, passage en JSON). La version locale appelle le moteur exactement comme l'ancien écran ; elle calcule par petits morceaux en arrière-plan (11 images prêtes en 1,7 ms au coup d'envoi), donc pas de gel.
- **Écran du match** : il lit le film image par image (pause, vitesse, vues inchangées) au lieu de faire avancer le moteur. À la mi-temps, il envoie les choix du joueur à l'arbitre, qui repart de l'état exact de la fin de la 1re mi-temps.
- **Décision du concepteur** : les listes de tactique et les interrupteurs « Tactiques » / « Styles » se changent avant le coup d'envoi et à la mi-temps seulement (grisés pendant le jeu).

## Ce qui ne change pas
Moteur (`src/sim/`) et données (`src/data/*.json`) non touchés. Mêmes règles, réglages, écrans ; même graine = même match.

## Preuves
- `tests/empreintes.test.ts` : empreintes au bit près (SHA-256 de chaque pas) de 6 matchs complets (dont des changements à la mi-temps) et d'une partie entière (draft, mercatos, championnat), **enregistrées avant toute modification**. Identiques par trois chemins : moteur appelé comme l'ancien écran, arbitre local lu image par image, film passé « par le réseau » en morceaux JSON.
- `tests/arbitre.test.ts` : calcul par morceaux pendant la lecture, mi-temps demandée avant la fin du calcul, arrêt, format JSON.
- 161 tests verts, `bun run verifier` passe.
- Dans Chrome au format téléphone, même partie (hasard à graine fixe) sur l'ancienne page (×4) et la nouvelle (×3,5) : panneaux de mi-temps et de fin identiques, avec et sans choix à la mi-temps.

author: vojtechsimetka
body:
Stacked on #431. Kalkul's analogue of swarm-id's "keep the publish token away from dependency code" (snaha/swarm-id#989): there it is the npm token, here it is the token that pushes to `gh-pages`, which is what kalkul.app serves.

Before, `deploy-prod` and the PR preview ran `pnpm install` and `pnpm build` in a job holding `contents: write`, with the token left in the checkout's git config, so any dependency's install or build script could push to the repo.

- **`build`** job: read-only token, `persist-credentials: false`, installs, builds, uploads the build as an artifact.
- **`deploy`** job: holds `contents: write` (and `pull-requests: write` for the preview comment), runs no project or dependency code, only downloads the artifact and pushes it.
- Workflow-level permissions drop to `contents: read`; `check.yaml` gets the same and stops persisting its token.

The preview's deploy job still runs when a PR closes, where the build is skipped and the preview is removed.

**To check on this PR itself:** its own preview deploy is the test of the split preview workflow. The production workflow only runs on `main`, so its first run is the merge.

## Exact-head C2 protocol/journal and W2-B containment acceptance

body:
## 요약

#31 이후 공개 `/api/leads/capture` 는 이미 있는 이메일이면 `leads` 행을 바꾸지 않고, 다시 보낸 계산 결과를 `email_events`(`event_type = 'resubmitted'`)에만 남긴다. 앱 안에서 두 테이블을 읽는 화면이 없어 영업이 이 값을 볼 수 없었다(#31 Codex 리뷰 P2 후속).

리드마다 **가장 최근 재제출 1건**을 저장된 값과 나란히 보여주는 뷰 `public.lead_latest_resubmissions` 를 추가한다.

| 열 | 내용 |
|---|---|
| `lead_id`, `email`, `stored_name` | 리드 |
| `resubmitted_at`, `resubmission_count`, `event_id` | 최근 재제출 시각·횟수 |
| `submitted_*` | 다시 보낸 이름·출처·총자산·부채·순자산·예상세액·배우자·자녀 수 (검증되지 않은 공개 입력) |
| `stored_*` | 리드에 저장된 같은 값(비교용) |

## 보안

- `security_invoker = true` — 뷰 소유자 권한으로 RLS 를 우회하지 않는다.
- `anon`·`authenticated` 권한 회수(Supabase 기본 권한이 새 뷰에 주는 것까지), `service_role` 은 `SELECT` 만. 대시보드(postgres)에서 조회.
- `event_data` 는 공개 입력이라 JSON 타입이 숫자·불리언일 때만 꺼내고 나머지는 `NULL`. 이름·출처는 100/50자로 자른다. 잘못된 값 하나가 뷰 조회 전체를 깨지 않는다.

## 배치

- `supabase/migrations/20261114000000_…` — `supabase db push` 로 운영에 적용된다.
- `leads`·`email_events` 는 이 체인이 아니라 `lib/supabase/migrations/20250127_email_automation_schema.sql` 에서 만들어지므로, 두 테이블이 없는 새 DB 에서는 실패하지 않고 NOTICE 를 남기고 건너뛴다. 스키마 적용 후 다시 실행하면 된다(멱등).
- 검증 스크립트는 pgTAP 가 아니라서 `supabase test db` 가 집어 가지 않게 `lib/supabase/tests/` 에 둔다.

## 적용

머지 후 운영 DB(`syyklnwynskwoxvcghkf`)에 마이그레이션 적용 필요 — `supabase db push` 또는 SQL Editor 에서 파일 실행. (이 PR 작성 환경에서는 해당 프로젝트 접근 권한이 없어 운영 스키마를 직접 확인하지 못했다. 저장소 스키마 파일과 같다고 가정.)

## 테스트 (로컬 Postgres 16, Supabase 역할·기본 권한·auth 스텁 + 저장소의 실제 스키마)

- [x] 최신 재제출 선택·횟수, 저장값 병기, 잘못된 타입 → NULL, 재제출 없는 리드 제외 (`BEHAVIOUR_OK`)
- [x] `anon`·`authenticated`(관리자 이메일 클레임 포함) 조회 거부, `service_role` 조회 가능·쓰기 불가
- [x] 새 DB(테이블 없음)에서 오류 없이 건너뜀, 기존 DB 에 2회 적용 가능
- [x] 결함 주입 3종 — REVOKE 제거 / `security_invoker` 제거 / 숫자 타입 가드 제거 → 모두 테스트 실패 확인 후 원복
- [x] `codex review --commit` 4회 — 지적(체인 위치 ×2, pgTAP 경로) 반영 후 무결함

## 범위 밖

기존 `lead_funnel_metrics` 뷰가 `security_invoker` 없이 정의돼 있어(소유자 권한으로 실행) API 역할로 집계가 읽힐 수 있다. 별도 확인 필요.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> New read path over unvalidated public `event_data`, but access is restricted to service_role/dashboard; incorrect grants or missing `security_invoker` would expose lead PII.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a Supabase migration that creates **`public.lead_latest_resubmissions`**, so sales can see each lead’s **most recent** `resubmitted` `email_events` row next to the values stored on **`leads`** (after PR #31 stopped updating existing leads on repeat capture).
> 
> The view picks the latest resubmit per lead, includes resubmission count, and safely extracts **`event_data`** with JSON type checks (bad types become `NULL` instead of breaking queries). It uses **`security_invoker`**, revokes access from **`anon`** / **`authenticated`**, and grants **`SELECT`** only to **`service_role`**. The migration no-ops with a notice if **`leads`** / **`email_events`** are missing (separate schema chain).
> 
> A transactional **`lib/supabase/tests/lead_latest_resubmissions.test.sql`** script verifies aggregation, type coercion, and role-based access. The commit message file is updated to match this work.

author: bwiemz
body:
Reviews the fifteen research proposals in `docs/research/` against their own arithmetic, the literature as of November 2026, and the code that implements them. Adds an errata file beside each PDF, and fixes the implementation defects that could be verified and fixed safely. Everything else the review found is listed as open in the errata.

## Errata

Each of CCR, CEP, CESH, CFA, CFIE, CFTP, CGAC, CIDP, CKVQ, CPDT, CPKD, CSHA, CSS, WGGO and WRGA has `docs/research/<name>-errata.md` with five parts: proposal errors and what is true instead; what later work supersedes; what the code actually implements; a recommended direction; and implementation defects, split into fixed and open. The existing WGGO errata keeps E1–E3.

Six proposals have no implementation (CESH, CFA, CGAC, CIDP, CKVQ, CSS). The Glossary described three of them under titles the PDFs do not have and several as existing machinery; it is corrected.

## Fixes

Silently wrong training:

- **Tape AD gave a zero gradient through a fused elementwise chain or a `clone`.** A chain such as `tanh(sigmoid(u))` inside a function or model method is fused into a call that records nothing on the tape; functions are compiled without knowing a tape may be live. Every parameter behind such a chain got a gradient of exactly zero, with the loss correct. Tape AD is the default for `nsl run`.
- **Reduced-precision optimizer moments stored Adam's second moment as f16**, where the increment for a gradient of 1e-3 is below the smallest subnormal. `--wggo-memory-budget` alone triggered it at any budget: a weight went from 1.0 to -0.85 in 200 steps where f32 moments reach +0.82. The second moment is now always f32 and a reduced first moment is BF16.
- **Gradient accumulation was a different optimizer for Lion, SOAP, Muon and `@fase(mode = off | full_buffer)`**: sum instead of mean, micro-batch count in the bias correction, clip per micro-batch. All paths now match standard accumulation; Muon under `--layerwise-accum` follows.
- `--checkpoint-blocks` re-drew `randn` when recomputing a block.
- `@wrga(mode = manual | hybrid)` trained nothing under `--source-ad`.
- MoE expert capacity ignored `top_k`; `--cpdt full` reset a user's capacity factor to 1.0.
- `quant` blocks destroyed any tensor whose values excluded zero.

Aborts, hangs and refusals:

- A packed `DataLoader` without `pack_separator` used token id 0 (the token "!"); it is now a compile error. A loader worker that panicked ended the epoch early with exit status 0, or hung; it now aborts.
- `m.blocks[i]` on a model array read garbage.
- An `@adapter` on a rank-3 activation aborted when the build pinned a target.
- `sample_top_k` / `sample_top_p` aborted at temperature 0.
- Any `-w` run with a half-zero matrix aborted in the weight-aware sparse matmul (now withheld behind `NSL_M52C_SPARSE_MATMUL`).

Misleading output: `--csha` on a model it does not apply to printed a fusion plan and a "6.00x speedup" while compiling an identical object.

## Behaviour changes to be aware of

- `DataLoader(..., packing = true)` requires `pack_separator`.
- The fused adapter kernel needs `NSL_WRGA_FUSED_CUDA=1` at compile time as well as a pinned target.
- Lion/SOAP/Muon runs with `grad_accumulation > 1` train differently from before (correctly).
- A reduced moment tier saves 2 of 8 bytes per parameter, not 4–6.

## Not fixed

Recorded as open in the errata, not addressed here: CEP (head importance on the wrong axis, FFN names, constraints that cannot steer the search); CFIE (the same random number at every decode step, a speculative acceptance rule that does not preserve the target distribution, grammar state fixed at 0, configurations that build a binary which cannot run); WGGO's nominal layer shape; the CSHA kernels' f16 gradients; and the decorators and flags that are accepted and ignored.

## Verification

- Each fix has a regression test that fails without it; nine new test files under `crates/nsl-cli/tests/`.
- Full workspace suite, `--release --features cuda`: 8,115 passed before the last follow-up commit, and every target that failed has been re-run green except three that fail identically on the base branch in that configuration and pass in CI's (`elementwise_unary_kir_equivalence`, `fase_adamw_multi_bf16sr_kir_equivalence`, `events_stream_gate`).
- `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings`, the doc-agreement, version-agreement, hand-PTX-freeze and GPU-inventory checks pass.
- An independent review of the branch found one bug in it (`labels = none` wrongly refused with packing), fixed here.

Confidence: HIGH Fix confidence is a rating derived from an internal benchmark and includes High, Medium, and Low confidence fixes. It comprises three weighted scores reflecting the safety, effectiveness and cleanliness of Pixee's code changes within a fix. [View Details in Pixee.](https://app.pixee.ai/scans/6ebda3d1-ee5e-4c4f-9a1e-fc03e8e4dd5e?fix-finding-id=AaHWYGl7DPOq_YAFiDQt)
--- ## Remediation This change fixes finding AaHWYGl7DPOq_YAFiDQt. ## Details Prevent Command Injection in cmd_lab3 Domain Lookup ## Summary Fixed command injection in `cmd_lab3` by validating domain input and running DNS lookups without a shell. ## Vulnerability Description Command Injection occurs when an application treats attacker-controlled input as part of an operating-system command. An attacker can use shell syntax in that input to execute additional commands with the privileges of the application, potentially exposing accessible data or disrupting the service. ## Changes Made `introduction/other_views.py` previously interpolated the submitted domain into a command string and ran it with `shell=True`, allowing shell metacharacters to alter the executed command. The handler now rejects empty or malformed domains, including labels that violate hostname syntax or exceed the permitted length, with an HTTP 400 response. It passes the fixed `nslookup` or `dig` executable and the validated domain as separate arguments to `subprocess.Popen` with `shell=False`. Regression tests in `introduction/tests.py` verify that injection-shaped input is rejected before process creation and that valid input is invoked as a shell-free argument list. ## Guidance Adherence **Source**: Pixee Knowledge Base Applied the following guidance from the provided **Remediation Guidance**: - **Library usage compliance**: The guidance does not prescribe a library or framework, so there is no preferred library requirement to verify. The patch uses Python’s standard `re` validation and `subprocess` APIs. - **Code pattern matching**: The guidance calls for validating user input to exclude malicious commands. The patch checks the submitted domain against a hostname-label pattern and rejects invalid values with `HttpResponseBadRequest` before invoking a process. - **Security approach alignment**: The guidance says to prevent command injection through sanitization and/or validation. In addition to domain validation, the patch passes a fixed executable and the domain as a separate argument, with `shell=False`, rather than interpolating user input into a shell command. This prevents shell metacharacters from being interpreted as commands. - **Style consistency**: The guidance specifies no formatting, naming, or other repository style conventions. The changes use the file’s existing Python/Django conventions and add focused tests for rejected input and shell-free argument passing. - **Dependency manifest updated**: The remediation uses existing standard-library and project APIs and adds no dependencies, so no manifest update is required.

author: unpainllama
body:
## Summary

Builds Kairo Movies as an independent movie-discovery workspace. It does not reuse Anime catalogue records, episode routes, or YouTube state.

### Backend
- Add D1 schema for canonical films, namespaced external IDs, genres, credits, a separate user movie library, and country-specific availability offers.
- Add provider-neutral Movies contracts and a TMDB movie metadata adapter.
- Add global trending, popular, top-rated, upcoming, now-playing, search, genre and detail queries.
- Add cached request orchestration with timeouts and stale-on-provider-error fallback.
- Add D1 upserts for explicitly ingested summaries/details plus local catalogue search.
- Add public Movies discovery/search/detail endpoints and bounded, administrator-only incremental ingestion endpoints.
- Staging opts in to read-only TMDB discovery/search for the owner's confirmed personal, non-commercial use. Local and production remain disabled by default.
- TMDB's required approved logo and exact non-endorsement notice are displayed in Kairo's About page.
- Movie ingestion remains disabled in all environments; no automated or unbounded catalogue harvest is enabled.

### Noir frontend
- Add a cinematic Movies home page with featured backdrop, category navigation and horizontal discovery rails.
- Add paginated browse pages for trending, popular, top-rated, upcoming, now-playing and genres.
- Add global search results and movie-specific autocomplete in the persistent shared search bar.
- Add movie detail pages with artwork, metadata, genres, cast and crew.
- Reuse Kairo's existing nav rail, top search bar, hamburger menu and mobile navigation; only the context-specific contents and destinations change inside Movies.
- Keep the Anime and YouTube workspaces and their routes intact.

### Routes
- `/movies`
- `/movies/browse/:category`
- `/movies/search?q=...`
- `/movies/:externalId`

### Guardrails
- Catalogue discovery is global and does not apply country/watch-region filters. Availability remains separate from catalogue membership.
- Search is live and short-term cached; search results are not silently persisted.
- D1 ingestion is page-bounded, administrator-only and disabled until durable storage/retention rules are separately reviewed.
- TMDB's developer API is free for non-commercial use with attribution; any commercial or revenue-generating use needs a separate TMDB commercial licence.
- JustWatch remains an availability-provider extension point until Kairo has partner access.
- No movie playback is implemented in this discovery/UI slice.

### Validation and deployment
- The Movies branch's previous GitHub Actions validation passed TypeScript typecheck, tests and build. The latest follow-up commits are awaiting their CI run.
- The PR workflow does not deploy. A merge to `main` deploys to staging when `STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED=true`; otherwise use the Actions workflow_dispatch target `staging`.
- A successful staging deployment applies the additive D1 migrations and then checks `/api/health` and `/api/ready`.
- Production remains unchanged and disabled.

author: cebelerk
body:
## Human comments

## What was wrong

Codex stores the model provider on its native session. Switching Account Pooler routing changes the app-server provider between `openai` and `bb-account-pool`, so `thread/resume` rejects an existing chat with a structured provider mismatch or missing-provider error. The bridge discarded the RPC error data and could not recover the history.

Fixes #6904

## What changed

- Preserve structured Codex RPC error data.
- On a resume mismatch between `openai` and `bb-account-pool`, fork the complete native history into the selected provider. For an unconfigured pool provider, resolve the effective configuration and migrate only to `openai`.
- Publish the new native session identity, including migrations triggered by a turn's environment change, while retaining the BB thread and original native session. Defer copied Goal continuation until the next explicit turn.
- Propagate unrelated errors and failed forks without starting an empty conversation.
- Add bridge and migration regression tests and document the recovery in the Codex skill. Use existing fork and identity protocol messages.

This recovers sessions inside BB; standalone clients opening pooled sessions, discussed in #6107, remain outside this change.

## How you verified

Based on `main` at `45b15edf0edcfef84be456d9f8fbdfa85626fa35`.

- `pnpm exec turbo run lint typecheck --filter=bb-plugin-provider-codex`: passed, lint reports zero warnings/errors.
- `pnpm exec turbo run test --filter=bb-plugin-provider-codex --env-mode=loose -- src/bridge/provider-migration.test.ts src/bridge/bridge.session-signature.test.ts src/bridge/app-server-connection.test.ts`: 34 tests passed.
- `pnpm exec turbo run test --filter=bb-plugin-provider-codex --env-mode=loose`: 587 passed, one failed. The same existing model-catalog route test fails against unchanged production sources at the base commit (`expected '' to be null`).
- Repeated the new provider-switch and missing-pool regressions with the base commit's bridge and connection: both fail with `Provider mismatch` / `Pool no longer configured`; both pass with the change.
- `oxfmt --check` on changed code and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent review caught a stale-identity case during in-turn reconstruction; fixed it and added release/restore coverage.

Tests use the hermetic app-server fixture. Live account switching was not exercised for this upstream change.

| `<id>.part.header` | An upload no longer writes and fsyncs it, and the three deletes go. The start-up sweep still removes one a 1.2 node left. | No read of it in `crates/cli`, `docs` or `FORMAT.md`. The full-disk test arms its fault after `begin`, so it is unaffected. |
| `WriteGate::fence(Fence::Start)` | `fence()` takes no reason and stores the operator's fence. | Its two callers (`cluster/fence.rs`, `cluster/close.rs`) both passed `Operator`. A start fence is only ever set by `WriteGate::new`. |
| `serve/feed.rs` | Three hand-built "the client went away" errors call `gone()`. | Same constructor and text. |
| `successor` / `prefix_end` | `router.rs` and `cluster/fanout.rs` call `cluster/route.rs`'s `prefix_end`; their two copies go. | Identical bodies. `fanout.rs`'s test now asserts on the shared one. |
| `pull_now`, `maybe_pull` | Both call `fetch_map`. | The inline blocks were `fetch_map`'s body. |
| `http_caller` | Calls `http::auth_header`. | Same header read. |
| Stream-limit refusal | Four inline copies in `service.rs` become `self.stream_slot()?`. | Same semaphore, code and text. |
| `later()` and `route()`'s unreachable arms | Three arms with three texts become one arm and one `Internal` answer; `later()` goes. | See below. |
| `Serving.dbs` | Removed. Shutdown closes `router.parts()`' databases on a single node too. | A single node's `parts()` is its one database; a cluster node already ignored the field. |
| `reserve` / `run_blocking` | `budget` and `run_blocking` go; `reserve` and `blocking` are the one name each. | Both were one-line forwards. |
| `From<JoinError> for ApiError` | 13 hand-written `map_err(\|e\| ApiError::internal(e.to_string()))` on a join become `?`. | Same code and text. |
| `CatalogStart` (engine) | The one-variant enum becomes `Option<&Catalog>`. | One constructor and one match arm used it. |

## Where it differs from the issue's wording

- **`route()`'s arms are collapsed, not dropped into `_`.** The catch-all answers `Unsupported` ("this call isn't served by a cluster node"), which would be the wrong answer if one of these calls ever did reach `route()`. They keep an `Internal` answer, in one arm. I checked them unreachable:
  - `Router::dispatch_by` answers the four schema calls, every scan, a subscription and both backup calls before `Cluster::target`, and fans out a traversal with no snapshot;
  - `Cluster.Forward` can't carry any of them except `CreateTable` and `DropTable` (`forward::op_of`), which `serve_forwarded` takes before it routes;
  - `fanout.rs` calls `route()` with a scan only when it has a snapshot.
- **The issue counted 14 `JoinError` sites; there are 13.** The other three matches of that `map_err` are `io::Error`s in `backup.rs`'s tests and stay.
- **`mcp/tools.rs` keeps its own `successor`.** It's outside the `serve` feature, so it can't call into `serve::cluster::route`.

## One edge worth a reviewer's eye

A full disk at the start of an upload used to answer `NoSpace` from the header's write. Now the empty `.part` file's create is the only write at `begin`, and the first chunk's write answers `NoSpace` instead.

## Tests

Run locally, all passing:
- `cargo quota clippy -p pigeonhole-engine -p pigeonhole-cli --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo quota test -p pigeonhole-cli --all-features` (409 lib tests and the integration suites)
- the tests named `feed` in `pigeonhole-engine` and `pigeonhole`, all features
- rustdoc with `-Dwarnings` on both crates

Not run locally: the rest of the workspace, and the cli built without `serve`.

## What

Second batch of `Kernel\Contracts` (after #1890). Eighteen more services get a contract that declares exactly what outside callers use: SettingsService, OrganizationSyncService, ContactpersoonService, ModuleRegistrationService, StackiqContactSyncService, ContactPersonHandler, ContactPersonOrganisationGuard, ContractApprovalService, ContractStatusService, EolSyncService, FederationConfig, FederationService, CronjobSettings, ConnectionReportService, PublicCatalogueRecords, CmdbImportPackStore, CmdbExportImportService and ArchiMateImportService. Controllers, jobs, commands, listeners and repair steps type-hint the contract; `ContractBindings` aliases each one to the same shared instance.

Keeping the contracts free of `Service` classes needed three small moves, each keeping every existing name working:

- `SettingsServiceInterface` extends the existing `RegisterConfigReaderInterface`, so the hand-built factories can pass it where a constructor asks for the reader.
- `LEGACY_SCHEMA_KEY` and `MIN_OPENREGISTER_VERSION` move from `CatalogueLocator` onto `ObjectTypeLocatorInterface`, which `CatalogueLocator` and `SettingsService` already implement. `CatalogueLocator::X`, `SettingsService::X` and the contract all resolve to the same value.
- The pure `logSafeMessage()` moves to `Kernel\LogSafeMessage::of()`; `CmdbExportImportService::logSafeMessage()` delegates to it, and the controller calls it directly.

Container look-ups by class name (`$this->container->get(SettingsService::class)` in listeners, a repair step and a command) are left as they are; their tests key the container mock by that class.

No behaviour change, no test changes.

## Verified locally

- `php -l` clean; phpcs: 0 findings on the new files, the modified files carry the same 21 warnings as before; phpstan: no errors

author: copybara-service[bot]
body:
Expose virtual NUMA topology for NVProxy workloads

On a two-GPU NVIDIA L40S system with driver 610, PyTorch
2.10.0+cu128 with NCCL 2.27.5 fails during a two-rank collective when NCCL's
cuMem host-allocation path is enabled. The same workload passes on driver 580
and with `NCCL_CUMEM_HOST_ENABLE=0`, which bypasses that path.

The cuMem host path discovers NUMA topology through
`/sys/devices/system/node`. gVisor already models NUMA as one virtual node, but
the sysfs tree was created only from an RDMA host snapshot, which NVProxy-only
workloads do not have.

Expose the fixed single-node topology whenever NVProxy or RDMAProxy is active.
The virtual node covers every application CPU. RDMA snapshots retain host NUMA
metadata for PCI device locality; the generic sysfs node always presents the
fixed single-node view.

This change does not emulate GPU PCI/NVML topology; `nvidia-smi topo -m`
remains outside its scope.

Validation:

- two-rank NCCL 2.27.5 `all_reduce` with `NCCL_CUMEM_HOST_ENABLE=1`
- direct cuMem host-buffer sharing for device pairs 0->1, 1->0, and 0->0
- `bazel test //pkg/rdma:rdma_test //pkg/sentry/fsimpl/sys:sys_test //pkg/sentry/fsimpl/sys:sys_integration_test //runsc/boot:boot_test`
- `bazel build //:release`

## Hva brukeren opplevde
Et planlagt opptak (søndagsopptaket uten noen ved maskinen) hoppet over enhetsoverleveringen som manuell Start gjør: stopp pre-roll, stopp VU-måler, 400 ms ro. Pre-roll (standard 15 s) og måleren holdt da fortsatt inngangen når opptaket åpnet den, og pre-roll ble bare stoppet hvis webviewet så `isRecording`. Kommentaren i `start_recording_impl` hevdet at scheduler-start var dekket. Det stemte ikke (scheduler-start, sen start og spesialopptak kalte `engine.start` direkte).

author: renaudlesage
body:
## Ce que ça fait

Nouvelle rubrique **Sécurité › Pont radio** (visible pour qui traite les signalements). Un poste du QG relié à une radio lit, à voix de synthèse, ce qui arrive dans Eventware : un bip qui ouvre le VOX, puis « Message du QG. Signalement. Malaise. Étape 1. Référence S, O, S, zéro, zéro, un. Je répète. … Terminé. »

| Ce qui arrive | Ce que fait le pont |
|---|---|
| Signalement d'un bénévole connecté (bouton « Signaler un incident », `INT-`) | part **seul** |
| Mayday | part **seul** (ni le nom ni le motif ; l'indicatif radio, oui) |
| Signalement d'un participant (page publique du QR) | attend **un appui du QG**, texte retouchable |
| SOS saisi au QG d'après un appel radio ou téléphonique (`RAD-`) | attend un appui |
| Signalement resté plus de dix minutes en file dans un téléphone | attend un appui |
| Tout ce qui était déjà là au démarrage du pont | attend un appui |

- Le message dit la nature, le lieu (le lieu choisi, sinon « près de » le lieu du dispositif à moins de 300 m) et la référence épelée. **Jamais** la description, le contact, un nom.
- Plafond : cinq annonces automatiques de signalements en dix minutes ; les suivantes attendent un appui. Un Mayday part toujours.
- Chaque annonce, le démarrage et l'arrêt s'inscrivent dans la main courante ; c'est elle (et la mémoire du poste) qui dit ce qui a déjà été annoncé.
- Annonce libre (240 caractères), essai de voix, choix de la voix française et du débit.
- Facultatif : si la sortie haut-parleur de la radio est branchée sur l'entrée micro du poste, le pont attend deux secondes de silence (quinze au plus) avant de parler.
- Si un autre poste a démarré un pont sans l'arrêter, l'écran le dit.

**Aucune migration, aucune fonction serveur, aucun secret.** La voix est celle du navigateur du poste.

## Deux écarts par rapport à ce qu'on s'était dit

1. **Le Mayday part seul lui aussi.** C'est le cas le plus net de « bénévole identifié » ; je l'ai ajouté. Dis-moi si tu préfères qu'il attende un appui.
2. **L'appui du QG se fait sur le poste du pont lui-même**, pas depuis n'importe quel écran du QG. Faire parler le pont depuis un autre poste demande une table dédiée avec ses droits : passer par la main courante aurait permis à n'importe quel membre de faire dire ce qu'il veut sur le canal d'urgence (`journaliser` est ouvert à tout membre). Ce serait une migration 175, à faire si l'usage le demande.

## Vérifié

- `npx vite build`.
- Banc d'essai complet : 105 sur 105. Nouveau scénario `pont-radio` (bureau, téléphone, tablette) avec une fausse voix qui note ce qu'on lui fait dire : rien ne part avant le démarrage ni de ce qui était déjà là ; un signalement de bénévole arrivé en cours part seul, deux fois, sans le nom ni le numéro que contenait sa description, une seule fois ; le Mayday part sans nom ni motif ; le signalement du participant ne part qu'à l'appui, avec le texte retouché ; l'inscription dans la main courante (objet, référence, « automatique ») ; le plafond (sept signalements d'un coup : quatre partent, trois attendent) ; plus rien ne part après l'arrêt.

## Pas vérifié

- **Rien n'a été entendu.** Ni la voix réelle d'un navigateur, ni une radio : intelligibilité sur un canal, déclenchement du VOX par le bip, niveau de sortie, tenue d'un onglet ouvert pendant des heures (les navigateurs ralentissent une page passée à l'arrière-plan).
- L'écoute du canal (seuil fixe) n'a été essayée sur aucune entrée audio réelle.
- L'écran réel connecté à la production (le bac à sable n'atteint pas Supabase).
- Deux ponts démarrés en même temps diraient les annonces deux fois : l'écran prévient, il n'empêche pas.

## À faire de ton côté

- **Avant toute émission : vérifier le droit d'émettre une voix automatique sur la fréquence utilisée** (licence de l'organisation, conditions de l'IBPT, PMR446 ou fréquence attribuée). Je ne l'ai pas vérifié.
- Essai à blanc sur un canal d'essai : câble sortie casque → entrée micro de la radio, VOX réglé, « Essai de voix », puis un signalement d'essai. Sur téléphone ou tablette, vérifier que l'appareil a une voix française installée.
- Garder le poste sur cet écran, allumé, au premier plan ; un seul pont à la fois.

L'écoute (radio → texte dans le fil « Entendu ») n'est pas dans cette PR : c'est l'étape suivante.

body:
## 做了什么

新栏目 `/chemistry/`（化学学科馆），顶栏在“学习”组。十四门学科分四组：

- 四大基础：无机、有机、物理、分析
- 结构、计算与电子：结构、量子与计算、配位与金属有机、电化学
- 大分子、生命与材料：高分子、生物、材料
- 环境、原子核与工程：环境、核化学与放射化学、化学工程

内容规模：110 章、52 个在浏览器里现算的演示、275 篇文献。

- 每章有讲解（标出基础、进阶、前沿三档）、核心公式和一道带数字的例题。
- 每馆有时间线、自测题、教材、开放问题和“接着逛”。
- 总入口有四组卡片、学科关系图和站内其他化学内容。
- 和已有栏目重叠的部分只写概览，链到谱图馆、核磁共振、量子嘉年华、讲解手册和新闻。
- 材料化学 #c-porous 链回新闻的两条 MOF 条目。

原计划的药物化学馆没能写出内容，站长决定删掉这一栏。环境、核化学、化学工程三馆依次改为 12–14 号，其他馆里指向药物化学的链接已经拿掉。`chem-subjects.js` 的 `soon` 机制保留，现在是空的。

## 结构

- `chem-subjects.js`：名单、分组、学科关系和每馆的数字。
- `chem.js`：通用的阅读器。
- `chem-models.js`：全部演示的数学，都是纯函数。
- 每个展馆的 `data.js`、`demos.js`。
- `math.js`：由 `tools/fundamental-math.mjs` 生成。
- 展馆页：由 `tools/chemistry-pages.mjs` 生成。

## 验证

- `node --test tools/chemistry-test.mjs`：31 项全过。
  - 模型对照解析解和教科书数值：Randles–Ševčík 对模拟 CV、Carothers、Flory、Mayo–Lewis、FH 双节线、DNA Tm、Brus、碳酸盐 pH 5.60、Fe-56 SEMF、Tc-99m 22.8 h、CSTR/PFR、McCabe–Thiele 11 板和 R_min 1.10、Antoine 沸点。
  - 内容：中英齐全，文献都被引用且都存在，站内链接和跨馆锚点都在，演示都已登记，数字对得上，页面是最新的。
  - 写测试时修正了 Slater 规则同组电子多扣一个的错误。
- `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1 node tools/chemistry-refs.mjs`：275 篇文献全部和 OpenAlex 的 DOI 记录对上。
- `node tools/e2e/run.mjs`：131 项全过。删掉药物化学之后重跑了一遍。
- 在副本里跑过 `build-seo.ts`。截图看过浅色、深色、英文和手机宽度。

没测：Safari 和真机触屏。桌面版等下一个标签。

body:
## 這是什麼

公開的「關係解方手冊」：伴侶最常反覆卡住的 8 種循環（親密被拒、教養不同、冷戰、家事分工、金錢觀、家人界線、不被看見、沒有相處時間）。每份手冊都是同樣七段：發生了什麼 → 雙方真正的感受（A／B，不預設性別）→ 為什麼一直重複 → 換個方式說（可複製的說法）→ 替代方案 → 建立共同約定 → 一起回顧。

漏斗：**Discover**（公開、可被搜尋、可分享）→ **Apply**（說法、替代方案、約定，按鈕直接進「說開一件事」或「替代方案協商」）→ **Reflect Together**（收藏與「我的經驗」，需要帳號）。

範圍是 PCS v1.0 的 Phase 1＋基本的 Phase 2。

## 改了什麼

- **內容**：`lib/playbooks/content.zh-TW.js`、`content.en.js`，共用一套有驗證的 schema（`lib/playbooks/index.js`），只會送出 `status: 'published'` 的手冊。新增手冊只要改內容檔。
- **公開 API**：`GET /api/playbooks`、`GET /api/playbooks/:slug`（依 `X-Locale` 回繁中或英文，找不到時回 `PLAYBOOK_NOT_FOUND`）。
- **SEO 頁面**：server 端輸出 `/playbooks`、`/playbooks/:slug`，每頁有自己的 title、OG、canonical、hreflang、JSON-LD 和文章 HTML（`lib/playbooks/render.js`）；`sitemap.xml` 自動加上所有手冊的繁中、英文網址。
- **私人資料**：migration 115 新增 `playbook_saves`、`playbook_reflections`（已開 RLS，只有本人能讀寫）。錯誤都有專屬 `error_code`（`REFLECTION_EMPTY` / `REFLECTION_TOO_LONG` / `REFLECTION_LIMIT` / `REFLECTION_NOT_FOUND`），並用 `logInfo`/`logWarn` 記錄。
- **前端**：`src/components/playbooks/`。網址跟著頁面走；收藏和經驗用樂觀更新（R7）；未登入時是三段式 gate；`?lang=en` 在使用者沒選過語言時開英文。
- **入口**：成長頁卡片、右上選單、未登入 今天／成長 的 `ExploreLinks`。沒有新增主分頁。
- **套用按鈕**：親密那份開「替代方案協商」（`IntimacyRequestForm` 新增 `initialCategory`），其他開「說開一件事」；未配對時改成邀請配對。
- **訪客模式**：內容走 `PUBLIC_GETS`，收藏和經驗只存在分頁裡；seed 新增一則範例並把 `buildSeed.VERSION` 升到 4。
- **量測**：`onboarding.playbooks.*` 事件（瀏覽、讀到第幾段、複製說法、收藏、寫經驗、按套用、看到註冊提示）。
- **文件**：`docs/RELATIONSHIP_PLAYBOOK.md`、UX playbook 中英版登記新入口、changelog fragment。

## 順便修的 bug

Vite 用 `base: './'` 打包，`index.html` 裡是 `./assets/…`。從 `/playbooks/<slug>` 這類深層網址打開時，瀏覽器會去抓 `/playbooks/assets/…`、拿到 HTML，結果是空白頁。手冊頁的 server 模板現在會把 bundle 連結改成 `/assets/…`，並加了測試。`/billing/result` 用的是同一套相對路徑，可能有同樣問題，這個 PR 沒有處理也沒有驗證。

## Migration 編號

`main` 已經有 116，這裡是 115。`database/migrator.js` 是看「哪些版本還沒套用」，不看大小順序，所以 115 合併後一樣會執行；兩個檔案也不衝突。

## 測試

- 新的 `tests/playbooks.spec.ts`：16 個全部通過。涵蓋 schema、繁中英文結構一致、沒有單獨的他／她或 he/she、沒有破折號、API 權限與錯誤碼、經驗只有本人看得到、SEO 頁與 sitemap、深層網址的 bundle 路徑、訪客模式不外流、未登入 gate。
- 受影響的既有測試：`guest-mode`、`language-switch`、`intimacy-negotiation-ui`、`ux-onboarding`、`communicate-nav` 共 31 個全部通過。
- `tsc -b`、eslint、`scripts/check-rls.js` 都通過。
- **沒有跑**：完整測試套件、`scripts/perf/measure-pages.mjs --mobile`。

## 還需要注意

- 內容在程式碼裡，不在資料庫：改內容不用動 UI，但要部署才會上線。後台編輯和草稿／審核流程留到下一階段。
- 親密、金錢控制、暴力相關的內容還沒經過專業諮商師審閱，建議推廣前先審。
- 尚未實作：和伴侶共讀手冊、Luma 引導對話、共同約定的進度追蹤（Phase 3–4）。

author: mikolalysenko
body:
Adds hot patch mode as a hidden, experimental subcommand. `socket-patch hot-patch -- <command>` patches everything installed on the machine in place, saves nothing, and then becomes the command. As a container's entrypoint it makes a restart the way a patch is deployed or withdrawn, with no image rebuild.

```dockerfile
COPY socket-patch /usr/local/bin/socket-patch
ENTRYPOINT ["socket-patch", "hot-patch", "--"]
CMD ["node", "server.js"]
```

```console
$ docker run --rm my-app
socket-patch: applied 17 patches [106 project + 186 global packages checked, 3.2s]
app: listening on :3000 as pid 1
```

`scan` and every other subcommand behave as before. The one change outside the new subcommand is the stop-signal fix below.

## What hot patch mode does

- **The command always starts.** A flag or environment value that does not parse, an unreachable API, packages that cannot be written and a panic are each one line on stderr, and the command starts anyway. socket-patch `exec`s the command, which keeps the PID, the signals, the environment it was given and its exit status.
- **Patches files as they are on disk, like agent mode.** It runs two ordinary agent-mode scans: the project under `--cwd`, then the system's globally installed packages (`--global` runs only the second).
- **Nothing is saved.** The manifests and patch data the engine works from live in a temporary directory that is removed before the command starts. `--manifest-path`, `--prune`, `--sync` and `--vex` are refused.
- **Every patch a scan would select is applied.** There is no severity default. `--min-severity`, `SOCKET_MIN_SEVERITY` and socket.yml narrow it as they do for `scan`, and they are where a policy or a target list would plug in later.
- **A time limit.** A pass that has not started writing patches within `--timeout` seconds of the start (default 10) is dropped, and it has touched nothing. A pass that has started writing is never interrupted.
- **One `socket-patch: ...` line on stderr**, nothing on stdout.
- **`SOCKET_OFFLINE=1` is the off switch.**

The subcommand takes scan's options plus `--timeout`. Without a command after `--` it patches nothing and exits 2.

Two things differ from running the two scans by hand:

- The project pass leaves Go modules to the global pass. A project run does not patch a Go module in place: it redirects the module through `go.mod` to a copy under `.socket/`, and drops the redirects its manifest does not list. This mode's manifest starts empty and it writes nothing but installed packages.
- The global pass reads the working directory's socket.yml, which a plain `--global` scan does not. The two passes can reach the same installed copy (a Python image's system site-packages), and a package the repository excludes has to stay unpatched in both.

## The stop-signal fix (every subcommand)

The kernel drops a signal that PID 1 re-raises with the default disposition, so when socket-patch was a container's main process `docker stop` did nothing until the grace period ran out. The handler now ends the process itself when it is PID 1, with exit status 128 + the signal's number. Measured with `docker stop` during a check that was waiting on a dead API: 0.2 s, exit 143.

## Start-up cost

Time added before the command starts, measured inside the container on a laptop (Docker Desktop, linux/arm64) against the public patch API with no token, median of 5 fresh containers:

| Image | Packages (project + global) | Patches applied | Added to start-up |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Small Node app | 106 + 186 | 17 | 3.2 s |
| Large Node app | 1,158 + 186 | 19 | 3.6 s (slowest 4.2 s) |
| Small Python app | 37 + 37 | 4 | 2.1 s |

Nearly all of it is round trips to the patch API. `SOCKET_OFFLINE=1` adds 2 to 3 ms, and an API that never answers costs the time limit. The default limit is 10 s because these starts were too close to 5 s.

## Size

`src/hot_patch.rs` is new (about 510 lines plus its unit tests). The rest of the non-test change is about 130 lines in six files: `main.rs` cuts the command off the command line before parsing and makes every way out start it, `lib.rs` declares the hidden subcommand, `ui/mod.rs` hands scan's JSON document to hot patch mode instead of printing it, `agent_download.rs` marks the start of the apply step, `scan/policy.rs` lets the global pass read socket.yml in this mode, and `interrupt.rs` holds the PID 1 fix. `ScanArgs`, the patch engine, the crawlers and the API client are untouched.

## Testing

- `tests/hot_patch_e2e.rs`: 19 end-to-end tests that spawn the real binary against a mock patch API. They cover both passes patching and the command's exit status, `--global`, the same PID, the command's own flags, an unreachable API, the time limit (the whole run, and the global pass alone), a severity floor, a dry run, socket.yml covering the global pass, a rollout cap, a withdrawn patch, a restart, usage errors and refused flags, the off switch, a missing command, the unchanged environment, a panic, and a stop signal.
- Unit tests in `hot_patch.rs` for the command-line split, the passes, the time parser and the summary line.
- Run by hand in Docker (linux/arm64) with a Node and a Python image: root, non-root (reported, app starts), read-only root file system (reported, app starts), no network (app starts at the limit), stderr on a full device (app starts; the previous build exited 101), `docker stop` during the check.
- The full CLI suite on macOS (arm64): 4,930 passed, 2 failed, 418 ignored. The 2 failures are `e2e_vendor_cargo_build` tests that need old x86 cargo toolchains this Mac cannot run (`'cargo': Bad CPU type in executable`); they fail the same way on `main`. The hot-patch end-to-end tests also pass on Linux (in the `rust:1.93-bookworm` image), including the one that needs `/dev/full`.
- The non-Unix path (run the command as a child and exit with its status) was not compiled or run locally.

## Known gaps

Review findings I chose not to fix in this PR, and why:

- **No lock across containers.** The apply lock lives with the temporary manifest, so two containers that share one mounted dependency tree can patch the same files at once. Each file is written by an atomic rename and checked against its hash before and after, and taking the lock in the project would mean leaving a `.socket/` directory behind.
- **A hung package-manager probe can outlive the time limit.** If a probe such as `yarn global dir` is still running when the limit is reached, it is left as a child of the command. Closing this needs a registry of live children in core.
- **The temporary directory is left behind when a stop signal ends the run.** A signal handler cannot remove a directory tree safely. A normal run, a timeout and every refusal remove it.
- **The two passes can cover the same packages.** In a Python image without a virtualenv, both passes find the system site-packages and each queries the API for them. The second pass finds the patches in place. It costs one extra round of queries.
- **Telemetry still gets its short exit grace** (up to 300 ms) before the command starts, when telemetry is on.
- **SIGPIPE is not passed through.** The command starts with SIGPIPE at its default even where socket-patch inherited it as ignored (under systemd, for example), because Rust's start-up replaces that setting before any of our code runs. In a container the two are the same.
- **Hot patch mode is carried by a few process-wide statics** (is a run active, has the apply step started, the documents reported) that `ui::print_json`, the agent engine and the policy loader consult. Passing them through `ScanArgs` instead would have touched every `ScanArgs` literal in the tests.
- **Path filters in socket.yml judge project paths only.** The global pass honors the file's package exclusions, severity floor and `enabled`, but a root excluded by `ignorePaths` does not exclude global packages.

Also out of scope here: containers that cannot write to their packages (non-root

Demo, row click opens the device placeholder: ![detail](https://github.com/pkkid/mesh-ui/blob/assets/M1.15-screenshots/demo-detail-dark.png?raw=true)

Fake eero server, dark: ![fake dark](https://github.com/pkkid/mesh-ui/blob/assets/M1.15-screenshots/fake-devices-dark.png?raw=true)

Fake eero server, light: ![fake light](https://github.com/pkkid/mesh-ui/blob/assets/M1.15-screenshots/fake-devices-light.png?raw=true)

## Decisions

- **Live rates.** The page runs `device.rates.refresh` once a minute while it is visible, fades the Now column and Throughput now to 40% while the burst is pending, and refetches `device.list` at `nextBurstAt` plus `BURST_SETTLE_SEC`. The once-a-minute limit stays in core.
- **Today column** comes from `usage.breakdown {range: "day", by: "device"}`, the same 24 h window `sort: "usage"` uses. Missing or zero shows `-`.
- **Guest count** in the segment is `device.list {ssid: "guest"}`'s length, so the renderer does no counting. Manufacturer options are the distinct manufacturers of the unfiltered `device.list` (an option list, not a filter).
- **Category colours** use `entityColor(i)` from `chartColors.ts` in category order (blue, purple, aqua, orange) and `seriesColors.neutral` for Other, which matches the mockup. No colour is picked inline. Profile avatars use `entityColors` per profile id.
- **Grouping** (view state): Category uses the mockup's groups (phones and computers as Computers & Personal; smart home as Home; offline devices under Recently online; blocked under Blocked). Home starts collapsed, as in the mockup. Empty category groups show "No devices online" only while no filter is active. Also Status, eero, Profile and None.
- **Status** follows the vocabulary (dot plus label): Blocked, then Offline, then Paused, then Online, so an offline paused device reads Offline with "5 h ago · paused" in Now.
- **Filter state** is kept per network while the app runs; hidden columns persist in localStorage (try/catch). Changing a filter keeps the last rows on screen, faded, until the new list answers.
- **Share Wi-Fi** is in the topbar but disabled: `wifi.share` does not exist yet.
- **Bulk bar** is always visible in a disabled state ("0 selected" with disabled Pause, Resume, Assign profile, Block, Clear), and checkboxes and the row menu are disabled, since selection only means something once M4's actions exist.
- The retired prototype `DevicesView.tsx` was already gone; nothing to delete.

## Open

- **Band insight line** ("6 GHz carries 41% of traffic with 19% of devices") is left out: the `device.list` summary has no per-band rate totals, and computing it in the renderer would duplicate core logic. Needs a summary field in `src/core/commands/device.ts`.
- **Counts in the eero, Profile and Manufacturer dropdowns** are left out for the same reason (the summary has counts by status, band and category only). Profile shows its `deviceIds` count from `profile.list`; Type shows the summary's category counts.
- **Sidebar count** in fake mode reads 7 (from `network.get` counts) while the page's All chip reads 8 (summary total, which includes the offline device). The doc says the sidebar count is the summary total; that is the sidebar's code (M1.7), not this story's.
- Bridge mode, no-permission and capability-missing states depend on commands and fields not wired to this page yet (M4 and later).

body:
## Summary

Two false positives in `lib/rules/code_safety.ex`, reported from gitbot-fleet#673 and reproduced by the rule reconciliation session at `main` (`CodeSafety.scan_content(src, "rust")`).

- **`unsafe_block`** said "requires SAFETY comment", but its pattern was the bare `unsafe\s*\{`, so a documented block was flagged like an undocumented one (alerts 860/861). A line is now excused when the nearest non-blank lines above it are a comment block naming `SAFETY:` (`//` or `/* */` form; `#[...]` attributes may sit between), or when every `unsafe {` on the line is inside a string literal. Excused matches are removed after the scan, so line numbers do not shift. Whole-line `/* */` block comments now keep their newlines when stripped, so all Rust findings after such a block report the correct line.
- **`from_raw`** (severity high) matched the bare name and flagged the safe `rustix::process::Pid::from_raw(i32)` (alert 863). It now matches only `Box/Arc/Rc/Weak/Vec/String/CString/OsString/NonNull/Waker::from_raw` (with turbofish and `<Box<T>>::` forms) and `from_raw_parts(_mut)` / `from_raw_fd` / `from_raw_handle` / `from_raw_socket`.

Rule ids and descriptions are unchanged, so `hypatia_rules_praxis.deed` needs no regeneration.

## Known limits

The rule matches with regular expressions, not a Rust lexer. These cases are not handled, and each gives a missed finding (not a false alarm):

- A multi-line string or a raw string (`r#"..."#`) that ends on the same line as a following `unsafe {`.
- Generic arguments split over lines before `::from_raw` (rustfmt does not produce this).
- A raw-pointer type used through an alias, such as `use std::boxed::Box as HeapBox;` then `HeapBox::from_raw(p)`.
- Two `unsafe` blocks on one line after one SAFETY comment: both are excused (rustfmt puts each statement on its own line).

Found during review, not changed here: `scan_content` calls `Enum.at` on the line list for every line of every rule (the inline-directive pass), so a scan is quadratic in file length. A 20,000-line Rust file takes about 24 s on `main`. The SAFETY lookup added by this PR is linear and is tested for it.

## Test plan

- [x] 8 new tests in `test/code_safety_test.exs`: SAFETY directly above → no finding; attribute between → no finding; `/* SAFETY: */` → no finding; SAFETY separated by code → finding on line 3; no comment → finding; `unsafe {` in a string → no finding; safe `Pid::from_raw` → no finding; `Box/Arc::from_raw`, `slice::from_raw_parts`, `File::from_raw_fd` → still flagged.
- [x] Against the old rules, exactly the 5 reproduced cases fail (4 `unsafe_block`, 1 `from_raw`).
- [x] Review rounds: each Codex and CodeRabbit finding that real code can contain has a test that fails before its fix. `test/code_safety_test.exs` now has 86 tests.
- [x] Full Elixir suite (OTP 27.3.4.19, Elixir 1.17.3): 3035 tests, 0 failures, 246 excluded. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` clean; changed files formatted.

## Verified incident
Canonical Update market data #212 was canceled after its 45-minute job limit, with `Run pipeline` still active. Completed job logs show SEC insider intelligence at only 300/351 companies at 19:05 UTC, repeated `www.sec.gov/Archives` ReadTimeoutError at 25 seconds with urllib3 retries. author: kasunsiyambalapitiya
body:
Replaces #40, which was opened from a fork: GitHub stacks need their branches in this repository. Earlier review: #40.

## Summary

Product photos for the Swag Store, stored in a private Azure Blob container.

- **Upload:** `POST /admin/products/{id}/images` (catalog managers), `multipart/form-data` with `view` and `file`. The type is read from the bytes (JPEG, PNG or WebP; SVG, HTML, GIF and HEIC get 415), 5 MiB at most, read part by part with nothing written to disk. The backend writes with its own Microsoft Entra identity (managed identity or app registration), never overwrites (`If-None-Match: *`), and audits each upload (`product_image_uploaded`). The product changes only when a PATCH saves `images`.
- **Naming:** `products/{productId}/{view}-{8 hex}.{jpg|png|webp}`, one photo per view: `front`, `back`, `left`, `right`, `top`, `bottom`, `detail-1` … `detail-4`. Every upload gets a new name, so caches never show an old photo.
- **Reading:** product JSON (shop and admin) returns each photo's `path` and a signed, read-only URL for that one blob (`sr=b`, `sp=r`, HTTPS only). One SAS per photo per UTC day, valid 48 h, signed with a user-delegation key the backend renews itself. No SAS or key is configured anywhere a browser can read.
- **Config:** `ASSETS_ACCOUNT_URL`, `ASSETS_CONTAINER` (default `swag-store-assets`), `ASSETS_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES`, `AZURE_TENANT_ID` / `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` / `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET`. `ASSETS_ACCOUNT_KEY` is accepted only for the local Azurite emulator. Unset: uploads answer 503 and photo URLs are null; everything else works. `/health/dependencies` reports `assets`. `IMAGE_URL_HOSTS` is gone.
- **Schema:** `0002_product_photo_paths.sql` recreates `swag_product_images` with `photo_view` + `path` and `UNIQUE (product_id, photo_view)`. Nothing is live yet; the old rows were pasted links with no blob behind them.

## Ops, per environment

- A private container (`swag-store-assets`) on an account with Entra authorisation.
- For the backend identity: **Storage Blob Data Contributor on the container** and **Storage Blob Delegator on the account**.
- (confirm) Choreo components can use a managed identity, else an app registration with its secret in a Choreo secret; the backend can reach `login.microsoftonline.com` and `*.blob.core.windows.net`.

## Testing

- `go vet ./... && go test -race ./...`: 213 tests pass, including config checks, SAS shape across UTC midnight, key renewal and retry backoff, multipart limits, type sniffing, the Blob PUT headers, and that no logged error keeps a query string.
- Integration tests on MySQL 8.4 (`SWAG_TEST_DATABASE_URL`): photos stored and read back in view order; uploads audited.
- Live against Azurite: upload 201; signed GET 200 with the same bytes; the URL without its SAS → 403; that SAS on another blob → 403; SVG → 415; `assets: ok`; no signature in the server log.
- Postman: new "Upload photo" request; collection lint clean.

Stacked on #45, in stack #46 (#41 → #42 → #45 → #43).

body:
## Summary

The two automerge engines disagreed on what a licence file is.

- **Elixir brain** (`PrAutomerge.licence_path?/1`): matched a basename *prefix*, case-sensitively, so `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES`, `License.md`, `REUSE.toml` and a nested `docs/LICENSES/` tree were not licence work.
- **Shell actuator** (`is_licence_path` in `scripts/sweeps/estate-pr-automerge.sh`): matched anywhere in the name but case-sensitively, and missed nested `LICENSES/` and `REUSE.toml`.

Both now use one set: a basename containing `LICENSE`/`LICENCE`/`COPYING`/`NOTICE`/`SPDX` in any case, `REUSE.toml`, or a `LICENSES/` directory anywhere. A wider veto only sends more PRs to owner review. `AdminMergeEligibility.licence_path?/1` (AM010) already delegates to the Elixir function, so it follows.

Also: the `chore_meta_only` policy class no longer lists "licence headers" (licence touches are never auto-merged; owner ruling on #1067).

Reproduced by the rule reconciliation session (the actuator still vetoed today's cases, so nothing merged wrongly; the brain was wrong).

## Consolidação (não é deploy)
Substitui a proposta de mesclar indiscriminadamente a pilha experimental de PRs #19–#29.

**Branch derivada diretamente de main** (base `aa105ccd21a5adb8b5db342e884f8219fc7d1bc7`) com **13 arquivos essenciais** de consulta read-only (8 módulos/páginas, 5 testes), mais runbook e CI. Não inclui REA/editor/laboratórios, protótipo SQLite 086 nem migrations.

body:
## 何をしたか

中央の予想で並べていた「◎ランク・的中率・配当率」の3つを、地方の発走前の通知と同じ「期待度」の1行（例 `期待度 A（点数 0.28）`）にした。

- 点数と線は前の ◎ランクのまま（◎ の1着の確率 ＋ 単勝の期待値 − 1。S 0.35 以上・A 0.15 以上・B 0 以上・C 0 未満）。木曜は単勝オッズが無いので `期待度 なし（単勝オッズが出る前なので出さない）`。
- 変わる場所: 発走前の通知の文（見出しの次の行）と表の画像の見出しの札（地方と同じ `期待度 S` の札）、開催日のまとめの一覧（「◎ランク（的中率）」「配当率」の2列を「期待度」の1列に）、標準出力の表の注、全頭の予想根拠の頭、検索画面の「今週の予想」タブ、道具「取得と予想の状況」、道具「印の成績」の表13 の名前。
- 変えないもの: 的中率・配当率・3連複の荒れ具合は予想の結果（JSON）に今までどおり入る（鍵の名前も同じ。前の版の結果もそのまま読める）。買うレースと買い目は変わらない。
- 文書: 設計書「買うレースと買い目を決める」の 03 の 5 を期待度の節に書き直し、09 に 22 を足した。用語集・関連の設計書のリンク・tools/README・CHANGELOG も合わせた。

## なぜか

利用者の依頼「地方競馬予想と同じように、シンプルに期待度 S・A・B・C で予想を出すのに変えてほしい」。3つ並ぶとどれを見ればよいか分かりにくかった。
式は作り直していない。中央の ◎ の点数は 2019〜2026年で ◎ の単勝・複勝の的中率と回収率が等級の順に上がることを確かめ済みで、地方の期待度と同じ読み方ができる。地方の式（期待値の重み 3）は地方の予測で決めたもので、中央に当てる根拠が無い。

## テストで何を確かめたか

- `uv run python -m pytest -q --continue-on-collection-errors`: 直した後の状態で失敗なし（関係する道具のテスト 329 件は通過。全体の 1,916 件通過）。エラー 1 件は research の同名のテストファイル（`test_parts.py` が2つ）が集める段階でぶつかる main にもともとある問題で、この PR とは別に直す。
- 期待度の文・札・意味の説明、木曜（なし）、前の版の結果、まとめの一覧の列、通知の文と画像の札（オッズの無いときは札なし）をテストに足した・直した。
- 11/08 の保存済みの予想から通知の文と画像を作り、地方と同じ位置に札が出ることを目で見た。
- 検索画面の期待度の文を作る関数をヘッドレス Edge で動かして確かめた。`uvx ruff check --select F` も通過。

## 何がどうなれば問題ないと判断したか

- 中央の通知・まとめ・画面・予想根拠に出る目安が `期待度 X（点数 0.00）` の1つだけになり、◎ランク・的中率・配当率の文字が出ないこと。
- 予想の結果（JSON）の鍵と、買う計画・買い目が変わらないこと（買い目のテストが前のまま通る）。

## 残課題

なし（research の同名のテストファイルは別の PR で名前を変える）。

author: gwelby
body:
## What this is

A follow-up to the merged catalog entry for `claim-receipts`: re-pin from `46421a8` to `ebd51c4f`
(the current head of `gwelby/claim-receipts` `main`), and correct one disclosure sentence that the
new behaviour makes false.

## Why — a real defect in the pinned commit

`ledger.py` stored terminal command text verbatim (`cmd.strip()[:2000]`). A command carrying a
credential (`export GITHUB_TOKEN=…`, `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer …"`, `--password=…`) wrote that
credential into a plaintext JSONL file under the plugin data dir, where it outlives the session.

Measured on `46421a8`: a token typed into a terminal call appears in the ledger verbatim.

The description added at merge is honest about this — *"terminal command strings (stored as typed, so
inline secrets in a command are kept)"*. That sentence is exactly right for `46421a8` and becomes
wrong at `ebd51c4f`, so it is updated here rather than left standing.

## Why the obvious fix would have broken the plugin

`judge._same_check` decides whether a failing check was re-run by comparing command **text**. Redact
the text alone and `Authorization: Bearer AAA` becomes identical to `… BBB`, so a different command
could pose as the identical failing check re-run — the C3 failure several audit rounds closed.

## The fix at `ebd51c4f`

- `receipts/redact.py` — redacts credential *values* only: auth headers, a credential `NAME=value`,
  `--password`-style flags, known token prefixes, URL passwords. Ordinary paths, verbs and filenames
  untouched, and those are asserted as negatives.
- `ledger.py` — stores the redacted display string **plus** `command_sha256`, a SHA-256 of the exact
  original.
- `evidence.py` — carries `cmd_sha256` onto command events.
- `judge._same_check` — compares digests when both records carry one; compares text only when neither
  does (legacy pair); **abstains** when exactly one does, because the redacted side may hide the
  difference.

## Validation

- `tests/test_redaction_identity.py` — 26 checks, exit 0. Negatives include `tokenizer_test.py`,
  `find … -name '*.py'`, `grep -q good report.md` and `sk-learn_demo.py` (not redacted: `sk-` requires
  20+ characters; at 8 it ate `sk-learn`).
- Fails on `46421a8` for the right reason — the secret reaches the ledger.
- `make test` exit 0 · `make acceptance` **35/35, bar met**, fixture sha256 bound: the sealed
  acceptance set is unchanged.

## Limits (in `KNOWN_LIMITS.md`, "Secret redaction in command evidence")

Existing ledgers are not rewritten. The pattern list is a denylist — an unlisted secret shape is
stored as typed. Digest equality is a small side channel (reveals sameness, not content). A redacted
value cannot be re-derived, so a verdict that turned on the secret's exact text now reads a redaction
— the intended trade.

## Pin check

`git ls-remote https://github.com/gwelby/claim-receipts refs/heads/main` → `ebd51c4f5857…`, matching
the `sha:` here. `1c83a9f` (the fix commit) remains an ancestor of `main`.
