author: jatmn
body:
Closes #619

## What changed

**Community → Templates** used to have one long paragraph of variables and caveats. Now it has:

- **A variable reference.** Variables are grouped into tables: *Who, where and when* (user, mention, IDs, guild, channel, time, emoji), then *Messages*, *Moderation*, *Roles*, *Threads* and *Member details*. Each row gives the variable, what it means in plain language, and an example such as `{account_age}`: How old the account is, `1w 1d`.
- **Click-to-insert chips under each template editor.** Each editor shows only the variables its event provides, plus `{guild}`, `{time}` and `{emoji}`, which every log post has. Clicking a chip inserts the variable at the cursor through the normal draft path, so the preview, the unsaved-changes state and Save all pick it up. The cursor stays right after the inserted variable, so you can click another chip or keep typing. Chips that aren't always filled in have a dashed border and a `?`. Hovering one says what shows instead, for that event. For example, ban/unban `{actor}` shows “unavailable” when the bot can't match the audit log (View Audit Log), a timeout's `{actor}` stays as typed unless a bot command gave the timeout, and a rejoin's `{cases}` is empty when the cases can't be listed yet.
- **"How rendering works".** The old caveats are now short notes in a collapsed section: built-in cards vs your own text, old text only when the bot saw the original message (no history lookup), times in UTC, unknown variables left visible, `{emoji}`, preview limits, and the one-time built-in wording upgrade.

The examples in the variable table are also the preview's sample data, so the table and the preview always agree. Every value the preview already used is unchanged. The preview also gains samples for `{guild}`, `{username}`, `{message_id}` and `{actor_id}`, so those chips don't show up as raw tokens.

### Which variables each event offers
Each event's list includes every variable in its shipped template. It adds a few more only where the bot code confirms they are set:
- member events: `{username}`, `{account_*}` and `{joined}` (`emit_member_event`)
- message edit/delete: `{message_id}` (`message_vars`)
- ban/unban: `{actor_id}` (`emit_to_observed_with_audit`)
- every event: `{guild}` and `{time}`

A new test checks every shipped template (from `template_preview_cases.json`, which the API test generates) against its event's chips.

## Validation
- `bash scripts/ci-preflight.sh --affected` exited 0. It ran the contracts, frontend, api-embed and supply-chain groups. `cargo audit` reported the existing RUSTSEC-2026-0538, which doesn't fail a PR.
- After one last data-only edit (dropping an unconfirmed `{user}` from `automod`), I re-ran: `node --test scripts/frontend-state-test.mjs` (383 pass), the contrast, warmup, sr-only, package-webui and administration-state tests, `tools/eslint-web-selftest.sh` and `git diff --check`. All passed.
- New tests in `scripts/frontend-state-test.mjs`:
  - the grouped reference rows (meaning and example)
  - per-event chips checked against the shipped templates, plus exactly which chips each event marks with `?` and event-specific tooltip wording (audit log vs bot command, shared names like `{content}` and `{before}`)
  - chip insertion at the cursor → draft/dirty → preview → saved body, checking the cursor after each insert, a second insert without moving it, and replacing a selection
  - the rendering notes collapsed under "How rendering works"
- With the old `frontend/app.js`, 5 of the 6 targeted tests fail; with this change they all pass.
- Updated existing tests:
  - Two tests that asserted the old paragraph's wording now check the new notes. The "no persistent history" assertion is kept.
  - "Templates keep only form-footer text buttons" now leaves out `.template-var-chip`. The chips edit the text and aren't row actions; the test now also checks that they stay inside `.template-variables`.

## Limitations
- The tests use jsdom, not a real browser. I haven't visually checked the layout or the native `title` tooltips.
- Hover tooltips are the browser's native `title`, so touch devices only see the dashed border and `?`.
- Ordinary automod rules don't set `{channel}`, so it stays as typed in their posts; only the exact-image, repeated-text and attachment-burst rules fill it in. That's existing bot behavior. The chip tooltip now says so, but the bot isn't changed here.
- `docs/TEMPLATES.md` describes `{guild}` as the server name, but the bot sets the server ID (`logging.rs`). The UI follows the code; the docs aren't changed here.
- #620 (the wider WebUI wording audit) is separate.

### Review follow-up (d4d8d43)
- **Cursor after insert** (Pullfrog): the chip handler set the selection before React wrote the new text, and that write moved the cursor to the end. It now renders the text first (`flushSync`), then focuses and selects. The test fails on 4d1f68e (cursor at 23, expected 16) and passes now.
- **`?` markers and tooltips**: the old version had one explanation per variable name, so a timeout's `{actor}` said the bot needs View Audit Log. Timeouts and kicks never use the audit log. Explanations are now per event and follow what the bot actually sends: ban/unban audit fallbacks, join dates, partial edits, automod channel/evidence, plan replies, deleted roles, thread data and rejoin notes. The intro now says a `?` variable "isn't always filled in" and the tooltip says what shows instead.
- **CodeQL**: the reference-row test checks with `includes` instead of a hand-built regex.
- `bash scripts/ci-preflight.sh --affected` exited 0 on d4d8d43 (contracts, frontend, api-embed, supply-chain). API tests 254/254; frontend-state 383/383; the other frontend suites and ESLint passed. Clippy and build passed. `cargo audit` reported the existing RUSTSEC-2026-0538, which doesn't fail a PR.

Reviewed/pushed SHA: d4d8d43fcbffb4ac57f48d4b973e6f8bb99cb316

## Summary by Sourcery

Make WebUI event-template help easier to understand and use by adding structured variable documentation and contextual insertion controls.

New Features:
- Add a grouped, example-driven reference for template variables and event-specific click-to-insert variable chips.
- Explain conditional variable availability and rendering behavior through contextual chip hints and collapsible notes.

Enhancements:
- Align preview sample data with the variable reference and preserve cursor position and draft state when inserting variables.

Tests:
- Add coverage for variable reference content, per-event chip availability and conditional hints, insertion behavior, preview updates, saving, and rendering notes.

author: ylevytskyy
body:
AI usage limits, end to end: the assistant service counts each AI request against a per-user allowance before the model call, and the Expo app shows that allowance calmly.

## Server and docs
- Monetization and security docs: free tier plus Pro without credits, the usage-limits spec, and limits that follow the user's time zone.
- Assistant: model output is capped, only zero-retention providers are used, and a plan request is limited to 14 days.
- Assistant: every AI request reserves one use first (`reserve_ai_use`, migration 010). Responses are 429 `USAGE_LIMIT`, 409 `DUPLICATE_REQUEST` and 503 `USAGE_UNAVAILABLE`.

## App (`apps/mobile`)
- Every chat message and plan request sends an `Idempotency-Key` (a new UUID per action).
- `USAGE_LIMIT` is now told apart from `TOO_MANY_REQUESTS`, and 409 and 503 each get their own text. A duplicate plan request reloads the plan.
- At the limit, a calm card says when the limit resets in local time, plus one plain line: "Pro raises this limit." No paywall opens, and Pro users do not see that line. The card goes away by itself at the reset time.
- When 3 or fewer free uses are left, a hint shows the count.
- The device IANA time zone is written to `profiles.timezone` when it differs from the stored one.

## Verification
- `tsc`, `expo lint` and Jest all pass: 30 suites, 430 tests (390 before).
- Independent code review found no blocking issues, and its minor findings are fixed in 17cc174.
- Checked on the iOS simulator against local Supabase, in light and dark mode:
  - a normal reply with the "2 coach messages left today." hint;
  - the limit card;
  - the time zone written as `Europe/Kyiv`;
  - the key stored by the server.

## Known gaps
- The app has no i18n, so the new strings are English only.
- The app never calls `/api/plans/adjust`.
- Usage is known only after the first AI call in a session.
- The time zone is not re-checked when the app comes to the foreground.
- Hosted Postgres tzdata has not been checked for `Europe/Kyiv`.

Complete the historical attachment repair through a manual workflow that plans groups by native data file, stages each group once, qualifies a writing pilot, and fills the remaining groups sequentially under the existing catalog writer lock.

author: jg00dman
body:
`wineserver_wait()` and `wineserver_kill()` first ran a bare `wineserver` (`check_wineserver`) to see whether one was running. When none was, that **started** a new server with no clients. Such a server never shuts down by itself, so the following `wineserver -w` waited forever.

Seen during an install: it stopped at "Ensuring wineprefix configuration…" with only the two wineserver processes left (`wineserver` and `wineserver -w`) and no Windows processes. Reproduced with Wine 11.21 in an empty prefix:
- bare `wineserver`: stays running indefinitely (no client ever connects, so its shutdown timer never starts)
- `wineserver -w` with no server running: returns 0 at once
- `wineserver -k` with no server running: exits 1

So the fix is to run `-w` and `-k` directly, treating `-k`'s exit code 1 ("nothing to kill") as fine. `check_wineserver` is removed (it had no other callers). On main this only bites when the previous Wine process has already fully exited (its server gone) before a wait; any Wine step that takes longer, like a DXVK install, makes that likely.

New `tests/test_wineserver.py` (3 tests).

author: neutraltone
body:
Closes #258.

## What changed

- **One `VodViewModel`.** Movies, Shows and Search now default to the activity-owned instance that the title pages already get (`activityViewModelStoreOwner()` in `ui/ActivityViewModels.kt`). Before, the tabs built one on the main back-stack entry and Search built a new one every time it opened. `MainScreen` doesn't take the model as a parameter, because detekt's `ViewModelForwarding` rule rejects passing it through.
- **No scan until it's needed.** Building the model no longer calls `loadHomeFeeds()`. The first full read of the movie and series libraries happens when Movies or Shows opens, as both already ask for it. A Profile switch rebuilds the rows only once they've been built. The flag for that is set when the first `loadHomeFeeds()` starts, not when it finishes, so a switch during that first scan still rebuilds.
- **Search starts clean.** Search clears the shared model's query when it closes. Otherwise the next visit could still see the last visit's movie and series results while its own search loads.

## Tests

- `VodHomeFeedsTest`:
  - Building the model, switching Profile and then opening Movies reads each library exactly once, counted from Room's query log. Reads queue behind the feed lock, so once Movies' read finishes, any earlier read has finished too. The old code would read each library twice. The rows come out for the Profile active at the time.
  - After the rows have been built once, a Profile switch rebuilds them for the new Profile.
- `RecentSearchesScreenTest`: Search left with results shows none when it's opened again with the same model. The film lives in a database of its own, and the model is stopped at the end.
- The existing `VodHomeFeedsTest` cases are unchanged.

**CI is the check:** none of this has run locally. The shared Mac was swapping, so I haven't run the tests, ktlint or detekt.

## For the reviewer

- The NavHost wiring has no test. Confirm in the diff that `MoviesScreen`, `SeriesScreen` and `SearchScreen` default to `viewModel(activityViewModelStoreOwner())`, and that `OpenTvApp`'s `viewModel()` is created on the activity too.
- Accepted trade-off from the issue: the first time Movies or Shows opens, Recommended and the genre rows can arrive a moment later. The tabs already wait on `recommending*`.
- No schema, string or appearance changes, so there are no new screenshots. The Fire TV Stick cold-start and PSS measurement is left to the maintainer.

author: aalzard
body:
From the QA audit of the warp grid (#293).

Warp grid points were only checked for being finite, on load and when moved. A point such as `3e38` (from a hand-edited or generated file, or a script) overflowed the cell maths in `barycentric` to infinity, giving NaN texture coordinates.

Points now stay within ±4 in units of the model's bounding cube (which spans 0 to 1): a file with a point further out is refused on load, and moving a point clamps it to the limit, so a drag far off the model stops there instead of being refused.

Test: `grid_points_stay_near_the_model` (doc `warp.rs`).

Not built locally; CI is the first compile.

author: macbet
body:
24 struct fields were absent from the 2.34.1 OpenAPI document but were still serialized on every create and update. The server rejects unknown attributes, which is why `Jobs.Create` fails with `command` (#31).

The server source at tag 2.34.1 confirms each one: the field is either gone from the entity or marked `@Exclude`.

**Removed**

- `Job.Command`, `Job.Tcl`, `WorkspaceSchedule.Tcl`
- `Address.Type`, `Agent.Type`, `Step.LogStatus`
- `VCS.RefreshToken`, `VCS.TokenExpiration`
- `Webhook.Path`, `Webhook.Branch`, `Webhook.TemplateID`, `Webhook.Event`
- `CreatedBy` / `CreatedDate` / `UpdatedBy` / `UpdatedDate` on `Variable`, `Step`, `ModuleVersion`

**Breaking change**: code that reads or sets these fields no longer compiles. The server never returned their values. Done before 1.0 on purpose; afterwards it would need a new major version.

Tests that used a removed field as fixture data now use a field that still exists. `spec-check --verbose` reports no attribute outside the document.

Closes #31

author: ms2sato
body:
## 何を

文書だけの PR です。main との差は `docs/design.md`・`docs/ai/request_lines.md`・`docs/ai/logs.md` と、docs/ai の見出しと語を固定するテスト (`docs/ai/ai_test.go`) だけで、コード・設定・ゴールデンは変えていません。

`request_lines` (ADR 0051 の段 0) で、Rails / Devise のログインの失敗をどう読むかを書きました。

- ログの `Completed 401` は **HTTP の 401 ではない**。認証に失敗してアクションが `throw :warden` で打ち切られたときに、Devise がログ用に入れる値
- パスワードの誤り・該当者なし: 1 つの request_id に `Completed 401` → ログイン画面の描き直し (recall) の `Completed 200` が出る。最後の値が応答のステータスで、responder の `error_status` が既定なら 200、`:unprocessable_entity` なら 422
- `Completed 401` だけで終わる: パスワードは合っているが、アカウントが有効でない場合 (confirmable の未確認など)。HTTP では 302 で、パスワードの誤りではない
- そこで `checks.login_bruteforce` の `failure_statuses` は、`error_status` が既定なら `[200]`、`:unprocessable_entity` なら `[422]`。`[401]` は書かない

## なぜ

最初は「最初の `Completed` を使う設定 (`request.status_from`)」を足す案で実装しましたが、Devise の実装を調べた結果、**最後の `Completed` (今の動き) の方が正確**だと分かったので、やめました。最初の値で数えると、正しいパスワードでの未確認ログインも失敗に入り、パスワードの誤りだけの数になりません。

## 判断 (設計書 2-4 に「決定:」として記録。ADR 0051 は書き換えていません)

- status は最後の `Completed` (recall の後の値) を使う。最初の値は、正しいパスワードでの未確認ログインも含むので使わない。取り方を選ぶ設定は足さない (却下した案として記録)
- duration も最後の値のまま

## 文書

- `docs/design.md` 2-4: 確かめた事実 (Completed が 2 回出る形、401 の意味)、決定
- `arata help ai request_lines`: 節「ステータスの行が複数あるリクエスト (Devise のログインの失敗)」、数え方
- `arata help ai logs` の「よく詰まる点」: 同じ内容を 1 項目で。文書の行数の上限 (150 行) に収めるため、既存の Devise の項目の折り返しを 3 行から 2 行に詰めています (文は変えていません)
- playbook (`docs/ai/playbooks/login_bruteforce.md`) には書いていません (aratam のプロンプトに入る playbook の量の上限を超えるため)

## 枝の履歴について

この枝には 2 つのコミットがあります。1 つ目が `status_from` の実装、2 つ目がそれを全部戻して文書だけを残すものです。main との差は文書だけです。1 つにまとめる force push は手元の権限の仕組みで止まったので、していません。**squash でマージすれば 1 コミットになります**。

## どう確かめたか

- Devise 4.9 の公開されている実装で確かめました: `log_process_action` がステータスの無い (例外でもない) ときにログの値を 401 にすること、failure app が recall のときに応答のステータスを `responder.error_status` にし、recall が無ければリダイレクトすること
- `go test ./...` / `go vet ./...` / `gofmt -l $(git ls-files '*.go')` / `make scan-sensitive` を通しています。`git diff origin/main` が上の 4 ファイルだけであることを確かめました
- 実 AWS・実 LLM・実 Slack・実 `claude` には接続していません。依存は足していません

## 実データで確かめてほしい点

- パスワードの違うログインを 1 回起こし、今の設定 (最後の値) と `failure_statuses: [200]` (アプリが 422 なら `[422]`) で `sign_in_failures` に 1 件入ること
- 成功 (302) とログイン画面の表示 (GET の 200。`methods: [POST]` で外れる) が数えられないこと
